text:
Introduction and Synopsis
5
In 2025, India pursued a pragmatic and outcome-
oriented foreign policy aimed at advancing national
interests through sustained multilateral engagement,
strengthened bilateral partnerships, and continued
advocacy for reformed multilateralism. Central
to India’s approach were the priorities of the
Global South, alongside enhanced cooperation on
technology, climate action, and security, as well as
the consolidation of strategic partnerships with like-
minded countries. These objectives were supported
by flagship initiatives focused on neighbourhood
connectivity,
the
promotion
of
Digital
Public
Infrastructure (DPI), and the provision of Humanitarian
Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR).
The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) played a central
role in steering India’s foreign policy and global
engagement in pursuit of these objectives. Throughout
the year, India remained committed to safeguarding
its strategic autonomy, championing reforms of
multilateral institutions, addressing the priorities of
the Global South, and protecting its national security.
The international environment in 2025 was shaped
by economic volatility, intensified climate change
deliberations, geopolitical tensions, and energy
challenges. In response, India pursued active global
engagements with countries and multilateral fora
including the United Nations, G20, G7, Quad, SCO,
and BRICS, with a focus on climate action, poverty
alleviation, counter-terrorism, connectivity, and trade.
India’s engagement with its neighbourhood remains
one of the defining pillars of its foreign policy, guided
by the ‘Neighbourhood First’ approach. This approach
is anchored in the principles of Samman (respect),
Samvad (dialogue), Sahyog (cooperation), Shanti
(peace), and Samriddhi (prosperity), as articulated by
the Prime Minister. India’s policy seeks to enhance
physical, digital, and people-to-people connectivity
across the region, with a focus on creating mutually
beneficial,
people-oriented
regional
frameworks
for stability and prosperity. Engagement with the
neighbourhood is pursued in a consultative, non-
reciprocal, and outcome-oriented manner.

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
6
The year witnessed high-level interactions between
India and Afghanistan, including Foreign Minister
Amir Khan Muttaqi’s visit to India in October. Through
these engagements, India and Afghanistan discussed
issues of mutual concern. India continues to provide
humanitarian assistance to the country in the field
of healthcare, capacity-building, infrastructure and
reconstruction. India also restored the embassy status
of its Technical Mission in Kabul. With Bangladesh,
development cooperation remained a cornerstone
of the bilateral relations. Major connectivity projects
were also advanced during the year, alongside the
joint dredging of critical stretches of the Brahmaputra
and Kushiyara rivers to enhance linkages with India’s
North-East.
Economic
connectivity
and
energy
cooperation grew steadily, with Bangladesh importing
approximately 2,750 MW of electricity from India.
India and Bhutan continued to strengthen their
bilateral partnership through sustained high-level
engagement and steady progress across key sectors.
King of Bhutan Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck
visited India twice during the year. The visits witnessed
advanced collaboration in emerging sectors such
as renewable energy, health, STEM, fintech, and
space. Bilateral relations with the Maldives reached
new heights during the year, marked by the Prime
Minister’s State Visit as Guest of Honour for the 60th
Independence Day celebrations of the Maldives,
coinciding with 60 years of diplomatic relations.
The political and security situation in Myanmar
has remained volatile since 2021, and India has
consistently called for the cessation of violence, a
dialogue-based resolution of issues, and a return to
democratic transition through free, fair, and inclusive
elections. High-level engagement continued, with
two meetings between the Prime Minister and Senior
General Min Aung Hlaing, as well as visits by several
Ministers from Myanmar to India.
India and Nepal continued engagement through high-
level and ministerial visits. The bilateral cooperation
advanced across several key domains. Connectivity
witnessed significant progress through new MoUs
for two 400 kV cross-border transmission lines,
authorisation for 1,131 MW of power exports
from Nepal to India, and ongoing work on rail and
infrastructure projects in Nepal.
With strategic autonomy at its core, India continued
to step up its engagement with all the major
powers of the world, taking independent decisions
in the national interest. Engagement with China
was guided by the strategic understanding reached
between the Prime Minister and President of China
Xi Jinping at their meeting in Kazan in October 2024.
Direct air connectivity resumed in October and the
Kailash Mansarovar Yatra reopened via both Nathu
La and Lipulekh. India and Russia marked 25 years
of Strategic Partnership. High-level engagements
including President of Russia Vladimir Putin’s State
Visit to India, parliamentary exchanges, five bilateral
meetings between Foreign Ministers and National
Security Adviser-level strategic dialogue strengthened
bilateral ties. India and the US jointly launched India-
US COMPACT (Catalyzing Opportunities for Military
Partnership, Accelerated Commerce & Technology), a
comprehensive initiative to deepen cooperation across
defence, technology, energy, trade and investment,
multilateral
engagement,
and
people-to-people
ties. As part of this renewed strategic push, they
also announced, “Mission 500” targeting USD 500
billion in bilateral trade by 2030, strengthening the
economic pillar of the partnership. During the 15th
Annual Summit in Tokyo, India and Japan adopted the
India-Japan Joint Vision for the Next Decade and a
Joint Declaration on Security Cooperation.
India’s engagement with Southeast Asian countries
and partners in the Indo-Pacific, under the overall
framework of the ‘Act East Policy’, continued to
expand and deepen on various levels. Bolstering
India’s engagement with the East Asia Summit (EAS),
EAM represented the country and delivered the
National Statement at the 20th East Asia Summit in
Kuala Lumpur. India’s strong commitment to maritime
cooperation, in line with the ASEAN Outlook on the
Indo-Pacific was reiterated.
India’s vision for the Indo-Pacific remains anchored
in promoting a free, open, inclusive, and rules-based
regional order. In 2025, India intensified its engagement
across Indo-Pacific mechanisms, including ASEAN,

Introduction and Synopsis
7
the EAS, the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA), the
Indian Ocean Commission (IOC), the Mekong–Ganga
Cooperation (MGC), the Ayeyawady–Chao Phraya–
Mekong Economic Cooperation Strategy (ACMECS),
the Asia–Europe Meeting (ASEM), and the Indonesia–
Malaysia–Thailand
Growth
Triangle
(IMT-GT);
advancing the MAHASAGAR approach of holistic and
cooperative regional growth.
India’s relations with countries in West Asia
continued to strengthen and deepen during the
year. India and Saudi Arabia Strategic Partnership
Council was expanded to four ministerial committees
covering critical areas of collaboration. India and
Oman concluded the Comprehensive Economic
Partnership Agreement (CEPA). India’s relations with
Qatar were elevated to a strategic partnership and
were strengthened by the State Visit of Amir of Qatar
Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani.
New momentum was given to our engagement with
Africa through rising trade, finance, and capacity-
building. Bilateral trade grew with Ghana, Angola,
Côte d’Ivoire, Cameroon, and the Republic of the
Congo. New lines of credit, including USD 200 million
to Angola, supported infrastructure projects such
as the Niangdo Dam. Training programmes, Indian
Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) slots, and
ICCR scholarships strengthened capacity-building
across governance, defence, and public administration.
Overall, diplomatic outreach continued vigorously
through the year. Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji undertook
State Visits to Portugal, the Slovak Republic, the
Vatican, Angola and Botswana. The visit to Portugal,
undertaken after a gap of 27 years, coincided with the
50th anniversary of the re-establishment of diplomatic
relations between the two countries. This milestone
was commemorated through the issuance of a postage
stamp. The visit contributed to further strengthening
long-standing bilateral ties, particularly in trade and
investment, science and technology, information
technology, renewable energy, connectivity, mobility,
and people-to-people exchanges.
This year marked the first visit in 29 years by the Hon’ble
Rashtrapati ji to the Slovak Republic. Two Memoranda
of Understanding (MoUs) were exchanged during the
visit, including one on cooperation in the field of micro,
small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) between the
National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC) and the
Slovak Business Agency, and another on diplomatic
training cooperation between the Sushma Swaraj
Institute of Foreign Service (SSIFS) and the Slovak
Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs.
In April, Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji attended the Mass of
His Holiness Pope Francis at Saint Peter’s Square in
Vatican City. In October, Hon’ble Vice-President visited
Seychelles to attend the swearing-in ceremony of the
President of Seychelles.
Continuing India’s high-level engagement with
partner countries, the Prime Minister visited Argentina,
Bhutan, Brazil, Canada, China, Croatia, Cyprus,
Ethiopia, France, Ghana, Japan, Jordan, Mauritius,
Namibia, Oman, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Sri
Lanka, Thailand, Trinidad and Tobago, the Maldives,
the United Kingdom and the US to participate in a
wide range of bilateral, plurilateral, and multilateral
engagements.
The Prime Minister also participated in several virtual
and in-person summit-level meetings during the year,
including the G20 Summit, the Outreach Session of
the G7 Summit, the BRICS Summit, and the SCO
Summit.
Throughout 2025, India worked closely with the
international community to combat terrorism in
all its forms and manifestations. A major security
development during the year was India’s response
to the Pahalgam terror attack through the launch of
Operation Sindoor, a calibrated and proportionate
response targeting terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan
and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir. The
operation received broad international support,
reaffirming India’s right to self-defence. India further
strengthened its counter-terrorism agenda through
Joint Working Groups with key partners including
Australia, Egypt, the European Union, France, Italy,
Tanzania, Uzbekistan and the US.
A defining feature of India’s multilateral engagement
in 2025 was its continued contribution to shaping
the G20 agenda. The Prime Minister participated in
the 20th G20 Leaders’ Summit held in Johannesburg

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
8
in November under South Africa’s Presidency. He
proposed six-forward looking initiatives including a
G20 Global Traditional Knowledge Repository, an
Africa Skills Multiplier, a Global Healthcare Response
Team, an Open Satellite Data Partnership, a Critical
Minerals Circularity Initiative, and an Initiative on
Countering the Drug–Terror Nexus, aimed at enhancing
global
resilience
and
cooperation.
The
Prime
Minister’s interventions were widely appreciated by
both developed and developing countries for their
emphasis on holistic and human-centric development,
anchored in the philosophy of Integral Humanism.
The year also witnessed the continued expansion
of the International Solar Alliance (ISA), with new
signatories and ratifications further strengthening its
global footprint. Countries such as Liberia, Angola, and
Mongolia became signatories to the ISA treaty, while
Moldova and Lebanon completed ratification. These
developments reaffirm India’s leadership in advancing
solar energy cooperation and strengthening global
climate action.
India’s development cooperation during the year
has remained demand-driven and grounded in
non-interference and mutual benefit, delivering
concessional finance, projects, debt relief, and
extensive capacity-building across the Global South.
India completed some key infrastructure projects
in partner countries such as Cameroon, Guyana,
Maldives, Mauritius, and Nicaragua. Under the ITEC,
over 14,000 individuals were trained, comprising 250
multi-country options and 3,900 Defence-ITEC slots.
The emphasis of the government on service delivery
and citizen-centric governance is reflected through
the successful roll out of the flagship upgraded version
of its flagship Passport Seva Programme (PSP). The
PSP Version 2.0 is designed to create a digitally
integrated ecosystem connecting all stakeholders
involved in passport services, with a focus on
efficiency, transparency, and user convenience.
The following pages present an integrated overview
of India’s external engagement in 2025. Drawing
upon the thematic and regional chapters that follow, it
outlines the strategic context, principal priorities, and
major diplomatic developments of the year.
India’s Neighbours
Afghanistan
India and Afghanistan strengthened their ties, through
ministerial engagements. Continuing humanitarian
assistance, India gifted 20 ambulances to help
strengthen emergency medical services for the Afghan
people. India and Afghanistan announced the initiation
of the Air Freight Corridor on the Kabul-Delhi and
Kabul-Amritsar sectors, welcomed the reactivation
of the Joint Working Group on Trade, Commerce and
Investment and agreed to explore opportunities for
collaboration in mining and other high-value sectors.
The countries have also agreed to depute Commercial
Representatives at their respective Embassies and
to institutionalise a Joint Chamber of Commerce and
Industry.
EAM handed over 5 ambulances to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Afghanistan Mawlawi Amir Khan Muttaqi, as part of India’s larger
gift of 20 ambulances and medical equipment for the Afghan people, October 2025.

text:
Introduction and Synopsis
9
Pakistan
Pakistan's continued policy of sponsoring cross-
border terrorism against India, including the barbaric
attack in Pahalgam, in the Union Territory of Jammu
and Kashmir on 22 April 2025 that killed 26 innocent
civilians (including one Nepali citizen), led to India's
resolute and multifaceted response. India's response
combined
diplomatic
measures
with
military
operations (‘Operation Sindoor’), targeting terrorist
infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan occupied
Jammu and Kashmir. ‘Operation Sindoor’ has set a
new benchmark in India’s fight against cross-border
terrorism and has established a ‘new normal’.
Furthermore, India continued to combat Pakistan’s
disinformation campaigns on Jammu and Kashmir
during the year and reiterated that terrorism is
incompatible with dialogue. India raised Pakistan’s
complicity in terrorism at bilateral and multilateral
platforms, including at the United Nations, where it
organised the exhibition ‘Human Cost of Terrorism’
from 30 June to 11 July to highlight the impact of
terror on ordinary people.
Despite the strained environment, India continued
to address humanitarian and people-centric issues.
Under the 1974 Protocol on Visit to Religious
Shrines, India facilitated pilgrimages for 5,135 Indian
devotees to religious shrines in Pakistan and hosted
289 Pakistani pilgrims in India, while temporarily
suspending Kartarpur services due to security
concerns. India remained committed to the welfare of
prisoners and fishermen, securing the repatriation of
22 Indian fishermen in 2025 and over 2,700 Indian
nationals since 2014.
Bangladesh
India and Bangladesh share deep bonds of history,
language, culture, and strong people-to-people ties,
which have gradually evolved into a broad-based
partnership. The Prime Minister met Chief Adviser
Professor Muhammad Yunus on the sidelines of
the BIMSTEC Summit in April and conveyed India’s
support following the tragic air crash in Dhaka. He also
extended his condolences on the passing of former
Prime Minister and BNP Chairperson Begum Khaleda
Zia. EAM visited Dhaka in December, to represent the
Government of India at Begum Zia’s funeral. Earlier
this year in February, EAM met Foreign Affairs Adviser
Touhid Hossain in Muscat in February, reaffirming
India’s commitment to a stable and mutually beneficial
partnership anchored in shared aspirations.
India has continued to extend support for various
development-oriented
initiatives
in
Bangladesh
through Lines of Credit and Grants-in-Aid Projects.
India has also extended support for High Impact
Community Development Projects, humanitarian
assistance, disaster relief and capacity building
programmes. Since 2014, India has extended
LoC amounting to USD 6.5 billion in assistance to
Bangladesh.
Major connectivity projects including the joint dredging
of critical stretches of the Brahmaputra and Kushiyara
rivers to enhance linkages with India’s North-East
were advanced during the year. A tripartite Power
Sale Agreement between Nepal Electricity Authority
(NEA), NTPC Vidyut Vyapar Nigam Ltd. (NVVN) and
Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB) was
operationalised in November 2024, following which
the power trade of 40 MW electricity commenced
from Nepal to Bangladesh through the Indian grid in
2025.
Myanmar
Myanmar is an important neighbour, central to India’s
Act East and MAHASAGAR visions, and a key link to
Southeast Asia and ASEAN. India and Myanmar share
deep civilisational and historical ties, reinforced by a
shared Buddhist heritage. Substantial progress was
made during the year in bilateral relations.
India continued to maintain a significant development
cooperation portfolio of about USD 2 billion,
including progress on the Kaladan Project, the
India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway, and
community development initiatives under Border
Area
Development
Program
(BADP),
Rakhine
State Development Program (RSDP), High Impact

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
10
Community Development Projects (HICDP), and Quick
Impact Projects (QIPs).
Reaffirming its role as a first responder, India launched
‘Operation Brahma’ following the March earthquake,
delivering nearly 1,000 MT of HADR and deploying
National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) search-
and-rescue teams, engineering units, and a field
hospital.
India and Myanmar signed an MoU on Cooperation in
the field of Implementation of Pilot Project for Digital
Identity and Programme for Cooperation in Science
and Technology. Under this MoU, a team from National
Institute of Smart Governance (NISG) visited Myanmar
in November and met concerned officials.
Bhutan
India and Bhutan continued to strengthen their
bilateral partnership through sustained high-level
engagement and steady progress across key sectors.
The commissioning of all six units of the 1020 Mega
Watt (MW) Punatsangchhu-II hydroelectric power
project, built with Indian assistance was completed in
August. Prime Minister and the King of Bhutan Jigme
Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck jointly inaugurated the
1020 MW Punatsangchuu-II Hydroelectric Project, a
major milestone in the vibrant and growing mutually
beneficial energy partnership between India and
Bhutan.
Prime Minister and King of Bhutan Jigme Khesar Namgyel
Wangchuck inaugurated the Punatsangchhu-II hydroelectric
power project located in the Wangdue Phodrang District of
Western Bhutan, November 2025.
The Je Khenpo (Chief Abbot) of Bhutan visited India in
September to preside over the consecration ceremony
of the Royal Bhutan Temple at Rajgir, Bihar, which
also saw participation of the Prime Minister Tshering
Tobgay. During the same visit, Prime Minister Tobgay
also visited the Ram Temple at Ayodhya.
Strong people-to-people ties were further reinforced
through education scholarships, capacity-building
programmes, youth exchanges, and cultural initiatives.
Bhutan is developing the Gelephu Mindfulness City
(GMC) as a Special Administrative Region, as per
the vision of the King of Bhutan. The Government of
India has conveyed its support for the project and is
engaging with Bhutan on the various facets of the
initiative.
Nepal
India-Nepal relations are unique, multifaceted and
underpinned by civilisational linkages and strong
people-to-people ties. Bilateral ties witnessed a
renewed momentum throughout the year with high-
level bilateral exchanges and meetings of various
dialogue mechanisms, some of which had resumed
after a long gap. The development partnership also
continued to move forward. Substantial progress was
also achieved in key areas of bilateral cooperation,
particularly in connectivity, including Integrated Check
Posts (ICPs), cross-border rail links, transmission lines
and petroleum product pipelines, motorable bridges
and roads as well as in hydropower projects.
In the wake of political developments in September,
the Government of India welcomed the formation of
the Interim Government, reiterated its commitment to
work closely with Nepal and conveyed full support
to Nepal in its efforts towards restoring peace,
progress and stability. The Government of India also
extended its full support to the Government of Nepal
in response to its request for vehicles and equipment
for its security forces in preparation for elections
scheduled to be held in the following year.
In 2025, Prime Minister held three interactions with
the then Prime Minister of Nepal K.P. Sharma Oli. In
March, the then Foreign Minister of Nepal Arzu Rana

Deuba, visited India to attend Raisina Dialogue. During
the visit, she met EAM and discussed various facets
of India-Nepal bilateral cooperation. Prior to this visit,
she also met EAM on the sidelines of Indian Ocean
Conference (IOC) 2025 in Oman in February.
China
India-China
bilateral
engagement
intensified
significantly in 2025, with Prime Minister visiting China
for the SCO Summit and holding a bilateral meeting
with President Xi Jinping in Tianjin in August. High-
level visits were frequent in the lead-up, including by
the NSA, Raksha Mantri, and EAM, while the Foreign
Secretary met Vice Foreign Minister Sun Weidong
twice during the year. India and China also maintained
regular engagement across multilateral platforms,
including BRICS, the SCO, the G20, and the UN.
Prime Minister met President of China Xi Jinping on the
sidelines of the SCO Summit in Tianjin, August 2025.
The Kailash Mansarovar Yatra resumed through both
the Nathu La and Lipulekh routes, and direct flight
connectivity between the two countries was restored
in late October.
Border-related discussions continued through the
33rd and 34th rounds of the Working Mechanism for
Consultation and Coordination on India-China Border
Affairs (WMCC), held in March and July, and the 24th
round of the Special Representative Mechanism held
in New Delhi in August. The year also marked the
75th anniversary of India-China bilateral relations,
celebrated through think-tank dialogues and cultural
activities. Total bilateral trade stood at USD 96.46
billion up to November, though a trade deficit of USD
75.05 billion remained a concern that both leaders
acknowledged needed to be addressed.
Indian Ocean Region
India advanced its outreach in the Indian Ocean Region
(IOR) through sustained high-level interactions and
collaborative initiatives. Engagements during the year
expanded cooperation in economic growth, defence,
maritime security, connectivity, digital transformation,
and cultural exchanges. These efforts underscored
India’s proactive role in fostering regional partnerships
and promoting a stable, prosperous, and inclusive
Indo-Pacific.
Sri Lanka
India and Sri Lanka share deep civilisational, cultural,
and historical ties, and the relationship occupies
a central place in India’s ‘Neighbourhood First’
policy and MAHASAGAR vision. Bilateral relations
continued to expand, marked by sustained high-level
political engagement and strengthened cooperation
across connectivity, energy, development partnership,
defence, and people-to-people exchanges. The Prime
Minister paid a State Visit to Sri Lanka in April - the
first by any Head of Government since President
Anura Kumara Dissanayake assumed office. The State
Visit witnessed the signing of seven MoUs across
defence, health, digital cooperation, and energy. At
the same time, debt restructuring arrangements were
concluded, and five India-assisted projects were
jointly inaugurated during the visit.

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
12
High-level exchanges continued throughout the year,
including the visit of the Sri Lankan Prime Minister
Harini Amarasuriya to India in October, during which
she met the Prime Minister and the EAM. A series of
ministerial-level engagements further strengthened
sectoral cooperation, including visits by Sri Lankan
Ministers responsible for Youth Affairs, Industry,
Digital Economy, Ports and Civil Aviation, Trade,
and Energy. Multiple parliamentary and political
delegations also visited India, reflecting the growing
breadth of people-centric and institutional linkages
between the two countries.
The year witnessed substantial progress across
development, economic, and defence cooperation.
Several major infrastructure projects, including
railway upgrades, solar initiatives, and agricultural
cold-chain facilities, were launched or completed with
Indian assistance. India extended financial support
for the passenger ferry service, signed new MoUs
in renewable energy, agriculture, and health, and
advanced the Trincomalee Energy Hub in partnership
with Sri Lanka and the United Arab Emirates (UAE).
Capacity-building remained a strong pillar, with
over 200 Sri Lankan civil servants trained under the
National Centre for Good Governance - Sri Lanka
Institute of Development Administration (NCGG-
SLIDA) programme and 700 additional annual training
slots announced. These developments collectively
reinforced the steady strengthening of India–Sri Lanka
ties across all domains.
Maldives
High-level engagements remained active throughout
the year, with multiple visits by the Maldivian
Foreign Minister and Defence Minister, parliamentary
delegations, and senior officials, as well as meetings
between the Prime Minister and President Mohamed
Muizzu in Malé and on the sidelines of the SCO
Summit in August.
Prime Minister and the President of Maldives
Mohamed Muizzu jointly inaugurated the state-of-
the-art Ministry of Defence (MoD) building in Male.
Prime Minister was conferred the ‘Sri Lanka Mitra Vibhushana’ award - Sri Lanka’s highest honour bestowed on foreign leaders during
his State Visit to the country, April 2025.

text:
Introduction and Synopsis
13
The 11-storey building was constructed with India's
financial assistance and will contribute towards
enhancing the capabilities of the defence and law
enforcement authorities of Maldives.
Bilateral cooperation continued to focus on maritime
security, connectivity, people-to-people exchanges,
and development partnership. Trade remained steady,
with USD 309 million recorded during the year, and
India extended its restriction-free export arrangement
for essential commodities for another year. The Prime
Minister’s visit witnessed the signing of the terms of
reference for FTA negotiations; the introduction of
UPI network-to-network payments in the Maldives;
the inauguration of key infrastructure, including the
aforementioned the Ministry of Defence Building;
and the handing over of 3,300 social housing units in
Hulhumalé. Eight MoUs were exchanged, expanding
cooperation in digital public infrastructure, fisheries,
meteorology, and pharmacopoeia standards.
Defence ties were reinforced through Joint Staff Talks,
the Defence Cooperation Dialogue, and extensive
capacity-building for Maldives National Defence
Force (MNDF) personnel. More than 400 Maldivian
nationals received training in India under ITEC and
institutional MoUs. At the same time, tourism and
people-to-people exchanges remained robust, further
cementing the enduring warmth and strategic depth
of the India–Maldives partnership.
Mauritius
In September, Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji welcomed Prime
Minister of Mauritius Navinchandra Ramgoolam, during
his State Visit to India. Prior to this, the Prime Minister
had paid a State Visit to Mauritius in March, during
which the relationship was elevated to an Enhanced
Strategic Partnership and a Joint Vision Document
was adopted. Eight MoUs were signed across sectors,
including training and capacity-building programmes
for public service officers, training of diplomats, local
currency settlement of bilateral trade, cooperation in
the field of small and medium enterprises, the blue
economy, an Indian rupee-denominated line of credit,
and white shipping information exchange.
Prime Minister of Mauritius Navinchandra Ramgoolam called on Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji during his eight-day state visit to India at

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
14
During the visit, the Prime Minister announced that
India’s maritime policy has evolved into MAHASAGAR
(Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and
Growth Across Regions), becoming a symbol of
India’s growing global footprint. The Prime Minister
stated that the vision of transforming ‘SAGAR to
MAHASAGAR’ will propel India towards achieving
the goal of becoming a global leader in the maritime
sector.
Seychelles
India views Seychelles as a crucial partner in the
IOR, aligning with its Vision MAHASAGAR and
India’s commitment to the Global South. Bilateral
engagements were strengthened with high-level
and ministerial visits. During his visit, Hon’ble Vice
President held talks with Vice President of Seychelles
Sebastien Pillay and addressed the Indian community
in Seychelles.
India continued its socio-economic partnership with
Seychelles by advancing HICDP projects, including
road construction and procurement of medical
equipment. Enhancing connectivity, tourism, trade
and people-to-people ties, direct flights commenced
between Mumbai and Mahe Island, with four flights
per week.
Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA)
India's engagement with the IORA deepened
significantly during the year, culminating in India
assuming the Chairship of the organisation for the
2025–2027 term on 12 November. India participated
in the 27th Committee of Senior Officials and the 24th
Council of Ministers held virtually in May under Sri
Lanka's Chairship, and continued to lead the Working
Group on Maritime Safety and Security, holding its
second meeting under Indian leadership in May to
update the work plan. India also participated in the
Working Group on Disaster Risk Management and
joined the Ad-hoc Committee on Finance to strengthen
the Secretariat's business processes.
South East Asia and Indo-Pacific
India’s engagement with Southeast Asian countries
and partners in the Indo-Pacific, under the overall
framework of the Act East Policy, continued to expand
and deepen on various levels.
President of Indonesia Prabowo Subianto paid
his first State Visit to India from 23 to 26 January
and was the Chief Guest at India’s 76th Republic
Day celebrations. In a historic first, a 352-member
marching and band contingent from the Indonesian
Armed Forces participated in India’s Republic Day
Parade. During the visit, the two sides concluded
several bilateral documents in the fields of health
cooperation, traditional medicine quality assurance,
maritime safety and security, digital development,
and cultural exchange. Indonesia’s Defence Minister
Sjafrie Sjamsoeddin visited India in November, and co-
chaired the third India-Indonesia Defence Ministers’
Dialogue with Raksha Mantri.
President of Singapore Tharman Shanmugaratnam
paid a State Visit to India in January as both countries
celebrated the 60th anniversary of the establishment
of diplomatic relations.
Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji and President of Singapore Tharman
Shanmugaratnam released a joint stamp commemorating
the 60th anniversary of diplomatic ties between India and
Singapore in New Delhi, January 2025.
Later in the year, Prime Minister of Singapore
Lawrence Wong paid an official visit to India from 2–4

September. During this visit, a Roadmap for the India–
Singapore
Comprehensive
Strategic
Partnership
(CSP Roadmap) was adopted. Following this, he held
talks with Prime Minister on the sidelines of the G20
Summit in Johannesburg in November. The relations
were subsequently strengthened with ministerial
visits.
The Prime Minister paid an official visit to Bangkok,
Thailand, in April. The Prime Minister held bilateral
talks with the then Prime Minister of Thailand
Paetongtarn Shinawatra, during which the two leaders
agreed to elevate the existing bilateral relationship to
a Strategic Partnership. Later in the year, EAM held
talks with his counterpart on the margins of ASEAN
Summit meetings in Malaysia and Foreign Minister of
Thailand Sihasak Phuangketkeow’s visit to India.
India-Australia bilateral relations witnessed high-
level interactions and deepening cooperation across
various domains. The Prime Minister of Australia
Anthony Albanese launched ‘A New Roadmap for
Australia’s Economic Engagement with India’ on 26
February to bolster economic ties between the two
countries. He met Prime Minister on the sidelines
of the G20 Leaders’ Summit in Johannesburg in
November. The India-Australia-Canada Technology
and Innovation (ACITI) Partnership was announced on
the margins of the Summit. It is a trilateral partnership
aimed at boosting cooperation on critical and emerging
technology, clean energy, AI and critical minerals.
Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister of
Australia Richard Marles visited India on 3–4 June.
Later in the year, Raksha Mantri paid his first visit to
Australia in 12 years, from 9–10 October. During this
visit, both sides decided to institute an Annual Defence
Ministers’ Dialogue between the two countries. Also
during the visit, the first Australia–India Defence
Industry Roundtable was held in Sydney on 10
October.
The EAM and the Foreign Minister of Australia Penny
Wong met on the sidelines of the Quad Foreign
Ministers’ Meeting (QFMM) in Washington DC on 21
January, and again on the sidelines of the QFMM in
Washington DC, on 2 July. Later, the two Ministers
held a pull-aside meeting on the sidelines of the G20
Foreign Ministers’ Meeting on 25 September in New
York, held on the margins of the UN General Assembly
(UNGA) high-level week. Later in November, Foreign
Minister Penny Wong visited India and co-chaired
the 16th Foreign Ministers’ framework Dialogue with
EAM.
India’s bilateral relationship with New Zealand
witnessed high-level exchanges. Prime Minister
Christopher Luxon paid an official visit to India in
March and was the Chief Guest and Keynote Speaker
at the 10th Raisina Dialogue. During the visit, New
Zealand joined the Coalition for Disaster Resilient
Infrastructure (CDRI) and the Indo-Pacific Oceans
Initiative (IPOI). The India-New Zealand FTA is one
of the fastest-concluded FTAs, enhancing market
access and tariff preferences for Indian exports to
New Zealand.
India stepped up its efforts to engage with countries
in this region through several high-level visits and
under the landmark initiative, the Forum for India–
Pacific Islands Cooperation (FIPIC). India continued
to enhance its engagement with the Pacific Island
Countries (PICs). Through South–South Cooperation,
India provides annual grant-in-aid to all 14 PICs,
including Fiji, Papua New Guinea, Nauru, Solomon
Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, Kiribati, Palau, Vanuatu, and the
Republic of the Marshall Islands, supporting diverse
development projects such as solar electrification,
water storage, disaster relief, and healthcare systems.
Prime Minister of Fiji Sitiveni Rabuka paid his first
official visit to India. The visit witnessed the exchange
of eight bilateral documents, including an MoU on the
design, construction, commissioning, operation, and
maintenance of a 100-bed super-speciality hospital
in Fiji as announced by the Prime Minister during the
third FIPIC Summit, and an MoU on the supply of
medicines under the Jan Aushadhi Scheme, along with
17 announcements aimed at deepening cooperation.
Fiji also joined the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI)
during the visit.

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
16
The EAM chaired a meeting of the FIPIC Foreign
Ministers in New York on 24 September, on the
sidelines of the 80th United Nations General Assembly.
During the 53rd Pacific Islands Forum, MoS Pabitra
Margherita (PM) announced that India will undertake
one Quick Impact Project (QIP) of each country’s
choice. QIPs related to socio-economic development
in Fiji and Nauru were initiated during the year.
India also provided significant assistance through
community-oriented projects, including an annual
grant-in-aid of USD 2.8 million (USD 200,000 to
each PIC). These projects span diverse areas, such
as community development, solar electrification,
purchase and supply of agricultural equipment,
computers, LED bulbs for schools, sewing machines,
dialysis machines, portable sawmills, boats and pickup
trucks, the construction of a sea wall, and coral farms.
In July, India sent 5 MT of high-quality cowpea seeds
to support food security and agricultural resilience in
Fiji. A tripartite agreement on Community Access to
resilient essential health in Micronesia, funded under
the India-UN Development Partnership Fund, was
signed on 29 November.
India supports a free, open, inclusive, and rules-based
Indo-Pacific underpinned by respect for sovereignty,
international law, and the peaceful resolution of
disputes. In 2025, India intensified its engagement
these projects span across Indo-Pacific mechanisms
and institutions.

(ASEAN)
Relations
with
ASEAN
deepened
under
the
Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, with 2025
designated as the ASEAN–India Year of Tourism
and the adoption of the ASEAN–India Plan of Action
(2026–2030). Prime Minister participated in the
22nd ASEAN-India Summit held in Kuala Lumpur in
October in virtual-mode, where he announced 2026
as the ‘ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation’
with an aim to forge partnerships in the blue economy.
Earlier, in July, MoS (PM) led an Indian delegation at
the ASEAN-India Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Kuala
Lumpur.
Prime Minister welcomed Prime Minister of Fiji Sitiveni Ligamamada Rabuka at Hyderabad House in New Delhi, August 2025.

Bolstering India’s engagement with EAS, EAM
represented the country and delivered the National
Statement at the 20th East Asia Summit in Kuala
Lumpur, in October. He underscored India’s strong
commitment to maritime cooperation, in line with the
ASEAN Outlook on the Indo-Pacific.
During the year, India hosted multiple connectivity,
capacity-building, and cultural initiatives across the
BIMSTEC, EAS, and MGC frameworks, operationalised
the BIMSTEC Energy Centre, and expanded QIPs in
Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, and Vietnam (CLMV)
countries.
Under the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI), India
worked with partner countries in co-leading thematic
pillars ranging from maritime security to disaster
management and digital connectivity. As Vice-

maritime safety, the blue economy, and disaster risk
management, and assumed chairship of IORA for the
period 2025-27.

reinforced its central role in shaping an Indo-Pacific

Democratic People’s Republic of Korea

Relations between India and the Democratic People’s
Republic of Korea (DPRK) remained on an even keel.
India remained consistently supportive of efforts to
bring about peace and stability in the Korean Peninsula
through dialogue and diplomacy.

The India–Japan Special Strategic and Global
Partnership was strengthened during the year.
Prime Minister paid an official visit to Japan on 29–
30 August for the 15th India–Japan Annual Summit
with the then Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba. The two
leaders adopted the India–Japan Joint Vision for the
Next Decade, outlining a 10-year strategic roadmap
for cooperation across eight priority areas: economic
partnership, economic security, mobility, ecological
sustainability, technology and innovation, health,
people-to-people and cultural exchanges, and state–
prefecture cooperation. The Summit led to ambitious
agreements on security cooperation, human resource
exchanges (envisaging two-way exchange of 500,000

On the defence front, bilateral exercises including

The year 2025-26 was designated the India-Japan
Year of Science, Technology and Innovation Exchanges,
with multiple scientific and academic collaborations
advancing.
Republic of Korea (ROK)
The year 2025 marked the 10th anniversary of the
India-ROK Special Strategic Partnership. It was marked
by early engagement with the new administration in
Seoul and sustained high-level exchanges. The Prime
Minister met President Lee Jae Myung on the sidelines
of the G7 Summit in Kananaskis in June, followed by
a visit by Special Envoys led by former Prime Minister
Kim Boo-kyum in July for meetings with the Prime
Minister, the EAM, and the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
Prime Minister met President of the Republic of Korea Lee

2025.
The EAM held multiple engagements with Foreign

New Delhi in August, and Kuala Lumpur in
October, reinforcing the growing political dialogue.
Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas led an inter-
ministerial delegation to RoK in November to discuss
possibilities of collaboration with RoK companies
in the shipbuilding sector. Parliamentary and state-
level visits added momentum, including an All-Party
Parliamentary Delegation in May and visits by the
Chief Ministers of Assam, Punjab, and Chhattisgarh.
Defence ties deepened through the inaugural bilateral

naval exercise in October, involving INS Sahyadri, and

expanded, with the Minister of State (Information

Mongolia
The highlight of India–Mongolia relations during the
year was the State Visit of President Khurelsukh
Ukhnaa to India from 13–16 October, coinciding
with the 70th anniversary of diplomatic ties and the
10th anniversary of the Strategic Partnership. During
the visit, he held talks with Prime Minister, EAM and
Speaker of Lok Sabha. The two sides signed and
exchanged ten agreements covering diverse sectors,
and the Prime Minister announced 70 additional ITEC
seats for Mongolian nationals. The visit underscored
growing political trust and reaffirmed the shared
civilisational and spiritual bonds that underpin the
partnership.
The year also saw active engagement across
ministerial, official, and defence channels. The EAM
met Mongolian Foreign Minister Battsetseg Batmunkh
in February, followed by a series of visits by senior
Mongolian officials to India, India Energy Week, and
the Raisina Dialogue. Defence cooperation advanced
through Director General-level talks, the 13th Joint
Working Group on Defence Cooperation, and the
participation of Indian Army contingents in Nomadic
Elephant 2025 and Khaan Quest 2025.
Eurasia and Shanghai Cooperation
Organisation (SCO)
Russia
The year 2025 marked the 25th Anniversary of the
Declaration of the Strategic Partnership between
India and Russia, established during the first State
Visit of President of Russia Vladimir Putin to India in
October 2000.
President of Russia Vladimir Putin paid a State Visit to
India, for the 23rd India-Russia Annual Summit, on 4-5
December. During the visit, agreements/MoUs were
signed in the fields of migration and mobility, health
and food safety, maritime cooperation and polar
waters, fertilisers, customs and commerce, academic
and media collaboration.
Prime Minister met with the President of Russia Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin during the 23rd India- Russia Annual Summit in New
Delhi, December 2025.

India continued to have cordial relations with

India and Azerbaijan maintained their interactions,

Raisina Dialogue and a meeting with the EAM in
March, as well as the eighth round of Foreign Office

Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)
India’s engagement with the Shanghai Cooperation
Organisation (SCO) was guided by the Prime
Minister’s ‘SECURE’ vision, which translates to
Security, Economic Development, Connectivity, Unity,
Respect for Sovereignty and Territorial Integrity,
and Environmental Protection. India consistently
advocated
for
more
decisive
action
against
terrorism, respect for sovereignty, digital inclusion,
and sustainable development. The Prime Minister
participated in the 25th SCO Summit in Tianjin on
1 September, where he outlined India’s approach
built on Security, Connectivity, and Opportunity;
urging a unified opposition to terrorism, including a
condemnation of the Pahalgam attack; and proposed
the creation of a Civilisational Dialogue Forum within
the SCO to strengthen people-to-people ties. The
Summit adopted key agreements on countering
security threats and drug trafficking.
India actively participated in the SCO’s mechanisms,
including the Foreign, Defence, and Security Council
meetings. India also hosted major SCO initiatives,
including the SCO Startup Forum, the Young
Authors’ Conference, and the 20th SCO Forum,
advancing cooperation on innovation, culture, and
regional stability under the ethos of unity and shared
responsibility.
GCC, West Asia and North Africa
Gulf
India’s relations with the Gulf countries continued to
strengthen and deepen during the year. The year saw
the exchange of high-level visits, an increase in trade
and investment, and the further deepening of ties
in areas including energy, security, defence, nuclear
cooperation, culture, education, technology, health,
and food security.
Gulf countries remained among India’s top trading
partners. With bilateral trade exceeding USD 178
billion, an upswing in the trade and commercial
relationship with the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC)
was evident. Investment flows also remained robust,
with cumulative foreign direct investment from GCC
countries standing at about USD 28 billion. India’s
energy imports from the region also remained
substantial.
Prime Minister undertook a State Visit to Saudi Arabia
on 22 April, his third visit to the Kingdom and his first
to Jeddah. Both leaders held official talks and co-
chaired the second meeting of the India–Saudi Arabia
Strategic Partnership Council. Both sides agreed to
collaborate on establishing two oil refineries in India
and signed four agreements in space, health, sports
(anti-doping), and postal cooperation. The Strategic
Partnership Council was expanded to four ministerial
committees covering political, consular, and security
cooperation; defence cooperation; economy, energy,
investment, and technology; and tourism and cultural
cooperation.

with the announcement of a new Ministerial Committee
on
Defence
Cooperation

Strategic

inaugural Army Staff Talks in New Delhi in April. In
December, the Chief of General Staff of Saudi Arabia
General Fayyad bin Hamed Al-Ruwaili visited India
for the first time and held a bilateral meeting with the
Chief of Defence Staff.

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
24
Prime Minister paid a State Visit to Jordan from 15–
16 December, his first full-fledged bilateral visit to
the country in 37 years. The visit coincided with the
75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic
relations between India and Jordan. Prime Minister
held discussions with King Abdullah II bin Al-Hussein
and Prime Minister Jafar Hassan.
During the visit, the two sides signed an MoU on
Technical Cooperation in the Field of New and
Renewable Energy; an MoU on Cooperation in
Water Resources Management and Development; a
Twinning Agreement between Petra and Ellora; the
renewal of the Cultural Exchange Programme for
2025–2029; and a Letter of Intent on cooperation in
sharing successful digital solutions implemented at
population scale for digital transformation.
The Raksha Mantri visited Morocco from 21–23
September, during which he and the Minister Delegate
in charge of the National Defence Administration of
Morocco Abdeltif Loudyi signed an MoU on defence
cooperation.
The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Egypt Badr Abdelatty
visited India from 16 - 17 October to co-chair the
inaugural India–Egypt Strategic Dialogue with the
EAM.
EAM co-chaired the inaugural India - Egypt Strategic Dialogue
with Minister of Foreign Affairs of Egypt Badr Abdelatty in
New Delhi, October 2025.
The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Israel Gideon Sa’ar
visited India from 3-5 November and met the EAM
and the NSA. Earlier in the year, the first India–Israel
Cyber Policy Dialogue was held in Jerusalem in March.
EAM met Minister of Foreign Affairs of Israel Gideon Sa’ar in New Delhi, November 2025.

text:
Introduction and Synopsis
25
The Embassy of India in Tripoli, reopened in July
2024, became fully operational during the year.
Humanitarian
assistance,
development
projects,
and capacity-building remained central to India’s
engagement with the region. India continued to
provide major development support to Palestine,
with projects worth about USD 40 million, including
a super-speciality hospital in Jenin, a women’s
empowerment centre, and the National Printing
Press, and completed several QIPs as well. Sudan
received 2,000 metric tonnes of rice and high-value
cancer medicines; Djibouti received 20 haemodialysis
units and a reverse osmosis plant as humanitarian aid;
Somalia was provided 10 tonnes of medicines; and
Syria received 5 metric tonnes of life-saving drugs.
Capacity-building was scaled up across the region,
including 60 ITEC slots and 12 ICCR scholarships
for Eritrea, 75 ITEC civilian slots for Lebanon, 42
Moroccan officials trained under ITEC, and substantial
ICCR and ITEC allocations and specialised training
for Palestinian and Sudanese students. India’s UN
peacekeeping contribution in Lebanon (INDBATT)
completed 27 years of deployment, continuing
medical, veterinary, and community QIP support.
Africa
During the year, India’s engagement with African
countries was marked by high-level diplomatic visits,
trade expansion, and the promotion of development
partnerships. The year saw active engagement and
high-level exchanges on both sides, including the
Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji’s State Visits to Angola and
Botswana (November), the Prime Minister’s visits to
Ghana and Namibia (July), South Africa (November),
and Ethiopia (December) and the President of Angola’s
State Visit to India in May.
This year, India and Angola marked 40 years of
diplomatic relations. The highlight was Hon’ble
Rashtrapati ji’s visit to Ethiopia in November, where
she also addressed the National Assembly of Angola
and took part in the Independence Day celebrations.
Earlier, President of Angola Joao Lourenco visited India
and met Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji and Prime Minister.
Angola also formally joined the International Solar
Alliance (ISA).
Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji’s visit to Botswana in November,
marked the first-ever visit to the country by an Indian
Head of State. A notable outcome of the visit was
the agreement on translocation of eight cheetahs
presented by Botswana to India under Project
Cheetah- a flagship conservation initiative of India.
Prime Minister paid a historic State Visit to Ghana on
2–3 July, the first such visit in three decades. During
the visit, the signing of four MoUs further cemented
bilateral ties. The Prime Minister also addressed a
special session of the Parliament of Ghana, becoming
the first Indian Prime Minister to do so.
Prime Minister met President of Ghana John Dramani Mahama
at the Presidential Palace in Accra, July 2025.
Prime Minister visited Namibia on 9 July, for the first
time in 27 years, boosting bilateral relations between
the two countries. He held talks with President
Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah and delivered an address
at the National Assembly of Namibia. Two MoUs on
cooperation in health and on setting up the India–
Namibia Entrepreneurship Development Centre were
signed.
India and Ethiopia elevated bilateral ties to ‘Strategic
Partnership’ during the visit of Prime Minister in
December. He met Prime Minister of Ethiopia Abiy
Ahmed and addressed a special joint session of the
two houses of the Ethiopian Parliament. Earlier, the

ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
26
two leaders had held a meeting on the margins of the
G20 Summit in Johannesburg, in November. Enhancing
cooperation through ministerial engagements, Raksha
Mantri and Defence Minister of Ethiopia signed an MoU
on Defence Cooperation on the sidelines of Aero India
in Bengaluru, and EAM met Ethiopian counterpart
Gedion Timothewos on the margins of G20 Summit.
Marking a milestone, India and Ethiopia held their
first-ever Joint Defence Cooperation meeting in New
Delhi in October.
The EAM called on President of South Africa Cyril
Ramaphosa on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign
Ministers’ Meeting held in Johannesburg in February.
On the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers’
Meeting, the EAM met the Foreign Ministers of
Angola and Ethiopia. Later in the year, he met the
Foreign Minister of Sierra Leone Timothy Musa Kabba
on the sidelines of the 80th United Nations General
Assembly (UNGA) on 26 September. The EAM also
held a bilateral meeting with the Minister of Foreign
Affairs of Eswatini Pholile Shakantu who participated
in the WAVES Summit in Mumbai from 1-4 May.
EAM called on President of South Africa Cyril Ramaphosa
on the sidelines of G20 Foreign Ministers’ meeting in
Johannesburg, February 2025
India shipped 15 haemodialysis machines, along with
RO plants and consumables, as grant assistance
to help Sierra Leone address the rising incidence of
kidney disease. During the year, 10 ICCR scholarship
slots granted to Angola were fully utilised.
Major
defence-related
engagements
included
port calls by Indian Navy and Coast Guard ships at
Mombasa in September as part of a deployment under
India’s Vision MAHASAGAR. The visit concluded with
a Passage Exercise (PASSEX) with the Kenya Navy,
reinforcing maritime interoperability. In January, INS
Tushil, India’s newest missile frigate, made a port call
at Walvis Bay, marking the fifth Indian naval ship to
visit Namibia in recent years.
Relations with Africa also saw a marked expansion
in trade, finance, and capacity-building cooperation
during the year. Bilateral trade rose significantly
across multiple countries. India was among Ghana’s
top trading partners and remained the largest
destination for Ghanaian exports. In 2025, bilateral
trade amounted to USD 4.90 billion. Trade with
Angola reached USD 5.03 billion, representing a
20 per cent increase; Côte d’Ivoire surpassed USD 1
billion with rising Indian investments in cashew and
rubber processing; Cameroon recorded USD 933
million with a 31 per cent rise in Indian exports; and
India–Republic of the Congo trade grew by over 83
per cent.
India extended major new lines of credit, including
USD 200 million to Angola. India continued to finance
key projects, such as the Niangdo Dam in Burkina Faso
and a greenfield cement plant in the Republic of the
Congo. Capacity-building accelerated with thousands
of new ITEC training slots allocated across the region,
including 2,088 for Central and West Africa, and
expanded ICCR scholarships, specialised programmes
for diplomats from Chad, the Democratic Republic
of the Congo, Guinea, and Sao Tome and Principe,
and sector-specific training in public administration,
defence, digital governance, and elections.
Europe and European Union
The year 2025 has been an exceptional year in
India’s relations with Europe. The relations with the
European countries and the European Union (EU)
have witnessed unprecedented momentum and a
renewed focus in the present complex geopolitical
circumstances. The high intensity of interactions and
title: mea_annual_report

text:
Introduction and Synopsis
27
exchanges pushed forward bilateral collaboration at
all levels, and is reflective of greater emphasis placed
by the leadership of India and European countries
(and EU) on elevating the traditionally strong ties to
newer heights as well as increasing consultations on
key global and regional matters of mutual interest.
Prime Minister visited France to co-chair the AI Action
Summit in Paris in February 2025, alongside President
of France Emmanuel Macron. This was followed by the
EU College of Commissioners' first-ever visit to India,
led by President of European Commission Ursula von
der Leyen.
Prime Minister met President of the European Commission
Ursula Von Der Leyen at Hyderabad House in New Delhi,
February 2025.
During the visit, the leaders expedited the India-EU
FTA negotiations with a goal to conclude within a
year, and the European Commission published a new
Strategic Agenda on India in September 2025. Hon’ble
Rashtrapati ji also paid a State Visit to Portugal in
April 2025. The year featured reciprocal bilateral
visits by the Prime Minister and Prime Minister of the
UK Keir Starmer in July and October, respectively. The
signing of the India-UK Comprehensive Economic
and Trade Agreement (CETA) marks a significant
milestone in bilateral relations, opening up substantial
opportunities for economic and trade collaboration.
Prime Minister and Prime Minister of UK Keir Starmer
witnessed the signing of the India–UK Comprehensive
Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) in London, July 2025.
Southampton University in the UK became the first
foreign university to establish a campus in Gurugram
under the New Education Policy. During the year, the
EU was India’s largest trading partner in goods, with
bilateral trade exceeding USD 135 billion, Germany
accounting for over 25 per cent and followed by
the Netherlands. Overall, bilateral cooperation has
grown in trade, investment, supply and value chains,
technology, green energy, defence and security,
space, nuclear energy, connectivity, education, and
mobility. India also opened three new Consulates –
Marseille (France), Belfast (UK), and Manchester (UK).
Collaboration with Germany in education, skilling,
and mobility has increased notably, with Indian
professionals and students in Germany doubling
over the past five years, now exceeding 60,000. The
strategic partnership with France was strengthened
through the signing of the Inter-Governmental
Agreement (IGA) for acquiring 26 Rafale aircraft for
the Indian Navy in April. Additionally, India and Italy
adopted a Joint Initiative to Counter Financing of
Terrorism in November.
The visit of the Prime Minister to Cyprus on 15-16
June and to Croatia on 18 June further strengthened
and expanded the partnership with the important
countries in the Mediterranean.
India and the European Free Trade Association
(EFTA), comprising Switzerland, Iceland, Norway,
title: mea_annual_report

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
28
and Liechtenstein had signed a Trade and Economic
Partnership Agreement (TEPA) in March 2024,
which entered into force on 1 October 2025. The
TEPA includes a commitment of USD 100 billion in
investment and the creation of 1 million jobs over the
next 15 years. This landmark agreement is set to boost
the Make in India initiative and create opportunities for
India’s young and talented workforce. Foreign Ministers
of Liechtenstein, Slovenia, Georgia and Moldova
participated in the 10th edition of the Raisina Dialogue,
held in New Delhi in March. Archbishop Paul Richard
Gallagher, Secretary for Relations with States of the
Holy See visited India in July and met EAM. Foreign
Minister of Cyprus Constantinos Kombos visited India
from 29-31 October and held delegation level talks
with EAM where both sides discussed cooperation in
areas of security, defence, trade and technology.
Moreover, some of the strongest support for India
following the Pahalgam terror attack came from
European countries such as Germany, France and EU.
The Americas
North America
India and the United States of America share a
Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership rooted in
shared democratic values, strong bipartisan support,
and deep people-to-people ties. Regular high-level
engagements provided strategic direction to the
partnership during the year.
The Prime Minister paid an official visit to the US in
February. During the visit, together with President of
US Donald Trump, the Prime Minister launched the
US–India COMPACT to advance cooperation across
defence, technology, energy, trade and investment,
multilateral
coordination,
and
people-to-people
linkages. The Prime Minister was also among the first
world leaders to meet President of US Donald Trump
following his second-term inauguration, underscoring
the priority both nations attach to this relationship.
Prime Minister visited Washington D.C. at the invitation of
President of the US Donald J. Trump for an Official Working
Visit, February 2025.
Focusing on leveraging Quad expertise to support
the development of sustainable and resilient port
infrastructure across the Indo-Pacific, the inaugural
Quad Ports of the Future Partnership Conference
was hosted by India in Mumbai alongside the India
Maritime Week, in October.
This year witnessed high-level visits by senior US
defence officials, the delivery of Apache helicopters,
and a full slate of major joint exercises, including
Malabar, Cope, Tiger Triumph, Tiger Claw, Sea
Dragon, and Yudh Abhyas, advanced interoperability
and defence industrial collaboration. Under the
Quad framework, the Annual Meeting and Table
Top Exercise (TTX) of the Quad Partnership on
Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR),
and third Quad Counter Terrorism Working Group
meeting and TTX were held in December.
India–Canada relations are grounded in shared
democratic values and extensive people-to-people
ties. The Prime Minister attended the G7 Summit in
Kananaskis on 17 June. On the margins of the Summit,
the Prime Minister held a bilateral meeting with the
Prime Minister of Canada Mark Carney. Both leaders
title: mea_annual_report

Introduction and Synopsis
29
agreed to take calibrated steps to rebuild trust,
including the early return of High Commissioners, the
resumption of ministerial and working-level dialogues,
and the development of a new roadmap focused on
mutual respect and sensitivities. The leaders met
again on the sidelines of the G20 Leaders’ Summit in
Johannesburg on 23 November, and agreed to begin
negotiations on the CEPA.
Prime Minister held a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister of
Canada Mark Carney on the sidelines of the G7 Summit held in
Kananaskis, June 2025.
Ministerial and official-level discussions addressed
shared priorities, including security cooperation, trade
and investment opportunities, critical minerals, civil
nuclear collaboration, and digital innovation. Both
sides are committed to revitalising frameworks for
energy, agriculture, science and technology, and higher
education. India and Canada expanded economic and
energy collaboration, reaffirmed by Ministerial and
delegation visits.
Latin America and Caribbean
During the year, India’s relations with countries in
Latin America and the Caribbean region steadily
strengthened across several areas. These relations
were marked by strong cooperation at regional and
multilateral fora such as the Caribbean Community
(CARICOM),
the
Central
American
Integration
System (SICA), and the Community of Latin American
and Caribbean States (CELAC). Increased political
engagement provided renewed momentum to these
relationships.
During the year, Ecuador and India commemorated 56
years of diplomatic relations, marking an important
milestone in their long-standing friendship. Prime
Minister paid a State Visit to Trinidad and Tobago from
3–4 July, highlighting the importance the region holds
for India. In the same month, he also visited Argentina
and met President of Argentina Javier Milei. They
discussed mutual interests in bilateral relations and
called for enhancing cooperation in multiple sectors
including energy, agriculture, science and technology,
DPI and transportation.
Prime Minister’s visit to Brazil in July was the first in
57 years. Agreements were signed for cooperation
in the fields of security and counterterrorism, digital
cooperation, renewable energy and agriculture.
Prime Minister was conferred with Brazil’s highest national
honour - The Grand Collar of the National Order of the
Southern Cross by President of Brazil Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
in Brasilia, July 2025.
On the sidelines of multilateral events, the Prime
Minister met President of Mexico Claudia Sheinbaum
Pardo in June; President of Cuba Miguel Díaz-Canel
Bermúdez and President of Bolivia Luis Alberto Arce
title: mea_annual_report

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
30
Catacora in July; and Prime Minister of Jamaica Andrew
Holness in November.
During the year, President of Chile Gabriel Boric
(April), President of Paraguay Santiago Peña Palacios
(June), Vice-President and Minister of Development,
Industry, Trade and Services of Brazil Geraldo Alckmin
(October), the then Executive Vice-President of
Venezuela Delcy Rodriguez (February), Prime Minister
of Guyana Brigadier (Retired) Mark Anthony Phillips
(March), and Deputy Prime Minister of Cuba Eduardo
Martinez Diaz (March) visited India, reflecting the
growing engagements in recent times.
The fifth India–SICA Foreign Ministers’ Meeting was
held on the sidelines of the high-level week of the
United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New
York on 25 September and was co-chaired by the
EAM and the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Panama
Javier Martínez-Acha in his capacity as Pro Tempore
President of SICA.
The Foreign Ministers of Jamaica, Costa Rica, and
Nicaragua; the Deputy Foreign Ministers of Cuba
and the Dominican Republic; and the Vice Minister
of Guatemala participated, along with the EAM, in
the India–CELAC Expanded Troika Foreign Ministers’
Meeting in New York on 26 September.
On the sidelines of UNGA in New York, the EAM
met with his counterparts from Panama, St. Vincent
and Grenadines, Nicaragua, Suriname, St. Lucia,
Guatemala, Cuba, Costa Rica, Mexico and Jamaica.
Relations with the region were enhanced by the visits
of MoS (PM) to Bahamas, Barbados, Cuba, Ecuador,
Nicaragua and Uruguay.
MoS (PM) accepted the prestigious ‘Honorary Order of
Freedom of Barbados’ on behalf of Prime Minister at the
Government House in Bridgetown, March 2025.
India’s bilateral trade with the region increased to
USD 12.539 billion during the year, a testament to the
strength and potential of the economic partnership.
The 10th edition of the Confederation of Indian Industry
(CII) India–LAC Conclave was held on 19-20 March.
Jaipur Foot Camps for providing prosthetic limbs to
persons with disabilities were held in Guatemala,
Trinidad and Tobago, and Nicaragua.
BIMSTEC and SAARC
The Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-
Sectoral Technical and Economic
Cooperation (BIMSTEC)
BIMSTEC fulfils India’s key foreign policy priorities of
‘Neighbourhood First’ and ‘Act East’. Six summits have
been held, with the latest in Bangkok in April. During
the sixth BIMSTEC Summit held in Bangkok in April,
India announced several initiatives, including centres
of excellence in disaster management, sustainable
maritime
transport,
agriculture,
and
traditional
medicine, the BODHI skill development programme,
digital public infrastructure studies, and regional
cancer care capacity building.
Prime Minister participated in the 6th BIMSTEC Summit in
Bangkok, April 2025.
India also hosted multiple events promoting youth
engagement, trade facilitation, cultural exchange,
maritime
security
cooperation,
and
disaster
management
exercises
to
strengthen
regional
integration. This gave further momentum to regional
cooperation in the Bay of Bengal Region.
South Asian Association for Regional
Cooperation (SAARC)
The 60th meeting of the South Asian Association
for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) Programming
title: mea_annual_report
creator: PDFium

text:
Introduction and Synopsis
31
Committee was held in Kathmandu from 28–30 April,
where annual activities of SAARC regional centres
and specialised bodies were finalised. India also
participated in several expert-level meetings across
different sectors during the year. Through these
engagements, India continues to support regional
cooperation, capacity-building, and development
initiatives within the SAARC framework while
maintaining dialogue with neighbouring countries.
United Nations and International
Organisations
India continued to actively engage as a member of
the United Nations (UN), playing a leading role in
advocating multilateralism and the reform of the
global order. The then President of the 79th session
of the UNGA visited India from 4-8 February and
met the Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji and the EAM during
the visit. He also visited several sites of commercial
and cultural significance in New Delhi and Bengaluru,
including India Stack and the Centre for Digital Public
Infrastructure. Prime Minister met Secretary-General
António Guterres on the margins of the AI Action
Summit in France (February) and BRICS Summit in
Brazil (July).
India actively participated in the 80th session of the
UNGA, with the EAM leading the Indian delegation
during the high-level week and delivering India’s
national statement on 27 September. In his address,
he emphasised India’s support for an ambitious UN80
agenda, pressed for comprehensive UN reform to
strengthen peacekeeping, mandate delivery, and
resources for development, and reiterated India’s
readiness to assume greater responsibilities in a
reformed Security Council.
EAM delivered India’s statement at the 80th Session of the
United Nations General Assembly (UNGA80) in New York,
September 2025.
Earlier, EAM had attended the inauguration of the
exhibition on ‘The Human Cost of Terrorism’ at the UN
Headquarters in New York, in June. On the sidelines
of the UNGA, the EAM participated in a High-Level
Meeting of Like-Minded Global South countries and in
ministerial interactions under the G4, G20, IBSA, BRICS,
BIMSTEC, CARICOM, and CELAC frameworks. Bilateral
ministerial meetings were held with a wide range of
partners, including Russia, the UAE, Australia, Brazil,
Canada, Italy, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, and the UK.
EAM hosted the High-Level Meeting and met Foreign Ministers of Like-Minded Global South Countries on the sidelines of the 80th
United Nations General Assembly (UNGA80) in New York, September 2025
title: mea_annual_report
creator: PDFium

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
32
EAM released the UN@80 commemorative stamp in
the presence of the then UN Resident Coordinator of
India Shombi Sharp. The stamp reflects 80 years of UN,
India’s contribution to peacekeeping and depicts the
need for peace in the wake of multiple simultaneous
conflicts across the globe.
The 20th session of the United Nations Educational,
Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)
Intergovernmental Committee for the Safeguarding
of the Intangible Cultural Heritage was held in New
Delhi from 8-13 December. The historic Red Fort
complex, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, was chosen
as the venue, symbolising the convergence of India’s
tangible and intangible heritage under one roof.
The session projected India’s leadership and global
concerted efforts to protect and promote both tangible
and intangible heritage.
MoS Kirti Vardhan Singh (KVS) participated in the 19th
Mid-Term Ministerial Meeting of the Non-Aligned
Movement (NAM) held in Kampala, Uganda, in
October. During the visit, he called on President of
Uganda General Yoweri Kaguta Museveni and met
Minister of Foreign Affairs Gen Jeje Odongo.
MoS (KVS) held talks with the Foreign Minister of Mozambique
Maria Manuela Lucas on the sidelines of the NAM Midterm
Ministerial meeting in Kampala, October 2025.
During Conference of Parties (CoP) 30 held in Belém,
Brazil, India strongly advocated the protection of
multilateralism and the centrality of equity and
common but differentiated responsibilities and
respective capabilities in global climate action. India
emphasised that climate finance remains the key
enabler of ambition, calling for a clear definition
of climate finance and enhanced public finance for
adaptation, among other priorities.
India hosted the second WHO Global Summit
on Traditional Medicine in December, reinforcing
the
leadership
in
evidence-based
traditional,
complementary and integrative medicine.
India participated in the 116th Session of the
International Organisation for Migration (IOM) Council
and delivered a statement emphasising alignment
between development and migration policies for
smart outcomes.
G20
In 2025, India actively engaged across all G20
platforms under the South African Presidency,
contributing to consensus-building on geopolitical
and development issues, strengthening efforts to
counter terrorism and its financing, and reinforcing
the centrality of the development agenda, including
Africa-focused priorities and the continuity of
outcomes from India’s own G20 Presidency.
India ensured robust participation at key G20 Ministerial
meetings hosted by South Africa, with representation
by EAM, Minister of Culture, MoS (PM), MoS
(Commerce and Industry), and the Principal Secretary
to the Prime Minister. EAM led the Indian delegation
to the first G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting on 20–
21 February, delivering interventions on the global
geopolitical situation and reviewing South Africa’s
G20 priorities. He also participated in the second
G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting on 25 September in
New York, held on the sidelines of the UNGA, making
interventions on the theme ‘The United Nations at 80:
Reaffirming Peace as a Path to Sustainable Economic
Development’. MoS (PM) led the Indian delegation
to the G20 Development Ministers’ Meeting on 24-
title: mea_annual_report
creator: PDFium

text:
Introduction and Synopsis
33
25 July in Skukuza, Mpumalanga, South Africa. The
meeting adopted a Ministerial Declaration and two
outcome documents: a Call to Action for Combating
Illicit Financial Flows and a Call to Action on Social
Protection Systems. At India’s behest, the Declaration
recognised ‘terrorism’ as a ‘global crisis’ for the first
time in a G20 Development Ministerial Declaration.
Prime Minister participated in the G20 Leaders’ Summit
on 22–23 November in Johannesburg, hosted by the
President of South Africa Cyril Ramaphosa. During
this meeting, the Prime Minister proposed seven
initiatives for G20 consideration: creation of a G20
Global Traditional Knowledge Repository, creation
of a G20 Africa Skills Multiplier, creation of a G20
Global Healthcare Response Team, establishment of
a G20 Open Satellite Data Partnership, creation of a
G20 Critical Minerals Circularity Initiative, creation of
a G20 Initiative on Countering the Drug–Terror Nexus,
and creation of a G20 Global Framework for Talent
Mobility.
These proposals reflect India’s focus on fostering
global collaboration, leveraging technology and
knowledge, and addressing shared challenges in
development, health, security, and sustainability.
Multilateral Economic Relations
BRICS
The 17th BRICS Summit, held in Rio de Janeiro on 6-7
July under the theme ‘Strengthening Global South
Cooperation for a More Inclusive and Sustainable
Governance’, saw the Prime Minister lead the Indian
delegation as leaders adopted the Rio Summit
Declaration and thematic documents on climate
finance, AI governance, and cooperation on socially
determined diseases.
India maintained active engagement across the BRICS
framework throughout the year, including participation
in the BRICS Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in April, the
virtual BRICS Leaders’ Meeting in September, and the
EAM’s chairing of the Foreign Ministers’ Meeting as
incoming Chair on the sidelines of the UNGA in New
York. A wide range of ministerial meetings, in areas such
as environment, agriculture, disaster management,
tourism, energy, transport, trade, culture, education,
youth, health, labour, communications, science and
technology, and finance, resulted in joint declarations
and cooperation instruments, underscoring the
breadth of India’s comprehensive participation in
BRICS initiatives.
Prime Minister participated in the 17th BRICS Summit in Brazil, July 2025.

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
34
IBSA
Prime Minister led the Indian delegation for the IBSA
Leaders’ Meeting held on the sidelines of the G20
Summit in Johannesburg, on 23 November. Prior
to this, boosting ministerial engagements, EAM
participated in the IBSA Foreign Ministers’ Meeting on
the sidelines of UNGA in September.
Disarmament and International
Security Affairs
This year, India remained actively engaged in the field
of disarmament, non-proliferation and international
security and maintained a strong and credible narrative
based on its experiences and engagements in various
regional and multilateral forums.
India participated actively in the meetings of the
UN
Disarmament
Commission,
Conference
on
Disarmament, Chemical Weapons Convention (CWC),
and Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons
(CCW), as well as various other multilateral forums
and mechanisms dealing with these issues. India also
participated in the meetings of the Australia Group,
Wassenaar Agreement, Missile Technology Control
Regime and the Hague Code of Conduct, contributing
to the global efforts towards realisation of the goals of
non-proliferation.
Economic Diplomacy
The Economic Diplomacy (ED) Division served as the
nodal division in MEA for processing foreign direct
investment (FDI) cases, playing a facilitative role in
coordination with DPIIT, Invest India, state investment
agencies and Indian Missions abroad. India recorded a
significant rise in FDI in the first quarter of FY 2025–26
compared to FY 2024–25, reaching USD 18.62 billion.
India has signed Local Currency Settlement System
(LCSS) agreements with the UAE, Indonesia, Mauritius
and the Maldives, while processes have been initiated
with Qatar, Kuwait, South Africa and Kenya; similar
arrangements are under consideration with Tanzania
and Nigeria. The Division also coordinated with the
Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) and Reserve
