Counter Terrorism
Due to sustained efforts in the bilateral counter
terrorism dialogues and multilateral engagements,
India garnered greater appreciation and support of
partner countries for our concerns on cross-border
terrorism and state sponsored terrorism, especially
in the aftermath of the Pahalgam terror attack of
22 April. The condemnation of the Pahalgam terror
attack and the joint resolve to bring perpetrators to
justice, was reflected in joint statements on counter
terrorism dialogues with partner countries including
USA, France, EU, Australia and Germany and in the
outcome documents at various multilateral fora,
including the United Nations Security Council (UNSC)
Press Statement of 25 April, the Joint Statement of
QUAD Foreign Ministers Meeting on 1 July and QUAD
Counter Terrorism Working Group on 5 December,
the BRICS Leaders Summit Declaration on 6 July,
the 4th India-Central Asia Foreign Ministers’ Dialogue
on 6 June, Financial Action Task Force (FATF) public
document on ‘Strengthening Efforts for Countering
Financing of Terrorism’ on 16 June.
The Quad Foreign Ministers Meeting was held at the
Department of State in Washington D.C. , July 2025.
In addition, the US State Department has designated
The Resistance Front (TRF), a proxy of the Pakistan-
based terrorist group, Lashkar-e-Taiba, as a Foreign
Terrorist
Organisation
(FTO)
and
a
Specially
Designated Global Terrorist (SDGT).
India has been at the forefront of global efforts to
counter terrorism. The topic of counter terrorism
found prominent mention in bilateral and multilateral
meetings at all levels. India has Joint Working Groups
on Counter Terrorism (JWG-CT) with 26 countries.
India has also been engaging with regional and
multilateral bodies such as BIMSTEC, G20, ASEAN
Regional Forum, SCO, BRICS, EU, FATF and the Quad
on Counter Terrorism.
It was imperative for India to send a clear, strong and
resolute message after the Pahalgam terrorist attack
in Jammu and Kashmir on 22 April. Accordingly, India
responded through Operation Sindoor, hitting terrorist
infrastructure at nine sites in Pakistan and Pakistan-
occupied Jammu and Kashmir. India’s action through
Operation Sindoor was measured, non-escalatory,
proportionate and responsible. India’s approach
earned strong backing from the international
community which supported India’s actions to punish
the perpetrators of cross-border terrorism as a right to
self-defence.
Development Cooperation
India’s development cooperation forms a central pillar
of its foreign policy and reflects its broader vision of
solidarity with the Global South. India’s approach is
demand-driven, consultative, and based on mutual
benefit and respect for sovereignty, distinguishing
it from many traditional aid models. Through the
Development
Partnership
Administration
(DPA)
of the Ministry, India undertakes a wide range of
development
initiatives,
including
concessional
finance, infrastructure projects, capacity building,
humanitarian assistance, digital cooperation, and
cultural heritage restoration. These initiatives span
across Asia, Africa, Latin America, the Caribbean,
and the Pacific Islands. A major component of
India’s development partnership is the provision

with Angola, Mongolia, Maldives and Mauritius. A

countries facing financial distress. In April, India
completed the debt restructuring process with Sri

crisis. Similarly, during the Prime Minister’s visit to
the Maldives, India signed an agreement reducing
Maldives’ annual repayment obligations to Exim Bank
by approximately 40 percent, easing its fiscal burden.
Several infrastructure projects financed through
Indian LoCs were completed, in Guyana, Nicaragua,
Maldives, Mauritius, Cameroon. India also closely
monitors its development portfolio through bilateral
review meetings and site visits.
India’s development cooperation places strong
emphasis on human resource development and
knowledge sharing. This is primarily implemented
through the ITEC programme, launched in 1964.
During the year, approximately 14,000 training
opportunities were offered to government officials
and professionals from 114 partner countries,
covering subjects ranging from agriculture and
entrepreneurship to emerging technologies such as
artificial intelligence and biotechnology.
India is promoting DPI solutions globally, including
UPI, Aadhaar-based identity systems, DigiLocker,
and telemedicine platforms. Several countries have
signed agreements to adopt these systems, reflecting
growing global interest in the India Stack ecosystem.
India’s development cooperation also includes the
restoration and conservation of heritage sites abroad,
implemented through the Archaeological Survey
of India. Major projects are underway at Ta Prohm
Temple and Preah Vihear Temple in Cambodia, Vat
Phou Temple in Laos, My Son temple complex in
Vietnam. India is also supporting the conservation of
murals, manuscripts, and historical artefacts.

development partner for the Global South. These
initiatives not only strengthen bilateral relations but
also reinforce India’s role as a responsible global

international collaboration.
Policy Planning and Research
The Policy Planning and Research Division serves
as the nodal division of the Ministry for medium-
term policy planning, research, and outreach with
the strategic and academic community. In 2025,
the Division held Policy Planning Dialogues with
counterpart bureaus of Poland, Indonesia and Vietnam,
as well as a joint dialogue with BRICS member states.
The Division spearheads four flagship initiatives, the
Raisina Dialogue, Indian Ocean Conference, Asia
Economic Dialogue, and Global Technology Summit,
which together drew thousands of participants from
across the world. The 10th Raisina Dialogue held in
March attracted over 3,500 representatives from 125
countries, the Indian Ocean Conference was held in
Muscat on the theme of maritime partnership, the Asia
Economic Dialogue focused on economic resilience in
an era of fragmentation, and the Global Technology
Summit explored how emerging technologies can
drive inclusive growth and digital governance.
Beyond the flagship events, the Division organised a
wide range of bilateral and multilateral Track 1.5 and
Track 2 dialogues throughout the year. These included
the India-US Forum where Vice President of the US
JD Vance delivered a virtual keynote, the India-Nordic
Track 1.5 Dialogue in Reykjavik, the India-Indonesia

regional themes, and hosted Sapru House Lectures

Fiji and the President of Chile. Bilateral Track 2 and

The Research and Information System for Developing
Countries (RIS) continued to serve as a key platform
for South-South cooperation, policy dialogue and
capacity building among developing countries. Housed
within RIS, the Global South Centre of Excellence
DAKSHIN organised consultations, workshops and
conferences on agriculture, health, digital public
infrastructure, gender-responsive budgeting and
triangular cooperation, and launched a Special Lecture
Series on the Global South. RIS also organised a
special capacity-building course for diplomats from

and roundtables on energy efficiency, blue economy,

Legal and Treaties Division
The Legal and Treaties Division continued to serve
as the Ministry's primary legal arm and advisor
on international law, vetting and facilitating the
ratification of treaties, and representing India in
multilateral negotiations spanning trade, climate,
maritime law, outer space, investment arbitration, and
international humanitarian law. Key engagements
during the year included active participation in the
UN General Assembly's Sixth Committee, The United
Nations Commission on International Trade Law
(UNCITRAL) working groups on investor-state dispute
settlement reform, the third UN Ocean Conference at
Nice, COP30 in Belém, and negotiations on the legally
binding instrument on plastics pollution. On the
bilateral front, the Division contributed to the signing
of the India-UK CETA in July and negotiations on Free
Trade Agreements with the EU, New Zealand, and
Oman. Across the year, 260 agreements and treaties
were signed on behalf of India, with 24 instruments
of ratification issued, all indexed into the publicly
accessible Indian Treaties Database which now
exceeds 4,000 agreements spanning from 1950 to
2025.

Consular, Passport and Visa
Services
Issuance of passports has emerged in recent years
as the most noticeable statutory and citizen service
rendered by the Ministry of External Affairs. The
Ministry has made many quantitative and qualitative
improvements in the delivery of passport services.
Indian Passports and e-passports, together with
other travel documents such as Identity Certificates
(IC), Emergency Certificates (EC) for returnees to India,
Police Clearance Certificates (PCC) and Line of Control
Travel Permits in Jammu and Kashmir, are issued by
the Ministry of External Affairs through the Central
Passport Organisation and its all India network of 37
Passport Offices, the CPV Division (only Diplomatic
and Official Passports) and the Andaman and Nicobar
Islands Administration. This network has been vastly
expanded by adding 93 Passport Seva Kendras
(PSK) in Public Private Partnership (PPP) mode, with
their total number being 545, and 452 Post Office
Passport Seva Kendras (POPSK) in association with
the Department of Posts, as extended arms of the
Passport Offices.
For Indians living abroad, passports, Overseas Citizen
of India (OCI) cards, EC and other miscellaneous
consular services, apart from attestation of consular
documents, are being rendered by the network of the
203 Indian Missions/Posts abroad, connected to the
PSP system. During this year, more than 1.27 crore
passports have been issued in India of which more than
89 lakhs are e-passports. Starting April this year, the
CPV Division under the supervision of Joint Secretary
(Consular, Passport and Visa Services) has been
appointed as the Nodal Authority for Public Grievances
pertaining to the MEA on Centralized Public Grievance
Redress
and

System
(CPGRAMS).
Pertaining to this, 20,818 grievances were received on
the CPGRAMS Portal, of which 20,482 grievances, i.e.
98.4 percent were disposed of successfully during this
year. The Central Passport Organisation (CPO) was
created in 1959 as a subordinate office of the Ministry
of External Affairs and is headed by Joint Secretary
(CPV) and Chief Passport Officer, who also acts as the
Appellate Authority under the Passports Act, 1967.
The personnel of the CPO Cadre are deployed in 37
Passport Offices, 93 PSKs, and 452 POPSKs across
the country. The sanctioned strength of CPO is 2640,
and the working strength is 1721.

India holds a pivotal position in global migration

The Government actively promotes safe, orderly

Mobility Partnership Agreements and Labour Mobility
Agreements. Key mobility agreements were advanced
during the year with Russia, the UK, Fiji and Australia,
while Joint Working Group meetings were held with
Denmark, Germany, Japan, Oman, Qatar and Saudi
Arabia to streamline labour cooperation, combat
irregular migration and expand skilled mobility
pathways. India also chaired the Colombo Process

States Division
The States Division works to strengthen the external
linkages of India’s States and Union Territories,
promoting trade, investment, tourism, academic
collaboration, and other international partnerships.
This is achieved through close coordination with the
Governments of States and Union Territories, Indian
Missions and Posts abroad, and Foreign Diplomatic
and Trade Missions in India. The Division also
supports the organisation of activities of States and
Union Territories in foreign countries through Indian
Missions and Posts abroad. Branch Secretariats,
Regional Passport Offices, and Passport Offices in
India contribute to the external outreach of States and
Union Territories.
Through continuous liaison with Chief Secretaries and
Resident Commissioners, the Division facilitates visits
of foreign dignitaries, resident Ambassadors, and High
Commissioners. It also supports the signing of MoUs
and Letters of Intent between State Governments and
their foreign counterparts in areas such as trade and
investment promotion, skill development, education,
health, and agricultural research.

and coordinating India’s positions on technology
governance, reinforcing the country’s role in shaping
national and global approaches to emerging and
strategic technologies.

the India-EU Trade and Technology Council (TTC),

on strengthening secure technology ecosystems,
facilitating talent collaboration, and building resilient
supply chains. During the visit of the Prime Minister
of the UK Keir Starmer, to India on 8 and 9 October,
both sides announced several joint initiatives in areas
such as telecommunications, artificial intelligence and
critical minerals.

Green Hydrogen Mission (NGHM) in its capacity as

cr, of which, INR 6375.00 cr (31.07 percent) was for
grant programmes and INR 375.00 cr (1.83 percent)
was for loans. The bulk of Ministry’s Development
Partnership budget, comprising about 49.19 percent,
is allocated to the neighbouring countries under the
Government’s Neighbourhood First Policy, followed
closely by allocation to the extended Indian Ocean
Region (13.62 percent), extended neighbourhood
(3.03 percent), Africa (3.33 percent), Latin American
countries (0.89 percent). The second largest allocation
in the Ministry’s budget was for maintenance of
Indian diplomatic Missions and Posts abroad. Of the
total budget for FY 2025-26 of INR 20516.61, the
bifurcation of allocations between establishment
heads and non-establishment heads is 33.25 percent
(INR. 6820.86 cr) and 66.75 percent (INR 13695.75 cr)
respectively. The Ministry has consistently maintained
its expenditure on Establishment heads within 35
percent of its total budget.
Parliament and Coordination
Division
The Parliament and Coordination Division oversees
parliamentary work, coordination within and outside
the Ministry, monitoring and review of MoUs signed
by India with foreign countries, admission of select
foreign students to Indian educational institutions,
and uploading the Ministry’s inputs on digital
portals to facilitate digital monitoring of work. The
Parliament Section serves as the Ministry’s interface
with Parliament and acts as the nodal point for all
Parliament-related matters, ensuring timely responses
to issues raised in Parliament, in accordance with
established guidelines.
The
Coordination
Section
processed
political
clearances for visits abroad, conferences, seminars,
sports events, exhibitions, and diplomatic or military
flights. In April, the Ministry launched an online portal
to streamline applications for political clearances
for foreign nationals participating in conferences,
seminars, workshops, and sports events in India.
The Division also served as the nodal unit for
facilitating the visits of seven all-party delegations to
key countries from late May to early June in connection
with Operation Sindoor, underscoring India’s collective
resolve against terrorism. The Division also followed
up on operationalising the Framework Agreement for
the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA), an initiative
launched by the Prime Minister on 9 April 2023 to
commemorate 50 years of Project Tiger and promote
the conservation of the world’s seven Big Cats. The

and agreements signed with foreign countries by

the

processed political clearances for foreign students

Conference and Summits Division
The Conference and Summits Division provided
comprehensive logistical support for high-level
international and multilateral events hosted at Sushma
Swaraj Bhawan and other venues in 2025. Key events
included the First India-League of Arab States (LAS)
Universities Presidents Conference on 5-6 February,
Quad Workshop on Pandemic Preparedness on
17-19 March, 11th International Day of Yoga on 21
June, and Third QUAD Counter-Terrorism Working
Group Meeting with Sixth Table Top Exercise on
4-5 December. The Division also facilitated around
450 MEA internal meetings and 50 inter-ministerial
engagements at SSB, ensuring seamless execution
even at short notice.
Rapid Response Cell
India’s humanitarian outreach in 2025 demonstrated
its steadfast commitment to serving humanity
and supporting its partners during times of crisis.
Reinforcing its role as a reliable first responder and
a credible provider of humanitarian assistance and
disaster relief (HADR), India extended timely support
to over 40 partner countries across Asia, Africa, Latin
America, the Caribbean, and the Pacific. In line with
the Neighbourhood First policy, priority was given
to countries in both the immediate and extended
neighbourhoods.
Major operations, such as Operation Sagar Bandhu
in Sri Lanka in response to Cyclone Ditwah and
Operation
Brahma
following
the
devastating

mobilise rapid, whole-of-government relief efforts.
India also continued to provide sustained humanitarian
support to Afghanistan, including relief supplies, food
assistance, vaccines, and medical equipment.
Throughout the year, India’s assistance highlighted
its expanding global humanitarian presence and
solidarity with the Global South. Relief efforts
following Hurricane Melissa reached countries in
the Caribbean, including Jamaica and Cuba, while
humanitarian and health assistance were offered to
Pacific Island Countries under the FIPIC framework.
These initiatives, along with support to countries across
Africa, West Asia, and Latin America, demonstrated
India’s commitment to the spirit of Vasudhaiva
Kutumbakam and South-South cooperation, further
establishing its role as a dependable partner in
addressing humanitarian emergencies worldwide.
Sushma Swaraj Institute of
Foreign Service
This year has been defined by digital transformation
and diversification. With the launch of the Digital
Learning Management System (LMS) on 1 January,
SSIFS has now developed a digital repository of course
materials, digital alumni lists, digital institutional
memory, AI-enabled training techniques, and efficient
and transparent assessment processes. This year, the
Institute conducted 15 training programs for foreign
diplomats including five thematic, five bilateral
and five regional programs. This showcased the
diversity of our partnerships, with 500 diplomats
and officers from over 105 countries benefiting from
these carefully curated programs. This year, we

The Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR)
continued to promote cultural exchanges and global

4047 scholarships to foreign nationals under its 21
Scholarship Schemes, including 1000 scholarships
for Afghan nationals to pursue online undergraduate
and postgraduate courses. ICCR also sponsored
688 artists from India to 67 countries around the
world, and hosted about 400 foreign artists from

gifted nine busts and statues of iconic Indian leaders
to various countries and hosted 63 delegates from
12 countries under its various Visitors Programmes.
ICCR continued to support 38 Indian Cultural Centers
(ICCs) in different parts of the world. During the year,
ICCR also set up 10 ICCR Chairs of Indian Studies in
foreign universities. ICCR in its efforts to strengthen
global cultural engagement, remained active across
its network of 38 Indian Cultural Centres abroad, five
zonal offices, four sub-zonal offices and two regional
offices in India, undertaking regular programming
alongside new initiatives and special events.
Nalanda University
Nalanda University continued to consolidate its role
as a modern international institution rooted in Asia’s
civilisational heritage. The year marked the first full
year of operations at its 455-acre Net-Zero Green
Campus in Rajgir, following its inauguration by the
Prime Minister in June 2024.
Supported by 18 East Asia Summit countries, the
University strengthened its academic and governance
framework through the appointment of a new Vice-
Chancellor, operated six multidisciplinary schools
and several specialised Centres, and announced the
establishment of a Centre for Southeast Asian Studies
to deepen Indo-Pacific academic engagement.
Student enrolment reached 1,268, including 332
international students from over 22 countries,
supported by 363 scholarships under ASEAN,
BIMSTEC, Bhutan, and endowed schemes, while
faculty strength stood at 76. Campus infrastructure
expanded substantially, with fully functional academic
blocks, hostels, an auditorium, sports and residential
facilities, and a Central Library nearing completion.
Academic
activity

robust
through

over 50 MoUs worldwide and active participation
in

of

alongside global outreach engagements in New
York and Washington, D.C., focussed on sustainable
development, knowledge diplomacy, and Digital

The division circulated the revised Records Retention

Afghanistan
India shares deep historical and cultural ties with
Afghanistan. As its contiguous neighbour, India’s
approach to Afghanistan has been guided by its long-
standing friendship and special relationship with
the Afghan people. Additionally, India’s pragmatic
approach to engaging with the Afghan government
has helped it facilitate humanitarian assistance and
address the development needs of the Afghan people.
High-Level Visits
EAM and Foreign Minister of Afghanistan Amir
Khan Muttaqi interacted thrice in 2025. On 16 May,
EAM held a telephonic conversation with Foreign
Minister Muttaqi. During the conversation, the Foreign
Minister strongly condemned the terrorist attack in
Pahalgam. EAM expressed deep appreciation for the
condemnation and welcomed Minister Muttaqi’s firm
rejection of attempts to create distrust between India
and Afghanistan through false and baseless reports.
EAM again spoke to Minister Muttaqi on 1 September
and 3 November, expressing condolences for the lives
lost in the earthquakes. India, as a first responder, sent
earthquake relief materials to Afghanistan.
Foreign Minister Muttaqi visited India on 9-15
October. Apart from his bilateral engagement with
EAM, Minister Muttaqi also visited Darul Uloom in
Deoband. Separately, he interacted with Indian traders,
journalists, think-tanks, members of the Afghan
community, and representatives of Afghan Hindu
and Sikh communities. Minister Muttaqi expressed
his understanding of India's security concerns and
reiterated the Afghan government’s commitment to
not allow any group or individual to use its territory
against India. He also emphasised the need to respect
each other’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. In
keeping with the decision announced during the visit,
the Government of India restored the status of the
Technical Mission of India in Kabul to that of Embassy
of India in Afghanistan w.e.f. 21 October.

Humanitarian assistance
India has been consistently extending humanitarian
aid to Afghanistan and over the past four years, India
has supplied around 50,000 tonnes of wheat, 327
tonnes of medicines and vaccines, 40,000 litres of
pesticide, 69 tonnes of earthquake relief materials and
45 tonnes of food items. Following the earthquakes
that struck in August and November, India supplied 42
tonnes of earthquake relief materials and 60 tonnes of
food items and 73 tonnes of medicines to Afghanistan.
In partnership with the United Nations Office on
Drugs and Crime (UNODC), India has provided over
68 tonnes of medical supplies and 32 tonnes of social
support items for the rehabilitation of drug addicts in
Afghanistan. India organized a Jaipur Foot Camp in
June in Kabul, during which 75 prosthetic limbs were
successfully fitted to Afghan nationals, an initiative
that received wide-appreciation from both local and
international communities.

Development cooperation, Capacity
Building and Human Resource
Development
India is undertaking several development projects,
including construction of hospitals and maternity
health clinics, Thalassemia Centre, Modern Diagnostic
Centre, Oncology Centre, Trauma Centre etc.
India continues to provide online scholarships to
Afghan students for undergraduate and postgraduate
courses at renowned Indian universities.
The Government of India launched a new visa module
on 29 April, to further facilitate visa processing for
Afghan nationals.
Bangladesh
India and Bangladesh share deep bonds rooted in
history, language, culture, and many shared traditions.
Over the years, this relationship has grown into a
broad-based partnership encompassing political
and security cooperation, trade and economic ties,
development partnership, as well as cultural and
people-to-people exchanges. Today, Bangladesh
stands as India’s largest trading partner in South
Asia, while India remains Bangladesh’s largest export
destination within Asia.
Even as Bangladesh’s political landscape witnessed
a significant transition in July 2024, the bilateral
relationship between India and Bangladesh remains
anchored in its deeply people-centric character and
the positive inter-dependencies built over decades.
High level interactions and bilateral institutional
mechanisms continue to be held post August 2024.
In December 2025, in view of the security situation in
Bangladesh, India expressed strong concerns at the
attacks on minorities in Bangladesh and conveyed
its expectations that the interim Government would
ensure the safety of Indian Mission and Posts in
Bangladesh in keeping with its diplomatic obligations.
The common economic aspirations of India and
Bangladesh and their strong people-to-people ties
mandate the need to sustain the momentum of the
bilateral relations for mutual benefit. The shared
prosperity of India and Bangladesh will rely on stable,
positive and constructive engagement between the
two governments.
High-Level Visits
Prime Minister met Chief Advisor Muhammad Yunus
on the sidelines of the BIMSTEC Summit in Bangkok
on 4 April. Prime Minister was the first Head of
Government to convey condolences at the loss of
lives in the tragic air crash in Dhaka on 21 July. He
also conveyed assurances of immediate support
and assistance for the early recovery of the injured.
On 23 July, a burn-injury specialist team from India
reached the National Institute of Burn and Plastic
Surgery (NIBPS) in Dhaka offering critical inputs on
treatment methodology to the Bangladeshi doctors
treating the victims. Prime Minister also extended his
condolences on the passing of former Prime Minister
and Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) Chairperson
Begum Khaleda Zia.
India extended relief assistance to Afghanistan in the wake of the earthquake in the Kunar Province, September 2025.

Prime Minister met Chief Advisor Muhammad Yunus on the
sidelines of the BIMSTEC Summit in Bangkok, April 2025.
EAM met Foreign Affairs Adviser of Bangladesh
Touhid Hossain on the sidelines of the 8th Indian Ocean

EAM visited Dhaka to represent the Government of

EAM met Foreign Affairs Adviser of Bangladesh Touhid
Hossain on the sidelines of the 8th Indian Ocean Conference

Development Cooperation
As on date, Bangladesh is India’s largest development
partner. Since 2014, India has extended LoCs worth
USD 6.5 billion to Bangladesh for infrastructure
development across key sectors such as roads,
railways, shipping, and ports. A comprehensive review
of ongoing and completed LOC projects was jointly
undertaken on 5–6 March. High Impact Community
Development Projects (HICDPs) continue to serve
as a vital pillar of India’s development cooperation
in Bangladesh, encompassing the construction of
student hostels, academic and training institutes,
cultural centres, orphanages, and initiatives for
preserving shared cultural heritage. The Akhaura–
Agartala cross-border rail link, implemented under
India’s grant assistance, was formally handed over to
Bangladesh on 30 June 2024. Following the Defect
Liability Period, the Defects Correction Certificate
was issued on 24 July 2025, marking the successful
completion of the project.
Security and Border Management
There has been active cooperation between relevant
agencies of both countries in countering trans-border
crimes such as illicit drug trafficking, fake currency and
human trafficking, to name a few. Bilateral cooperation
also covers cooperative management mechanisms
for the security of the 4,096 kms long international
border between India and Bangladesh through
border fencing, joint inspection of boundary pillars,
and joint boundary demarcation, including of riverine
boundaries. India seeks cooperation from Bangladesh
border authorities to complete border fencing as a
sustainable measure to ensure border security.
Other bilateral mechanisms including - the DG-level
talks between Border Guarding Forces and DG-
level talks between nodal Drugs Control Agencies
are held regularly. The 56th DG-level BGB-BSF
border conference took place in Dhaka on 25-28
August, pledging deeper coordination to maintain
peace along the border. The 46th Joint Boundary
Conference (Mizoram sector) was held in Dhaka on
9-11 September.
River Water Sharing and Flood
Management
India and Bangladesh share 54 trans-boundary rivers
and bilateral meetings of the Joint River Commissions
(JRC) for sharing of Ganges water are held regularly.
The 88th Meeting of the JRC on sharing of Ganges

waters was held in Delhi on 8-10 September. The
delegations were led by the JRC Members of both
countries. With the increasing risks of floods and
droughts, through mutual understanding between
both countries, India’s Ministry of Water Resources
also shares transboundary river water levels and flood
forecasting data with the relevant authorities from
Bangladesh on a real-time basis to enable preventive
measures and improve flood control.
Economic and Trade Cooperation
Bangladesh is India’s biggest trade partner in South
Asia and India is the second biggest trade partner of
Bangladesh in Asia. India exported USD 11.49 billion
of goods to Bangladesh in 2024-25 while its imports
from Bangladesh were valued at USD 2.00 billion for
the same period. The total bilateral trade in FY 2024-
25 was reported at USD 13.49 billion and the bilateral
trade for the period April-October 2025 stood at USD
7.42 billion.
Connectivity
Connectivity has been a priority area of bilateral
cooperation. Both sides are working to facilitate
seamless movement of people and goods, both in
bilateral and sub-regional contexts. Efforts are being
made to revive the rail, road and waterways that
traditionally linked the people and economies on both
sides as well as establish new connectivity links.
India and Bangladesh are jointly undertaking
dredging of two critical stretches of the Brahmaputra
and
Kushiyara
river
on
the
India-Bangladesh
Protocol routes. This is an ongoing project under
grant assistance, aimed at boosting connectivity of
the North-Eastern states of India with Bangladesh
as well as the rest of the country. Additionally, India
supplied 420 railway freight wagons to Bangladesh
Railway. Both countries are also working towards the
implementation of Bangladesh, Bhutan, India and
Nepal (BBIN) Motor Vehicle Agreement to boost sub-
regional connectivity.
The Inter-Governmental Railway Meeting (IGRM)
between India and Bangladesh was held in New Delhi
on 20-22 January. The meeting featured discussions
on the comprehensive set of issues related to railway
connectivity between both nations. At present, there
are six cross country rail links between India and
Bangladesh. Freight Train movement between India
and Bangladesh is ongoing through cross border rail
links, while passenger train movement between the
two countries has been halted since 19 July 2024, in
view of the current security scenario in Bangladesh.
On the bus connectivity, there are five approved Bus
Protocol Routes between India and Bangladesh.
However, given the current security scenario in
Bangladesh only two buses are plying between
Dhaka-Kolkata-Dhaka.
Power and Energy Cooperation
Cooperation in Power and Energy sector has emerged
as one of the crucial pillars of India-Bangladesh
relations. Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) was
registered as a G2G supplier in 2023 and is supplying
Petroleum, Oil and Lubricants (POL) products to
Bangladesh.
The Joint Working Group (JWG)/Joint Steering
Committee (JSC) on Power provides an institutional
framework to promote bilateral cooperation in cross-
border trade of electricity between the two countries.
Bangladesh is currently importing 2750 MW of power
from India. The Maitree Super Thermal Power Plant
(2 x 600 MW) is operational and has been supplying
electricity to the Bangladesh grid.
A
tripartite

Sale

between

electricity commenced from Nepal to Bangladesh
through the Indian grid.

Development
Since 2014, more than 7240 civil servants and 1250
judicial officers have been trained at Indian Institutions
in the fields of administration including police,
customs, narcotics detection, science and technology,
agriculture and wild life conservation under the aegis

53
Bhutan
India and Bhutan share a distinguished partnership,
characterised by ties of friendship and collaborative
engagement. Benefiting from the outcomes of high-
level meetings, this year saw sustained progress across
the entire spectrum of bilateral cooperation, including
economic cooperation, trade, connectivity, energy,
capacity building, youth exchanges, development
partnership, health, fintech, environment, and people-
to-people ties.
The tradition of regular high-level visits between
the two sides witnessed renewed momentum in
2025. This year witnessed incoming visits of the
King of Bhutan Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck,
Je Khenpo (Chief Abbot) of Bhutan, Prime Minister
of Bhutan Dasho Tshering Tobgay, as well as several
ministerial visits. These engagements provided an
impetus to further enhance and strengthen multi-
sectoral cooperation.
As Bhutan progressed in implementing its 13th Five-
Year Plan (2024-2029), India continued to uphold
its commitment to contribute towards the former’s
development priorities through Project-Tied Assistance
(PTA), High Impact Community Development Projects
(HICDPs), and Economic Stimulus Programme (ESP).
Energy cooperation between India and Bhutan also
achieved a significant milestone with the completion
of the 1020 MW Punatsangchhu-II hydropower
project in Bhutan.
India-Bhutan trade continued to grow during the year
and India remained Bhutan’s top trading partner, both
as an import source and as an export destination.
The year also witnessed an advancement in sectoral
cooperation including in border management, defence,
health, education, capacity building, environment,
sports, space, judiciary, and fintech.
High-Level Visits
Prime Minister of India paid a State Visit to Bhutan on
11-12 November. During the visit, he attended the
70th birth anniversary celebrations of the Fourth King
of Bhutan on 11 November as the Guest of Honour
and participated in the Global Peace Prayer Festival in
Thimphu. Prime Minister and the King of Bhutan Jigme
Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck paid respects to the
Holy Piprahwa Relics of Lord Buddha from India that
were on exposition in Bhutan on 8-25 November, and
jointly inaugurated the 1020 MW Punatsangchuu-II
Hydroelectric Project, a major milestone in the vibrant
and growing mutually beneficial energy partnership
between India and Bhutan.
The King of Bhutan Jigme Khesar Namgyel
Wangchuck visited India twice this year. In February,
the King paid a special visit to India to attend the Maha
Kumbh Mela at Prayagraj. During his second visit in
April, the King visited Assam to view the facilities at
the Inland Waterways Terminal (IWT) and the Multi
Modal Logistics Park at Jogighopa. In February, Prime
Minister of Bhutan Dasho Tshering Tobgay visited New
Delhi as Guest of Honour and the keynote speaker at
the SOUL Leadership Conclave. The Je Khenpo (Chief
Abbot) of Bhutan visited India in September to preside
over the consecration ceremony of the Royal Bhutan
Temple at Rajgir, Bihar, which also saw participation
of the Prime Minister Tobgay. During the same visit,
Prime Minister Tobgay also visited the Shri Ram
Janmabhoomi Temple at Ayodhya.
The Chief Justice of India (CJI) paid a visit to Bhutan
on 22-26 October. His visit was aimed at enhancing
exchanges and cooperation between the judiciaries
of India and Bhutan under the Memorandum of
Understanding (MoU) signed in October 2024. The
two sides considered cooperation in applications of
digital technology, sharing judicial practices and legal
education. During his visit, CJI also addressed the Jigme
Singye Wangchuck School of Law Research Centre’s
Fifth Wisdom for Future Talk Series in Thimphu and
the Third Distinguished Speaker’s Forum at Paro. The
Chief Justice of Bhutan Lyonpo Norbu Tshering visited
New Delhi on 23-27 November to attend the Supreme
Court of India’s Constitution Day Programme. The
two visits further strengthened cooperation, mutual
goodwill and respect between the two judiciaries
and helped in furthering the ties of cooperation and
goodwill between the two judiciaries.

54
Regular Ministerial meetings continued to enable the
two sides to strengthen cooperation in various areas.
Minister of Industry, Employment and Commerce
Lyonpo Namgyal Dorji visited New Delhi for the
Bhutan Investment Roadshow in January and for the
inauguration of Jogighopha Multi-Modal Logistics
Park in Assam in February. Minister of Agriculture and
Livestock Lyonpo Younten Phuntsho represented the
Royal Government of Bhutan and also participated in
the Bengal Global Business Forum in Kolkata and at
Advantage Assam 2.0 in Guwahati in the same month.
The Je Khenpo (Chief Abbot) of Bhutan presided over the
consecration ceremony of the Royal Bhutan Temple at Rajgir in
Bihar, September 2025.
Minister of Foreign Affairs and External Trade of Bhutan
Lyonpo D. N. Dhungyel participated in the Raisina
Dialogue in New Delhi in March and the World Audio
Visual & Entertainment Summit in Mumbai in May.
Home Minister of Bhutan Lyonpo Tshering attended
the Dharma Dhamma Conference in Ahmedabad in
September.
The Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment met
the Minister of Home Affairs and called on the Prime
Minister of Bhutan in November in Thimphu. The
Minister of Parliamentary Affairs and Minority Affairs
had an audience with the King of Bhutan in November
in Thimphu. He also called on the Prime Minister of
Bhutan during the visit.
Foreign Secretary visited Bhutan in October to review
the entire spectrum of the special and multifaceted
India-Bhutan partnership. Similarly, Foreign Secretary
of Bhutan Pema Choden visited India twice - in June
and September for bilateral consultations.
Trade
India continued to account for about 80% of Bhutan’s
global
trade.
India-Bhutan
merchandise
trade
recorded a healthy growth, increasing from INR
10,787 Cr in 2023-24 to INR 16,125 Cr in 2024-25.
India’s exports to Bhutan rose from INR 7,979 Cr to INR
10,696 Cr while imports from Bhutan increased from
INR 2,807 Cr in 2023-24 to INR 5,428 Cr in 2024-25.
In line with bilateral free trade agreement and special
relations, India has notified special exemption for
Bhutan with regard to export of essential agricultural
commodities such as non-basmati rice, wheat, sugar,
milk, potato, tea, areca nut among others. Building on
previous achievements in fintech connectivity of BHIM
application and RuPay cards in Bhutan, an important
milestone was reached this year. Bhutan now accepts
payments from Indian visitors through major UPI
apps- BHIM, PhonePe, Paytm, and Google Pay using
the existing National QR system.
Foreign Secretary held consultations with his Bhutanese
counterpart Pema Choden during her visit to New Delhi,
September 2025.
Connectivity
India and Bhutan signed an Inter-Governmental MoU
for the ‘Establishment of Railway Links between
India and Bhutan’ in September. The MoU follows-
up on the high-level discussions between India
and Bhutan on establishing railway linkages, and
envisages establishment of the Kokrajhar-Gelephu
and Banarhat-Samtse rail links, aimed at connecting
the people and economy of both countries. The first
meeting of the bilateral Project Steering Committee
under the MoU was held in November in New Delhi.

text:
India’s Neighbourhood
55
Secretary (Department of Border Management),
Ministry of Home Affairs visited Bhutan for the 14th
Secretary-Level Meeting on Border Management
and Security Issues held in October. During his visit,
the Secretary called on the Prime Minister and Home
Minister of Bhutan. In keeping with the bilateral
commitment to enhance border infrastructure, both
countries are working towards establishment of the
Integrated Check Posts at several locations along the
India-Bhutan border. Director General Border Roads
(DGBR) visited Bhutan in July to review the ongoing
and planned road infrastructure projects being
undertaken under Project Dantak.
Development Cooperation
The Government of India’s development support of
INR 10000 Crore for Bhutan’s 13th FYP period (2024-
29) continued to be implemented in cooperation
between the two governments. The second tranche
of 10 projects amounting to INR 1113 Crore under
India’s Project Tied Assistance, was agreed between
the two sides, following the first tranche of 61 projects
amounting to INR 5537 Crore. The second batch of
297 High Impact Community Development Projects
(HICDPs) amounting to INR 406 Crore, was agreed
between the two sides in 2025. The total number of
agreed HICDPs between the two countries during the
13th Plan period currently stands at 572, and amounts
to INR 847 Crore.
Foreign Secretary of Bhutan Pema Choden visited
India in July to co-chair the fourth India-Bhutan
Development Cooperation Talks of the 13th Five Year
Plan. Notable developmental projects completed
in Bhutan with India’s assistance this year include -
Tsirang Multi-Sports Hall, Kheri-Pam Crafts Outlet,
Nganglam Water Treatment Plant and Chokeydensa
Water Supply Scheme.
Energy Cooperation
Cooperation in the hydropower generation and supply
sector is an important pillar of India-Bhutan ties. The
commissioning of all six units of the 1020 Mega Watt
(MW) Punatsangchhu-II hydroelectric power project,
built with Indian assistance was completed in August.
The project was jointly inaugurated by Prime Minister
and the King of Bhutan on 11 November during the
former’s visit to Bhutan. The two sides have reached
an understanding on the resumption of work on the
main dam structure of 1200 MW Punatsangchhu-I
hydroelectric project, which was announced during
Prime Minister’s visit to Bhutan.
Chairperson of India’s Central Electricity Authority
(CEA) visited Bhutan in June and held talks with
his counterpart to review aspects of India-Bhutan
electricity trade.
In accordance with the 2024 Joint Vision Document on
the India-Bhutan Energy Partnership, Indian entities in
the energy sector entered into strategic partnerships
with the Druk Green Power Corporation (DGPC),
Bhutan’s state-owned enterprise for development
of hydropower and other energy projects in Bhutan.
Power Finance Corporation Ltd, India’s leading non-
banking financial company in the power sector,
signed a credit agreement for the development of the
600 MW Khorlochhu hydroelectric power project in
Bhutan which is being jointly developed by DGPC and
Tata Power.
Defence Cooperation
Chief of the Army Staff of India visited Bhutan in June.
Chief Operations Officer of the Royal Bhutan Army
Lieutenant General Batoo Tshering paid an official
visit to India in February, where he visited Gaya, New
Delhi and Kolkata. Lt General Batoo Tshering also
participated in the United Nations Troop Contributing
Countries’ Chiefs Conclave, held in New Delhi on 13-
16 October.
Health Cooperation
Bilateral cooperation in the health sector progressed
during the year through further support for
development of healthcare facilities and augmentation
of healthcare services in Bhutan. During Prime
Minister’s visit to Bhutan in November, the two sides
signed two MoUs- a framework MoU on cooperation
between the two Health Ministries, and an MoU on

ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
56
mental health services between National Institute of
Mental Health and Neurosciences, Bengaluru and the
PEMA Secretariat, Bhutan. 20 Indian nurses joined the
National Referral Hospital in Thimphu.
Agriculture and Allied Sectors
Secretary, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’
Welfare visited Bhutan in August and signed the
MoU to further strengthen cooperation in the fields of
agriculture and allied sectors. During his visit, he also
held the first session of the Joint Technical Working
Group (JTWG), under the MoU.
Education Cooperation, Capacity Building
and People-to-People Ties
India remains Bhutan’s steadfast partner in capacity
building of government officials and professionals/
entrepreneurs in various fields. Bhutan is allotted
325 training seats for upgrading administrative and
technical skills of officials and experts under India’s
ITEC programme. Bhutanese civil service officers join
their Indian counterparts at premier Indian training
institutions and academies every year. During the
year, the Government of India conducted customised
training programmes for officials of Bhutan’s Election
Commission, Parliament, Judiciary, Agriculture, Animal
Husbandry, creative sector and energy professionals.
The Government of India provides over 1500 annual
scholarships to Bhutanese students for studying in
India, across a wide range of disciplines including
engineering, medicine, pharmacy, natural and social
sciences under various scholarship schemes. Under
the India-Bhutan education partnership, 22 Indian
STEM teachers were recruited to teach at Bhutanese
schools this year, taking the total number of Indian
STEM teachers under this arrangement to over 50.
India also extended financial and technical support
for Bhutan’s National Service Programme- Gyalsung,
which places youth and skill development at the
heart of national efforts. The first India-Bhutan Youth
Friendship Camp was organised at Officers’ Training
Academy, Gaya in September, bringing together
NCC cadets and Desuung (Bhutan’s volunteer corps)
for joint activities on disaster management, nature
preservation, and cultural engagements. A Bhutanese
Scouts delegation visited India for India’s Republic
Day celebrations in January and an NCC delegation
participated in Bhutan’s National Day Celebrations on
17 December.
Cultural Cooperation
India’s Nehru-Wangchuck Cultural Centre in Thimphu
continued to impart knowledge on Yoga, Indian
traditional music, and other cultural activities between
the people of two countries. An ICCR Kathak cultural
troupe visited Bhutan in January and performed at
several locations in the country. A Traditional Music
Group from Bhutan visited India for the BIMSTEC
Traditional Music Festival held in New Delhi in July-
August.
India and Bhutan share close spiritual and cultural
linkages, an enduring pillar of the unique friendship
between the two countries. A number of Bhutanese
pilgrims travel to Buddhist sites in India. The
construction of the Royal Bhutan Temple was
completed this year and the Je Khenpo presided over
its consecration ceremony in September, with the
participation of the Prime Minister and Home Minister
of Bhutan.
During Prime Minister’s visit to Bhutan in November,
the Government of India announced the grant of land
to Bhutan for building a Buddhist temple at Varanasi.
The Holy Piprahwa Relics of Lord Buddha from
India were in Bhutan for a public exposition on 8-25
November. The Holy Relics were enshrined at the
prestigious Grand Kuenray Hall of Tashichhodzong
in Thimphu, and the exposition coincided with the
Global Peace Prayer Festival organised by Bhutan, as
well as the 70th Birth Anniversary of the Fourth King
of Bhutan Jigme Singye Wangchuck. The Holy Relics
received enormous response including visits by the
King and Queen of Bhutan, the Chief Abbot, members
of the Royal Family, Prime Minister and Ministers
of Bhutan and about 1,08,000 visitors. Minister
of Social Justice and Empowerment accompanied
the Holy Relics on arrival on 8 November and the
Minister of Parliamentary Affairs and Minority Affairs

accompanied the Relics on their return to India on 25

Gelephu Mindfulness City
Bhutan is developing the Gelephu Mindfulness City
(GMC) as a Special Administrative Region, as per
the vision of the King of Bhutan. The Government
of India has conveyed its support for the project and
is engaging with Bhutan on the various facets of
the initiative. During Prime Minister’s visit to Bhutan
in November, the Government of India announced
the decision to establish an Immigration Check Post
at Hatisar, Assam, to facilitate easy movement of
investors and visitors to Gelephu.
Maldives
India and the Maldives are close maritime neighbours
and share deep ethnic, linguistic, and cultural bonds.
The Maldives hold a key place in India’s ‘Neighbourhood
First’ policy and the vision of MAHASAGAR, which
aims to bring stability and prosperity in the region.
India is Maldives’ most trusted friend and has always
stood by the Maldives as the ‘First Responder’. The
bilateral relations scaled newer heights with the
State visit of Prime Minister as the ‘Guest of Honour’
for the celebrations marking the 60th Anniversary of
the Maldives’ independence on 26 July. This year also
marks 60 years since the establishment of diplomatic
relations between India and the Maldives.
High-Level Visits
Prime Minister paid a State Visit to Maldives on 25-
26 July, coinciding with the 60th Independence Day
celebrations of the country and met President of the
Maldives Mohamed Muizzu. The two leaders held
discussions on bilateral, regional, and international
issues of mutual interest. Prime Minister and President
Muizzu also met in Tianjin, on the sidelines of the SCO
Summit held in September.
Foreign Minister of the Maldives Abdulla Khaleel
visited India thrice this year- in January, March and May,
during which he held bilateral meetings with EAM.
The two Ministers also met in Oman on the sidelines
of the Indian Ocean Conference (IOC) in February and
in September in New York on the sidelines of UNGA.
Foreign Minister of the Maldives Abdulla Khaleel met EAM on the sidelines of the Raisina Dialogue in New Delhi, March 2025.

Defence Cooperation

conducted in New Delhi on 26-28 May and the sixth

India remained the leading source of tourists to Maldives

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
60
Myanmar
Myanmar is an important neighbouring country that
shares a 1643 km land border and 1060 km maritime
boundary with India. At the convergence of India’s key
foreign policy priorities, Neighbourhood First, Act East
and MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement
for Security and Growth Across Regions) including
the Indo–Pacific, Myanmar remains critical to India’s
connect with Southeast Asian countries including
ASEAN. India and Myanmar share strong civilisational,
historical and people-to-people ties, with Buddhism
constituting an important cultural link and a part of
India’s shared heritage with Myanmar.
Political and security situation in Myanmar remains
volatile since February 2021. The current security and
humanitarian situation in Myanmar remain a cause of
concern, as it has direct implications for India. The State
of Emergency ended, after 4.5 years, on 31 July and
the State Security and Peace Commission was formed
to supervise the general elections in Myanmar from
December 2025 - January 2026. India’s interest lies in
seeing peace and stability in Myanmar, and therefore,
India continues to call for immediate cessation of
violence, resolution of issues through dialogue, and
return to the path of democracy through free, fair and
inclusive elections.
Marking
a
significant
milestone
in
bilateral
cooperation on boundary matters and effective
border management, India and Myanmar signed 36
boundary strip maps at Plenipotentiary level on 29
July. An ‘Agreement for Authorising the Dependents
of Members of a Diplomatic Mission or Consular Post
to Engage in Gainful Employment between India and
Myanmar’ was signed on 26 August.
High-Level Visits
Prime Minister and Senior General Min Aung Hlaing
met twice in 2025 and reviewed the entire gamut
of bilateral relationship. In their first interaction of
the year, the leaders met on the sidelines of the
BIMSTEC Summit in Bangkok on 4 April. During their
second meeting on 31 August, the leaders met on the
sidelines of the SCO Summit in Tianjin.
Myanmar’s Minister for Investment and Foreign
Economic Relations Kan Zaw participated at the Global
Business Summit organised by Economic Times in
February in New Delhi. Deputy Minister of Information
U Ye Tint participated in the WAVES Summit in April.
Deputy Minister of Electric Power U Aye Kyaw visited
India for the 6th Joint Steering Committee Meeting and
7th JWG on Cooperation in Power Sector held in New
Delhi on 10-11 July. Deputy Minister of Education
Zaw Myint participated in the International Conclave
organised by Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT),
Chennai on 18-19 September.
Prime Minister met Senior General Min Aung Hlaing on the
sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)
Summit in Tianjin, August 2025.
Deputy Minister of Electric Power U Aye Kyaw
attended the eighth session of the Assembly of the
International Solar Alliance (ISA) on 27-30 October
in New Delhi. Deputy Minister of Transport &
Communications U Aung Kyaw Tun attended the India
Maritime Week on 27-31 October in Mumbai. Deputy
Minister of Commerce U Minn Minn attended the
Bharat International Rice Conference 2025 on 30-31
October in New Delhi and the CII Partnership Summit
on 14-15 November in Visakhapatnam.

text:
India’s Neighbourhood
61
Trade and Economic Cooperation
India is the fourth largest trading partner of Myanmar.
Bilateral trade with Myanmar in the Financial Year
2025-26 reached USD 1.489 billion in the first three
quarters of (April-December). The total exports to
Myanmar between April-December 2025 grossed
USD 573.35 million, a growth of 28% year-on-year
and the imports from Myanmar grossed USD 916.46
million. In 2025, pharmaceuticals and beans & pulses
remained major items of India’s export and import
from Myanmar, respectively. Presently India is the
11th largest investor with an approved investment
of USD 782.821 million by 39 Indian enterprises.
The first Joint working Group (JWG) meeting on
the recognition of the Indian Pharmacopoeia was
held on 9 December at Nay Pyi Taw co-chaired by
Deputy Director General (DDG) of Department of
Food and Drugs Administration (FDA), Ministry of
Health and Secretary-cum-Scientific Director, Indian
Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC), Ministry of Health
and Family Welfare.
Development Cooperation
India has a significant development cooperation
portfolio worth approximately USD 2 billion in
Myanmar, with most of the projects being undertaken
under grant-in-aid. Despite the challenges posed by
the ongoing security situation, this year witnessed
progress on ongoing socio-economic development
projects and major connectivity projects including
the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project
(KMTTP) and the India-Myanmar-Thailand (IMT)
Trilateral Highway. The exchange of technical
documentation of work done on the 52 km segment
(first phase) of the IMT Trilateral Highway was
conducted on 1 October.
India has also been implementing human-centric
development projects throughout Myanmar under
various frameworks, namely, the Border Area
Development Programme (BADP), Rakhine State
Development Programme (RSDP), HICDP and Quick
Impact Projects (QIP) for construction of civilian
infrastructure including bridges, roads, schools and
small health centres, among others.
The MoU on Cooperation in the field of Implementation
of Pilot Project for Digital Identity and Programme for
Cooperation in Science and Technology were signed
on 29 July. Under this MoU, a team from National
Institute of Smart Governance (NISG) visited Myanmar
in November and met concerned officials.
As a testament to Government of India's enduring
commitment to long term preservation of Myanmar's
invaluable religious heritage, the Archaeological
Survey of India (ASI) has been conserving and
restoring earthquake-affected pagodas in Bagan.
The inauguration of Phase-II of the restoration
conservation works for earthquake-affected Pagodas
in Bagan took place on 3 October.
India and Myanmar signed an MoU on the ‘Implementation of
Pilot project for Digital Identity in Myanmar’ in Nay Pyi Taw,
July 2025.
Humanitarian Assistance
In solidarity with the people of Myanmar and
reaffirming India’s role as the region’s ‘First Responder’
to natural disasters, the Government of India swiftly
launched Operation Brahma in the immediate
aftermath of the 28 March earthquake. India’s
comprehensive humanitarian rescue and relief mission
delivered nearly 1,000 MT of HADR assistance to
Myanmar through nine aircraft and five naval ships.
India also deployed NDRF Search and Rescue teams,
an Indian Army Engineer unit for damage assessment

text:

62
and established mobile medical clinics and a fully
functional Field Hospital, underscoring India’s deep
commitment to humanitarian needs of the people of
Myanmar.
India inaugurated a Jaipur Foot Limb Fitment Camp
in Yangon from 2 October-13 November. Over 633
individuals from across Myanmar, including civilians
& service personnel were provided with artificial
limbs completely free of cost. India is also involved in
Myanmar’s post-earthquake reconstruction efforts.
India’s comprehensive humanitarian rescue and relief mission
delivered nearly 1,000 MT of HADR assistance to Myanmar
under Operation Brahma, March 2025.
Cultural Cooperation
India and Myanmar share a strong cultural bond
rooted in shared Buddhist heritage. Regular classes
of Yoga, Bharatanatyam, Indian classical vocal singing
and Hindi are conducted for Myanmar nationals at the
Swami Vivekananda Cultural Centre.
During the year, MEA organised various ‘Lecture
Series’ on Indian culture across Myanmar focusing
on cities with high concentration of Indian diaspora,
under the Promotion of Cultural Ties with Diaspora
(PCTD) Scheme.
A six-member cultural troupe from Myanmar
participated in the first BIMSTEC Traditional Music
Festival held on 4 August. An ICCR sponsored dance
troupe Purulia Chhau performed on 12 August in
Yangon, as part of celebrations marking the 79th
Independence Day of India. Vice-Chairman of the
State Samgha Maha Nayaka Committee Bhaddanta
Kovida participated in the ninth International Dharma
Dhamma Conference held on 18-20 September.
Events including the celebration of Rashtriya Ekta
Diwas (National Unity Day), 150 years of completion
of ‘Vande Mataram’ and International Gita Mahotsav
celebrated by Swami Vivekananda Cultural Centre
witnessed enthusiastic participation from members of
the Indian community and friends of India, reflecting
the strong people-to-people ties and cultural bonds
between India and Myanmar.
Education Cooperation and Capacity
Building
Capacity building initiatives continued throughout
the year, with a focus on supporting human resource
development in Myanmar under various schemes
including ITEC, ICCR scholarships, other specialised
training programs and also under BIMSTEC and
ASEAN programmes. 53 students from Myanmar
utilised the ICCR scholarship slots in the current
academic
year
and
several
students
availed
scholarships at Indian universities under various
PhD fellowships offered to the ASEAN students.
Additionally, the Indian government trained nearly
338 Myanmar officials under various capacity building

India’s Neighbourhood
63
Nepal
Nepal
occupies
a
special
place
in
India’s
‘Neighbourhood First’ policy. The open borders
and free movement of citizens between both sides
is a reflection of these unique, multifaceted and
strong ties. As two countries that share historical,
civilisational and cultural linkages, India and Nepal
are committed to rapid expansion and strengthening
of various connectivity initiatives- energy, trade,
railways, financial and digital.
The year has witnessed a renewed momentum as far
as bilateral mechanisms between both sides were
concerned. In addition to regular meetings of bilateral
mechanisms dealing with power, trade, defence
and development cooperation, both sides also
restarted crucial meetings in the border and boundary
management
sectors.
Despite
recent
political
developments in Nepal, India’s bilateral engagement
across various sectors is continuing apace – with
ministerial as well as technical visits and meetings
of bilateral mechanisms held as per schedule.
Furthermore, the development partnership continues
to witness substantial progress with new proposals
being processed and completed development projects
being inaugurated as scheduled.
Important Developments in Nepal
Nepal witnessed widespread youth protests on 8-9
September. The response of the law-enforcement
authorities and the ensuing violence led to a death
toll of 74 people. These developments led to the
resignation of then Prime Minister K.P. Oli, following
which an Interim Government led by former Chief
Justice Sushila Karki was sworn-in. The Government
of Nepal and Gen Z representatives concluded a
10-point understanding on 10 December and the
Election Commission of Nepal (ECN) approved the
schedule for the election of members of the House of
Representatives, to be held on 5 March 2026.
The Government of India welcomed the formation
of the Interim Government and reiterated its
commitment to work closely with Nepal. Prime
Minister had a telephonic conversation with Prime
Minister of the Interim Government of Nepal Sushila
Karki on 18 September, wherein he extended heartfelt
condolences for the tragic loss of lives during the
protests in Nepal and conveyed India’s full support
to Nepal in its efforts towards restoring peace and
stability, and for the progress of the people of Nepal.
High-Level Visits
Prime Minister and the then Prime Minister of Nepal K.
P. Sharma Oli interacted thrice in 2025. Prime Minister
first met the then Prime Minister Oli on the sidelines
of the 6th BIMSTEC Summit in Bangkok on 4 April. On
23 April, the then Prime Minister Oli had a telephonic
conversation with the Prime Minister, during which
he strongly condemned the heinous terror attack
in Jammu and Kashmir and offered his sincere
condolences. On the third occasion, Prime Minister
met the then Prime Minister Oli on the sidelines of the
SCO Summit in Tianjin, China on 31 August.
Prime Minister met the then Prime Minister of Nepal K. P.
Sharma Oli on the sidelines of the 6th BIMSTEC Summit in
Bangkok, April 2025

Trade and Economic Cooperation
Indian firms are among the largest investors in Nepal,

India is Nepal’s largest export destination, receiving

On 13 November, both countries exchanged letters

located in 48 districts of the country.

Assistant Chief of the Army Staff (ACOAS), Nepali

Pakistan
The year 2025 was marked by India's resolute
and multifaceted response to Pakistan's unabated
sponsorship of cross-border terrorism, a reality brutally
underscored by the barbaric attack in Pahalgam on 22
April that killed 26 innocent civilians, including one
Nepali citizen. This act triggered a decisive shift in
India’s policy, placing the onus for any possible future
engagement squarely on Pakistan's willingness to
cease its support to terrorism as an instrument of
statecraft.
In response to the Pahalgam terrorist attack, India
took a series of diplomatic measures that included
holding in abeyance of the Indus Waters Treaty of
1960, closing the Integrated Check Post (ICP) Attari,
stopping visa services to Pakistani nationals and
cancellation of active SVES Pakistani visas, declaring
Defence/Military, Naval and Air Advisors in the
Pakistani High Commission as Persona Non Grata and
bringing down the strength of the High Commission
to 30. Further, India banned all direct and indirect
imports of goods from Pakistan, closed its airspace for
Pakistani aircraft, suspended all postal services to and
from Pakistan and barred ships bearing Pakistani flag
from docking at Indian ports.
Subsequently, as there was no demonstrable step
from Pakistan against the terrorist infrastructure on
its territory, India launched ‘Operation Sindoor’ on 7
May targeting terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan and
Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir. On 10 May,
the Director General of Military Operations (DGMO) of
Pakistan approached his Indian counterpart to request
for cessation of firing and military activities, which was
agreed to later that day.
Operation Sindoor has set a new benchmark in
India’s fight against cross-border terrorism and has
established a new normal. First, if there is a terrorist
attack on India, a fitting reply will be given. India will
take strict action at every place from where the roots
of terrorism emerge. Second, India will not tolerate
any nuclear blackmail. India will strike precisely
and decisively at the terrorist hideouts developing
under the cover of nuclear blackmail. Third, India will
not differentiate between the Government which
is sponsoring terrorism, and the masterminds of
terrorism. India will continue to take decisive steps to
protect India and its citizens from any threat.
Following
Operation
Sindoor,
seven
all-party
delegations travelled to 33 countries to convey
India’s strong national consensus and resolute
approach to combating terrorism in all its forms and
manifestations. Each delegation comprised Members
of Parliament and eminent personalities from different
political parties across India, as well as veteran
diplomats. The delegations briefed their interlocutors
on the Pahalgam terror attack and Operation Sindoor,
and also the long history of Pakistan-sponsored
terror attacks in India. The delegations were able not
only to raise awareness on Pakistan’s complicity in
terrorism on a global scale but also address Pakistani
propaganda on Jammu and Kashmir and Operation
Sindoor. The interlocutors unequivocally condemned
the use of terrorism against India, recognising India’s
right to defend itself against terrorism.
It was due to greater appreciation of India’s position
and the persistent diplomatic efforts that the terrorist
group ‘The Resistance Front’ (TRF), responsible for
the Pahalgam terror attack, was mentioned in the
report of the Monitoring Team of the United Nations
Security Council (UNSC) 1267 Sanctions Committee,
published on 29 July. Moreover, on 18 July, TRF
was designated by the US as a Foreign Terrorist
Organisation (FTO) and as a Specially Designated
Global Terrorist (SDGT). In July, India organised an
exhibition titled the ‘Human Cost of Terrorism’ at the
UN Headquarters to showcase the human impact of
terrorism in India and beyond, and highlighted India’s
contribution towards combating terrorism.

Indus Water Treaty
Following the Pahalgam terrorist attack, India has, in
exercise of its rights as a sovereign nation under the
international law, placed the Indus Waters Treaty
in abeyance, until Pakistan credibly and irrevocably
abjures its support for cross-border terrorism. Until
such time that the Treaty is in abeyance, India is no
longer bound to perform any of its obligations under
the Treaty.
Religious Pilgrimages
Visits of pilgrims between India and Pakistan are
facilitated under the 1974 Bilateral Protocol on Visits
to Religious Shrines. This year, India facilitated the
visits of 5135 Indian pilgrims across various religious
shrines to Pakistan on the occasions of birth anniversary
of Sant Shadaram Saheb Ji (Shadani Darbar, January),
Mahashivratri (Katas Raj Dham, February-March),
Baisakhi (April) and Gurupurab (November). During
this period, India also facilitated the visit of 289
Pakistani pilgrims to religious shrines in India on the
occasions of Urs of Hazrat Khawaja Moinuddin Chisti
(January) and Urs of Hazrat Amir Khusro (April). Since
7 May, the services of Sri Kartarpur Sahib corridor
remain suspended given the extant security situation.
Humanitarian issues - Prisoners and
Fishermen
India attaches high importance to the issue of
Indian prisoners held in Pakistan’s custody and
regularly takes up the matter of their early release
and repatriation to India. As on 1 July, Pakistan has
acknowledged the custody of 53 civil prisoners and
193 fishermen who are either Indians or are believed-
to-be Indians. Similarly, there are 382 civil prisoners
and 81 fishermen in Indian custody, who are either
Pakistanis or are believed-to-be Pakistanis. As a result
of sustained efforts by the Government, 2661 Indian
fishermen and 71 Indian civil prisoners have been
repatriated from Pakistan since 2014. In 2025, 22
Indian fishermen have been repatriated from Pakistan.
India has sought early Consular Access, release
and repatriation of the remaining Indian nationals in
Pakistan’s custody.
Treatment of Minorities in Pakistan
Given
the
continued
persecution
of
minority
communities in Pakistan, India has raised the issue
of atrocities against the members of these groups in
Pakistan on several occasions. India has also conveyed
its concerns regarding the incidents of vandalism/
desecration of places of worship and cultural heritage
of minority communities as well as discrimination,
killing, abduction, forced conversion and marriages of
the members of the minority communities
Sri Lanka
India is Sri Lanka’s closest neighbour, sharing a strong
civilisational and historical connection. Sri Lanka has
a central place in India’s ‘Neighbourhood First’ policy
and ‘MAHASAGAR’ vision. Bilateral relations between
the two countries have matured and diversified,
encompassing all areas of contemporary relevance,
particularly with several high-level engagements,
including the visits of President of Sri Lanka Anura
Kumara Dissanayake to India in December 2024 and
the Prime Minister to Sri Lanka in April 2025.

five

Project in Anuradhapura, the Exposition of Lord
Buddha relics in Sri Lanka, and a comprehensive
capacity-building programme in India covering 700
Sri Lankans annually. In recognition of his significant

Subsequent to announcement made by the Prime

year 2025-26, an enhanced financial assistance
programme for 100 students from economically
backward background each from the University of
Jaffna and Eastern University Batticaloa with financial
assistance of USD 24.24 per month per student has
been rolled out. The construction of Multi-Ethnic
Trilingual School in Polonnaruwa with Indian grant
assistance of USD 1.4 million has been completed
and the project was inaugurated in October.
India launched ‘Operation Sagar Bandhu’ on the day
of Cyclone Ditwah’s landfall in the country. India’s
Aircraft Carrier INS Vikrant as well as INS Udayagiri
delivered relief material and deployed helicopters
to execute rescue and relief operations. Separately,
the Indian Air Force mobilised Mi-17 helicopters as
a part of rescue efforts and an 80-member National
Disaster Response Force contingent conducted rescue
and relief operations. The Indian Army set up a field
hospital with 85 medical personnel near Kandy, giving
emergency care to more than 8000 people. Two
modular BHISHM emergency care units were also air
lifted to Sri Lanka and utilised. Indian Army Engineers
erected a Bailey bridge along A35 road in Kilinochchi.
Overall, Operation Sagar Bandhu delivered over 1100
tonnes of relief material, including dry rations, tents,
tarpaulins, hygiene kits, essential clothing and water
purification kits. The relief material also comprised
nearly 14.5 tonnes of medicines and medical
equipment.
During EAM’s visit to Sri Lanka in December, as the
Prime Minister's Special Envoy, he announced an
assistance worth USD 100 million grant and extension
of four LOCs worth USD 350 million for Sri Lanka’s
recovery and rehabilitation efforts post-Cyclone
Ditwah. This comprehensive package covering at least
16 different projects is structured along five pillars
- Physical Connectivity Infrastructure, Housing and
Water, Health and education, Agriculture, Disaster
Response and Prevention Measures.

been trained under the December 2024 MoU signed

investigation, human rights, among others.

Mauritius
India and Mauritius share a special, close, and enduring
relationship rooted in shared ancestry, culture, history,
and strong people-to-people ties. This partnership
lies at the confluence of India’s Neighbourhood First
policy, Vision MAHASAGAR, and India’s commitment
to the Global South. This year, bilateral ties were
elevated to an Enhanced Strategic Partnership, India’s
first in the region, underscoring the trust and depth of
this special relationship.
Over the years, the cooperation has expanded to
diverse sectors including health, education, science
and technology, space, maritime security, and capacity
building. Following the terrorist attack in Pahalgam
in April, Prime Minister of Mauritius Navinchandra
Ramgoolam conveyed his condolences to the Prime
Minister and strongly condemned the heinous act—
reflecting the solidarity and mutual empathy that
define the India–Mauritius bond.
Bilateral Cooperation
The year witnessed several high-level engagements.
Prime Minister paid a State Visit to Mauritius on 11-12
March, during which the relationship was elevated to
an Enhanced Strategic Partnership and a Joint Vision
Document was adopted.
Eight MoUs were signed across sectors, including
training and capacity-building programs for public
service officers; training for diplomats; local currency
settlement of bilateral trade; cooperation in the field of
small and medium enterprises; cooperation in the blue
economy; an Indian rupee-denominated line of credit;
and white shipping information exchange. Several
development projects, including Atal Bihari Vajpayee
Institute of Public Service and Innovation (AIPSI), were
jointly inaugurated.
Prime Minister of Mauritius Navinchandra Ramgoolam
paid a State Visit to India from 9 to 16 September, during
which India extended a Special Economic Package
worth USD 680 million to Mauritius and signed seven
MoUs, including cooperation in renewable energy,
space, hydrography, and port development.
Prime Minister Ramgoolam met with the Hon’ble
Rashtrapati ji at Rashtrapati Bhavan on 16 September.
During his visit, he travelled to Mumbai, Varanasi,
Ayodhya, and Tirupati.
While welcoming Prime Minister Ramgoolam and
his delegation to the Rashtrapati Bhavan, Hon’ble
Rashtrapati ji emphasised that Mauritius holds a
special place in India’s Neighbourhood First policy,
Vision MAHASAGAR, and in India’s commitment to
the Global South.
India also agreed to set up a 17.5 MW Floating
Solar PV project at Tamarind Falls under the G2G
framework, assist in the development and surveillance
of the Chagos Marine Protected Area, redevelop and
restructure the port in Mauritius, and provide annual
budgetary support of USD 25 million for the current
financial year.
Hon’ble Vice-President met Prime Minister of
Mauritius Navinchandra Ramgoolam on his visit to
Seychelles to attend the swearing-in ceremony of
the President of Seychelles on 26 October. The then
Chief Justice of India also undertook an official visit
on 3 October, during which he met the Mauritian
leadership and delivered the inaugural ‘Sir Maurice
Rault Memorial Lecture’ on ‘The Rule of Law in the
Biggest Democracy.’

Development Cooperation
Development cooperation is a key pillar of the
Enhanced Strategic Partnership between India and
Mauritius. This partnership includes over 130 projects,
of which 96 are classified as High Impact Community
Development Projects (HICDPs). About 98 projects
have already been completed, with notable recent
projects include AIPSI, Metro Express projects, ENT
hospital, and a mediclinic.
Among the ongoing initiatives are the supply of
e-buses, the construction of the National Archives
and Library Building, the renal transplant unit, and the
forensic science laboratory. India has also announced
support for the construction of a new Parliament
building in Mauritius and provided grant assistance
for phase II of the HICDPs.
Furthermore, institutional linkages and people-centred
initiatives have been strengthened. The first batch of
10 e-buses were handed over to Mauritius. Several
delegations from the Central Electricity Authority
and the National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC)
have also visited Mauritius. India has also conducted
training and capacity-building efforts in Mauritius
under the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation
(ITEC) program and India-Africa Maitri Scholarship
program.
Opportunities for enhanced collaboration have been
identified in areas such as renewable energy, digital
innovation, and maritime security, reflecting the
vibrant ties between the two nations.
Mauritius is one of the largest beneficiaries of the
ITEC Program. 352 Mauritians (201 under Civilian
programs; 151 under Defence Program) were trained
in India. In September, an MoU was signed between
the National Centre for Good Governance and the
Ministry of Public Service and Administrative Reforms
of Mauritius for the training of Mauritian Civil servants
in India. Under this MoU, 47 civil servants were trained.
Also, 17 officers, including seven Mauritian diplomats,
underwent training at the Sushma Swaraj Institute of
Foreign Service.

November. Also, India trained 30 Seychelles citizens
under ITEC civil and defence programmes. Under
the Quad-climate initiative, three ISA projects (solar
rooftop, solar pump and solar chiller) are being
executed in Seychelles.
Economic and Trade Cooperation
India-Seychelles bilateral trade grew by 10.97 per
cent in 2024-25. The value of trade stood at USD
94.19 million for the period from April to September
2025, with Indian exports totalling USD 91.73 million
and imports totalling USD 2.46 million during FY
2024-25. In March, Indigo Airlines commenced direct
flights between Mumbai and Mahe Island, operating
four flights per week to increase tourism, trade, and
people-to-people ties.
Defence Cooperation
During the year, Patrol Boat (PB) Hermes was
replaced by the new Indian Coast Guard vessel PB
Bodeuse, gifter to the Seychelles Defence Forces
(SDF). Seychelles also participated in Ex-AIKEYME in
April and the ‘Indian Ocean Naval Symposium’ (IONS)
Emerging Leaders Panel Discussion (ELPD-2025) in
August.

Seychelles Coast Guard base on Île Perseverance, Seychelles, February 2025

National Museum. A cultural group from Seychelles
visited India to participate in Surajkund Mela on 7-23
February.

Australia
In 2025, the India–Australia Comprehensive Strategic
Partnership marked five years, achieving remarkable
growth in bilateral ties across trade and investment,
renewable energy, defence and security, skills and
education, research and innovation and people-
to-people and cultural exchanges. Earlier in the
year, Prime Minister of Australia Anthony Albanese
launched ‘A New Roadmap for Australia's Economic
Engagement with India’ on 26 February to bolster
economic ties between the two counties.
Later in the year, Prime Minister met with Prime
Minister Albanese on the sidelines of the G7
Summit in Canada on 17 June. Both leaders also
met on the sidelines of the G20 Leaders’ Summit in
Johannesburg, South Africa on 21 November and the
India-Australia-Canada Technology and Innovation
(ACITI) Partnership on 22 November.
Prime Minister met Prime Minister of Australia Anthony

EAM and Foreign Minister of Australia Penny Wong
met on the sidelines of Quad Foreign Ministers’

and then on the sidelines of Quad Foreign Ministers’
