EAM met Minister of Foreign Affairs of Australia Penny Wong
on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting in New
York, September 2025.
This year, defence cooperation was strengthened
with sustained momentum. Deputy Prime Minister
and Defence Minister of Australia Richard Marles
visited India on 3-4 June. Later in the year, Raksha
Mantri paid his first visit in 12 years to Australia on
9-10 October. During this visit, both sides decided
to establish an Annual Defence Ministers’ dialogue
between the two countries. Later in the visit, the first
Australia-India Defence Industry Roundtable was
held in Sydney on 10 October. Raksha Mantri held
discussions with his Australian counterpart, and both
sides signed three agreements to further enhance
cooperation in information sharing, maritime domain,
and joint activities.
Earlier in the year, the ninth round of Defence Policy
Talks was held in New Delhi in March. The Chief
of Defence Staff (CDS) paid his first official visit to
Australia (4-7 March), after which the Chief of the
Australian Army visited India (11-14 August). Defence
and security cooperation was further enhanced
through mutual participation in military exercises,
namely-TALISMAN SABRE 2025, TARANG SHAKTI
and AUSTRAHIND. Chief of Integrated Defence Staff
(CISC) visited Australia on 26-28 July to witness the
11th edition of the Exercise TALISMAN SABRE 2025.
India also hosted the third edition of the General Rawat
Young Defence Officers’ Exchange Programme from
14-26 October. Later in the month, the 12th Army-to-
Army Staff talks were held on 29-31 October.
On the energy cooperation front, the fifth India-
Australia Energy Dialogue was held in New Delhi
on 16 October co-chaired by Minister for Power and
Housing and Urban Affairs and Australia’s Minister for
Energy and Climate Change Chris Bowen.
The third Australia-India Education and Skills
Council (AIESC) meeting was held in New Delhi on
8 December, co-chaired by Minister of Education and
MoS (IC, Skill Development and Entrepreneurship)
with the Minister of Education of Australia Jason Clare
and the Minister for Skills and Training of Australia
Andrew Giles.
Further mutual exchange of bilateral visits deepened
cooperation in key areas. These included the outgoing
visit to Australia by MoS (Skill Development and
Entrepreneurship) from 10 to 15 September. Incoming
visits from Australia to India during this period
included the visit of Minister for Multicultural Affairs,
International Development and Small Business of
Australia (15-18 October), visit of Premier of South
Australia (23-28 March) and the visit of the Premier
of Queensland (30 August-1 September). Both sides
also held the first-ever Senior Officials-level Consular
Dialogue in New Delhi in September.

Under Mekong Ganga Cooperation Plan of Action

Bodhgaya,

address malnutrition in Lao PDR through fortification

announcement of this project for improving nutrition
security in Lao PDR was made during the visit of Prime
Minister to Vientiane in October 2024. Under the ITEC
programme, 22 Lao officials have been trained.
This year, Embassy in Vientiane, in coordination with
Lao authorities, carried out the rescue and repatriation
of 1418 Indian nationals trapped in cyber-scam
centres at Golden Triangle Special Economic Zone in
Lao PDR.

Leaders’ Summit attended by Prime Minister virtually
on 26 October and with the participation of EAM in

India has strong historical engagement with the Pacific

region. India stepped up its efforts to engage with

with the Pacific Island Countries (PICs).

Port Moresby from 30 August to 8 October and
participated in the celebrations marking the 50th
anniversary of PNG’s independence. INS Kadmatt led
the International Fleet Review, underscoring India’s
solidarity with PNG on this historic occasion. INS
Kadmatt also made a three-day port call in Fiji for a
goodwill visit in September as part of this overseas
deployment.
As a part of outcomes of the Prime Minister of
Fiji’s visit to India in August, a group of 10 pandits
from TISI Sangam Fiji and Shree Sanatan Dharam
Pratinidhi Sabha of Fiji travelled to India in November
to participate in the International Gita Conference and
a month-long “Purohit Course” organised at Banaras
Hindu University under the ITEC program of the
Ministry.
Development Cooperation
India supports the PICs in their socio-economic
development through community-oriented projects by
providing annual grant-in-aid of USD 2.8 million (USD
200,000 to each of the PICs). These projects are in
diverse areas such as community development, solar
electrification, purchase and supply of agricultural
equipment, computers, LED bulbs for schools, sewing
machines, dialysis machines, portable saw mills,
boats and pick-up trucks, construction of sea wall, and
coral farms. India sent five MT of high-quality cowpea
seeds in July to support food security and agricultural
resilience in Fiji.
In line with the announcements made by Prime
Minister during the third FIPIC Summit in Port Moresby
in May 2023, India supplied Haemodialysis machines
to Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, Samoa,
Palau, Nauru, Republic of Marshall Islands and Kiribati
among the Pacific Island Countries. Two Yoga Centres
were also set up in Fiji.
A Tripartite Agreement on Community Access to Resilient
Essential Health in the Federated States of Micronesia
(FSM), being funded under the India-UN Development
Partnership Fund, was signed on 29 November.

Quick Impact Projects
During the 53rd Pacific Islands Forum, MoS (PM)
announced that India will undertake one Quick Impact
Project of each country’s choice, worth USD 50,000,
in each of the 14 PICs, based on proposals received.
QIPs are short-gestation, high-visibility projects with
a normal gestation period of up to one year, aimed
at providing direct benefit to local communities, with
results that are immediate and visible. The QIPs
related to socio-economic development in Fiji and
Nauru were initiated during the year.

of development assistance under South-South

Diplomats from the PICs regularly attend special
training courses organised by the Sushma Swaraj
Institute of Foreign Service in New Delhi.

and
medical

bilateral grants. A consignment of Anti-Retro Viral

India has close cultural and historical ties with

a State Visit to India on 4-8 August, accompanied by
a high-level delegation comprising 14 key Ministers,
senior officials and a large business delegation.

elevated to Strategic Partnership and a Plan of
Action for implementation of the same was adopted.
Some of the major outcomes from the visit included
an invitation to the Philippines for participation at
the Information Fusion Centre – Indian Ocean region
(IFC-IOR) the conclusion of 13 MoUs in the areas of
defence, space, science & technology, trade, digital
technologies, culture, tourism, mutual legal assistance

Sovereign Data Cloud Infrastructure in the Philippines;
and the exchange of 19 business agreements
during the business engagements of the Philippine
President in Bengaluru, on 7 August. A joint stamp
commemorating 75 years of diplomatic ties between
India and the Philippines was also released during the
visit.
This year also witnessed the visit of the then Secretary

and demonstration of hydrographic capabilities. As
part of the ongoing cooperation in HADR, Indian
Coast Guard rescued the Filipino crew members on-

Singapore
India and Singapore celebrated the 60th anniversary
of establishment of diplomatic relations in 2025.
President of Singapore Tharman Shanmugaratnam
paid a state visit to India (New Delhi and Odisha) on

China

visits for bilateral mechanisms and meetings on the

he held a bilateral meeting with President Xi Jinping

Japan
The year witnessed continued deepening of the India–
Japan Special Strategic and Global Partnership, marked
by the Annual Summit in August and the first meeting
between Prime Minister and the new Japanese Prime
Minister Sanae Takaichi on 23 November. In addition,
there were frequent high-level political engagements
and expanding cooperation in critical areas including
economic security, clean energy, technology, and
people-to-people exchanges.

Prime Minister held a bilateral meeting with the Prime
Minister of Japan Sanae Takaichi on the margins of
G20 Summit, Johannesburg on 23 November. In
this initial meeting between the two leaders, they
acknowledged the steady progress made in bilateral
ties during the 15th India-Japan Annual Summit
and called for expeditious implementation of the
outcomes agreed upon, and discussed collaborative
opportunities between India and Japan in strategic
sectors. Earlier, Prime Minister had congratulated

Earlier in the year, Prime Minister paid an official
visit to Japan on 29–30 August for the 15th India–
Japan Annual Summit with the then Prime Minister
Shigeru Ishiba. The two leaders adopted the India–
Japan Joint Vision for the Next Decade, outlining a
ten-year strategic roadmap for cooperation across
eight priority areas: economic partnership, economic
security, mobility, ecological sustainability, technology
and innovation, health, people-to-people and cultural
exchanges, and state–prefecture cooperation.
Bilateral documents released during the Annual
Summit, included the Joint Declaration on Security
Cooperation, Action Plan for India–Japan Human
Resource Exchange (envisaging two-way exchange
of 500,000 people, including 50,000 skilled and
semi-skilled Indian workers to Japan over five years),
Memorandum of Cooperation (MoC) in the Field
of Mineral Resources, MoC on India–Japan Digital
Partnership 2.0, Implementing Arrangement between
ISRO and JAXA for the Joint Lunar Polar Exploration
Mission (Chandrayaan-5/LUPEX), Joint Declaration
of Intent on Clean Hydrogen and Ammonia, MoC
on the Joint Crediting Mechanism, and MoCs on
Environmental Cooperation, Cultural Exchange, and
Decentralized Wastewater Management, as well as a
Joint Statement of Intent between India’s Ministry of
Science and Technology and Japan’s MEXT.
Other notable outcomes of the Summit included
the announcement of a private investment target of
approximately USD 68 billion in India over the next
decade, the launch of the India–Japan Economic
Security Initiative and an accompanying Fact Sheet
on Economic Security Cooperation, the India–Japan
AI Initiative to foster collaboration in Large Language
Models and trustworthy AI, the Next-Generation
Mobility Partnership, the India–Japan SME Forum,
and the Sustainable Biofuel Initiative. Both sides
also agreed to intensify state–prefecture linkages,
including through new business forums in the Kansai
and Kyushu regions.
Prime Minister and the then Prime Minister Ishiba met
earlier in the year on the sidelines of the G7 Leaders’
Summit in Kananaskis, Canada held on 17–18 June,
where they discussed bilateral cooperation and
regional developments. Following the terrorist attack
in Pahalgam on 22 April, the then Prime Minister
Ishiba telephoned Prime Minister on 24 April to
convey condolences on Pahalgam terrorist attack and
solidarity with India in combating terrorism.

D.C. for another round of discussions during the Quad
Foreign Ministers’ Meeting.
Speaker of Japan’s House of Representatives Fukushiro
Nukaga visited India on 1-5 May, during which he held
meetings with the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the
EAM. As part of the visit, he also travelled to Assam,
where he met the Chief Minister and visited the Tata
Semiconductor Project in Jagiroad.
The India–Japan Defence Ministerial Meeting was held
in New Delhi on 5 May, when Japan’s Defence Minister
Gen Nakatani visited India and met Rakshamantri. The
two Defence Ministers reaffirmed cooperation under
the new Joint Declaration on Security Cooperation and
emphasized joint defence technology and capacity-
building initiatives.
An all-party parliamentary delegation led by a senior
Member of Parliament visited Japan on 22-24 May
in the aftermath of Operation Sindoor, where they
interacted with senior Japanese political leaders,
including Speaker of the House of Representatives
Fukushiro Nukaga, the then Foreign Minister of Japan
Takeshi Iwaya, former Prime Minster Yoshihide Suga,
and other key stakeholders. During these interactions,
the delegation underscored India’s zero-tolerance
policy towards terrorism.
EAM met the then Foreign Minister of Japan Takeshi Iwaya
in Washington, D.C. on the sidelines of the Quad Foreign
Ministers’ Meeting, January 2025.
Prime Minister met the then Prime Minister of Japan Shigeru Ishiba at the 15th India-Japan Annual Summit in Tokyo, August 2025.

105
Defence and Security Cooperation
Defence and security ties remained a key pillar of the
partnership. Chief of the Naval Staff paid an official visit
to Japan on 29 July-3 August, aimed at strengthening
bilateral Defence Cooperation, Maritime Partnership
and reaffirming India’s commitment to a free and
Open Indo-Pacific.
The sixth edition of the bilateral Army exercise
‘DHARMA GUARDIAN-25’ was conducted at the Fuji
Manoeuvre Training Area, Japan, on 24 February- 9
March, focusing on counter-terrorism operations and
interoperability between the Indian Army and Japan
Ground Self-Defence Force. The Indian Air Force
supported troop transportation using C-17 aircraft.
The two sides continued to strengthen defence
cooperation through regular exchanges, consultations,
and defence technology collaboration. Indian Naval
Ship (INS) Sahyadri participated in the sea phase of the
Japan-India Maritime Exercise (JAIMEX-25) conducted
between 16-18 October, which was followed by a
port call at Yokosuka for the Harbour Phase.
Earlier, in January, Indian Coast Guard Ship ICGS
Shaunak visited Yokohama on a goodwill visit and
held a bilateral exercise with Japan Coast Guard (JCG).
A JCG ship ‘Itsukushima’ made a reciprocal goodwill
visit to Chennai as a part of the JCG’s Global Ocean
Voyage Training in July.
Economic and Industrial Cooperation
Economic engagement remained a major pillar of
bilateral relations. Minister of Petroleum and Natural
Gas visited Japan on 16-19 November and met
with Japan’s State Minister of Economy, Trade and
Industry Toshiro Ino. Productive discussions were
held with leading Japanese industry representatives
on opportunities for collaboration across the energy
value chain. The fourth India–Japan Energy Dialogue
was held virtually on 25 August, co-chaired by the
Minister of Power and Housing & Urban Affairs and
the Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) of
Japan. Under the framework of the Japan–India Clean
Energy Partnership (JICEP), both sides reaffirmed their
commitment to energy security and inclusive growth,
welcomed progress in areas such as energy efficiency,
clean hydrogen, ammonia, and renewable energy,
and agreed to expand cooperation in carbon capture,
utilization and storage (CCUS), green chemicals,
biofuels, and advanced technologies in the energy
sector.
The third India–Japan Steel Dialogue was held in
New Delhi on 4 February to deepen cooperation in
advanced steelmaking technologies, decarbonization,
and workplace safety. The third India–Japan Joint
Working Group on Textiles met in Tokyo in June,
followed by the visit of Minister of Textiles to Tokyo
on 14–17 July, to expand cooperation in apparel
manufacturing, trade, and skill development.
EAM met the Foreign Minister of Japan Toshimitsu Motegi on the sidelines of East Asia Summit in Kuala Lumpur, October 2025.

ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
106
The seventh India–Japan Industrial Competitiveness
Partnership (IJICP) meeting was held in Tokyo on 17
September. Both sides reviewed progress across key
sectors and agreed to enhance industrial cooperation,
human resource development, and investment
promotion toward the USD 68 billion target.
The
eighth
India-Japan
Joint
Working
Group
meeting on ICT led by Secretary, Department of
Telecommunications (DoT) and Vice Minister for
International Affairs, Ministry of Internal Affairs and
Communications, Japan was held on 10 October in
New Delhi to take forward strategic ICT collaboration,
and to drive digital innovation through discussions
involving the government as well as the private
sector. India also participated in the Tokyo Economic
Security Forum organized by Japan’s Ministry for
Economy, Trade and Industry on 15 December at the
Joint Secretary-level. During the visit of Joint Secretary
(East Asia) for the aforementioned forum as well as
the visit of Joint Secretary (Cyber Diplomacy) on 16-
17 December, discussions were held on AI, economic
security and other outcomes of the 15th Annual
Summit.
Science, Technology, and Innovation
The year 2025–26 was designated the India–Japan
Year of Science, Technology and Innovation Exchanges,
reinforcing scientific and research collaboration.
The 11th Joint Committee Meeting on Science and
Technology Cooperation was held in June, reviewing
ongoing
research
partnerships
and
identifying
new areas for joint innovation. The Joint Institute of
Excellence established by IIT Bombay and Tohoku
University in April further strengthened academic
collaboration in advanced technologies.
The fourth Meeting of the India–Japan Joint Working
Group on Civil Nuclear Cooperation was held in India
on 7 July.
The fourth India-Japan University Forum was held at
IIT Hyderabad in November for enhancing exchange
of talent in science and technology domain.
State-Prefecture Engagements
The year witnessed Chief Ministerial visits to Japan
from Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Haryana, Madhya
Pradesh, Meghalaya, Nagaland and Punjab, which
further strengthened sub-national collaborations
and promoted partnerships in investment, tourism,
and human resource development. Governors of
Yamanashi, Ibaraki, Shizuoka, Toyama, Kagawa and
Ehime Prefectures visited India in 2024–2025 and
signed cooperation MoUs with Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat,
Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu, reflecting growing
momentum in state–prefecture linkages.
Cultural and People-to-People Exchanges
Cultural and tourism exchanges remained a vibrant
component of bilateral ties. The India–Japan Year of
Tourism and Cultural Exchanges 2025 was celebrated
with a series of events highlighting the shared
heritage and contemporary connections between the
two nations. Further, the Action Plan for India–Japan
Human Resource Exchange, released during the 2025
Summit, aims to facilitate the movement of 50,000
skilled Indian professionals to Japan over the next five
years, strengthening people-to-people and economic
linkages. The MoC on Cultural Exchanges was also
renewed in August to further deepen collaboration in
arts, heritage, and youth exchanges.
The Japan Institute of International Affairs (JIIA) and
the Delhi Policy Group (DPG) co-hosted the eighth
Japan-India Indo-Pacific Forum (11th Japan-India Track
1.5 Dialogue) on 5 November in Tokyo. EAM and State
Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan Ayano Kunimitsu
delivered keynote addresses at the dialogue.
Expo 2025 Osaka–Kansai
Expo 2025 Osaka–Kansai concluded successfully in
September under the theme ‘Designing Future Society
for Our Lives.’ The India Pavilion ‘Bharat’ was among
the top five most visited pavilions. The Pavillion
was awarded the Bronze Medal in the category of
External Design for Module Pavilions (Type B+X) at
the Expo 2025 Official Participant Awards, organized

Pavilion served as a major platform to promote India’s

International Day of Yoga and Independence Day was
celebrated at the Osaka Expo in June and August
respectively.
Mongolia
India and Mongolia continued to deepen their strategic
partnership. The period witnessed enhanced bilateral
relations with multifaceted engagement extending to
new areas of partnership. India continued to support
Mongolia’s capacity building initiatives as an important
‘third neighbour’ and ‘spiritual sibling’.
Major Developments in India-Mongolia
bilateral relations
During the year, the highlight of the bilateral
relations was the State Visit of President of Mongolia
Khurelsukh Ukhnaa to India on 13-16 October. The
State Visit coincided with the 70th anniversary of the
establishment of diplomatic relations between India
and Mongolia and the 10th anniversary of Strategic
Partnership. A total of 10 MoUs/Agreements were
signed and exchanged during the visit. Prime Minister
announced 70 additional seats for Mongolia under
the ITEC programme. Mongolia formally joined the
International Solar Alliance (ISA) and International Big
Cat Alliance (IBCA), while reiterating support to India
for the permanent seat in UNSC.
Prime Minister welcomed President of Mongolia Khurelsukh
Ukhnaa on his State Visit in New Delhi, October 2025.
At the ministerial level, EAM met and held discussions
with Foreign Minister of Mongolia B. Battsetseg during
the Munich Security Conference on 15 February.
Other engagements during the year included a visit
by the State Secretary and Head of the Strategic
Planning Division from the Ministry of Energy of
Mongolia for the India Energy Week 2025 held on 11–
14 February. This was followed by the participation
of State Secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
of Mongolia Lhanaajav Munkhtushig in the Raisina
Dialogue in New Delhi on 17–18 March. Foreign
Office Consultations were subsequently held on 19
March in New Delhi.
A high-level composite delegation from various
Ministries of India, led by the Special Secretary &
Financial Adviser (SS &FA) of the Ministry of External
Affairs, visited Mongolia on 11–16 May to review the
progress of the Oil Refinery Project. Thereafter, the
fourth Joint Working Group Meeting between the
Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) of India and the
Nuclear Energy Commission (NEC) of Mongolia was
held in virtual mode on 9 June.
Later in the year, Secretary (East) visited Mongolia on
21–24 September and held broad discussions with
the State Secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
In addition, dialogues were held with the Ministers
of Education, Industry & Mineral Resources, and the
Secretary of the National Security Council of Mongolia.
Defence cooperation included DG-level talks at the 13th
Joint Working Group (JWG) on Defence Cooperation
held in New Delhi in February. A contingent of the
Indian Army participated in the ‘Nomadic Elephant
2025’ bilateral exercises on 31 May-14 June held in
Ulaanbaatar. Defence Secretary participated in the
opening event of ‘Khaan Quest 2025’, a multilateral
peacekeeping exercise in Mongolia with a 40-member
Indian Army contingent.
Development Partnership
On the development cooperation projects, the Oil
Refinery Project with a total cost, under LoC, standing
at USD 1.7 billion progressed well. The construction
of ‘Atal Bihari Vajpayee Centre of Excellence for

Cultural Cooperation
During the year, cultural engagement between
India and Mongolia remained anchored in shared
civilizational and Buddhist heritage. It was further
strengthened through concrete initiatives including
the distribution of 40 sets of the Holy Mongolian
Kanjur (108 volumes) to Monasteries/organisations
in Mongolia and joint inauguration of the ‘Grant-in-
Aid Project for Digitization of One Million Buddhist
Manuscripts’ at Gandan Monastery to preserve and
digitize important Buddhist manuscripts.
Republic of Korea
The Special Strategic Partnership between India and
the Republic of Korea (RoK) continued to deepen in
2025, which also marked the ‘10th Year of the Special
Strategic Partnership.’ There was early contact with
the new administration of the RoK which assumed
power in June.
Prime Minister met the new President of RoK Lee Jae
Myung twice in 2025, on the sidelines of the G7 Summit
held in Kananaskis, Canada in June as well as the G20
Summit held in Johannesburg on 22 November. The
leaders reaffirmed their commitment to deepen the
India–RoK Special Strategic Partnership during the
Johannesburg summit and expand cooperation across
trade, investment and advanced technologies.
A delegation of Special Envoys of President Lee Jae
Myung led by former Prime Minister Kim Boo-kyum
visited India in July and met the Prime Minister, EAM,
and Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
Prime Minister met the President of Republic of Korea Lee Jae
Myung on the sidelines of the G7 Summit held in Canada, June
2025.
At the Ministerial level, EAM held several meetings
with RoK Foreign Minister Cho Hyun. EAM met Foreign
Minister Hyun during his visit to New Delhi in August
and again in Kuala Lumpur in October on the sidelines
of the India–ASEAN Summit. He also held a bilateral
meeting with the then Foreign Minister Cho Tae Yeol
on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers Meeting
in Johannesburg, South Africa in February.
Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas led an inter-
ministerial delegation to RoK in November to discuss
possibilities of collaboration with RoK companies in
the shipbuilding sector.
EAM met with the Foreign Minister of the Republic of Korea
Cho Hyun in New Delhi in August, 2025.

An All-Party Parliamentary Delegation visited the
RoK on 25-26 May for the outreach with countries on
the significance of Operation Sindoor. Delegations led
by the Chief Ministers of Assam and Chhattisgarh also
visited RoK in January and August, respectively.
A high-level delegation from Andhra Pradesh led
by Minister of Municipal Administration & Urban
Development and Minister of Infrastructure &

apprise the local stakeholders about business and

A delegation led by the Chief Minister of Punjab
visited the RoK during 6-10 December to promote

The Korea–India Strategic Symposium, co-hosted
by the Embassy of India in Seoul and the Institute
for Future Strategy at Seoul National University was
held in Seoul on 13 November. The 24th India-Korea
Strategic Dialogue was held on 17-19 December in
Seoul, convened by the Ananta Centre in partnership
with MEA, the Korea Foundation, and the Seoul Forum
for International Affairs.
Defence Cooperation
The inaugural India-RoK Navy bilateral exercise
was conducted in Korea on 13-16 October, with
INS Sahyadri participating from the Indian side. An
MoU was signed between the two Coast Guards on
‘Maritime Search & Rescue Cooperation’.
A delegation from Korea Coast Guard participated in
the 10th NATPOLREX Exercise conducted by the Indian
Coast Guard in October. A four-member contingent
from 60 Parachute Field Hospital visited the RoK in
November on the 75th Anniversary of the Korean War.
Cultural Cooperation
MoS (Information & Broadcasting) led the first
ever ministerial delegation from India to the Busan
International Film Festival (BIFF) and the Asian
Contents & Film Market (ACFM) in September in
Busan.
Member of the Culture, Sports and Tourism Committee
of the National Assembly of the Republic of Korea
Jaewon Kim visited New Delhi and Goa in November
and participated in the 56th International Film Festival
of India held in Goa.

Frequent exchanges between EAM and Minister of
Foreign Affairs of Armenia Aarat Mirzoyan, including
his bilateral visit to India during 9–11 March,
underscored the expanding scope of the partnership.
EAM also met him at the Raisina Mediterranean
Conference held in Marseille, France in June and
coordinated closely during the evacuation of Indian
nationals from Iran via Armenia during the Israel-Iran
conflict under Operation Sindhu.
Minister of Foreign Affairs of Armenia Aarat Mirzoyan met the
EAM during his bilateral visit to New Delhi, March 2025
The Secretary of the Security Council of Armenia
(NSA) Armen Grigoryan, visited India on 13 May and
met with the National Security Advisor (NSA). They
also had a telephonic conversation on 22 September.
Trilateral cooperation gained momentum with the
third India–Iran–Armenia consultations held in Tehran
in September, focusing on regional connectivity and
energy corridors. The 11th Round of Foreign Office
Consultations was held in Yerevan on 7 November,
co-chaired by Secretary (West) and Deputy Foreign
Minister of Armenia Mnatsakan Safaryan. During the
Consultations, an Agreement between the Ministry of
Health & Family Welfare and the Ministry of Health of
Armenia on cooperation in the field of Public Health
and Medical Science was signed by the First Deputy
Minister of Health of Armenia Lena Nanushyan and
the Ambassador of India to Armenia. Secretary (West)
also called on the Foreign Minister of Armenia Ararat
Mirzoyan.
A National Defence College (NDC) delegation visited
Armenia in June. An Armenian delegation led by
Deputy Chief of Armenian Armed Forces Major
General Temur Shahnazaryan visited India to attend
the United Nations Troop Contributing Countries
Chiefs’ Conclave on 14-16 October. During the visit,
Maj Gen Shahnazaryan met Vice Chief of the Army
Staff. The India-Armenia Defence Staff Talks (the first
Joint Working Group on Defence Cooperation) were
held in Hyderabad on 23-24 October. A Defence
Industry Seminar, CAMT-India 2025 (Cooperation
Armenia Military Technology) Seminar, was organised
by the Military Industrial Committee (MIC) of the
Ministry of High-Tech Industry (MHTI) of the Republic
of Armenia, in coordination with the Indian Embassy’s
Defence Wing at Yerevan, on 4-6 November. Joint
Secretary (Defence Industries Promotion) from the
Ministry of Defence led the Indian delegation, which
included 20 Indian defence companies. The delegation
aimed to explore opportunities and forge partnerships
in co-development, joint ventures, collaborative
R&D and co-investment. Joint Secretary (Defence
Industries Promotion) also called on Armenian Deputy
Minister of Defence Karen Brutyan and First Deputy
Minister of High-Tech Industry Gevorg Mantashyan
on 6 November. Defence cooperation also expanded
following the Chief of Defence Staff's visit in
November.
Economic relations expanded with focused sectoral
collaboration. The Armenian Minister of Economy
Gevorg Papoyan visited India to attend the 30th
edition of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII)
Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam, Andhra
Pradesh on 14-15 November. He met the Minister of
Commerce & Industry on the sidelines of the Summit
on 14 November. He also met the Minister of Civil
Aviation on 17 November.
The CDSCO–CDMTE MoU was complemented by
a Business Forum in March, attended by over 200
pharma companies from both countries, promoting
pharmaceutical and medical technology trade. The
India–Armenia Business Networking Event in May and
the Virtual Meeting on Tourism in October furthered
B2B engagement and tourism promotion.

Belarus
India-Belarus relations in this year were marked by
sustained high-level engagements across political,
defence, parliamentary, and diplomatic channels.
Prime Minister met President of Belarus Alexander
Lukashenko on 31 August during the Shanghai

Raksha Mantri met Defence Minister of Belarus
Lieutenant General Viktor Khrenin on the sidelines

26 June.
Prime Minister met President of Belarus Alexander Lukashenko

Foreign Office Consultations was held in Minsk during
the Secretary (West)’s visit in October. Discussions
covered the full spectrum of bilateral relations, regional
and global issues, and opportunities to enhance
cooperation. Secretary (West) also called on Minister
of Foreign Affairs of Belarus Maxim Ryzhenkov and
addressed the third Minsk International Conference
on Eurasian Security, presenting India’s perspectives
on pressing regional and global challenges. This

momentum.

and one Georgian Diplomat attended the third Global
South Young Diplomats Forum (GSYDF) conducted by
S ushma Swaraj Institute of Foreign Service (SSIFS) on
8-19 September.

of the Parliament of Georgia Shalva Papuashvili

Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)
India’s priorities in SCO are shaped by Prime Minister’s
vision of a ‘SECURE’ SCO. SECURE stands for
Security, Economic development, Connectivity, Unity,
Respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, and
Environmental protection. India remained actively
engaged in the SCO format, including through various
mechanisms/initiatives within the SCO framework,
and reiterated its mutual respect for sovereignty,
independence, territorial integrity, equality, mutual
benefit, and non-interference in internal affairs in
the Forum. India also consistently advocated for
greater emphasis on combating terrorism, enhancing
economic ties, promoting Digital Public Infrastructure,
digital inclusion, lifestyle for sustainable development
and WTO reforms. India’s advancement in economy,
trade, energy, technology, startups, innovation,
traditional medicine, etc., was also highlighted at
various SCO meetings.
Summit of SCO Council of Heads of State
Prime Minister attended the 25th SCO Summit in
Tianjin on 1 September held under the Chinese
Chairmanship. In his country statement, Prime Minister
outlined India’s vision and policy towards SCO, built
on three key pillars: S – Security, C – Connectivity,
and O - Opportunity. On Security, he emphasised
that security, peace and stability form the foundation
of development and that terrorism, separatism and
extremism remain challenges in this path. On the
heinous terrorist attack in Pahalgam, Prime Minister
thanked the friendly countries that stood by India
and urged the unacceptability of double standards
on terrorism. On Connectivity, he outlined initiatives
such as Chabahar Port and the International North-
South Transport Corridor (INSTC) to enhance India’s
connectivity with Afghanistan and Central Asia. Prime
Minister also underlined the importance of upholding
the principles of sovereignty and territorial integrity.
On Opportunity, he spoke about opportunities
for cooperation and reform, citing examples such
as India’s initiatives in start-ups and innovation,
traditional medicine, empowerment, digital inclusion,
and its shared Buddhist heritage.
Prime Minister also proposed creating a Civilizational
Dialogue Forum within the SCO to strengthen people-
to-people ties. On the occasion of the 80th anniversary
of the United Nations, he urged a unanimous call
for UN reform. Two significant Agreements were
signed at the Summit- the Agreement to establish
the Universal Centre for countering challenges and
threats, and the Agreement to establish the Anti-Drug
Centre, which reinforces one of the key objectives
of the Organisation: to fight terrorism, separatism,
extremism, and the drug menace.
In the main Summit declaration, the Member States
strongly condemned the terrorist attack in Pahalgam
on 22 April. The leaders also expressed their deepest
sympathies and condolences to the families of the
dead and the wounded. They further stated that
perpetrators, organisers and sponsors of such attacks
must be brought to justice.

Salman Nasser. The delegation also met prominent
think tanks of Bahrain, namely International Institute
for Strategic Studies (IISS) and the King Hamad Global
Center for Coexistence and Tolerance.
Minister of State for Law and Justice and for
Parliamentary Affairs visited Bahrain on 28-30 May
and held meetings with the Crown Prince and Prime

of Legal Affairs, and Minister of Justice and Islamic
Affairs Nawaf bin Mohammed Al Maawda. He also
met officials of the Bahrain Chamber for Dispute
Resolution. The Minister visited the 200-year-old
Shrinathji Temple along with Minister of Social
Development Osama bin Saleh Al Alawi.
Minister of State for Law and Justice and for

on 5 November and Conference on the Future of
International Commercial Courts on 6 November.
On 30 April, Undersecretary Ministry of Information
Yousif Mohammed Albinkhalil along with Noora
Mahmood Al Doy visited India to attend the World
Audio Visual Entertainment Summit (WAVES), held in
Mumbai on 1-4 May.
Economic and Trade Cooperation
Trade and economic relations between India and
Bahrain remained robust. In FY 2024-25, bilateral trade
reached USD 1.64 billion, with the trade gap reducing
to a marginal USD 48 million. India remained among
Bahrain’s top five trading partners. In FY 2025-26 (from
1.4.2025 to 30.11.2025) India’s exports to Bahrain
reached USD 553 million and imports from Bahrain
reached USD 480 million. Two-way investments
increased around 60 percent since 2019 and India
remained the sixth-largest investor in Bahrain.
The
international
arm
of
National
Payments
Corporation of India (NPCI), the NPCI International
Payments Limited (NIPL) and Bahrain’s leading
fintech and electronic financial transactions company
BENEFIT, entered into a partnership to enable real-
time cross-border remittances between India and
Bahrain, in November. This will connect India’s United
Payments Interface (UPI) with Bahrain’s Electronic
Fund Transfer System (EFTS), specifically through the
Fawri+ service, enabling users in both countries to
send and receive money instantly and securely.

and Commerce of Bahrain Abdulla bin Adel Fakhro,
Bahrain Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BCCI),
the Economic Development Board of Bahrain (EDB)
and the Bahrain Development of Small and Medium

June, India deployed five Navy officers as RAINBOW

INS Mormugao, INS Tarkash and INS Tabar, made a
port call at Manama from 8-11 September. The visit
reinforced India-Bahrain friendship and interactions
with the Bahraini leadership, USNAVCENT and
Combined Maritime Forces partners underscored
the Indian Navy’s commitment to regional maritime
security reflecting the implementation of the Security
and Growth for All in the Region (SAGAR) initiative.

E-Visa facility has been extended across 14 categories
to Bahraini nationals travelling to India in 2025. This
system allows Bahraini citizens to apply for and receive
e-visas for categories such as tourism, business,
medical, medical attendant, conference, Ayush,
Ayush attendant, student, student dependents, film,
mountaineering, transit and production investment
through the Indian Visa Online website.
A Senior Auditor at the National Audit Office of
Bahrain participated in the ‘Use of Data Analytics
and Emerging Technologies in Audit’ course from 19
August - 4 September at the International Center for
Information Systems and Audit, India.
Bahrain gave Royal Pardon to 164 Indian nationals in

Iran
This year marked the 75th anniversary of India-Iran
diplomatic ties. Bilateral cooperation between India
and Iran maintained its strong momentum in the
period, with regular contacts at the leadership and
official levels.

during his visit to India from 7–8 May. During the visit,
he co-chaired the 20th India–Iran Joint Commission
Meeting with EAM. This was his first visit to India
since assuming office as Minister of Foreign Affairs in
August 2024. He also met the NSA during the visit.

Iraq
India has been a traditional partner of Iraq with strong
historical and civilisational linkages.
Economic and Trade Cooperation
Iraq is now the seventh largest trade partner of India.
During FY 2024-25, the bilateral trade amounted to
USD 32.16 billion. This includes imports worth USD
28.89 billion and exports worth USD 3.21 billion.
During the period 1 January – 31 December, the
bilateral trade amounted to USD 29.98 billion. This
includes imports worth USD 26.67 billion and exports
worth USD 3.30 billion.
India’s crude imports from Iraq in 2024-25 amounted
to 50.90 MMT accounting for 20.90 percent of the
total imports of India’s crude oil. India’s crude imports
from Iraq for the period from 1 January – 31 December
amounted to 51.447 MMT accounting for USD 26.12
billion.

the academic year 2024-25, while 50 scholarships
were availed during the current academic year. In

Kuwait
India–Kuwait relations continued to build on the
momentum generated by the visit of Prime Minister to
Kuwait in December 2024, during which the bilateral
partnership was elevated to a strategic partnership.
During the year, India – Kuwait relations were further
strengthened by high level visits and interactions.
High Level Exchanges
EAM held a telephonic conversation with the then
Foreign Minister of Kuwait Abdullah Ali Al-Yahya in
April following the Pahalgam terror attack. An all-
party Indian delegation visited Kuwait from 26 to
27 May to reaffirm India’s position against terrorism
following Operation Sindoor. The delegation met
the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of State for
Council of Ministers Affairs Sherida Abdullah Saad
Al-Maousherji. The delegation also interacted with
local and Indian media, civil society, and the Indian
community.
Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas met Minister

margins of the ninth OPEC International Seminar in
Vienna on 9 July.
The seventh round of Foreign Office Consultations

reviewed bilateral cooperation, agreed to implement
the action points identified during Prime Minister’s
2024 visit to Kuwait, and committed to expediting
pending Joint Working Group meetings in order to
convene the first Joint Committee for Cooperation at
the earliest opportunity. Bilateral outcomes included
the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding
between the Financial Intelligence Unit of India and
the Financial Intelligence Unit of Kuwait in July and
the signing of an agreement on bilateral seat-sharing
capacity between India and Kuwait in July.

Total bilateral trade during FY 2024-25 reached
USD 10.22 billion, including Indian exports valued
at USD 1.93 billion. Kuwait continues to play an
important role in India’s energy security by accounting
for approximately 3.5 percent of India’s total energy
needs, ranking as India’s sixth-largest crude oil
supplier and fifth-largest LPG source. The Mission
organised a series of trade and investment promotion
activities during the period. To strengthen investment
cooperation, the Kuwait Investment Authority held
interactions with key Indian stakeholders led by the
Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal
Trade, followed by meetings with the Department
of Revenue and the National Investment and
Infrastructure Fund Limited.
Defence and Security Cooperation
India and Kuwait ratified the MoU on Defence
Cooperation in September. The Indian Coast Guard
ship ICGS Sarthak undertook a goodwill visit from
9-13 December and conducted a joint maritime
exercise with the Kuwaiti Navy patrol boat Garoh.
Cultural
The Mission organised several events highlighting
India’s cultural heritage and the growing partnership
between the two countries. These included ‘Rihla-
e-Dosti,’ an exhibition marking 250 years of India-
Kuwait partnership held with the National Council
for Culture, Arts and Letters at the Kuwait National
Library in May; ‘Bharat Mela’ in February, showcasing
Indian art, cuisine, music and fashion; and the 11th
International Day of Yoga, conducted for the first time
on a large public scale at Salmiya Boulevard. India
Corners were established at the American University
of Kuwait and the Kuwait National Library to deepen
cultural engagement.

Industry met Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign

held meetings at the National Archives of India in New
Delhi and the Maharashtra State Archives in Mumbai.

140
Economic and Trade Cooperation
India-Qatar bilateral trade remained robust at USD
14.14 billion in FY 2024-25. Energy continued to
form the core of bilateral trade, with Qatar remaining
a major supplier of LNG and LPG to India. Both sides
discussed a Bilateral Investment Treaty and the Terms
of Reference for launching FTA negotiations.
Qatar National Bank and Doha Insurance Group
announced the opening of offices in GIFT City
in March. On 15 September, NPCI International
Payments Ltd and Qatar National Bank announced
the acceptance of UPI payments in Qatar at its point-
of-sale systems. NPCI also concluded an agreement
with the Commercial Bank of Qatar for the launch of
UPI on its payment terminals.
Several Indian business delegations visited Qatar
to
explore
commercial
opportunities,
including
delegations from the IGTD EXIM Chamber of Commerce
from 16-19 June and PHD Chamber of Commerce
and Industry (PHDCCI) from 21-23 September. The
Embassy, in partnership with state governments,
organised tourism roadshows promoting Goa on 9
April and Madhya Pradesh on 3 May. A tribal products
exhibition was held from 26-28 January to promote
indigenous
handicrafts,
jewellery,
textiles
and
organic products. A Buyer-Seller Meet on agarwood
and its derivatives was held on 6 September. Qatar
announced a year-long partnership with the Nita
Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre in Mumbai on 22 July
to promote Qatar's heritage, attractions and luxury
experiences to Indian tourists.
People-to-People Contacts
Indian
diaspora
being
the
largest
expatriate
community in Qatar act as a living bridge between
India and Qatar. A large cultural festival was organised
in association with Indian community organisations
to celebrate Labour Day in May. The second edition
of the Indian Mango Festival was held from 12-21
June, with over 50,000 visitors from more than 60
nationalities attending the festival and total sales of
130,000 kilograms of mangoes.
Saudi Arabia
India and Saudi Arabia continued the momentum of
wide-ranging cooperation under the framework of the
Strategic Partnership Council underpinned by regular
high-level political and commercial exchanges.
High Level Exchanges
India’s engagement with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
advanced significantly during the year. Prime Minister
undertook a State Visit to Saudi Arabia on 22 April,
his third visit to the Kingdom and first to Jeddah. He
was received by Crown Prince and Prime Minister of
Saudi Arabia Prince Mohammed bin Salman at the
Royal Palace and accorded a ceremonial welcome.
Both leaders held official talks and co-chaired the
second meeting of the India–Saudi Arabia Strategic
Partnership Council.
Prime Minister met Crown Prince and Prime Minister of the
Kingdom of Saudi Arabia Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin
Abdulaziz Al Saud, in Jeddah, April 2025.
During the visit, Prime Minister received separate calls
from Secretary General of the Muslim World League
Sheikh Mohammed Al Issa, Padma Shri awardee
Nouf Marwaai and Deputy Editor-in-Chief of Arab
News Noor Nugali. He also interacted with the Indian
community. A Joint Statement issued after the visit
condemned cross-border terrorism. The Strategic
Partnership Council was expanded to include two
new pillars for defence cooperation, and tourism and
cultural cooperation. Both sides agreed to collaborate

Authority for Small and Medium Enterprises of Saudi

Economic and Trade Cooperation

steady progress. India is the second-largest trade
partner of Saudi Arabia, while Saudi Arabia is the
fifth-largest trading partner of India. In FY 2024-25,
total trade stood at USD 41.88 billion. In FY 2025-26

30.8 billion. Major Indian exports included engineering
goods, rice, petroleum products, chemicals, textiles,
food products and ceramic tiles. Major imports

included crude oil, LPG, fertilizers, chemicals, plastics
and related products. Saudi Arabia was India’s third-

imported 33.14 MMT of crude oil from Saudi Arabia
in FY 2024-25, accounting for 13.58 percent of total

supplier of fertilizers, particularly as the second-
largest source of Diammonium Phosphate (DAP) for

Defence and Security Cooperation
Defence cooperation registered substantive progress
during the year. On 3- 4 December the Chief of
General Staff of Saudi Arabia General Fayyad bin
Hamed Al-Ruwaili visited India for the first time. He
held a bilateral meeting with the Chief of Defence
Staff. A new Ministerial Committee on Defence
Cooperation under the Strategic Partnership Council
was announced in April. The inaugural Navy Staff
Talks were held in Riyadh in February, followed by
the inaugural Army Staff Talks in New Delhi in April.
A high-level Saudi military delegation participated in
Aero India from 9–11 February. Indian Naval Ships
Tamal and Surat made a port call at Jeddah in August
and conducted a PASSEX with the Royal Saudi Naval
Forces.
INS Tamal and Surat made a port call at Jeddah and conducted
a PASSEX with the Royal Saudi Naval Forces, August 2025
Indian Coast Guard Ship ICGS Sarthak conducted a
goodwill visit to Dammam, Saudi Arabia, on 21–25
December.
A Saudi delegation undertook a study visit to the
Information Fusion Centre–Indian Ocean Region in
Gurugram in July. The seventh meeting of the Joint
Committee on Defence Cooperation was held in
New Delhi in August. A delegation from the National
Defence College of India visited Saudi Arabia in
September for a familiarisation tour.
People-to-People
Cultural and people-to-people exchanges expanded
during the year. On 17 December, a bilateral
agreement for mutual exemption from short-stay
visa requirements for holders of diplomatic, special
and official passports of India and Saudi Arabia was
signed in Riyadh.
The Saudi Film Commission organised ‘Saudi Film
Nights’ in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad from 31
January to 5 February. The Literature, Publishing and
Translation Commission of Saudi Arabia participated
in the New Delhi World Book Fair in February. In the
same month, the Embassy and the Royal Commission
for Riyadh City hosted the musical performance ‘Three
Generations, One Melody’ featuring Indian sarod
maestro Ustad Amjad Ali Khan. A delegation led
by Chairman of the Saudi Esports Federation Prince
Faisal bin Bandar Al Saud participated in the WAVES
Summit in Mumbai, in May.
A two-member delegation from the National
Archives of India attended a symposium titled ‘Arabic
Documents in Indian Archives’ on 29 July, jointly
organised by the National Archives of India and the
King Abdulaziz Foundation. In October, a delegation
from the Darah Foundation undertook a study visit to
the National Archives of India.
Indian participation in sporting and cultural events
in Saudi Arabia also increased. Esports team S8UL
visited Riyadh to participate in the Esports World
Cup in July–August. The Indian men’s basketball team
visited Jeddah for the 31st FIBA Asia Cup in August.
The Embassy organised Hindi Diwas celebrations in
September with participation from Saudi nationals.

The Hajj and Umrah pilgrimages for the year were

2024-2028. Under the Joint Action Plan, online
meetings and interactions were also held on health,

food security pillars during the year.
India’s economic linkages with the Gulf Cooperation
Council continued to increase steadily. In FY 2024-25,
India–GCC bilateral trade reached USD 178.56 billion,
accounting for 15.42 percent of India’s global trade.
In FY 2025-26 (April - December 2025), India-GCC
bilateral trade stood at USD 136.72 billion. Saudi
Arabia remained India’s second largest GCC trade
partner after the United Arab Emirates.
UAE
India and the United Arab Emirates further deepened
their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in 2025
through regular high-level visits, stronger institutional
mechanisms and sustained strategic dialogue. This
political momentum enabled closer defence and
security cooperation, supported by upgraded dialogue
platforms, tri-service staff engagements and frequent
joint exercises.
High Level Exchanges
The Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister
and Minister of Defence of the United Arab Emirates
Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum,
undertook an official visit to India from 8-9 April.
During the visit, he called on Prime Minister in New
Delhi.
The visit resulted in the signing of MoUs and several
key announcements, including the establishment of
a campus of IIM Ahmedabad in Dubai and the first
overseas campus of the Indian Institute of Foreign
Trade at Expo City Dubai. The visit also marked the
launch of the construction of Bharat Mart and its 3D
model, allocation of land for the UAE–India Friendship
Hospital, development of ship-repair clusters at Kochi
and Vadinar, and the opening of an India office of the
Dubai Chamber of Commerce.
Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Defence
Minister of UAE Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum
called on Prime Minister during his visit to New Delhi, April 2025

of Abu Dhabi Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed;
and Crown Prince of Dubai Deputy Prime Minister and
Minister of Defence Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed
bin Rashid Al Maktoum.

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
146
Minister of Environment and Climate Change held
meetings in the United Arab Emirates from 11–13
February. The Minister of Food Processing and
Industries visited from 17–21 February. The Minister
of Culture travelled on 28–29 April. The Minister of
Heavy Industries and Steel visited from 30 June to
2 July. The Minister of Communications visited from
7–9 September, followed by the visit of the Minister
of Education from 10–11 September. The Minister
of Commerce and Industry visited from 18–19
September. MoS (KVS) undertook a visit from 9–11
October. MoS (Defence) visited from 17-18 November.
Ministerial visits from UAE to India included the visit
of Minister of State for Cultural Affairs Noura bint
Mohammed Al Kaabi for the Raisina Dialogue in New
Delhi in March; the visit of Minister of State for Foreign
Trade Thani bin Ahmed Al Zeyoudi on 29–30 August
and the visit of Minister of State for International
Cooperation Reem Al Hashimy on 10 September.
India and the United Arab Emirates maintained strong
institutional mechanisms across sectors. Several
platforms met during the year to review and advance
the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. The first
Joint Steering Committee of the India–UAE Cultural
Council was held in New Delhi on 19 March, followed
by the second meeting of the India–UAE Cultural
Council in Abu Dhabi on 9 October. The 13th Joint
Defence Cooperation Committee meeting, along with
the fourth Army-to-Army, ninth Navy-to-Navy and
inaugural Air-to-Air Staff Talks, was held from 28–30
July in New Delhi. The 13th meeting of the UAE–India
High-Level Joint Task Force on Investments convened
on 18–19 September in Abu Dhabi. The sixth meeting
of the India-UAE Joint Committee on Consular Affairs
was held in Abu Dhabi on 26 November. The third Joint
Committee meeting under the India – UAE CEPA was
held on 27 November. The Mid-Year Review was held
on 9–10 June followed by the 16th Joint Commission
meeting and fifth Strategic Dialogue on 15 December.
Economic and Trade Cooperation
United Arab Emirates is India’s second-largest
export destination. Bilateral trade reached USD
100.06 billion in FY 2024-25. In FY 2025-26, trade
continued to expand, with total trade at USD 89.44
billion during April–January, reflecting an 11.11
percent increase over the corresponding period of the
previous year. Non-oil trade also remained strong,
reaching USD 49.45 billion during April–November
FY 2025-26, marking a 14.80 percent rise, reflecting
continued diversification under CEPA. The Minister of
Commerce and Industry visited on 18-19 September
and attended the 13th High-Level Joint Task Force
on Investments, during which he announced the
establishment of the first overseas campus of the
Indian Institute of Foreign Trade at Expo City Dubai.
Economic cooperation expanded into fintech, digital
public infrastructure, artificial intelligence, renewable
energy, green hydrogen, critical minerals, healthcare
innovation and logistics, indicating a shift toward a
broad-based strategic economic partnership.
Defence and Security Cooperation
Defence cooperation advanced through the visit of
the Crown Prince of Dubai and Defence Minister of
UAE Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum to
India in April. This was followed by the visits of the
Commander of the UAE Navy (July), UAE Land Forces
(October) and the Commander of the UAE Air Force
and Air Defence (October).
India participated in Exercise Desert Flag-10 in the
United Arab Emirates from April to May, and both
countries held the joint exercise Desert Cyclone-II
from 18 to 30 December between the Indian Army
and the UAE Land Forces. These engagements were
further strengthened through the 13th Joint Defence
Cooperation Committee meeting held on 30 July,
which, for the first time, was convened at the Secretary
level.
Indian Air Force participated in the Exercise Desert Flag-10
along with United Arab Emirates Air Force in Al Dhafra Air
Base, April 2025

was preceded by the fourth Army-to-Army, ninth

28-29 July, and was followed by the second India–

A MoU between the Indian Coast Guard and

signed on 30 July to strengthen maritime security,
information sharing, coordinated search and rescue
operations and capacity-building. India participated
with a large delegation along with an India Pavilion,
at the International Defence Exhibition and Naval
Defence Exhibition held in Abu Dhabi in February.
India also participated in the Dubai Airshow 2025
held in November led by MoS (Defence) who also
inaugurated the India pavilion featuring HAL, DRDO,
Corel
Technologies,
Dantal
Hydraulics,
Image
Synergy, Ekxplor and SPO Technologies. A UAE

People-to-people Ties
People-to-people ties remained robust, with the
Indian community in the United Arab Emirates
growing from approximately 3.89 million in December
2023 to around 4.36 million by December 2024.
The education sector gained momentum in 2025,
marked by the expansion of leading Indian institutions
and innovation ecosystems. On 10 September, the
Minister of Education launched the first overseas Atal
Innovation Centre at the IIT Delhi–Abu Dhabi campus
and also inaugurated PhD and BTech programmes in
energy and sustainability. On 11 September, the IIM-
Ahmedabad Dubai Campus was jointly inaugurated
by the Minister of Education and Crown Prince of
Dubai Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid
Al Maktoum marking the launch of IIM-A’s first
overseas MBA programme. India also announced the
establishment of the first overseas Atal Tinkering Labs
in CBSE schools across the United Arab Emirates.
Cultural cooperation advanced through the first and
second meetings of the Joint Steering Committee of
the India–UAE Cultural Council on 19 March and 9
October, focusing on cultural exchanges, heritage
collaboration, youth engagement and institutional
partnerships.
Yemen
India’s relationship with Yemen is centuries old,
anchored in strong people-to-people ties. Despite
the challenging security situation, both countries
continued to maintain close relations. India remained
committed to a peaceful, Yemeni-led and Yemeni-
owned political resolution of the conflict through
dialogue.
India opened the new building of its representative
Office in Aden, Yemen in October to facilitate
consular services. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs
and Expatriates of Yemen welcomed the decision,
noting that the establishment of the office reflected
the strength of bilateral relations and the shared
commitment to deepen cooperation across political,
economic and cultural fields.
On 16–17 February, a delegation led by the
Ambassador
visited
Aden
and
handed
over
approximately 25 tonnes of essential medicines and
medical equipment to Minister of Health of Yemen
Qassem Mohammed Buhaybeh during a ceremony at
Port Aden. The consignment, dispatched from India at
the request of the Yemeni Government, was delivered
by the Indian Coast Guard Ship Sujeet.
After a gap of nearly ten years, the Embassy organised
Republic Day celebrations in Aden on 17 February.
The event was attended by the Minister of Public
Health and Population Qasem Mohammed Buhaybeh
as the chief guest. The Ambassador addressed the
gathering, and the Minister expressed appreciation

Defence cooperation remained an important pillar
of the bilateral partnership. 10 Yemeni cadets
continued training at the National Defence Academy,
Khadakwasla, and one officer attended the staff
course at DSSC Wellington.
A Yemeni delegation led by the Raksha Mantri

Mohsen Mohammed Al-Daeri. Both sides underlined
the long-standing bilateral relationship and India’s
continued support for capacity-building of Yemeni
personnel. They agreed to enhance cooperation

engagements.
On 3 December, nine Filipino nationals and one
Indian national, crew members of the cargo vessel
MV Eternity C, which had sunk in the Red Sea in July,
arrived in Muscat.
West Asia and North Africa Region
During the year, India continued to strengthen its
bilateral relations with countries in West Asia and
North Africa. High-level engagements included
visits from Egypt, Israel and Algeria, as well as
visits to Morocco, Algeria and Egypt. The inaugural
meeting of the India–Egypt Strategic Dialogue was
also convened. Several working-level delegations
were exchanged, contributing to the deepening
of cooperation across political-security, economic,
cultural and people-to-people pillars. The year also
witnessed the re - opened Indian Embassy in Tripoli
establishing full functionality and the reopening of the
Embassy of India to Somalia, after more than thirty
years, with operations based in Nairobi.
Countries in the region reiterated strong support
to India in its fight against terrorism. A multi-party
delegation visited Egypt and Algeria following the
terrorist attack in Pahalgam.
Capacity building and human resource development
continued to remain central to India’s engagement
with several countries in the region, particularly
through ITEC and ICCR scholarship programmes.

conveyed its support to India in the fight against
terrorism.

Djibouti
India values its ties with Djibouti and the partnership
with Djibouti continued to strengthen during the year.
Defence and security cooperation
This year, Defence Wing was established at the
Embassy of India in Djibouti. Indian Naval ships
continued to make regular port calls at the Port of
Djibouti under Operation Turn Round to counter piracy
in the Gulf of Aden and the Red Sea region. During the
year, six Indian Naval ships visited Djibouti.
Commander of the Navy of the Armed Forces of Djibouti
Ahmed Daher Djama led a two-member delegation to
the Africa–India Key Maritime Engagement (AIKEYME)
held in April off the coast of Dar es Salaam, Tanzania.
Humanitarian Assistance
India donated 20 units of Haemodialysis machines and
one RO plant, along with consumables as humanitarian
assistance to Djibouti in March. A five member
delegation led by the Director General of Purchasing

Djibouti Hassan Abdourahman Elmi participated in

September in New Delhi.

India and Egypt held many high-level visits, strong
trade and economic ties, and growing defence and

Following the terrorist attack in Pahalgam, Egypt

The President of Egypt Abdel Fattah El-Sisi held a
telephonic conversation with Prime Minister soon

conversations with the Minister of Foreign Affairs of
Egypt Badr Abdelatty. An all-party Parliamentary

held meetings with senior leadership, including the
Minister of Foreign Affairs of Egypt, the Secretary
General of the League of Arab States, the heads of
parliamentary foreign affairs committees, the Egyptian
Council for Foreign Affairs, and representatives of the
media.
The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Egypt Badr Abdelatty
visited India from 16 to 17 October to co-chair the
inaugural India–Egypt Strategic Dialogue with the
EAM.

Israel
The year 2025 witnessed continued strengthening and
deepening of the India-Israel strategic partnership with
robust cooperation in the areas of defence, innovation
and technology, agriculture, water management and

commitment to advancing mutual growth and security
through collaborative initiatives and regular high-level
interactions.

Prime Minister of Israel Benjamin Netanyahu

attack in Pahalgam over a telephone conversation
with Prime Minister on 24 April. On 13 June, Prime
Minister Netanyahu spoke with Prime Minister and
briefed him on the prevailing situation in the context of
the Israel–Iran conflict. On 9 October, Prime Minister
called Prime Minister Netanyahu to congratulate him
on the progress made under President Trump’s Gaza
Peace Plan, including the release of hostages and the
facilitation of humanitarian assistance for the people
of Gaza.
Minister of Foreign Affairs of Israel Gideon Sa’ar visited
India from 3 - 5 November and met EAM and the NSA.

India and Israel took significant steps towards
deepening their economic engagement. During the
visit of Finance Minister of Israel Bezalel Smotrich
in September, the two sides signed a Bilateral

both sides signed a memorandum of understanding

India conducted Operation Sindhu on 18 June to
evacuate Indian nationals from conflict zones in Iran
and Israel. A total of 818 Indian nationals from Israel
returned to India in four special flights, including three
IAF C-17 aircraft from 23-25 June.

2025 marks the 75th anniversary of the establishment
of diplomatic relations between the two countries.

Abdullah II and Prime Minister held a telephonic

rejected in all its forms and manifestations.

16 December, his first full-fledged bilateral visit to
the country. The visit, which took place after a gap of
37 years, coincided with the 75th anniversary of the
establishment of diplomatic relations between India
and Jordan. Prime Minister was accorded a ceremonial
welcome and held discussions with King Abdullah II
bin Al-Hussein and Prime Minister Jafar Hassan.

Marrakech from 17–21 February. Minister of State

Entrepreneurship and Education participated in the
third GITEX Africa in Marrakech from 14–16 April. The
fifth meeting of the Joint Working Group under the
MoU on Cooperation in the Field of Water Resources
was held with participation of an official delegation
from the Ministry of Jal Shakti from 1–6 June. The third
meeting of the Joint Working Group under the India–
Morocco MoU on Cooperation in Health was held
virtually on 15 September.
Raksha Mantri visited Morocco from 21–23 September.
During the visit, he and the Minister Delegate in
charge of the National Defence Administration of
Morocco Abdeltif Loudyi signed an MoU on defence
cooperation.
The two Ministers jointly inaugurated the new plant of
Tata Advanced Systems – Morocco for the production
of the WhAP 8x8 ground combat vehicle in Berrechid.
Defence and security cooperation
A delegation from the National Defence College
comprising 16 senior defence officers visited Morocco
on a study tour from 1–7 June. Colonel Mustapha
Hmadou from the Moroccan Royal Armed Forces
(FAR) attended the 65th NDC Course on ‘National
Security and Strategic Studies’ at the National Defence
College, New Delhi from 6 January – 28 November.
INS Tamal, a Talwar-class frigate of the Indian Navy,
made a port call at Casablanca Military Port from 6–9
August.
Capacity Building
More than 42 Moroccan officials participated in various
training courses in India under the ITEC programme
during the year. A Special ITEC Course on Green
Hydrogen for Morocco was conducted at the NTPC
School of Business, Noida from 3–7 February.
Palestine
India has continued its persistent support through
various developmental and humanitarian assistance
to the Palestinian people amidst the continuing Israel-
Hamas conflict.
Projects valued at USD 40 million remained under
implementation, including the Indian Super-Specialty
Hospital in Jenin, the India–Palestine Centre for
Empowering Women Turathi, and the Palestinian
Institute of Diplomacy. The commissioning of the
National Printing Press in Ramallah was completed
during the year.
In addition to major projects, India completed
three Quick Impact Projects in Qalqilia, Nablus and
Bethlehem governorates, covering the renovation
of houses, establishment of an IT Centre and
development of a public library.
Capacity-building cooperation continued through
scholarship and training programmes. Under the ICCR
scholarship scheme, 50 annual slots are available,
of which 24 were utilised by the Palestinian side.
Under ITEC, 168 annual slots are allocated, with 74
utilised during the year. A specialised training course
for 45 officials of the Palestinian Customs Police was
conducted at Rashtriya Raksha University in August.
Somalia
India and Somalia continued to strengthen their
bilateral cooperation during the year, especially in the
fields of capacity building, humanitarian assistance
and people to people exchanges. The leadership of
both countries continued their engagements on the
sidelines of multilateral fora.
EAM met the Foreign Minister of Somalia Abdisalam
Abdi Ali in September on the margins of the 80th
UNGA High-Level Week in New York. EAM also
spoke with him in April following the terrorist attack
in Pahalgam. The Deputy Minister of Environment
and Climate Change Hussein Ali Haji Abdulle visited
India on 16 June to attend the First Assembly of the
International Big Cat Alliance in New Delhi. MoS (KVS)
met the State Minister of Foreign Affairs of Somalia
on 15 October on the sidelines of the 19th Mid-Term
Ministerial Conference of the Non-Aligned Movement
in Uganda.

text:
GCC, West Asia & North Africa
159
Capacity building remained a key pillar of cooperation.
A special course for foreign diplomats from North and
East African countries was organised at the Sushma
Swaraj Institute of Foreign Service from 4–13 August,
attended by ten Somali diplomats. Two Somali media
personnel participated in a familiarisation programme
in India from 10–18 June.
India continued to extend humanitarian assistance
to the Somali people. Ten tonnes of medicines and
medical supplies including essential life-saving
medicines, surgical items, hospital consumables and
medical equipment were donated in September.
South Sudan
Bilateral relations between India and South Sudan
continued to strengthen during the year, with capacity
building and human resource development remaining
central to the partnership. A 12-member delegation
from the Committee on Finance and Economic Planning
of the Transitional National Legislative Assembly
undertook a benchmarking study tour hosted by the
Lok Sabha Secretariat in February. Minister of Defence
and Veterans Affairs of South Sudan Lieutenant
General Chol Thon J Balok attended Aero India 2025
in Bengaluru in February.
A delegation of eight Members of Parliament from
the Transitional National Legislative Assembly, led by
Chairperson of the Standing Specialized Committee
on Information, Communication and Technology and
Spokesperson of Parliament Oliver Mori Benjamin,
participated in a training course on cyber security
for Members of Parliament held at the Lok Sabha
Secretariat from 18 July - 1 August.
As part of the first Special Course for Diplomats
from Eritrea, Libya, Somalia and South Sudan, 10
diplomats from South Sudan attended training at the
Sushma Swaraj Institute of Foreign Service (SSIFS),
New Delhi from 4-13 August. With this, a total of 90
South Sudanese diplomats have undergone training
in India so far. The Vice-Chancellor of Dr. John Garang
Memorial University of Science and Technology
visited India in July–August under the Academic
Visitors Programme of the Indian Council for Cultural
Relations.
India continued its support through developmental
initiatives, including Quick Impact Projects, provision
of veterinary medicines for free veterinary camps,
construction of a seismological observatory, and
renovation of the South Sudan Learning Centre.
India continued its focus on capacity building under
the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation
(ITEC) programme, with over 70 training slots utilised
by South Sudanese nationals during the year. In
addition, 35 South Sudanese students received ICCR
scholarships for higher education in India.
Sudan
Bilateral cooperation with Sudan remained steady
during the year despite the ongoing conflict, with India’s
engagement focused on humanitarian assistance and
capacity building. In March, India delivered two tonnes
of high-value cancer medicines to support Sudan’s
healthcare system. In July, India donated 2,000 metric
tonnes of rice as humanitarian assistance, reaffirming
its solidarity with the people of Sudan.
In line with India’s commitment to capacity-building
cooperation,
the
Mission
facilitated
72
ICCR
scholarships for Sudanese students to pursue higher
education in India, reflecting a significant increase in
utilisation compared to the previous year.
Under
prospective
humanitarian
assistance,
preparations were underway for organising a Jaipur
Foot Camp in late December. India also proposed
to donate 20 haemo-dialysis machines and two RO
plants to Sudan, with delivery expected by the end of
December.
Syria
India and Syria continued to nurture their cooperation
during the year, marked by the formation of a new
government in Syria and sustained engagement in
capacity building and people-to-people exchanges.

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
160
In July, an Indian delegation visited Syria and handed
over humanitarian assistance comprising life-saving
medicines including five metric tonnes of life-saving
medicines, including anti-cancer drugs, antibiotics and
anti-hypertensives. During the visit, the delegation
called on the Minister of Health and the Minister of
Foreign Affairs and Expatriates, and held discussions
with senior officials. From the Syrian side, the Director
of the Afro-Asia and Oceania Division visited India in
November.
India continued its partnership with Syria in the field of
capacity building under various flagship programmes
of the Government of India. During the year, ninety
ITEC seats were offered to Syria. In addition, 25 ICCR
scholarship seats were offered to Syrian students.
Tunisia
India and Tunisia have fostered a partnership rooted
in mutual respect, shared values, and common
interests. In February 2025, Agriculture Minister of
Tunisia Ezzeddine Ben Cheikh visited India to attend
the 21st AARDO Conference in New Delhi. The fifth
meeting of the India-Tunisia Joint Working Group on
Scientific & Technological Cooperation was held in
Tunis in January, where both sides reviewed priorities
and agreed to launch the fourth edition of joint R&D
initiatives focusing on climate change, eco-innovation,
e-health, and geospatial technology.
Economic and Trade Cooperation
Between January and July 2025, (No update from
Division) total bilateral trade between India and
Tunisia stood at USD 319.96 million, comprising
Indian exports worth USD 237.24 million and imports
from Tunisia amounting to USD 82.72 million. In May,
KPIT Technologies became the first Indian IT company
to establish operations in Tunisia with a Software
Engineering Centre in Sfax. M/s Jakson Green was
awarded an EPC contract for a 100 MW Solar PV
Project in Kairouan Governorate. The Tunisia-India
Fertilizers (TIFERT) joint venture, with GSFC Ltd. and
CIL holding a combined 30 percent stake, reached a
milestone in August with a financial restructuring plan
including a USD 20 million investment from Indian
partners and a debt conversion by the Tunisian side.
The 60th ITEC Day was celebrated in March with
participation from over 80 alumni, including senior
Tunisian Parliamentarian Tarak Rebai, while the 61st
ITEC Day was marked in September with over 50
alumni and senior officials from the Tunisian Ministry
of Foreign Affairs in attendance.

Africa
161
Central & West Africa
During this year, bilateral relations between India
and the Central and West African (C&WA) countries
continued to strengthen, building on the deep-rooted
partnership cultivated over decades. The year was
marked by sustained engagement and high-level
exchanges from both sides, including the state visit
of Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji to Angola in November, the
state visit of Prime Minister to Ghana in July, the state
visit of the President of Angola to India in May.
Bilateral trade between India and the C&WA region
during FY 2024–25 reached USD 26.3 billion, with
exports totalling USD 14.48 billion and imports valued
at approximately USD 11.89 billion. For this year, the
bilateral trade between India and the C&WA region
reached USD 25.38 billion, with exports totalling
USD 9.4 billion and imports amounting to USD
15.9 billion. The India-Africa Confederation of Indian
Industry (CII) Business Conclave held in August, saw
robust participation from the region, underscoring
growing mutual interest in expanding economic and
commercial partnerships. Indian investment in the
region is estimated to exceed USD 40 billion. Indian
companies operating across the region are engaged
in sectors such as mining, agriculture, automobiles,
pharmaceuticals, medical tourism, power, and energy.
Several Indian companies have established assembly
plants, including TVS, Mahindra, TATA, and Ashok
Leyland, among others.
The region continued to benefit from India’s capacity-
building initiatives, including the Indian Technical and
Economic Cooperation (ITEC) programme and ICCR
scholarships. During this year, India offered 2,106 ITEC
training slots (civilian and defence) and 293 Indian
Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR) scholarships for
undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral students
from the C&WA region. Additionally, the External
Publicity and Public Diplomacy (XPD) Division
organised a familiarisation visit to India in May for
social media influencers from the region to promote
stronger people-to-people and digital engagement.

ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
162
Defence and maritime cooperation further expanded,
with a focus on capacity-building, training, and
information sharing to enhance maritime security and
safeguard shared interests in the Gulf of Guinea and
the broader Atlantic corridor.
Cultural exchanges also gathered momentum, with
artists from the region participating in India’s annual
Surajkund Mela, reflecting shared cultural vibrancy.
The Indian diaspora across the region continued
to play a pivotal role in strengthening bilateral ties
through entrepreneurship, investment, and community
engagement.
Angola
India and Angola marked 40 years of diplomatic
relationship in 2025. During the year, President of
Angola Joao Lourenco paid a state visit to India in
May after almost three decades. He held talks with
Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji and delegation-level talks with
the Prime Minister. During the visit, three MoUs were
signed, a Line of Credit (LoC) for USD 200 million
was announced, and Angola formally joined the
International Solar Alliance (ISA).
President of Angola Joao Lourenco held talks with Hon’ble
Rashtrapati ji and Prime Minister during his state visit to India,
May 2025
The President of Angola Joao Lourenco invited Hon’ble
Rashtrapati ji and Prime Minister to participate in
the 50th Independence Day of Angola in November.
Following this, Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji paid a state visit,
addressed the National Assembly of Angola on 10
November and also took part in the Independence
Day celebrations on 11 November.
Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji addressed the National Assembly of
Angola in Luanda, November 2025
EAM and Foreign Minister of Angola Tete Antonio met
on the sidelines of the G-20 Foreign Ministers Meeting
in February, in Johannesburg. Minister of State and
Chief of the Military House of the President of Angola
General Francisco Pereira Furtado visited India and
met MoS (Defence) on 26-28 February.
Minister of Industry and Commerce of Angola
Rui Miguens de Oliveira participated in the 30th
CII Partnership Summit held in Visakhapatnam
in November, underlining expanding trade and
investment cooperation.
Director General of the Angolan National Authority
for Arms Control and Disarmament José Paulo Isabel
participated in the International Conference on ‘50
Years of the Biological Weapons Convention (BWC):
Strengthening Biosecurity for the Global South’ held
in New Delhi, in December.
EAM met Foreign Minister of Angola Tete Antonio on the
sidelines of G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Johannesburg,
February 2025
