Africa
163
India has been among the top three trading partners
of Angola for some years and currently it is second
after China sharing about 10 percent of Angola's
external trade. India is the second largest oil importer
of Angola, which accounts for 90 percent of bilateral
trade. During 2024-25, bilateral trade amounted to
USD 5.03 billion, an increase by 20 percent compared
to 2023-24. Indian exports amounted to USD 524
million. For this year, the bilateral trade amounts to
USD 3.2 billion, with exports totalling USD 422
million and imports amounting to USD 2.8 billion.
Moreover, 12 ITEC slots were offered to Angola. 10
ICCR scholarship slots that were granted to Angola
were fully utilized.
Benin
The re-opening of the Beninese Embassy in New
Delhi in May, was one of the most significant steps in
strengthening bilateral relations. The newly appointed
Ambassador of Benin to India presented credentials
to Hon'ble Rashtrapati ji in the same month.
Defence cooperation between the two countries has
witnessed steady growth over the years. A high-level
Benin Air Force delegation led by Chief of Air Staff
Senior Col Hermann William Avocanh, participated in
Aero India on 10-14 February, in Bengaluru. On the
sidelines of the event, he held bilateral discussions
with the Chief of Air Staff to explore avenues for
further strengthening bilateral defence cooperation.
India is among the five top trading partners of Benin.
Bilateral trade with Benin stood at USD 1,325.49
billion in 2024-25. For the current year, the bilateral
trade amounts to USD 618 million, with exports
totalling USD 565 million and imports amounting to
USD 52 million. Aimed at strengthening trade relations
between the two countries, a B2B for CII’s multi-
sector delegation was held in Cotonou in April. More
than 90 Indian owned/operated companies active in
Benin, India is Benin’s one of the largest investors with
a total investment topping USD 1.5 billion.
ICCR offered two scholarships under the ‘ICCR-Africa
Scholarship Scheme’ for Beninese students to pursue
post-graduate courses in India. In total, 25 civilian
training slots have been allotted to Benin under ITEC/
e-ITEC.
Burkina Faso
On the invitation of Speaker of Lok Sabha, President
(Speaker) of Transitional Legislative Assembly (ALT)
of Burkina Faso Ousmane Bougouma visited India on
24-30 November.
India-UN Development Partnership Funded Project -
Niangdo Dam project - is expected to be handed over
to the Burkinabe authorities by end of the year.
Burkina Faso participated in the Aero India held in
Bengaluru. The bilateral trade between India and
Burkina Faso stood at USD 224.82 million in 2024-
25. For the current year, the bilateral trade amounts
to USD 344 million, with exports totalling USD 93.52
million and imports amounting to USD 250.48 million.
Burkina Faso participated in the eighth session of the
International Solar Alliance (ISA) Assembly held in
New Delhi on 27–30 October, reflecting cooperation
in renewable energy and climate action.
A
23-member
CII-India
Business
delegation
participated in the first edition of the International
Investment Forum organised by the Government of
Burkina Faso on 9-10 October.
Burkina Faso continued to benefit from India’s
ITEC Programme, Professional Courses for Foreign
Diplomats (PCFD), ICCR Scholarships and tariff
benefits under India’s Duty-Free Tariff Preference
(DFTP) Scheme. This year, two scholarships slots
under ICCR and 30 ITEC slots are offered to Burkina
Faso.
Cabo Verde
After the first ever Foreign Office Consultations (FOC)
in 2024, the relations between India and Cabo Verde
continued to grow. Cabo Verde extended support to
Indian candidatures to various posts in the UN and
multilateral fora.

164
Cabo Verde participated in the eighth Session of the
ISA Assembly in October, International Conference on
50 Years of the BWC in December, and the second
World Health Organisation (WHO) Global Summit on
Traditional Medicine in December, in New Delhi.
A 15-member cultural troupe from Cabo Verde visited
India to participate in the 38th edition of Surajkund
International Crafts Mela 2025. A Business-to-

in Praia with APEDA and the local Chamber of

Cameroon
Minister Delegate at the Ministry of External Relations
Felix Mbayu, attended the CII India-Africa Business
Conclave in August. On the sidelines, he met MoS
(KVS), on 27 August.
Minister of Public Health of Cameroon Manaouda
Malachie participated in the second WHO Global
Summit on Traditional Medicine in December, in New
Delhi.
MoS (KVS) met Minister Delegate for External Relations
of Cameroon on the sidelines of CII India-Africa Business
Conclave in New Delhi, August 2025
The first-ever delegation from the International War
College of Yaounde, comprising 68 members, visited
India as part of a study tour, on 3-12 July. General
Donatien Melingui Nouma also led a delegation to
attend Aero India in February, in Bengaluru.
During 2024-25, the bilateral trade stood at USD
933 million, with India’s exports valued at USD 596
million and Cameroonian exports to India at USD
337 million. Indian exports registered an increase of
31.27 percent during the year, while the Cameroonian
exports to India declined by 57.23 percent compared
to the previous year. For this year, the bilateral trade
amounts to USD 619.7 million, with exports totalling
USD 406.07 million and imports amounting to USD
213.66 million.
A delegation from the Ministry of Public Health of
Cameroon visited India in June to participate in the
second edition of the Policymakers’ Visit on Indian
Pharmacopoeia.
In view of the devastating floods in the Far North
Region of Cameroon, India extended humanitarian
assistance by sending 1000 MT of rice, medicines and
other relief materials, in May.
During the year, India offered 181 ITEC training
slots and three ICCR scholarships to Cameroonian
nationals.
Central African Republic (CAR)
Despite the conflict between the rebel groups and
the government forces in CAR which has been an
impediment to all aspects of bilateral relations since
2013, the bilateral trade grew significantly from USD
65.49 million in 2023-24 to USD143.70 million in
2024-25. CAR supports India’s candidature at various
international fora. India has extended LoC worth
USD 56.50 million to the CAR for its developmental
projects.
Chad
The first India-Chad FOC was held on 13 February,
in N’Djamena. Both sides discussed and reviewed

the entire gamut of bilateral relations, paving way for
opportunities to collaborate in areas including trade,
technology, innovation and people-to-people ties.
A senior official delegation from the Chadian Ministry
of Water and Energy participated in the eighth Session
of the ISA Assembly in New Delhi, in October. Follow-
up engagements continued after Chad’s participation
in India-Africa business platforms, with Indian
companies exploring opportunities under ‘Tchad
Connexion 2030’. Capacity-building cooperation
under ITEC and ICCR remained robust.
Bilateral trade between the two countries saw a

During last two years, nine senior diplomats have
attended a Special Training at Sushma Swaraj Institute
of Foreign Service (SSIFS), 16 Chadian professionals
have attended various ITEC courses in India, 20 ICCR
scholarship slots allotted to Chadian students and
five students have been selected for Hindi Language
Learning Course at Kendriya Hindi Sansthan Agra; a
batch of 24 Chadian diplomats and senior officials
underwent English language course at English and
Foreign Language University, Hyderabad.
Cote d’Ivoire
The first India–Côte d’Ivoire Defence Seminar in
Abidjan, in July, featured top Indian manufacturers,
bolstering strategic security collaboration.
Bilateral trade surpassed USD 1 billion from January
to August (up from the prior year), with Indian exports
at USD 615.7 million, a 13 percent rise from USD
543.75 million in 2024. An increase in bilateral trade
highlighted the expanding economic cooperation and
India’s growing commercial presence in Côte d’Ivoire.
Key achievements included the inauguration of two
Indian-managed cashew processing units and laying
the foundation for Côte d’Ivoire's first Indian rubber
transformation investment.
Capacity building remained a key pillar of bilateral
relations, with India offering 112 ITEC training slots
and 12 ICCR scholarships.
Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC)
The bilateral trade for the current year amounted to
USD 477.82 million.
An All-Party Indian Parliamentary delegation visited
DRC on 24-28 May as part of India’s diplomatic
outreach aimed at projecting India’s united and
unwavering stance on the fight against all forms
of terrorism. The delegation held meetings with
Deputy Prime Minister & Minister of Transport Jean-
Pierre Bemba Gombo, Minister of Foreign Affairs,
International Cooperation and Francophonie Therese
Kayikwamba Wagner, Speaker of the National
Assembly Vital Kamerhe Lwa Kanyiginya Nkingi,
President of the Senate Jean-Michel Sama Lukonde
Kyende, and Member of Parliament and President
of Committee on Foreign Affairs of the National
Assembly Berthold Ulungu.
The Permanent Secretary of Defence Major General
Lukwikila Metikwiza Marcel visited India in February
and met the Defence Secretary on the sidelines of
Aero India in Bengaluru. The first India-DRC Defence
Industry Seminar & Expo on 28-29 January, in
Kinshasa, with the participation of 12 Indian defence
companies marked a significant step forward in
enhancing bilateral engagement in the defence sector.
Under India’s capacity building programme, 32
Diplomats from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of DRC
attended the second special training course at the
SSIFS on 19-28 March. 13 Congolese officials visited
India to attend various ITEC training programmes. An
eight-member cultural group ‘La Sanza Asbl’ from
DRC visited India from 30 September to 5 October to
participate in the ninth edition of the India International
Folk Festival held in New Delhi, as well as for other
performances, under the sponsorship of MEA and
ICCR.

ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
166
Equatorial Guinea
Equatorial Guinea continued to support Indian
candidature to various posts in the UN and other
multilateral fora.
The first India and Equatorial Guinea FOC was held on
February 10, in Malabo. It was co-chaired by Additional
Secretary (C&WA), and Secretary General of the
Ministry of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation
and Diaspora Matias Nguema Mba Medja. On the
sidelines of FOC, the Additional Secretary (C&WA)
handed over a humanitarian aid of anti-retroviral
drugs and diagnostic kits for management of HIV/
AIDS weighing around 10,000 kgs to the Minister of
Health, Social Welfare and Health Infrastructures of
Equatorial Guinea.
The Minister of State for Information, Press, and
Culture Jeronimo Osa Osa Ecoro, participated in the
World Audiovisual & Entertainment Summit held on
1-4 May, in Mumbai.
Bilateral trade between two countries stood at USD
463.32 million during the year 2024-25. In the current
year, the bilateral trade amounted to USD 105.7
million. During the year, India offered 42 ITEC training
slots and one ICCR scholarship. Nine candidates from
Equatorial Guinea have been selected so far. Further,
two officers attended the ITEC Executive Programme
on ‘Land Governance’ at Haryana Institute of Public
Administration, in March. A special ITEC course on
‘Computer Science and New/emerging Technologies
has been approved for 22 officials of the Equatorial
Guinea from 12-25 November at CDAC, Noida and
the participation is under process.
Equatorial Guinea’s cultural troupe ‘National Ballet
Ceiba’ participated in the 38th Surajkund International
Craft Fair in February.
Gabon
During the year, India appointing its first resident
High Commissioner, who presented his credentials
on 24 February, marked a significant development in
bilateral relations.
Defence Minister Brigitte Okinawa participated in the
Aero India in February, in Bengaluru.
For this year, the bilateral trade amounted to USD
522.06 million. Mission started passport and visa
services in August, facilitating mostly medical,
business and student travellers to India.
Five diplomats underwent training at SSIFS, New Delhi
and four government personnel underwent training
under various ITEC schemes. Under development
assistance, India supported an agriculture project
titled ‘Empowering Youth and Women-led SMEs
to Revitalize the Cassava Value Chain in Gabon’,
estimated at USD 1 million through the IBSA
framework. The project commenced on 26 May.
Ghana
For the first time in three decades, the Prime Minister
paid a historic state visit to Ghana on 2-3 July. Ghana
President John Dramani Mahama conferred one of the
highest national honours ‘Order of the Star of Volta’, on
Prime Minister. During the visit, signing of four MoUs
further cemented bilateral ties. The Prime Minister also
addressed a special session of the Parliament of Ghana,
becoming the first Indian Prime Minister to do so.
Prime Minister was conferred with national honour of Ghana
‘Order of the Star of Ghana’ by President of Ghana John
Dramani Mahama, July 2025

text:
Africa
167
Foreign Minister of Ghana Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa
visited India in March to participate in the 10th edition
of the Raisina Dialogue, in New Delhi. Commonwealth
Secretary General (CSG) and former Ghanaian Foreign
Minister Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey visited India ahead
of assuming her responsibilities and met EAM in
March.
India is among the top trading partners of Ghana
and is the largest destination for Ghanaian exports.
In 2024-25, bilateral trade stood at USD 3,1 billion.
For this year, the bilateral trade amounted to USD 4.9
billion. Indian companies are playing an important
part in Ghana’s economic growth with around USD 2
billion investments across 900 projects.
A 20-member cultural troupe from Ghana participated
in the 38th Surajkund International Crafts Mela 2025
held at Faridabad on 7-23 February.
Guinea-Bissau
India’s relations with Guinea-Bissau remained warm
and friendly. Guinea-Bissau continued to support
India at various multilateral fora.
Ambassador of India to Senegal, The Gambia and
Guinea-Bissau represented India in the 15th Summit of
Community of Portuguese Speaking Countries Summit
(CPLP) held in Bissau, capital of Guinea-Bissau from
17-18 July in India’s capacity as Associate Observer.
Inspector General of Ministry of Energy Fernandes
Silva Dojo participated in the eighth Session of the ISA
Assembly on 27-30 October, in New Delhi.
Bilateral trade between India and Guinea-Bissau
touched USD 204 million during 2024-25, maintaining
the steady rise in the volume of trade with Guinea-
Bissau in recent years. In this year, the bilateral trade
amounted to USD 238 million.
Under capacity building, Guinea-Bissau has been
offered eight slots for the year under the ITEC civilian
program.
Liberia
Minister of Internal Affairs Francis Sakila Nyumalin led
a delegation to the 21st Afro-Asian Rural Development
Organization (AARDO) Conference in New Delhi, in
February.
As part of Government of India’s diplomatic outreach
following the terrorist attack in Pahalgam on 22 April,
an All-Party Parliamentary Delegation visited Liberia
from 31 May to 3 June. Minister of Commerce and
Industry Magdalene Dagoseh attended India Maritime
Week and the second Edition of Sagarmanthan: The
Great Oceans Dialogue on 27-29 October, in Mumbai.
Liberia joined the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA)
and also signed the Framework Agreement in ISA. It
participated in the ISA Assembly in October and the
BWC Conference in December.
The first India–Liberia United Nations Consultations
were held on 29–30 December in New Delhi,
reflecting enhanced coordination ahead of Liberia’s
United Nations Security Council (UNSC) tenure in
2026-27.
India sanctioned a USD 1 million project under the
IBSA Fund for South-South Cooperation (India, Brazil,
and South Africa) titled ‘Women Legislators in Liberia:
Promoting Voice, Leadership, and Gender-Responsive
Governance’.
Bilateral trade between India and Liberia has recorded
significant growth in 2024-25 reaching USD 397
million, an annual increase of 55 percent. For the year,
the bilateral trade amounts to USD 234 million.
Liberia continues to benefit from ITEC courses and
ICCR Scholarship. Liberia utilized 67 ITEC slots and
four ICCR scholarships for under graduate / post-
graduate studies.
Mali
India and Mali have traditionally maintained friendly
relations based on shared values, mutual trust and
goodwill. India and Mali continued to support each

other’s candidature in various UN and international

condemning the dastardly terror attack of Pahalgam

delegation visit to Bamako in October, particularly in
economic and trade sectors.

delegation led by Secretary General of Ministry of
Defence and Veteran Affairs of Mali Major General
Sidiki Samake, visited Bengaluru to participate in the
Aero India show on 9-13 February and met Raksha

Mali continued to benefit from capacity building
assistance provided by GoI. Malian citizens were
offered 70 ITEC slots and 15 ICCR respectively.
Overall, the friendly relations between India and Mali
continued to progress and strengthen during the year.
Mauritania
In a major development, Mauritania has opened its
Embassy in New Delhi and the first-ever Resident
Ambassador of Mauritania to India also assumed
charge in this year.
India introduced e-Visa facility for Mauritanian ordinary
passport holders, promoting tourism and business
exchanges. An MoU on visa exemption for diplomatic
and official passport holders was implemented this
year, following Presidents’ visit in October 2024,
strengthening bilateral ties.

137.46 million. For the year, the bilateral trade
amounts to USD 150 million. Prominent business
personalities from Mauritania also attended the 20th
edition of CII India Africa Business Conclave, held in
Delhi on 27-29 August.

from MoFA attended the Professional Course for
Foreign Diplomats (PCFD) conducted by SSIFS, and
two candidates from Mauritania attended the ITEC
training courses.
India and Mauritania continued to work closely at
the multilateral fora and supported each other’s
candidatures to various UN and international bodies.
Niger
India and Niger maintained cordial relations and close
co-operation at the international fora and supported
each other when need arose. Niger has conveyed its
consent to become a member of International Big Cat
Alliance (IBCA), an initiative from India.
Total bilateral trade in the year 2024-25 stood at USD
105.60 million with exports from India at USD 72.68
million and imports from Niger at USD 32.92 million.
In this year, the bilateral trade amounted to USD 71
million.
India has continued to support Niger through various
capacity building programmes through ITEC and ICCR
scholarships. Niger was allocated 156 ITEC training
slots including 10 Defence Training Slots and five
ICCR Scholarships. ICCR has recently allocated six
additional Scholarship slots for this academic year.
Till date, 33 ITEC slots for civil training, seven Defence
training slots and seven ICCR Scholarship slots have
been utilised.
Nigeria
This year India and Nigeria continued to strengthen
the strong, multifaceted Strategic Partnership that
received fresh impetus from the State Visit of the Prime
Minister in November 2024. Cooperation in sectors
like space, renewable energy, defence, research &
development, maritime security and intelligence

sharing, health, agriculture and food security,
training & capacity building was further deepened.
Both countries continued to collaborate in various
multilateral fora including reciprocal support for each
other's candidatures at various UN/multilateral bodies.
In February, India Corner in the Library of American
University of Nigeria (AUN) in Yola, Adamawa was
inaugurated.
The bilateral trade between India -Nigeria reached
USD 7,132.72 million in 2024-25. In the current
year, the trade amounted to USD 6.3 billion. The
High Commission organised/participated in over
18 Business-to-Business (B2B) events including
Business-to-Business for CII’s multi-sector delegation
in Lagos, inaugural edition of India Trade Expo, Lagos
Chamber’s International Business Conference & Expo
2025, 20th Abuja International Trade Fair.
In this year, India and Nigeria deepened their long-
standing defence partnership through a series of high-
level engagements. Minister of State for Defence Bello
Mohammad Matawalle led a delegation to India in
August, for bilateral discussions with MoS (Defence).
Earlier in February, a Nigerian Air Force team led
by Air Marshal H. B. Abubakar participated in Aero
India. Nigerian Army officers, Major General Kevin
Aligbe and Maj Gen Ademola Adedoja, attended the
inaugural UN TCC Army Chiefs’ Conclave in October,
in New Delhi. Maritime ties also strengthened with
the operational deployment of INS Tushil to Nigeria
in January.
Training and capacity building remain central to the
defence partnership, with 83 ITEC Defence training
slots offered to Nigerian Armed Forces personnel
during the current year. ICCR offered 30 scholarships
under the ‘ICCR Africa Scholarship Scheme’ for
Nigerian students to pursue under-graduate, post-
graduate, and PhD courses in India. In this yera total
250 civilian training slots were allotted to Nigeria
under ITEC/e-ITEC.
In February, a 20-member Nigerian cultural troupe
participated in the 38th edition of Surajkund Craft Mela,
for the fourth time in a row. As part of Mission’s active
outreach in propagating diaspora Programmes, NRI
couple from the city of Port Harcourt, was amongst
the winners of Bharat Ko Janiye (BKJ) Quiz and went
on a 15-day Bharat Yatra including participation in
Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (PBD) Convention in January.
Republic of Congo (ROC)
Bilateral relations between India and Republic of
Congo (ROC) continued to strengthen during the
year. India is an important development partner of the
Republic of Congo.
A four-member delegation, led by Brigadier General
Ambroise Mopendza, Director General of Equipment,
visited Bengaluru on 9-13 February to participate
in ‘Aero India’ and ‘BRIDGE’. The delegation also
included Air Force Brigadier General Jean Baptiste
Philippe TCHICAYA, Air Force Chief of Staff.
In August, a delegation from Exim Bank, the National
Council for Cement and Building Materials and Promac
visited the ROC regarding the Greenfield 600 TPD
Rotary Kiln-based cement plant, financed through the
Government of India’s USD 55 million concessional
Line of Credit (LoC). The delegation undertook a site
visit to the cement plant on 5–6 August in Dolisie,
to review the ongoing progress. On 7 August, the
delegation met Minister of Industrial Development
and Private Sector Promotion Nicephore Antoine
Thomas Fylla Saint-Eudes.
During FY 2024-25, bilateral trade between India
and the ROC showed a significant upward trajectory.
The total trade increased from USD 298.42 million in
2023–24 to USD 548.58 million in 2024-25, marking
a growth of over 83 percent. For this year, the bilateral
trade amounted to USD 497 million.
India offered 10 slots (both Civilian & Defence) to
Congolese nationals under the ITEC programme for
the current year. ROC nominee attended the 10th
Edition of the National-Level Pollution Response
Exercise (NATPOLREX-25) at Chennai during 4-6
October. ROC has also utilised one ICCR scholarship
offered for the year 2025-26.

Republic of Guinea
On 7 April, Guinea signed the ‘Framework Agreement
on the establishment of the International Big Cat
Alliance (IBCA)’ and became the seventh country
to join it along with, Nicaragua, Eswatini, India,
Somalia, Liberia and Cambodia. A two-member
Guinean delegation led by Chief of Staff of Ministry
of Environment and Sustainable Development Dia
Balde, attended the first meeting of the Assembly
(the apex body) of IBCA which was held on 16 June,
in New Delhi.
A delegation led by Chief of Staff of Ministry of
Planning and International Cooperation Fatoumata
Toure participated in the 20th CII-Africa Business
Conclave on 27-29 August, in New Delhi. Advisor
to the Prime Minister in Charge of Trade, Industry,
Foresight and Financial Resource Mobilization Thierno
Illiassa Balde was also part of the delegation. India
offered assistance in digital public infrastructure,
agriculture, health and in other areas, allowing further
investment opportunities for Indian companies in
Guinea.
Bilateral trade in 2024-25 stood at USD 1.5 billion,
with the trade balance in India’s favour. In this year, the
bilateral trade amounts to USD 1.5 billion. Rice (other
than basmati), two and three wheelers, engineering
goods, drugs and pharmaceuticals are major exports
to Guinea, while gold, aluminum, pearls/stones/
jewellery, and cashew are main imports from Guinea.
This year, the locomotives for Guinea's ambitious
Simandou Project are being assembled in India.
India has offered USD 225.22 million of development
assistance through LoCs for different projects in
Guinea. These projects are under process. Additionally,
India offers capacity building through ITEC and
under Defence ITEC. ICCR scholarship for long term
studies is also offered on an annual basis. 15 Guinean
diplomats participated in the first Special Course for
Diplomats from Central and West African Countries
at organised by the Ministry at SSIFS, on 16-25 July. A
15-member cultural troupe from Guinea visited India
to participate in the 38th edition of Surajkund Art and
Craft Mela from 9 to 23 February.
Sao Tome & Principe (STP)
Bilateral relations between India and Sao Tome &
Principe (STP) continued to strengthen during the
year. STP continued to support India’s candidatures to
various posts in the UN and at multilateral fora.
In October, a two-member delegation from STP
attended the eighth Session of ISA Assembly held in
New Delhi. ISA is in the process of setting up a 50 kW
rooftop solar project at the Prime Minister’s Office in
Sao Tome.
India continued to provide support for capacity
building to STP. Diplomats from the Ministry of
Foreign Affairs, Cooperation and Communities of STP;
officers from the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and
Rural Development of STP; and auditors from the
Court of Auditors of STP attended various training
and executive courses under the ITEC programme
of the Ministry. Officers from the Coast Guard of STP
attended the National Pollution Response Exercise
(NATPOLREX), and the Maritime Law & Operations
Course conducted by the Indian Coast Guard this year.
The Minister of Health of STP inaugurated the 11th
International Day of Yoga which was organised at the
University of STP. The Minister of Environment, Youth
and Sustainable Tourism of STP and the Secretary
General of the Ministry of Education, Culture, Science
and Higher Education of STP participated in the event.
In January, India provided humanitarian medical
assistance of essential and life-saving medicines
for the main hospital in STP. In April, India gifted six
school buses to reinforce the school transport fleet of
STP and make school education more accessible.
In May, two content creators from STP visited India
under the familiarisation visit programme of content
creators, organised by the Ministry for C&WA
countries.
Senegal
The launch ceremony for the project for ‘Mine
Clearance for Development in Casamance’ was held

BWC Conference in December, in New Delhi.

USD 1740 million during 2024-25, registering over
10 percent growth in the volume of trade with Senegal
over the previous year. For this year, the bilateral trade

between

remained friendly and warm during the year. EAM met
Foreign Minister of Sierra Leone Timothy Musa Kabba
on the sidelines of the 80th UN General Assembly on
26 September.
An Indian All-Party Parliamentary Delegation visited
Sierra Leone in May. The Parliament of Sierra Leone
strongly condemned the Pahalgam attack and
observed a moment of silence in memory of the
victims. In November, India organised an exhibition
‘The Human Cost of Terrorism’ in November, in
Freetown.
The second FOC between India and Sierra Leone was
held in March, in New Delhi. It was co-chaired by

discussions on UN Security Council reforms in
Freetown.
A USD 990,000 project was launched under the
India–UN Development Partnership Fund to support
persons with disabilities in Sierra Leone, in May. In
October, India shipped 15 haemo-dialysis machines,
along with RO plants and consumables, as grant
assistance to help Sierra Leone address the rising

USD 408 million in 2024-25, with Indian exports

Under capacity building, a batch of 18 mid-level civil

Togo
The bilateral relations between the two countries
continued to grow across multiple sectors. Togo
supported India’s candidatures to the UN HRC for
the term 2026-2028 held on 14 October and the
Postal Operations Council (POC) and the Council of
Administration (CA) of the Universal Postal Union
(UPU) held from 6-20 September. Togo participated
in the International Conference on BWC in December,
New Delhi.
The Indian Naval Ship ‘Tushil’ undertook an operational
visit to Lomé on 10-11 January. Following the hijacking
incident involving the Panama-flagged vessel Mt. Bitu
River in March, the Togolese authorities extended their
full cooperation to the Mission by providing updates
on the developments.
In a significant development, Fertilisers and Chemicals
Travancore Ltd. (FACT) and Société Nouvelle des
Phosphates du Togo (SNPT) signed an agreement
in February for the sale and purchase of Togo’s
phosphate rock. The agreement further strengthens
bilateral economic ties between India and Togo and
contributes to mutual growth in the agricultural and
industrial sectors.
The Agreement on reciprocal Visa Exemption for
holders of Diplomatic, Official and Service passports,
that was signed on 27 June 2024, came into effect
on 15 April this year. MoU was signed between
the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR),
New Delhi, and the Togolese Institute of Agronomic
Research (ITRA), Togo on 11 September.
Between January and October, a total of 33
scholarships were utilised by Togo under ITEC civilian
and defence slots for officials and ICCR’s India-
Africa Maitri Scholarship Scheme and ICCR’s AYUSH
Scholar Scheme for students. One Togolese diplomat
participated in the 72nd Professional Course for Foreign
Diplomats (PCFD) organised by SSIFS from 19-30
May. The ITEC Day was celebrated on 28 March, with
participation of over 100 ITEC and ICCR alumni, senior
government officials and Secretary Genaral Ministry

guest.

held on 15 April, and was attended by the Minister of
Higher Education and Research of Togo as the Chief
Guest. More than 500 students explored academic
opportunities in India during the event. A 20-member
Togolese cultural troupe ‘Zogbeadji’ participated in
the 38th edition of the Surajkund International Crafts
Mela on 7-23 February.
East & South Africa
In this year, India continued to deepen its friendly
relations with countries in the East and Southern
African region. Continuous engagements with these
countries provided impetus to strengthen bilateral
cooperation in the fields of development partnership,
defence, trade and economy, agriculture, commerce,
art and culture, education, digital technology,
renewable energy, health and medical tourism, and
people-to-people exchanges.
The 20th edition of CII India-Africa conclave was
organised on 27-29 August, in New Delhi. It witnessed
high-level participation from East & Southern Africa
Countries.

Botswana
India and Botswana enjoy warm and time-tested
relations founded on shared values of democracy,
development, and mutual respect. The partnership
has continued to expand steadily across political,
economic, developmental, and cultural domains, with
this year marking several important initiatives that
underscore the growing dynamism of the bilateral
engagement.
Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji paid a historic State Visit
to Botswana at the invitation of the President of
Botswana Duma Gedeon Boko on 11-13 November.
It marked the first-ever visit by an Indian Head of
State to Botswana. The visit consolidated the warm
and friendly relationship that exists between the
two countries by opening new vistas of collaboration
in areas such as trade, capacity building, health,
education, renewable energy, diamond trade and
beneficiation and digital transformation. The visit
also helped deepen people-to-people connections
between the two countries.
A notable outcome of the State Visit was the agreement
on translocation of eight cheetahs presented by
Botswana to India under Project Cheetah, a flagship
conservation initiative of the Government of India.
Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji held talks with President of Botswana
Duma Gideon Boko in Gaborone, November 2025
On the economic front, bilateral trade and investment
linkages were further strengthened through the
visits of delegations from the Federation of Indian
Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) and the
CII. These engagements, organised in collaboration
with the Botswana Investment and Trade Centre
(BITC), brought together business leaders from key
sectors such as infrastructure, agriculture, water
management, food processing, health, and finance.
These visits provided an effective platform for
identifying new avenues for economic partnership and
investment under Botswana’s Vision 2036.
In the aftermath of the severe floods that struck parts of
Botswana, India extended HADR support amounting
to USD 50,000, consisting of essential medicines and
relief materials, reflecting India’s commitment to be
the first responder.
Burundi
The Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of National
Defence and Veterans Affairs participated in 15th
edition of Aero India in February, in Bengaluru.
India supported Burundi’s socio-economic growth
through LoC, scholarships under the ITEC programme,
and collaboration in sectors such as agriculture,
healthcare, education, and information technology.
Bilateral trade grew, particularly in pharmaceuticals,
machinery, and manufactured goods.
Eswatini
In December, Eswatini formally initiated the process
of opening its resident Mission in New Delhi. So far
India was concurrently accredited to the Embassy of
Eswatini in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.
Minister of Foreign Affairs of Eswatini Pholile
Shakantu, participated at the World Audio Visual &
Entertainment Summit (WAVES) in Mumbai on 1-4
May. During the visit, the Minister held a bilateral
meeting with EAM. This was the first ever visit of a
Foreign Minister of Eswatini ever since diplomatic
relations were established in 1970.

MoS (PM) visited Eswatini on 17-20 July, called on

of Ethiopia from the Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed
Ali. Earlier, both leaders had held a meeting on the
sidelines of the G20 Summit in Johannesburg.

Prime Minister met Prime Minister of Ethiopia Abiy Ahmed Ali in Addis Ababa, December 2025.

follows a ClI-led business delegation's visit to Ethiopia
on 19-21 February and meeting with the officials
of Ethiopian Ministries, the Ethiopian Investment
Commission, International Organisations and other
stakeholders to explore trade and investment
opportunities.
On 5 June, the African Union Commission joined the
Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI).
strengthening Africa's commitment to resilient
infrastructure. The announcement was made at a
high-level event in Geneva. Subsequently, CDRI held
a side event at the Africa Climate Summit, highlighting
the need for climate-resilient infrastructure. The event
featured the launch of the 'Infrastructure Resilience in
Africa' report, offering risk assessments and guidance
for key sectors.
On 11-12 June, a three-member delegation led
by Secretary (ER) visited Ethiopia for preparatory
meetings ahead of upcoming Fourth India-Africa
Forum Summit (IAFS-IV). The delegation held
constructive discussions with key stakeholders,
including the Chairperson and senior commissioners
of the African Union Commission, the Director General
of Africa CDC, the Executive Secretary of UNECA, the
Secretary General of the Organisation of Southern
Cooperation (OSC). Secretary (ER) held meetings
with Ethiopia's State Minister of Foreign Affairs and
discussed issues of mutual interests. A six-member
delegation from AU Commission participated in the
follow-up visit on the matters pertaining to IAFS-IV
held on 1-5 December, in New Delhi.

Agreement on Establishment of the International Big
Cat Alliance' in June, which aims to conserve seven
major big cat species: tigers, lions, leopards, snow
leopards, cheetahs, jaguars and pumas.
Kenya
Former Prime Minister of Kenya Raila Odinga passed
away in Kerala on 15 October, where he had been
undergoing medical treatment. India extended its full
support in facilitating expeditious repatriation of his
mortal remains. A high-level Kenyan delegation led
by Prime Cabinet Secretary and Cabinet Secretary
for Foreign and Diaspora Affairs Musalia Mudavadi,
travelled to India to accompany the mortal remains.
Governor of Kerala laid a wreath on behalf of the
Prime Minister. The mortal remains were accorded a
guard of honour at Kochi airport and flown from Kochi
to Mumbai by an Indian Air Force aircraft.
MoS (KVS) visited Kenya to attend the UN
Environmental
Assembly
(UNEA-7)
on
9-13
December. He met Kenyan Cabinet Secretary for
Environment Deborah Mlongo Barasa and Principal
Secretary for Tourism John Ololtuaa, along with
meetings with Environment Ministers of other
countries on the sidelines.
Minister of Women and Child Development met
Advisor to the President of Kenya on Women's Rights
Harriette Chiggai on 10 July, in New Delhi.
MoS (Defence) visited Kenya from 22 to 24 June.
Alongside Kenya's Cabinet Secretary for Defence,
he jointly unveiled the India-Africa Commemorative
Pillar at Taita Taveta to honour fallen Indian soldiers
of World War I.
At Aero India held in Bengaluru in February, Vice
Admiral held discussions with Vice Chief of the
Kenyan Defence Forces Lieutenant General John M.
Omenda focusing on maritime challenges, training,

A business delegation led by Federation of Indian
Export Organisations visited Bulgaria in June, and held
meetings with India-Bulgaria Business Chamber of
Commerce and various other major business groups.
ICCR sponsored Odissi dance troupe performed in
different Bulgarian cities namely, Kyustendil, Sofia,
Varna and Burgas from 13-17 August. World-
renowned Indian classical music troupe-Maharaj Trio
performed in various cities of Bulgaria like Pernik,
Sapareva Banya, Sofia and Plovdiv in September.
Croatia
2025 was a landmark year in the India-Croatia
relations. The first ever visit to Croatia by any Indian
Prime Minister took place on 18 June when he
visited Croatia at the invitation of Prime Minister
of Croatia Andrej Plenković. Both the leaders had
a comprehensive exchange of views on further
advancing bilateral relations, India-EU strategic
partnership and cooperation in multilateral fora. Prime
Minister met President of Croatia Zoran Milanović and
attended a ceremonial dinner hosted by Prime Minister
Andrej Plenković. During the visit, four agreements
were signed in the field of Agriculture, Science and
Technology, Cultural Exchange Programme and Hindi
Chair at the University of Zagreb.
Prime Minister met President of the Republic of Croatia Zoranc
Milanovic in Zagreb, June 2025.
On 22-23 April, Secretary (Commerce) paid an
official visit to Croatia and held bilateral talks with
State Secretary for Foreign Trade and Development,
Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs Zdenko
Lucić, and State Secretary at the Ministry of Economy
of Croatia Ivo Milatić.
Under the cultural exchange program between
India and Croatia, a six-member ICCR-Sponsored
Kathak group visited Croatia on 19-29 August, to
participate in the International Folklore Festival
Split and Spancirfest Festival Varazdin. The Group
had performances in the city of Split, Maria Bistrica,

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
188
Ludbreg, Varazdin, and Osijek with 10 performances
and three workshops attended by over 4,000 people.
Member
of
the
Croatian
Parliament
Zvonimir
Troskot, visited India from 10-20 December under
the Distinguished Visitors Programme of ICCR and
experienced India's political, institutional, cultural and
human dimensions.
Sandra Carić Herceg, journalist from Nacional
Weekly Magazine attended a familiarization visit to
India organized by XP Division from 28 October-6
November.
At the second WHO Global Summit on Traditional
Medicine held in New Delhi from 17-19 December,
the Prime Minister conferred the Prime Minister’s Yoga
Award upon Yogacharya Jadranko Miklec of Croatia,
in recognition of his outstanding contribution to the
promotion and development of Yoga.
Cyprus
Prime Minister paid an official visit to Cyprus on 15-16
June, the first visit by an Indian Prime Minister in over
two decades. During the visit, he held atête-à-tête
meeting with the Cypriot Prime Minister, delegation-
level talks, and a roundtable interaction with business
leaders from Cyprus and India. Prime Minister was
also conferred Cyprus’ highest civilian honour, the
"Grand Cross of the Order of Makarios III," by President
Nikos Christodoulides. A Joint Declaration on the
Implementation of the Comprehensive Partnership
was issued during the visit. Subsequently, India-
Cyprus Joint Action Plan (2025-2029) was approved
by EAM and Foreign Minister of Cyprus.
Foreign Minister of Cyprus Constantinos Kombos paid
an official visit to India on 29-31 October, marking the
first such visit by a Foreign Minister from the country
to India. During his visit, he met the EAM on 30
October and held delegation-level talks. The Ministers
reviewed progress on the implementation of the Joint
Action Plan 2025-29, envisaged under the Joint
Declaration issued during the Prime Minister’s visit to
Cyprus in June. During his visit, the Foreign Minister
Kombos participated in the 55th Sapru House Lecture
and delivered a keynote address titled “Cyprus and
the World” at the Indian Council of World Affairs.
The two Ministers also met on the sidelines of 80th
UNGA High-Level Week on 24 September, in New
York. Post the Pahalgam terror attack, Foreign Minister
Kombos had a telephonic conversation with EAM on
29 April where he condemned the terror attack and
expressed solidarity with India. The two Foreign
Ministers again held a telephonic conversation on 30
May and discussed ways to enhance cooperation, and
exchanged views on advancing EU-India relations,
especially in the context of Cyprus’ upcoming
Presidency of the EU Council.
Deputy Minister for Research, Innovation and Digital
Policy Nicodemos Damianou, attended the ICC
Global Business Summit 2025 along with a business
delegation on 18–20 September, in Mumbai.
A parliamentary delegation of the Republic of Cyprus
led by the President of the House of Representatives
Annita Demetriou, visited India on 24–28 November.
The delegation consisted of three Members of
Parliament from different parties and senior officials
from the House of Representatives of the Republic of
Cyprus. During the visit, President Demetriou called
on Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji, met Hon’ble Vice President,
EAM and Speaker of Lok Sabha. The delegation also
held meetings with the Chairman and members of the
Foreign Affairs Committee of Lok Sabha.
The Cypriot Parliamentary delegation led by President of the
House of Representatives of Cyprus Annita Demetriou met
EAM during their visit to India, November 2025.
The
Defence
and
Security
Cooperation
has
strengthened with the signing of a Bilateral Defence
Cooperation Programme (BDCP) for 2025 in Nicosia
on 23 January. A Cypriot delegation led by Anna
Aristotelous, Permanent Secretary of the Defence
title: mea_annual_report
creator: PDFium

text:
Europe & the European Union
189
Ministry of Cyprus, participated in Aero India 2025 in
Bengaluru on 10–14 February. A delegation led by
Secretary (Defence Production), Ministry of Defence,
along with defence PSUs, visited Cyprus from 11–13
September.
Greece
With Greece’s entry into the Security Council in
January, and as a follow up to a decision taken during
the visit of Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Hellenic
Republic George Gerapetritis to India on February,
the second round in February the second round of
consultations on UN and UNSC matters were held in
June in Athens.
The
inaugural
India-Greece
Maritime
Security
Dialogue was held on 11 December in Athens, Greece.
The Indian delegation was led by the Joint Secretary
(D&ISA) and the Greek delegation was led by Political
Director and Ambassador Andreas Fryganas, and
Head of the Task Force for UNSC, Minister of Foreign
Affairs, Maria Theofili.
Foreign Minister of Greece George Gerapetritis with EAM
during his official visit to India, February 2025.
Defence cooperation activities also continued with
110 strong IAF contingent participation in the Greek
multinational exercise INIOCHOS in April. Chief of
Air Staff, visited Greece on a bilateral visit from 23-
26 June. A bilateral naval exercise in the Eastern
Mediterranean was held with Greece during the
visit of INS Tamal in August. The new mechanisms
established as part of the collaboration between
SEV (Greece)-Indian Chamber of Commerce, to assist
entry of businesses in each others’ markets started
functioning.
Greece’s leading airline Aegean Airline and IndiGO
Airlines entered into a code share agreement on 15
September as part of the decision of the two airlines
to commence direct flights between the two countries
under the aegis of the Air Services Agreement signed
on 27 November 2017 between the Government of
India and the Government of the Hellenic Republic.
Principality of Liechtenstein
The India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership
Agreement (TEPA) signed in 2024, came into
effect on 1 October 2025. Liechtenstein is also a
member of European Free Trade Association (EFTA).
Foreign Minister of Liechtenstein Dominique Hasler
visited India for the inauguration of the EFTA Desk
on 10 February, and met the Minister of Finance
and the Minister of Commerce and Industry. She
again visited India on 19 March to participate in
the Raisina Dialogue and met with EAM on the
margins. Hereditary Prince Alois met MoS (IC), Skill
Development and Entrepreneurship, on 23 January
in Davos, Switzerland on the sidelines of World
Economic Forum (WEF).
Liechtenstein organized an investment promotion
event titled ‘From Agreement to Action’ to advance
the India–EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership
Agreement on 4 November. Liechtenstein’s Deputy
Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sabine Monauni
and the Ambassador of India to Switzerland
participated in the event.
Malta
The traditionally close and friendly relations between
India and Malta continued to gain momentum during
the year. This year marked the 60 years of the
establishment of diplomatic relations between India
and Malta.
High Commission of India in Valletta celebrated
60 years of India-Malta diplomatic relations at the
National Day celebrations on 31 January which was
attended by the President of Malta Myriam Spiteri
Debono and Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for
Foreign Affairs and Tourism Ian Borg.

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
190
A Rajasthani Folk Song and Dance Group, sponsored
by ICCR, performed on 7-8 August in Malta. An eight-
member Maltese troupe named Kantera participated
in the ninth India International Folk Festival from 29
September to 10 October, in India. This was the first
ever participation from Malta in Festivals in India
organised by ICCR.
President of Malta Myriam Spiteri Debono and Deputy Prime
Minister, Minister for Foreign Affairs and Tourism Ian Borg
participated in the celebrations commemorating 60 years of
India-Malta diplomatic relations, January 2025.
Malta hosted the UN Conference on National and
Regional Counter-Terrorism Strategies in March and
the High Commissioner represented India at the
conference.
The then Chief Justice of India represented India in
the 24th Commonwealth Law Conference held on
5-9 April in Malta. He also visited the IMO Maritime
Law Institute (IMLI) where two officers from India also
completed Masters courses.
For the first time, a Maltese diplomat joined the
Professional Course for Foreign Diplomats course at
the Sushma Swaraj Institute of Foreign Service. The
High Commission also facilitated academic exchanges
and collaborations between Universities in India and
Malta.
Focusing on technology, to harness the synergies
between India and Malta in ICT and Fintech sectors,
‘India Means Business 2.0’ event was organised on 12
March. In collaboration with the Coffee Board of India,
the High Commission of India in Valletta organized
an Indian Coffee Promotion event, on 11 June, with
participation of coffee importers from Malta and coffee
exporters from India.
The second edition of Indian Film Shows was
organised on 11-12 April in Valletta and on 6 June
in Gozo.
Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade of North Macedonia organized a reception commemorating the 30th anniversary of the
establishment relations in Skopje, December 2025.

text:
Europe & the European Union
191
North Macedonia
Bilateral relations between India and the Republic
of North Macedonia remained cordial and witnessed
further expansion during 2025, marked by exchanges
of greetings between leaders of both the countries. Both
countries continued to strengthen their engagement
through collaboration in trade, education, culture,
and information technology. Cultural exchanges and
participation in each other’s national events further
contributed to fostering people-to-people contacts
and mutual understanding.
India-North Macedonia celebrated the 30th anniversary
of the establishment of their diplomatic relations.
On this occasion, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
and Foreign Trade of North Macedonia organized a
reception on 18 December in Skopje.
Moldova
The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign
Affairs, Mihai Popsoi visited New Delhi on 17-19
March and met with EAM on the sidelines of Raisina
Dialogue.
Moldova’s ratification of the International Solar
Alliance on 4 August reflected growing alignment
on clean energy priorities. Economic cooperation
saw active expansion with focused engagement
on infrastructure, energy, technology and markets.
KEC International’s 400 kV Vulcănești–Chișinău
transmission line remained a major pillar of
collaboration, along with discussions on future Indian
participation in its inauguration.
Ambassador’s meetings with the Secretariat of
the Economic Council, Invest Moldova Agency and
the Chamber of Commerce and Industry helped
identify opportunities in pharmaceuticals, electronics,
automotive components, agro-processing, textiles and
renewable energy. Dialogues with the Ministries of
Energy, Economic Development and Digitalization and
Infrastructure advanced cooperation in clean energy,
digitization, logistics and sustainable development. A
key milestone was the entry of Moldovan apples into
the Indian market, helping diversify Moldova’s export
destinations. People-to-people ties and cultural
cooperation remained central to bilateral engagement.
Collaboration with leading universities strengthened
education partnerships and ensured student welfare.
Montenegro
Bilateral relations between the two countries further
deepened during the year 2025. The bilateral trade
has more than tripled in the Financial Year 2024-
2025. One Montenegrin professional has participated
in the ITEC capacity building training program in India
after a gap of five years. A CanSat and Model Rocket
making competition was organised in cooperation with
Montenegro Space Research on 12 October to foster
innovation and expand interaction with students in
Montenegro.
Romania
High-level engagements continued during the year
to reinforce strong diplomatic ties. EAM met the then
Foreign Minister Emil Hurezeanu 15 February on the
sidelines of Munich Security Conference and both
sides expressed intention to cooperate in sectors such
as connectivity, mobility and labour.
Minister of State for Commerce and Industry visited
Romania from 3-6 November for the Joint Committee
for Economic Cooperation (JCEC), and signed the
protocol for the JCEC. He met with Romanian Ministers
responsible for Labour, Infrastructure and EU Projects,
Energy, Economy, Foreign Affairs, as well as the
State Secretary for Transport and representatives of
Romanian business chambers.
Economic
engagement
also
expanded
across
multiple sectors such as IT, manufacturing, pharma,
energy, logistics and maritime cooperation. Business
interactions with Chambers of Commerce in Prahova,
Arad, Timiș, Brașov, Iași and Constanța highlighted
Romania’s regional potential and Indian investments
already generating employment. Port and logistics-
related meetings in Constanța strengthened supply
chain connectivity, while multiple B2B sessions

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
192
supported new partnerships in packaging, defence
components, healthcare, agri-trade, safety equipment
and EV battery manufacturing. Bilateral trade
remained strong at over USD 2.9 billion with scope
for further growth.
Serbia
Serbia is India’s important partner in the Balkans.
India-Serbia bilateral relations continued to strengthen
during the year. Both countries continued to support
each other at various multilateral fora including at the
United Nations and worked together to strengthen
multilateralism and the voice of Global South. The
Serbian Government celebrated the NAM day, for the
first time, on 1 September in the National Assembly
building in Belgrade where the Embassy of India also
participated.
A delegation from Serbia participated in the Aero
India show in February. New initiatives were taken to
improve bilateral relations in various areas through
trade, science and technology, education, culture and
tourism. For promoting Indian tourism, the Embassy of
India in Belgrade participated in the 46th International
Tourism Fair held at Belgrade in February. International
Schools Sports Organization (ISSO) India sent a
contingent of about 150 students for participation in
the ISF U-15 World School Gymnasiade at Zlatibor,
Serbia in April. Reputed Indian author Geetanjali
Shree was awarded Luna Virino award by the Serbian
Writers Association in Belgrade in September.
The Holy See
India attaches great importance to its friendly ties with
the Holy See. Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji visited the Holy
See to attend the funeral mass of Pope Francis on 26
April. Deputy Chairman Rajya Sabha led a delegation
comprising Deputy Chief Minister of Nagaland
attended the Solemn Ceremony of the Inauguration of
the Pontificate of Pope Leo XIV on 18 May. Archbishop
Paul Richard Gallagher, Secretary for Relations with
States met EAM on 17 July, in New Delhi.
Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji visited the Holy See to attend the
funeral mass of Pope Francis, April 2025
Slovenia
India and Slovenia share a warm and friendly
relationship marked by mutual trust and shared
values. The steadfast growth of bilateral partnership
is testimony to the importance attached in the
bilateral relation with Slovenia. India and Slovenia
have maintained steady bilateral trade relations in
recent years.
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of
Slovenia Tanja Fajon visited India from 16-18 March
to attend the Raisina Dialogue and held a bilateral
meeting with EAM. She also spoke with EAM on 29
April and reiterated Slovenia’s strong condemnation
of a brutal terrorist attack in Pahalgam and expressed
full solidarity.
The 10th session of the bilateral India-Slovenia Joint
Commission on Trade & Economic Cooperation (JCTEC)
was held at New Delhi on 25 November. The meeting
was chaired by the Joint Secretary, Department of
Commerce and Director General, Ministry of Foreign
and European Affairs of Slovenia Amb. Peter Japelj.
Both sides reviewed the multi-sectoral collaboration
between the two countries and charted a way forward
for deepening the partnership. On the sidelines of
JCTEC, an MoU was signed between Survey of India,
and the Surveying and Mapping Authority, Slovenia
on 27 November.

text:
Europe & the European Union
193
The 10th India-Slovenia FOCs were held in New Delhi
on 6 May Co-chaired by Secretary(West) and State
Secretary, Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs of
Slovenia Marko Stucin. State Secretary also called on
EAM on 6 May and discussed India’s strong bilateral
and multilateral partnership with Slovenia.
All Party Parliamentary delegation visited Slovenia
from 25-27 May following Operation Sindoor. The
delegates held meetings with the President of the
National Council, Chairperson of the Foreign Policy
Committee of the National Assembly, Member of the
India-Slovenia Parliamentary Friendship Group. They
also had Interaction with the President and members
of the Slovenian Association for International
Relations and Media Interaction with major Slovenian
newspapers and TV Channels.
The delegation conveyed India’s strong commitment
on zero tolerance against terrorism and national
consensus on this issue. The Slovenian side reaffirmed
its condemnation of terrorism as pure evil that cannot
be justified in any form.
The Embassy of India in Ljubljana in collaboration
with Slovenian Science Foundation and Ministry of
Foreign and European Affairs celebrated the First
ever Indian-Slovenian Science Festival on 25-26
September in Ljubljana. The event highlighted the
strong India-Slovenia collaboration in the field of
science, innovation, smart technologies and economy.
Indian-Slovenian origin NASA Astronaut Sunita
Williams attended the event virtually as its Honorary
Patron. The event saw the collaboration of multiple
stakeholders including Slovenian Ministries of Foreign
and European Affairs; Higher Education, Research and
Information System and IIT Kanpur from India.
Switzerland
The year marked a milestone in bilateral ties with the
entry into force of the India–EFTA (European Free Trade
Association, comprising of Switzerland, Liechtenstein,
Norway and Iceland) Trade and Economic Partnership
Agreement (TEPA) on 1 October, consolidating
economic engagement and broadening cooperation
in innovation, sustainability, and technology. The
entry into force of TEPA was commemorated at the
“Prosperity Summit” in New Delhi, hosted by Minister
of Commerce and Industry, and attended by Swiss
State Secretary for Economic Affairs Helene Budliger
Artieda.
Minister of Commerce and Industry paid an official visit
to Switzerland on 9–10 June at the invitation of Federal
Councillor Guy Parmelin, Swiss Minister for Economic
Affairs, Education and Research. Accompanied by a
100-member Indian business delegation, the Minister
participated in the Swissmem Industry Day, one of the
largest gatherings of the mechanical and electrical
engineering (MEM) sector. A roundtable with Swiss
technology
firms
highlighted
opportunities
in
advanced manufacturing, clean energy, and digital
solutions.
A high-level Indian delegation participated in the
World Economic Forum (WEF) Annual Meeting in
Davos from 20–24 January, including Union Cabinet
Ministers Minister of Railways, Information and
Broadcasting, Electronics and Information Technology,
Minister for Jal Shakti, Minister of Civil Aviations,
Minister of Food Processing Industries and MoS (Skill
Development and Entrepreneurship.) In addition,
Chief Ministers from the states of Andhra Pradesh,
Telangana and Maharashtra also participated.
EAM and Swiss Federal Councillor for Foreign Affairs
Ignazio Cassis held a telephonic conversation on 2
May, during which Cassis expressed condolences and
solidarity following the Pahalgam terrorist attack.
Institutional mechanisms continued to guide the broad-
based India–Switzerland partnership across political,
scientific, and environmental domain. The 13th Round
of FOC was held in Berne on 13 February, at Secretary
level, covering political, economic, and multilateral
cooperation. The seventh Joint Committee Meeting
(JCM) on Science and Technology was convened in
Berne on 1 September, co-chaired by Secretary (DST)
and Swiss State Secretary for Education, Research
and Innovation Martina Hirayama. The 4th Joint
Working Group on Climate Change and Environment
was held in New Delhi on 22 September, co-chaired

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
194
by Joint Secretary (MoEFCC,) and Swiss Ambassador
to India Maya Tissafi, to review cooperation in climate
mitigation, clean technologies, and circular economy
initiatives.
Principal Scientific Advisor to the Government of
India visited Switzerland from 13-16 October to
participate in the Geneva Science and Diplomacy
Anticipator (GESDA) Summit. He met Foreign Minister
Ignazio Cassis, the State Secretary for Foreign Affairs
Alexandre Fasel, and SERI State Secretary Martina
Hirayama.
State Secretary for Economic Affairs Helen Budliger
accompanied by a pharma and biotech delegation
visited New Delhi on 26 November and held a meeting
with Minister of Commerce and Industry.
Türkiye
As part of the strategic outreach, an International
Conference on ‘India-Türkiye Relations: Historical
and Contemporary Perspectives’ in collaboration
with Turkish Think-Tank the Foundation for Political
Economic and Social Research (SETA) and Indian
Think-Tank International Dialogue and Diplomacy
Foundation (IDDF) was organized at SETA, Ankara on
26-27 February. Deputy Foreign Minister of Türkiye
Amb. Berris Ekinci addressed the inaugural session
as the Keynote Speaker. The think tanks, which
participated in the Conference included IDDF, SETA,
Indian Council for World Affairs (ICWA), Observer
Research Foundation (ORF), Manohar Parrikar Institute
for Defence Studies and Analyses (MP-IDSA), Centre
for Strategic and Defence Research (CSDR), Centre for
West Asian Studies (CWAS), Centre for Global India
Insights (CGII), Vivekananda International Foundation
(VIF), as well as members of academia from Indian
and Turkish Universities. The members of the Indian
Think-Tank Delegation also met the Chairman of the
Foreign Affairs Commission of the Grand National
Assembly of Türkiye Fuat Oktay on 27 February.
The
India-Türkiye
economic
and
commercial
cooperation constitutes an important dimension of the
bilateral relations. In January, Indo-Türkiye Friendship
Association (ITFA) and T-Hub (Telangana Startup
Incubator Hub) signed an MoU aimed at strengthening
innovation, trade and investment in sectors like
technology, pharmaceuticals, and renewable energy.
In February, Foreign Economic Relations Board of
Türkiye (DEIK) delegation visited Mumbai to hold the
meetings with FICCI, IMC Chamber of Commerce
and Industry, Maharashtra Industry, Trade and
Investment Facilitation Cell, Exim Bank of India, All
India Association of Industries and IMC Bharat Calling
Conference. WTC Mumbai and DEIK-Türkiye-India
Business Council signed an MoU, which seeks to
enhance B2B engagements with Türkiye.
A delegation from the Engineering Export Promotion
Council (EEPC) visited Istanbul and Bursa in April
to hold meetings with DEIK, Istanbul Chamber of
Commerce (ITO) and Bursa Chamber of Commerce
and Industry (BTSO). EEPC also signed MoUs with
DEIK and BTSO.
A 35-member delegation led by Coffee Board of
India participated in COFFEX Istanbul in May and
a delegation of 37 companies from CHEMEXIL
participated in Beauty Istanbul 2025 in May. The
Mission participated at the 94th Izmir International
Fair in August, promoting Indian handicrafts, jewelry,
Ayurveda, Yoga and wellbeing. Separately, the Mission
participated in the ‘Incredible India’ campaign, and at
Antalya Tourism Fair, held in October were India was
a focus country.
25 Indian Companies participated in one of the world's
leading trade fairs for greenhouse, horticulture and
agricultural technologies, organised by Informa
Markets at Antalya International Fair and Congress
Center (ANFAŞ) from 18-21 November
Türkiye issued a statement to condemn the terrorist
attack in Pahalgam, J&K on 22 April. Subsequently,
following Operation Sindoor, the Ministry of Foreign
Affairs of Türkiye issued a statement on 7 May calling
India’s response provocative and supported Pakistan’s
call for an investigation of the Pahalgam terror attack.
Türkiye also issued a statement, welcoming the
ceasefire on 10 May.
A bust of Mahatma Gandhi was installed in the
Embassy complex on the occasion of Mahatma Gandhi
Jayanti on 2 October.

text:
Europe & the European Union
195
Denmark
During the year 2025, bilateral relations between
India and Denmark continued to evolve under the
framework of ‘Green Strategic Partnership’ announced
in 2020. In 2025, India’s bilateral political outreach
to Denmark was also guided by the importance of
Denmark as a non-permanent member of the United
Nations Security Council (2025-26) and its Presidency
of the Council of the European Union during the
second half of the year.
Prime Minister held two telephonic conversations with
Prime Minister of Denmark Mette Frederiksen on 15
April and 16 September. EAM visited Denmark from
20-21 May. EAM called-on Prime Minister Frederiksen
and Speaker of the Danish Parliament Søren Gade.
During these meetings, the two sides discussed the
developments under the Green Strategic Partnership.
Both sides also discussed regional and international
developments of mutual interest. EAM met with
Foreign Minister of Denmark Lars Løkke Rasmussen,
and took stock of bilateral relations and discussed
the ways to strengthen the ties further. EAM also met
Minister of Industry, Business and Financial Affairs of
Denmark Morten Bødskov, to deliberate on the ways
to foster bilateral trade and investment.
EAM called-on Prime Minister of Denmark Mette Frederiksen
during his visit to Denmark, May 2025.
Following
Operation
Sindoor,
an
All-Party
Parliamentary Delegation visited Copenhagen from
29-31 May. The delegation was received in the
Danish Parliament by Deputy Speaker and Member
of the Presidium of the Parliament Lars Christian
Brask. Chairman of the Foreign Policy Committee of
the Danish Parliament Christian Friis Bach, called on
the All Party Delegation. The Indian delegation also
met a group of former Ministers, parliamentarians
and officials. During these meetings, the All Party
Delegation
conveyed
the
message
of
India's
unwavering stance against terrorism and its resolve to
obliterate every trace of it.
Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways paid an
official visit to Denmark on 5-6 June and met the
Danish Minister of Industry, Business and Financial
Affairs Morten Bødskov. The two ministers reviewed
the robust bilateral maritime cooperation under
the auspices of the Green Strategic Partnership
and the bilateral MoU on Maritime Issues signed in
September 2024. During the visit, Letter of Intent
on Cooperation between the National Maritime
Heritage Complex (NMHC) and Maritime Museum
of Denmark, Helsingor was also signed. During the
year, there were ministerial-level visits by the state
government delegations of Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh
and Rajasthan.
The eighth round of India-Denmark FOC was held on
17 November in New Delhi, co-chaired by Secretary
(West) and State Secretary for Foreign Policy of the
Royal Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs Lotte Machon.
Economic and commercial ties have continued on
an even level. The bilateral trade in goods and
services was around USD 6 billion in 2024. Over 200
Danish companies have business presence in India,
contributing to sectors such as shipping, renewable
energy, pharmaceuticals, and agri-food. Several
of these companies have built their manufacturing
facilities in India, thus creating jobs, fostering
technology transfer and reinforcing India’s ‘Make in
India’ initiative. During its Presidency of the Council
of the European Union in the second half of 2025,
Denmark remained committed to the early conclusion
of the India–EU Free Trade Agreement.

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
196
The fourth Joint Committee Meeting for cooperation in
Science & Technology, seventh Joint Working Group
Meeting on Power, first Joint Working Group Meeting
on Migration & Mobility and sixth Joint Working Group
Meeting on Maritime Cooperation were held during the
year. Denmark also participated as a Partner Country
in the India Maritime Week 2025 held in Mumbai from
27-31 October.
Finland
India and Finland share warm and friendly ties rooted
in common values and commitment. The telephonic
conversations between Prime Minister and Finnish
President Alexander Stubb on April 16 and 27
August, and their interaction in the margins of the G20
Leaders’ Summit in South Africa in October, have given
a new momentum to our bilateral political relations.
On 30 August, EAM had a telephonic conversation
with Finnish Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen, focusing
on the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
The 13th round of India-Finland Foreign Office
Consultations was held in Helsinki on 6 November,
co-chaired by Secretary (West) and Permanent
State Secretary of Finland Jukka Salovaara. Secretary
(West) also called on Minister of Employment of
Finland Matias Marttinen, on 6 November to discuss
avenues of mobility of talent.
Finland, with over 100 companies operating in India
and investments exceeding USD 4 billion, remains
committed not only to the early conclusion of the

Mumbai in 2024, underscores Finland’s continued

to explore the vast opportunities that India offers.
This year also saw broadening of the bilateral
cooperation in the technology sector with Team
Finland-India participating in the Startup Mahakumbh
2025 and the Karnataka government delegation
visiting Helsinki in September to attract Finnish
companies in the tech sector. In recent months, there
has been a growing interest among Finnish companies
in emerging technologies such as quantum computing
and space technology. Finnish firms specializing in
quantum technologies, including IQM, Quantrol, and
Semicon, are actively participating in India’s National
Quantum Mission, reflecting deepening technological
collaboration between the two countries. Similarly,
the bilateral collaboration in 6G between the Bharat
6G Alliance and Finnish universities, particularly
through the University of Oulu’s 6G Flagship program,
is playing a pivotal role in advancing next-generation
communication technologies.
In the field of education, especially under the
New Education Policy, Finland has emerged as an
important partner for Indian schools. In March, 72
primary teachers from Punjab underwent a 3-week
training at the University of Turku. From 22 April to
3 May, Sikkim’s Education Minister led a delegation
to Finland to study its education system and explore
opportunities for collaboration.
Finnish engagements with the Indian think tank
community continued with the Finnish Ambassador
for Arctic affairs participating in the Arctic Circle India
Forum 2025 held on 3-4 May.
Iceland
India and Iceland bilateral relations witnessed great
momentum in 2025 with increased engagements.
On 2 January, EAM met former President of Iceland
and Chairman of the Arctic Circle Ólafur Ragnar
Grímsson, in New Delhi. The Arctic Circle India Forum
was held on 4-5 May in New Delhi in which EAM
participated in a panel discussion along with Ólafur
Ragnar Grímsson. Former Prime Minister of Iceland
and Chair of the Polar Dialogue, Katrin Jakobsdóttir
also travelled to India for the same.
Iceland hosted the second India-Nordic Dialogue
on 4-5 September for which MoS (KVS) visited
Reykjavik. He held a meeting with Foreign Minister of
Iceland Þorgerður Katrín Gunnarsdóttir and delivered
the inaugural address at the Dialogue. Additional

speaker from the Indian side.

Dialogue in Reykjavik, September 2025.

Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas visited Iceland
on 11 July. This was the first Cabinet Minister to visit
Iceland since 2011. Minister held a meeting with
the Foreign Minister of Iceland Þorgerður Katrín, and
interacted with Icelandic companies in the renewable
energy space.
In the context of signing of India-EFTA-TEPA, the
Commerce Secretary and Special Secretary visited
Iceland on 23 June. Secretary, Department of Fisheries,
visited Iceland from 10-12 September to explore the
opportunities for cooperation in the fisheries sector.

Martin Eyjólfsson visited India and held meetings
with Minister of Commerce and Industry on the
sidelines of the inauguration of the India-EFTA desk
for implementation of TEPA. He also attended India
Energy Week 2025. The India-EFTA Prosperity
Summit was organised on 1 October in New Delhi to
mark the coming into force of the India-EFTA TEPA.
On 21 July, a team of 9 scientists from National Centre
for Polar Research (NCPOR), Goa undertook a 15 day
research expedition from Reykjavik, Iceland to the east
Greenland Sea.
A team of 9 scientists from National Centre for Polar Research
(NCPOR), Goa undertook a 15 day research expedition from
Reykjavik, Iceland to the east Greenland Sea, July 2025.
Norway
The political relationship was consistently guided by
engagements including at high levels throughout the
year. Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide visited India in
March for participation in the Raisina Dialogue 2025
and met EAM on the margins.
Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways visited
Norway on 1-4 June with an Indian shipping delegation
which had installed a pavilion at the Nor Shipping
event. Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas visited
Oslo and met Norwegian companies working in the
areas of oil and gas industry and renewable energy,
on 7-8 July.
From 27–30 October, a delegation led by Norwegian
Minister of Fisheries and Ocean Policy, Marianne
Sivertsen Næss, visited Mumbai to attend the India
Maritime Week 2025. Norwegian Minister of Health
and Care Services Jan Christian Vestre visited India
in November to participate in the Bengaluru Tech
Summit.
Bilateral trade and investment ties are expected to
get a boost through the India-EFTA-TEPA. Norway's
Government Pension Fund Global (GPFG), which is
valued at approximately USD 2 trillion, has invested
around USD 32 billion in the Indian capital market, and
cumulative Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) inflows
from Norway stood at only USD 880 million. Over 148
Norwegian companies are registered in India, with
approximately 130 active in sectors like hydropower,
renewable energy, food processing, and IT services.
Indian IT majors like TCS, Infosys, and Wipro have also
established reciprocal investments in Norway.
A delegation led by Joint Secretary of the National
Security Council Secretariat (NSCS) attended the
Arctic Frontiers Conference at Tromsø from 29
January- 7 February, focusing on enhancing India's
participation in Arctic Council Working Groups and
strengthening polar research. In the space domain,
ISRO continues to utilize Norway’s Svalbard ground
station commercially, and this collaboration will
continue to deepen further with ISRO’s hosted
antenna, set up by KSAT in Svalbard.
The Inaugural India-Norway Maritime Security,
Disarmament and Non-Proliferation Dialogue was
launched on 11 September. To take forward the
sector-specific cooperation, the meetings of Joint Task
Force on Blue Economy, Joint Working Group (JWG)
on Science and Technology, JWG on Maritime Matters
and JWG on Education were held.

Sweden
India and Sweden have had longstanding close
relations based on common values and strong business,
investment and R&D linkages. The relationship was
guided by high-level ministerial interactions. Foreign
Minister of Sweden Maria Malmer Stenergard visited
India in March to participate in the Raisina Dialogue
and held meetings with EAM and the Minister of
Commerce and Industry. She also participated in
a meeting between Indian and Swedish business
leaders within the framework of the “India Sweden
Business Leaders Roundtable”. The meeting also
witnessed the signing of a MoU by representatives
from Ericsson, Volvo Group, and Bharti Airtel.
Minister of Commerce and Industry along with a
high level business delegation, visited Stockholm on
11-12 June, during which 21st session of the India-
Sweden Joint Commission for Economic, Industrial
and Scientific Cooperation was held. He also
participated in the India-Sweden High-Level Trade
and Investment Policy Forum at the Confederation
of Swedish Enterprises. Ministerial-level delegations
from the State Governments of Maharashtra, Uttar
Pradesh, Gujarat and Jharkhand visited Sweden.
Parliamentary
exchanges
received
an
impetus
with the visit of Swedish Members of Parliament
representing India-Sweden Friendship Group in
Swedish Parliament in March. From 7-14 June, a
delegation from the Election Commission of India
led by the then Chief Election Commissioner visited
Sweden to attend the high-level session celebrating
the 30th Anniversary of International Institute for
Democracy and Electoral Assistance.
The 27th edition of India Trilateral Forum (ITF) was
held on 6-7 October in Stockholm, Sweden. The ITF is
a closed-door, track 1.5 conference, bringing together
senior policy makers, top strategic experts, academia
and companies from India, Europe and the US. It
was attended by Swedish National Security Adviser
Niclas Kvarnström as Keynote Speaker and Additional
Secretary, (Northern Europe Division) as a panel
speaker from the Indian side. The event was also
attended by representatives of the Ministry of Foreign
Affairs of Sweden, France, Germany, Czech Republic
and Netherlands and of the European Commission.
The 12th India Sweden Innovation Day (ISID) was
organised in Stockholm on 29 September with the
theme of ‘Co-Creating a Sustainable Future: Scaling
Innovation Through Partnership’. Opening remarks
were delivered by Minister of Road Transport and
Highways virtually and State Secretary to the Minister
for Energy, Business and Industry, Swedish Ministry of
Climate and Enterprise Sara Modig.
To take forward the sector-specific cooperation,
meetings of Joint Working Groups on Environment
and Defence Cooperation and Sustainable Urban
Development were held. Under the India-Sweden
joint global initiative, Leadership Group for Industry
Transition (LeadIT 2.0) aimed at decarbonization
of hard to abate sectors, India-Sweden Industry
Transition Partnership (ITP) Summit 2.0 was held on
7 May in Stockholm. From 30 October- 1 November,
State Secretary in Ministry for Energy, Business and
Industry of Sweden Sara Modig, visited India with a
focus to deepen collaboration in the areas of trade
& investment, innovation, sustainability and green
transition.
In 2025, the bilateral trade and investment ties
between India thrived and business linkages continued
to expand. Around 280 Swedish companies remain
active in India including Ericsson, Spotify, Truecaller,
Volvo, Scania, Sandvik, AstraZeneca, Tetra Pack, IKEA,
HandM and SAAB. Reciprocally, nearly 70 Indian
companies are present in Sweden. Sweden remains
supportive of the early conclusion of India-EU-FTA.
On 14 September, Namaste Stockholm, a day-long
celebration of Indian culture, took place in Stockholm.
The event featured Indian dance, music, yoga,
delicious cuisine, and beautiful handicrafts. This year's
event was inaugurated by Swedish Culture Minister
Parisa Liljestrand.
Estonia
The India-Estonia bilateral relations remained cordial
and friendly. On 11 February, Prime Minister met
Estonian President Alar Karis on the sidelines of the
Al Summit in Paris.

India's relations with Lithuania progressed steadily

Political Director in the Lithuanian Ministry of Foreign
Affairs Laimonas Talat-Kelpša, attended the Raisina

Lithuanian Vice Foreign Minister Julius Pranevičius
led the delegation of Lithuanian Laser Association

During the India Maritime Week 2025 in October, a

Bosnia and Herzegovina
India and Bosnia and Herzegovina maintained friendly
relations, setting a positive trajectory as both nations
mark the 30th anniversary of diplomatic ties in 2025.
The two countries have a lot in common such as

consultations and high level engagements have
yielded an understanding of mutual perspectives
