Czech Republic
India and the Czech Republic relations continued to
develop through visits and official engagements.
A Czech Parliamentary delegation led by Vice
Presidents of the Senate of the Parliament of the Czech
Republic, Jitka Seitlova and Jiri Oberfalzer visited India
from 9-13 December and met Deputy Chairperson of
Rajya Sabha, and Chairman of the Standing Committee
on Tourism, Culture and Transport.
The eighth round of FOC was held in New Delhi on
15 January.
A 16-member high-level delegation from National
Defence College (NDC), India visited Czech Republic
for a foreign study tour on 9-13 June.
The seventh edition of India-Czech Joint Defence
Committee (JDC) was held in Prague on 7 October. On
8 October, India-Czechia Defence Industry Seminar
was also held on the margins of JDC. The first-ever
India Pavilion was set up at the International Defence
and Security Technologies Fair (IDET) in Brno from
28-30 May. An Indian Pavilion was set up by the

at the MSV International Engineering Fair held in Brno

Hungary
Relations between India and Hungary continued on
an upward trajectory through the year. Minister of
Foreign Affairs and Trade of Hungary Péter Szijjártó,
visited New Delhi to attend Raisina Dialogue in March
and met EAM, Commerce and Industry Minister,
Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas and Minister
of Civil Aviation on the margins. Discussions were
focused on furthering the bilateral cooperation in the
areas of trade and investment, air connectivity, green
hydrogen and civilian nuclear energy.
A four-member delegation led by the Speaker of
Uttar Pradesh Legislative visited Hungary from 11-14
October and met Hungarian Parliamentarians.
India-Hungary space cooperation reached new
heights with both countries jointly sending astronauts
to the International Space Station through a landmark
private mission facilitated by Axiom Space and
SpaceX.
Poland
India and Poland share a long-standing friendly
relationship, which was elevated to a strategic
partnership during Prime Minister’s official visit to
Poland in August 2024.
In fulfillment of the Prime Minister's announcement
during his official visit to Poland in August 2024, the
first visit of a 20-member Polish youth delegation to
India was organized from 19-27 February under the
Jamsaheb Memorial Youth Exchange Programme. The
youth group visited the Balachadi and Valivade camps
in Jamnagar and Kolhapur respectively where Polish
children and evacuees lived for several years in the
1940s. They also called on EAM and the Minister of
Youth Affairs and Sports, during the visit.
Chairman of the Foreign Affairs Committee of the Sejm
(lower House of Polish Parliament) Pawel Kowal,
visited India leading a Parliamentary delegation of six
MPs from 7 to 13 February.
The 11th round of India-Poland Foreign Office
Consultations was held on 1 December in New
Delhi, co-chaired by Secretary (West) and Secretary
of State, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Poland, W. T.
Bartoszewski.
India and Poland continued strengthening their
economic relations with bilateral trade reaching
close to USD 6 billion, registering a growth of over
200 percent in the last decade. Indian investments
in Poland are close to USD 3 billion whereas Polish
investments in India are worth nearly USD 1 billion.
Lieutenant General Marek Sokołowski, General
Commander of the Polish Armed Forces led a three-

Foreign Minister of Slovak Republic Juraj Blanár

several senior functionaries of the government and

Foreign Minister had a meeting with EAM during his
visit. He also inaugurated the Honorary Consulate of
Slovakia in Kolkata on 20 March.
Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji with Prime Minister of the Slovak

Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji visited Slovakia on 9-10 April.

Andorra
India and Andorra continue to share cordial and
friendly relations since the diplomatic relations were
established in 1994.
Bilateral trade between India and Andorra stood at
USD 3.24 million in 2024, with indian exports at USD
3.15 million. It included textiles and garments, spirits
and precious and semi-precious stones. Similarly for
the year 2025 (January to September), trade between
the two countries reached USD 3 million with nearly
all trade being exports from India to Andorra.
Around 140 Indians/PIOs live in Andorra. The Indian
community has been in Andorra since the 1970s
starting mainly as businesspersons selling electronic
goods and diversifying to other areas later.
Belgium
India and Belgium share a close bilateral relationship
which over the decades, has developed into robust
and multifaceted partnership that spans a wide
range of sectors from trade and investment to science
and technology, from healthcare and clean energy
to sustainable growth, research and innovation,
education, culture, and people-to-people exchanges.
This year has seen a positive and forward-looking
trajectory in bilateral relations, marked by several
high-level engagements and exchanges.
High-level engagements
On 27 March, Prime Minister held a conversation with
King Philippe of Belgium, as a follow up to the Belgian
Economic Mission.
Princess Astrid led a second Economic Mission (last
mission was in 2013) from 1-8 March to India. She
was accompanied by the Deputy Prime Minister and

Minister of Foreign Affairs, the Minister of Defence
and Foreign Trade and the Minister President
Flanders Region. The Economic Mission had over
330 participants and comprised 147 companies, 6
chambers of commerce, 9 academic institutions and
18 public sector organisations. During the Mission, 38
MoUs were signed across various sectors including
life sciences, defence, renewable energy, academic
collaborations and digital innovation. During her visit,
the Princess called on the Prime Minister and also met
with Ministers of Defence, Commerce and Industry,
Electronics and Information Technology and NSA.
EAM also had a bilateral meeting with the Deputy
Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of
Belgium, and also met with Princess Astrid and the
accompanying the official delegation.
EAM visited Brussels from 9-11 June, and held a
bilateral meeting with Belgian Deputy Prime Minister
and Foreign Minister Maxime Prevot on 9 June. During
this visit he also called on Belgian Prime Minister and
King Philippe on 10 June. The Minister of Commerce
and Industry also visited Brussels in January and May.
A nine-member all-party Parliamentary delegation
visited Brussels from 3-5 June to convey India’s strong
national consensus and resolute approach to combating
terrorism in all its forms and manifestations. They met
with the President of Chamber of Representatives and
members of Belgian Parliament and also interacted
with think-tanks, media and members of the Indian
community.
Institutional/Dialogue Mechanisms
The third Foreign Office Consultations were held in
Brussels on 4 November, co-chaired by Secretary
(West) from the Indian side and the Secretary General
of the Belgian Ministry of Foreign Affairs from the
Belgian side.
Trade and Investment
India-Belgium bilateral trade amounted to USD
12.91 billion in 2024-25. Major Indian exports
include precious metals and stones, chemicals,
and base metals, while key imports are precious
metals and stones, base metals, chemicals, textiles,
and machinery. Trade in diamonds is a significant
component of bilateral trade. FDI inflows to India, from
April 2000 to March 2025, amounted to USD 4.023
billion, positioning Belgium as a significant contributor
to India’s FDI.
European Union
This year witnessed unprecedented momentum
in India–European Union relations, marked by the
landmark visit of the College of Commissioners to
New Delhi and a series of high-level engagements
that underscored a shared commitment to deeper
partnership. The India-EU Strategic Partnership was
further strengthened with intensified interactions
at all levels and closer cooperation in the areas of
trade, technology, defence, security, mobility and
connectivity. The period saw the second Ministerial
meeting of the India-EU Trade and Technology
Council, the first-ever Strategic Dialogue between the
EAM and the EU High Representative/Vice-President
(HRVP), as well as the inaugural visit of the Political
and Security Committee to India representing all EU
member states.
High-level engagements
President of the European Commission Ursula von
der Leyen led the EU College of Commissioners for
a landmark visit to India on 27-28 February and
met Prime Minister. Prime Minister met President of
the European Council Antonio Costa and President
von der Leyen on the sidelines of the G7 Summit in
Kananakis, Canada on 10 June. Prime Minister also
had telephone conversations with President Antonio
Costa on 7 January, together with both the EU leaders
on 4 September and with President von der Leyen on
17 September.
There have been regular Ministerial-level interactions
with the EU. EAM visited Brussels in June and
co-chaired the first India EU Strategic Dialogue
with EU High Representative and Vice President
(HRVP) Kaja Kallas. During the visit, EAM called on
President von der Leyen, President of the European
Parliament, and met European Commissioners for

European Parliament (MEPs) from the Delegation for
Relations with India (D-IN), the Committee on Foreign
Affairs (AFET), and the Committee on Security and

manifestations.

Maros Sefcovic’s visited India in December and had

Institutional Dialogue Mechanisms
These include the Strategic Partnership Review
Meeting (in Brussels, November 2025), Foreign Policy
and Security Consultations (in Brussels, November
2025), Inaugural edition of Space Dialogue (in Brussels,
November 2025), Dialogues on Migration and Mobility
(New Delhi, November 2025), Counterterrorism
(Brussels, September 2025), Maritime Security (New
Delhi, March 2025), Cyber (New Delhi, March 2025),
and the Joint Working Group on Agriculture (Brussels,
May 2025).
Further, a delegation of the Society of Indian Defence
Manufacturers visited Brussels in December and met
EU Commissioner for Defence and Space Andrius
Kubilius.
Key highlights
The visit of EU College of Commissioners to India
enabled
a
whole-of-government
approach
to
strengthening bilateral relations across domains. 20
ministerial meetings were held and the outcomes were
presented to the leaders and reflected in the February
Leaders’ Statement. The second India-EU Trade and
Technology Council (TTC) was also held during the
college visit during which the two sides agreed to
work in the fields of Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI),
e-signatures, semiconductor supply chains, AI, 6G,
joint research cooperation focusing on areas of EV

hydrogen, market access, screening of Foreign Direct

and Technology Council between India and EU is
an important platform for India for anchoring the

importance like Semiconductors, quantum computing,
AI, Green energy and resilient supply chains. This is
the first such mechanism for India with any partner
and the second for the EU after its TTC with the USA.
Subsequent to the College visit, EU published a new
India – EU Strategic Agenda in September outlining
concrete steps to further bilateral cooperation

strengthen under key pillars of prosperity and

and defence, connectivity and global issues, and

on the Free Trade Agreement, six rounds on the

Trade
India and the European Union continued to remain
robust trading partners. Bilateral trade in goods during
FY 2024-25 stood at USD 135.7 billion of which
Indian exports amounted to USD 75.7 billion and the
EU’s exports stood at USD 59.9 billion, making EU
India’s largest trading partner in goods as a bloc. In
addition, the India–EU bilateral trade in services in
2023 stood at approximately USD 65 billion, up 17
percent compared to 2022 and with a balance of USD
8.5 billion in India’s favour.
France
India and France have a long-standing Strategic
Partnership, established in 1998. France has been one
of India’s most trusted partners, not only in Europe but
globally. Both countries enjoy an exceptionally strong
and multifaceted bilateral cooperation, which extends
to close consultations on global and regional matters.
The India France Strategic Partnership continues to
grow with deep-rooted trust and confidence in each
other, consistency and strength, strong belief in
sovereignty and strategic autonomy, which have paved
the way for cooperation and collaboration in areas of
strategic domain such as defence, space, civil nuclear
energy, and critical and emerging technologies.
High-Level Exchanges
On 10-12 February, at the invitation of the President
of the French Republic, Emmanuel Macron, the Prime
Minister paid a visit to France to co-chair the AI Action
Summit, hosted by France. This was Prime Minister’s
sixth visit to France, and follows President Macron’s
visit to India in January 2024 as the Chief Guest for
the 75th Republic Day of India. Both countries signed
the India-France Declaration on Artificial Intelligence.
The leaders participated in India-France CEO Forum,
travelled to Marseille to jointly inaugurate India’s
Consulate General in Marseille and concluded key
agreements/MoUs in the domains of civil nuclear
energy, AI, Innovation, and development cooperation.
Both leaders met on the sidelines of the G7 Summit
in Kananaskis, Canada, on 17 June and maintained
regular contact over telephone calls, as on 21 August
and 6 September. Prime Minister met President Macron
on the sidelines of the G20 Summit in Johannesburg,
South Africa in November.
EAM made an official visit to France from 11-14 June
during which he held discussions with the French
Foreign Minister and called-on President Macron.
During the visit, he also inaugurated the first edition
of the Mediterranean Edition of Raisina Dialogue
in Marseille on 12-13 June, together with French
Foreign Minister Jean Noel Barrot. On 21 February,
on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Minister’s
meeting in Johannesburg, South Africa, EAM met
with his counterparts from Australia and France,
giving an impetus to India-France-Australia trilateral
cooperation. EAM met with the French Foreign
Minister on the sidelines of the G7 Foreign Ministers
meeting in Niagara in Canada in November.
The Minister of Commerce and Industry Minister
visited Paris on 3-4 June to attend the WTO Ministerial
Meeting. Minister of Earth Sciences visited Nice from
9-13 June to participate in the third United Nations
Ocean Conference. Minister of State of Electronics and
Information Technology visited France from 10-13
June to attend the 9th edition of Vivatech. The Principal
Secretary to the Prime Minister, visited Nice on 6-7
June to co-chair the seventh International Conference
on Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (ICDRI). Minister
of Culture and Tourism visited France on 26-28
September. From France, the French Minister to the
Minister of State, Minister of the Interior François-Noël
Buffet, visited India on 23 April, to jointly inaugurate the

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
206
second edition of 2025 MILIPOL India. On 20 January,
both sides also held the Foreign Office Consultations
at the level of Foreign Secretary in Paris.
Parliamentary Exchanges
A delegation of French Senators from the Senate’s
Committee of Foreign Affairs and Defence visited New
Delhi, Bangalore, and Mumbai from 18-25 May. The
delegation expressed solidarity with India in the fight
against terrorism, as the visit took place immediately
after the Operation Sindoor in May. This was
followed by the nine member all-party Parliamentary
delegation which visited Paris from 25-27 May, and
met with India-France Friendship Groups, as well
as the Committee on Foreign Affairs and Defence in
both the French National Assembly and Senate. They
interacted with think-tanks, media and members of
the Indian community. In all these engagements, the
French side expressed their support to India in the
fight against terrorism.
Defence Cooperation
France is among our trusted partners in Defence
collaboration with wide ranging cooperation across
the air, land and naval domains comprising industry
collaborations, technology transfer and regular
exchanges. The year 2025 continued to witness
growth in bilateral defence cooperation with a range
of activities including key agreements, bilateral
military exercises, staff-level talks, bilateral visits and
training exercises.
On 15 January, the sixth submarine of the P75
Scorpene-class
project,
INS
Vaghsheer,
was
commissioned in the Indian Navy. An Inter-
Governmental Agreement between India and France
for the procurement of 26 Rafale Marine aircrafts for
the Indian Navy, was signed on 28 April.
During the year, Chief of Army Staff visited France
from 24-27 February, and the French Chief of Army
Staff Gen. Pierre Schill visited New Delhi to participate
in the United Nations Troop Contributing Countries
Chiefs’ Conclave on 13 October.
Bilateral Naval Exercise, “VARUNA” was held from
19-22 March in the Arabian Sea. The bilateral Army
Exercise, “SHAKTI” was conducted in France from 18
June – 1 July. The Indo-French bilateral Air Exercise,
“GARUDA” was held in France on 16-27 November.
French Carrier Strike Group made port call in Goa and
Kochi from 3-9 January. There were also a number
of other port calls between India and France during
the year. The fifth edition of multilateral exercise La
Perouse was conducted in the Indian Ocean Region
on 16-24 January in which India participated. In the
field of defence-space, the Defence Space Agency
participated in multilateral Aster-X 25 exercise held
from 17-28 March in France.
This year marked the launch of the first joint Indo-
French challenge co-organised by the French Defence
Innovation Agency (AID) and Defence Research
Development Organisation (DRDO) of India, to invoke
interest of students on emerging defence technology
and artificial intelligence. The 'India Pavilion' was set
up during the 55th Paris Air Show, held on 16-22 June
at Le Bourget, France showcasing systems developed
by HAL, DRDO and industries.
To
deepen
collaboration
in
defence
research
and development a Technical Agreement was
signed between Defence Research Development
Organisation (DRDO) and Directorate General of
Armaments (DGA), France on 20 November. A letter
of intent between National Security Guard of India and
National Gendarmerie Intervention Group (GIGN) of
France was signed on 19 November in Paris, enabling
deeper synergy in sharing expertise, experience and
specialised counter terror skills.
Civil Nuclear Cooperation
A letter of intent on Small Modular Reactor (SMR) and
Advanced Modular Reactor (AMR) and an agreement
for cooperation in training and education of nuclear
professionals was signed in February. Two meetings
of the Special Task Force on Civil Nuclear Energy
(co-chaired by Foreign Secretary and the French
Secretary-General) were held on 20 January in Paris
and 22 September in New Delhi.

text:

207
An India Pavilion was established for the first time
ever at the Sixth World Nuclear Exhibition in Paris in
November.
Economic Cooperation
Within the EU, France remains India’s major trading
partner. The bilateral trade between India and
France has more than doubled in the last decade to
USD 15.21 billion in 2024-25. For the year 2024-
25, Indian exports to France amounted to USD 7.95
billion. France contributed a cumulative investment
of USD 11.75 billion from April 2000 to March 2025.
Chairman, SEBI visited Paris on 24-26 September
to attend the Financial Stability Engagement Group
(FSEG) meeting and also interacted with French
foreign investors and stakeholders.
Innovation, Technology and Other
Sectoral Cooperation
India and France have a rich history of cooperation in
the fields of science and technology. The cooperation
ranges from health, digital, energy and oceans to
applied mathematics. The 38th Governing Body
meeting of the Indo-French Centre for the Promotion
of Advanced Research (IFCPAR/CEFIPRA) was held
in New Delhi on 24 February. After the enabling of
Unified Payment Interface (UPI) at the Eiffel Tower
and Galleries Lafayette, in 2025, India and France
continued to advance multi-stakeholder exchanges
through the InFrastructures (India France Structures)
and InFinity (India France Innovation in Information
Technology) platforms.
During Prime Minister’s visit to France in February,
both countries signed a number of agreements/
LoI’s in areas like Digital Sciences and Life Sciences
Innovation. In the field of AI, in March, India signed a
contract with Station F and HEC Paris for the IndiaAI
Startups Global Acceleration Program. India and
France also signed a Joint Declaration of Intent on
Indo-Pacific Triangular Development Cooperation,
and a Declaration of Intent in the Field of Environment.
Community in France and Indian Students
in France
There is a large presence of Indian diaspora in the
French mainland and its overseas territories. There are
an estimated 1,19,000 Indian community in mainland
France. The estimated Indian-origin population
in French Overseas Territories is-Reunion Island
(3,00,159), Guadeloupe (57,180), French Guiana
(12,000), Martinique (8,090) and Saint Martin (1950).
The number of Indian students in France crossed
nearly 10,000 for the first time. The first OCI card
to the Indian-origin communities in Guadeloupe and
Martinique was issued in February and a delegation
from the Embassy visited French Guiana on 11-13
September, commemorating the arrival of Indians to
French Guiana, who arrived between 1856 and 1876.
Germany
The year 2025 marked successful completion of
25 years of India-Germany Strategic Partnership.
Germany is India’s largest trading partner in Europe
and the ties between the two countries have
expanded to cover all domains including mobility of
skilled talent, education, renewable energy, defence
and security, green and sustainable development and
people to people ties. The Strategic Partnership has
been further strengthened with the Intergovernmental
Consultations (IGC) at the level of Heads of
Government with the 7th IGC held on October 25,
2024 in New Delhi.
High-level Engagements
Prime Minister had a telecon with German Federal
Chancellor Friedrich Merz on 20 May and congratulated
him on assuming office. On 17 June, Prime Minister met
Chancellor Merz, on the sidelines of the G7 Summit
in Kananaskis, Canada. Prime Minister thanked
the Chancellor for Germany’s strong expression of
solidarity with and support for India’s fight against
terrorism. Prime Minister and Chancellor Merz met on
the sidelines of G20 Summit in Johannesburg, South

text:

208
Africa. Minister of Commerce and Industry visited
Germany from 22-24 October, and held discussions
with his counterpart Katherina Reiche, apart from
meeting business leaders in Germany.
Ministerial Visits
EAM held a joint telephone call with Foreign Ministers
of Germany and France in May. EAM visited Germany
from 22-24 May during which he called on Chancellor
Merz. EAM held discussions with his counterpart,
Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul as well as with
Minister for Economic Affairs and Energy and Foreign
and Security Policy Advisor to the Federal Chancellor.
EAM also engaged with Members of the German
Parliament, Foreign and Security policy experts and
members of the Indian community.
From the German side, German Foreign Minister
Johann Wadephul made his maiden visit to India on
1-3 September. During the visit, the Minister called on
Prime Minister and held delegation-level talks with
EAM. The two sides agreed on gratis visas for short-
term school and college visits between the countries.
The Minister also engaged with Minister of Commerce
and Industry.
Visit of All-Party Parliamentary
Delegation
A nine-member All-Party Parliamentary Delegation
visited Germany from 5-7 June and reiterated India’s
resolute commitment to the policy of zero tolerance
for terrorism. The visit was marked by high-level
engagements with Foreign Minister Wadephul,
Chairman of Foreign Affairs Committee of Bundestag,
Armin Laschet, senior political leaders and Members
of the Bundestag as well as with leading think-tanks
and representatives of the Indian community.
Other Ministerial visits
Minister of Commerce and Industry visited Berlin
in October for high-level bilateral meetings, as well
as engagements with business leaders. Minister of
Textiles visited Germany in January to participate
in Heimtextil 2025 (a Global symposium on
Textiles). Minister of State for Skill Development
and Entrepreneurship (Independent Charge) visited
Germany in July.
Multilateral Cooperation
India and Germany are committed to the strengthening
and reform of the multilateral system and, as members
of the Group of Four (G4), support the expansion of
both the permanent and non-permanent membership
of the UN Security Council. Both countries also support
each other on UNSC expansion within the framework
of the G4. The last meeting of the G4 at the level of
Foreign Ministers was held on the sidelines of the 80th
UNGA in New York, in September, and at the working
level, a G4 Director General meeting was held in June.
Economic Cooperation
Germany was ranked as India’s eighth largest trading
partner in Financial Year (FY) 2024-25. Bilateral trade
in goods and services reached USD 51.23 billion.
Germany is India’s ninth largest foreign direct investor,
with total German FDI in FY 2024-25 amounting to
USD 469million. Over 2,000 German companies are
currently active in India. During 2025 so far, German
companies have announced significant investments in
India. In March, Infineon opened its GCC in GIFT city
Gujarat. Several major investments include companies
like BASF, Schaeffler, Festois, Nordex SE, Knorr-
Bremse, Vensys Energy, amongst others.
Development Cooperation
In September, under the Green and Sustainable
Development Partnership (GSDP), consultations
between the Government of India and the Government
of Germany were held on development projects
across a wide variety of sectors such as renewable
energy (including solar, green hydrogen and energy
efficiency); sustainable urban development; e-mobility;
agriculture and agro-ecological sector; skilling; quality
infrastructure and standardization, among others.
In the annual bilateral negotiations on development
cooperation held in New Delhi on 5 December, Germany
committed assistance of about USD 1.49 billion across
key areas such as energy transition, sustainable urban
development, green mobility, sustainable agriculture,

209
skilling etc. The assistance consists mainly of
concessional loans. Some key projects include Green
Energy Corridor Projects in various states (such as
Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and
Tamil Nadu), Urban Mobility projects (Ahmedabad,
Surat, Bangalore Metro), Ganga Rejuvenation and
Renewable Energy Partnership.
Trilateral development cooperation (TDC)
Trilateral development cooperation (TDC) has been
progressing well with five pilot projects completed
and two ongoing. The Joint Steering Committee
meeting of TDC was held in December in New Delhi.
TDC has been progressing well with seven pilot
projects completed. Three pilots are being scaled
up in 2025, including Cameroon (Climate Adaptive
RAC Technology Laboratory for Nationwide Potato
Seed Innovation), Malawi (Technical Innovation and
Entrepreneurship Hub in Agri Value Chain for Women
and Youth) and Ghana (Digital Technology Centre for
design and processing in Bamboo).
Science, Technology and Innovation
Building on the 50th anniversary of S&T collaboration
between the two countries last year, Indo-German
cooperation in Science, Technology and Innovation
(STI) deepened across several emerging domains
during the year. The Indian National Science Day 2025
was celebrated in March at Darmstadt, in association
with FAIR-GSI and the Max Planck Society. New
MoUs and LoIs were announced in August between
(a) Technische Universität Berlin and Siemens Mobility
with IIT Kharagpur and IIT Tirupati in dynamic charging,
(b) FAIR and IIT Kharagpur in particle research, and (c)
DESY and IIT Kharagpur in quantum/nano research.
The InDeVet was launched at the University of Leipzig
in April, for opening new avenues in veterinary and
life sciences research.
The BITS Pilani delegation visited TU Dresden on 17
October to facilitate the signing of an MoU between
the two institutions. Our Mission hosted a Seminar on
“Indo-German Tech Dialogue in which MoUs between
University of Stuttgart and IIT Kharagpur & IIT Tirupati
were exchanged. The Joint S&T Committee Meeting
was held in New Delhi on 24-25 November.
Defence Cooperation
India and Germany have reaffirmed their commitment
to strengthening bilateral defence cooperation in
various fora, with a broad horizon encompassing high
level visits, military engagements, sharing of best
practices and defence industrial partnership.
A high-level delegation led by Lt Gen Thorsten
Poschwatta, Commander Air Operations Command
attended Aero India 2025 at Bangalore from 10-
14 February. A defence seminar cum exhibition
was conducted in Berlin, Germany on 10 April.
30 Indian defence companies and 100 German
defence companies attended the event. Military
Cooperation Sub Group (MCSG) Meeting is part of
the institutionalised mechanism of bilateral defence
cooperation between India and Germany. The 18th
MCSG meeting was held in New Delhi from 29 to
30 September. Upon invitation from the German
side, India’s formal admission as an observer state in
this programme took place on 21 January. India has
nominated DRDO as the lead agency for interaction
and coordination with OCCAR Eurodrone Programme
Working Group (PWG). Germany will be deploying its
Navy LO in the Integrated Fusion Centre-Indian Ocean
Region (IFC-IOR) at Gurugram.
The 12th India-Germany High Defence Committee
(HDC) meeting co-chaired by Defence Secretary
from the Indian side and by State Secretary, Federal
Ministry of Defence, from the German side was held
at New Delhi on 18 November.
Mobility and Education
Mobility of skilled talent is an important pillar in the
India-Germany relations. The first India-Germany
Consular Dialogue was held on 6 May in Berlin.
Meetings of the German-Indian Joint Working
Group (JWG) on Migration and Return and the Sub-
Committee on Labour Migration were held in Berlin
on 8-9 April. India and Germany agreed to gratis visas

210
for short-term school and college visits between the
two countries to further promote student exchanges
and education ties during the visit of German Foreign
Minister to India in September.
Around 60,000 Indian students are enrolled in
German Universities for higher studies (doubled in the
last 5 years), making them the largest cohort among
the international student community in Germany.
Culture and People to people ties
During the year, the Tagore Centre organized around
45 cultural events. Notable examples include: a three-
day Indian Film Festival across four cities in Germany
showcasing over 30 films. Moreover, Germany hosted
first India and Ayurveda Week organized at Bleiche
Hotel, Spreewald from 5–12 October.
Ireland
India and Ireland share strong political ties rooted
in our freedom struggle movements and growing
economic and people-to-people connections.
High-level visits and meetings
EAM paid an official visit to Ireland from 6 and 7
March which was the first ever stand alone visit
of an EAM to Ireland. During the visit, EAM called
on the then President of Ireland Michael D Higgins,
and held discussions on the growing bilateral
ties and exchanged views on regional and global
developments. EAM held delegation level talks with
his Irish counterpart the then Deputy Prime Minister
and Foreign Minister Simon Harris and reviewed the
entire spectrum of bilateral cooperation. EAM also
met the Minister of Higher Education James Lawless
and the former Prime Minister Leo Varadkar. An
MoU on diplomatic exchanges aimed at deepening
institutional cooperation and experience sharing on
training programmes for diplomats was signed during
the visit. The two sides also agreed to set up an
India-Ireland Joint Economic Commission. At an event
organised at the University College of Dublin, EAM
delivered the keynote address and interacted with
prominent academicians and scholars and discussed
perspectives on India and global affairs. EAM also
interacted with the Indian community in Ireland,
appreciating their rich contributions to Irish society.
EAM met with his Irish counterpart Simon Harris TD
at the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Minister Meeting
on 24 February.
EAM with the then Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister
Tánaiste Simon Harris during an official visit to Ireland, March
2025
Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas led a high-
level delegation comprising of senior legislators
from Punjab, Jammu and Kashmir, UP, Rajasthan,
Uttarakhand and Delhi to Ireland from 22-24 June for
the Commemoration event held on 23 June marking
the 40th Anniversary of the Air India Kanishka (AI 182)
bombing.
Minister of Higher Education, Lawless visited India
from 15-22 March as part of the St. Patrick’s Day
celebrations. A delegation of 7 Vice Chancellors
from the leading Indian Universities visited Ireland in
February.
Trade and Economic cooperation
Bilateral Trade (Goods and Services) between the
two countries stood at USD 18.4 billion in 2024, with
diversification in import and export baskets. India’s
total trade in goods with Ireland for April 2024-March
2025 is USD six billion, India’s export to Ireland stood
at USD 0.8 billion and imports from Ireland at USD
5.2 billion.

Education, Cultural cooperation and
people to people exchanges
Under Ek Bharat Shresth Bharat initiative India
conducted several commercial, cultural and tourism
promotion activities focused on specific Sectors and
States of India in various parts of Ireland during the
year.
There are around 80,000 Indian diaspora members
residing in Ireland mostly working in healthcare,
IT, engineering and senior management positions.
Ireland has also become a significant destination
for Indian students (around 13,000) seeking higher
education, particularly post-graduate, doctoral and
post-doctoral students in the areas of engineering,
technology, medicine and management.
Italy
India-Italy relations are on an upward trajectory with
both sides taking concrete steps to implement the
bilateral Joint Strategic Action Plan for 2025 to 2029
announced by Prime Minister and Prime Minister
Giorgia Meloni in November, 2024. Regular dialogue
between the two leaders, Ministerial visits and
exchange of business delegations were instrumental
in broadening and deepening bilateral cooperation
across sectors. Italy has joined India led multilateral
initiatives viz. India Middle East Europe economic
corridor (IMEEC), Coalition for Disaster Resilient
Infrastructure (CDRI), International Solar Alliance
(ISA), Global Biofuel Alliance (GBA) and Indo Pacific
Oceans Initiatives (IPOI).
High-level visits and meetings
Prime Minister met Prime Minister Meloni on the
sidelines of the G7 meeting in Kananaskis, Canada
on 18 June. On 24 April, Prime Minister Meloni had
a phone call with Prime Minister and reiterated
Italy’s commitment to combat international terrorism,
strengthen bilateral dialogue and joint actions to
counter terrorism. Prime Minister Meloni was among
the first world leaders to condemn the terrorist attack
in Pahalgam, Kashmir on 22 April. On 10 September,
Prime Minister had a phone call with Prime Minister
Meloni and welcomed ongoing efforts towards
implementation of the Joint Strategic Action Plan
(JSAP 2025-29). Prime Minister Meloni reiterated
Italy’s strong support for early conclusion of a
mutually beneficial India-EU Free Trade Agreement.
On the sidelines of the G20 Summit in Johannesburg,
South Africa, Prime Minister met Italian Prime Minister
Giorgia Meloni. The ‘India-Italy Joint Initiative to
Counter Financing of Terrorism’ was adopted.
EAM and Minister of Commerce and Industry along
with Deputy Prime Minister Antonio Tajani and
Minister of University and Research Anna Maria
Bernini co-chaired an inaugural India-Italy Business,
Science and Technology forum on 11 April in New
Delhi. Minister Tajani, was accompanied by nearly 100
Italian companies, six university rectors and Heads of
six Italian research centres. The delegation had fruitful
interactions with Indian companies and educational
institutions. Minister Tajani also called on the Hon’ble
Rashtrapati ji of India during the visit. Minister Bernini
met Minister of State for Science and Technology,
Earth Sciences. A Memorandum of Understanding
for cooperation in scientific research was signed.
Both sides agreed to implement the 2025–2027
Executive Programme for Scientific and Technological
Cooperation for collaboration in critical technologies
such as AI and digitalization. The Joint Science and
Technology Committee approved joint funding for 10
mobility related projects and 10 projects in research
excellence.
EAM met Antonio Tajani on the sidelines of the
United Nations General Assembly in New York, on 25
September. Minister Tajani conveyed Italy's support
for an early finalisation of the India-EU FTA. Antonio
Tajani visited India on 10-11 December and called on
Prime Minister and Minister of Commerce and Industry
and the National Security Advisor.
Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs visited Milan
from 4-6 May to attend the 58th ADB Annual Meeting
and met Italy’s Finance Minister. Minister of Commerce
and Industry along with Deputy Prime Minister Tajani
co-chaired the 22nd India-Italy Joint Commission for
Economic Cooperation (JCEC) on 4-5 June in Brescia,

212
Italy. Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and
Dairying visited Italy from 28 September-1 October
and interacted with the Italian seafood business
association to explore ways of augmenting seafood
exports to Italy.
Deputy Minister for Infrastructure and Transports
Edoardo Rixi, accompanied by Italian companies
visited India from 28-30 October to participate in the
India Maritime Week in Mumbai. During the sidelines
of maritime week, the Minister met the Minister of
Ports, Shipping and Waterways and Ministers of
State for Railways and Urban Affairs, Under Secretary
of State of Foreign Affairs, Maria Tripodi visited New
Delhi on 17 February and met EAM and Minister of
Commerce and Industry. Ambassador Francesco Talo,
Italian Special Envoy for IMEEC participated in the first
technical meeting of IMEC stakeholders in New Delhi
on 5-6 August, hosted by India’s National Security
Council Secretariat. President of the Italian Republic
Sergio Mattarella sent a letter of condolence to the
Hon'ble Rashtrapati ji of India following the tragic Air
India crash in Ahmedabad on 12 June.
Parliamentary visits
An All-party Parliamentary delegation visited Italy
from 27-29 May. The delegation conveyed India's
strong national consensus and resolute approach
on zero tolerance towards terrorism and conveyed
appreciation to Italy for expression of solidarity with
India in the fight against terrorism. The delegation met
several parliamentarians including Presidents of the
Foreign Affairs Committees in both Houses, President
and members of the India-Italy Parliamentary
Friendship Group and Maria Tripodi, Under Secretary
of State for Foreign Affairs. They also interacted
with think tanks, media, and members of the Indian
community.
Other Visits
The Chief Justice of India visited Italy from 16-20
June to attend the Constitutional Law Conference
organised by the Chamber of International Lawyers
in Milan. Secretary (Agriculture and Farmers Welfare)
visited Rome from 19-22 October and met Luigi D’
Eramo, Italy’s Under Secretary of State for Agriculture.
Trade and Economic Cooperation
Italy is India’s fourth largest trading partner in the
European Union with bilateral trade in FY 2024-25
standing at USD 13.75 billion. Trade balance is in
India’s favour with our exports to Italy standing at
USD 7.73 billion. Italy ranked 19th in terms of FDI
inflows into India during April 2000 to March 2025
which stood at USD 3.61 billion. A delegation from the
Ministry of Food Processing Industries visited Milan
and Bologna on 26- 28 June to meet Italian business
chambers, CEOs of food processing companies and
site visits.
Several Indian exporters participated in trade fairs
and exhibitions in Italy including Artigiano in Fiera (29
May to 2 June), in Milan, Riva Schuh and Gardabags
leather fair (14-17 June) in Riva del Garda, Vicenza
Oro-Jewelry Boutique show (10-13 July and 5-9
September) in Vicenza, and Host Milano international
exhibition (17-21 October) in Milan. Indian oil and
gas PSUs participated in the Gastech Exhibition and
Conference 2025 in Milan from 9-12 September.
Science and Technology
Italy was Country Partner at the fourth India Space
Congress in New Delhi from 25–27 June with
participation of the Italian Space Agency (ASI), and
several space companies. An Italian space delegation
comprising senior officials, Italian Space Agency and
leading space companies visited India from 22-26
September for productive interactions with ISRO,
Department of Space, Ministry of External Affairs,
InSpace and Indian space companies, to explore G2G
and B2B space collaborations.
Defence and Security Cooperation
Italy’s Under Secretary of State for Defence, Italy
Matteo Perego di Cremnago led Italy’s official
delegation to Aero India in February and interacted
with Raksha Mantri and the Chief of Defence Staff.
In March, the 13th India-Italy Military Cooperation

Group meeting was held in Rome to review military-
to-military bilateral cooperation and prepare a plan of
action for 2025-26.
Defence Secretary led the Indian delegation for the 11th
India- Italy Joint Defence Committee (JDC) meeting
in Rome on 14-15 April. A delegation of Society of
Indian Defence Manufacturers (SIDM) accompanying
the Defence Secretary interacted with Italian defence
companies. The Italian Federation of Aerospace,
Defence and Security (AIAD) and SIDM signed a
Memorandum of Understanding which would provide
a framework for defence industrial collaborations.
Maritime cooperation and exchanges between the
respective Navies continued with the Italian Navy
Ship ‘ITS MARCEGLIA’ visiting Mumbai port in June.
Indian Navy’s Ship, INS TAMAL visited the port of
Naples in August. INS TRIKAND visited the port of
Taranto in September. Director General of Indian
Coast Guard, visited Italy from 10-12 September to
participate in the Coast Guard Global Summit hosted
by Italy. His interaction with his Italian counterpart
further strengthened India-Italy maritime security
cooperation.
On 25 June, Embassy in collaboration with Italian think
tank Institute of International Affairs organised the
first India Dialogue on ‘Indo-Pacific and the Enlarged
Mediterranean,’ with participation of strategic experts
from both countries. India’s growing ties with the EU
and Italy, and India’s economic rise and its strategic
potential were the focus of discussions. The 5th Joint
Working Group on counter-terrorism met in Rome
on 15-16 January co-chaired by officials from the
respective Foreign Ministries.
On 5 July, a memorial for Indian soldier Yeshwant
Ghadge, was inaugurated in Montone, Italy. Ghadge
had sacrificed his life for the liberation of Montone
town during the Second World War. The memorial,
supported by the Ministry of Defence, gives visibility
to the bilateral historical ties and contribution of Indian
soldiers to the liberation of Italy.
Education, Cultural and people to people
exchanges
The number of Indian students enrolled in Italian
Universities stands at 5,500. Most are enrolled in
engineering, finance/economics, medicine. Universities
with a large Indian student population are Politecnico
di Milano (Milan); La Sapienza University (Rome);
Tor Vergata University (Rome), Politecnico di Torino
(Turin). Academic cooperation is an important
aspect of diplomatic outreach with the signing of a
Memorandum of Understanding with the University
of Bergamo in March to establish a Chair for Indology,
supported by ICCR. On 2 April, an MoU was signed
with the Luiss University in Rome for establishment
of an ICCR Chair of Indian Studies. On 14 June, the
Istituto Europeo di Design (IED), Italy's premier design
school, signed a Letter of Intent (LoI) with India’s
Ministry of Education to open its branch campus in
Mumbai. This agreement marks India’s approval for
IED to offer its Bachelor’s degree programmes in India.
In February, the first five-day Indian Film Festival was
held at several locations in Italy with screening of
Indian films. In July a bronze bust of Maharishi Valmiki
was unveiled in Camporotondo village. The bust was
gifted by ICCR under the initiative, ‘Connecting the
world through Ramayana’.
A delegation from Ministry of Information and
Broadcasting and NFDC participated in the Venice
Film Festival in August and had interactions with
Italian counterparts and stakeholders. A Networking
event to promote WAVES Bazaar was held in Venice
on 31 August. The Embassy, in collaboration with
Teatro di Roma organised the ‘Incredible India Cultural
Festival’ from 26-28 September at Teatro India, Rome
which featured around 100 Indian and Italian artists
based in Italy.
The Indian diaspora standing at around 1,86,000, is
the largest in the EU and the second largest in Europe.
Regular outreach programs were held to connect with
members of the Indian community.

214
Luxembourg
India and Luxembourg enjoy warm and friendly
relations characterized by a high degree of mutual
understanding and cooperation at bilateral and
multilateral levels. Luxembourg has an Embassy
in New Delhi and Honorary Consuls in Mumbai,
Chennai, Kolkata and Bengaluru. The Indian Embassy
in Brussels is concurrently accredited to Luxembourg.
High-level engagements
Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji congratulated Guillaume V
on his accession to the throne as the Grand Duke of
Luxembourg in October.
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of
Luxembourg Xavier Bettel visited India from 16-18
March for the Raisina Dialogue. During his visit he
also met the EAM. The Minister of Commerce and
Industry met with the Deputy PM and Foreign Minister
of Luxembourg on the sidelines of Global Berlin
Dialogue on 23 October.
Trade and Investment
Trade and investment comprise important elements
of India-Luxembourg relations. India and Luxembourg
have a Double Taxation Avoidance Treaty (DTAA),
a Social Security Agreement, and a Civil Aviation
Agreement, that lays the fundamental basis for
enhanced bilateral economic and trade cooperation.
Total trade with Luxembourg (2024-25) totalled
EUR 97 million of which India's export was worth
EUR 33 million and India's import totalled EUR 64
million. There have been significant FDI flows from
Luxembourg to India, standing at USD 5.19 billion for
the period April 2000 to March 2025.
Monaco
India and Monaco enjoy cordial relations and the two
countries have gradually developed their relations
in various fields. Blue economy, trade, tourism and
taxation matters are some of the leading areas of
cooperation.
On 8 June, Secretary (Ministry of Earth Sciences)
attended the Blue Economic Finance Forum in Monaco,
which was convened as a special event of the third
UN Ocean Conference. The aim of the conference was
to identify and mobilize solutions to support initiatives
to promote the blue economy and conserve marine
ecosystems.
Monaco
hosts
the
International
Hydrographic
Organization (IHO), in which India has been an
active and influential member since 1955. On 14-16
October, Chief Hydrographer to the Government of
India, visited Monaco to attend the 9th meeting of the
IHO Council.
The Netherlands
India and the Netherlands share a multifaceted
relationship covering diverse areas of trade and
investment,
defence
and
security,
renewable
energy, water, agriculture, critical technologies and
semiconductors, education and people to people ties.
The Netherlands is the largest investor in India from
Europe.
High-Level Exchanges
India and the Netherlands have regular contact at high
levels. Prime Minister Schoof called and conveyed
his condolences to Prime Minister in April on the
Pahalgam terrorist attack. Prime Minister Schoof and
Prime Minister had a meeting on the sidelines of G20
Summit in Johannesburg on 23 November.
EAM visited the Netherlands in May and met with
Prime Minister Schoof, then Foreign Minister Veldkamp
and Defence Minister Brekelmans. This followed the
visit of then FM Caspar Veldkamp to India at the end
of March. He met with EAM and NSA. EAM met with
Foreign Minister David van Weel on the sidelines of
80th UNGA in New York in September.Foreign Minister
of Netherlands David van Weel visited India on 17-
19 December and had a meeting with Raksha Mantri,
EAM, and NSA.
Defence
Minister
of
the
Netherlands
Ruben
Brekelmans visited India in February to participate in

the Raisina Dialogue. During the visit he also met with
Raksha Mantri and NSA.
Minister of Infrastructure and Water Management of
the Netherlands Robert Tieman visited India from 27-
31 October and attended the India Maritime Week
(IMW) 2025 held in Mumbai.
India and the Netherlands discuss issues covering
the entire gamut of bilateral relations, through annual
consultations led by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
on both sides at Secretary level. The 13th India-
Netherlands Foreign Office Consultations were held
on 4 December in New Delhi co-chaired by Secretary
(West) and Secretary General, Ministry of Foreign
Affairs of the Netherlands.
The two sides have ongoing Joint Working Groups
(JWGs)/Dialogues at functional level in the fields of (i)
Science and Technology (ii) Agriculture (iii) Healthcare
(iv) Urban Development (vi) Counter Terrorism (vii)
Maritime Cooperation (viii) Water (ix) Policy Planning
(x) Cyber Dialogue (xi) Consular.
Trade and Commerce
The Netherlands is India’s 10th largest trading partner
in the world. The Netherlands is also the third largest
export destination for India in the world and the
largest in Europe. During the F.Y. 2024-2025, the
total merchandise trade with the Netherlands stood at
USD 27.779 billion. The total merchandise trade with
the Netherlands accounts for 2.45 percent of India’s
total merchandise trade. The Netherlands is India’s
largest merchandise export destination in Europe and
third largest in the world. In the F.Y. 2024-2025, India
exported USD 22.761 billion worth of goods to the
Netherlands.
Netherlands is the fourth largest investor in India.
The cumulative Dutch investments in India from
2000 onwards are around 54 billion dollars. Indian
companies are also investing in the Netherlands in
a big way, with a total investment of USD 26 billion.
Netherlands is now the fourth largest destination
for Overseas Direct Investment (ODI) by Indian
companies. There are over 300 Dutch companies
present in India, including major players like Philips,
Signify, Akzo Nobel, DSM, KLM, Rabobank, Heineken,
TomTom, Paques, Boskalis, Van Oord, Damen
Shipyards, Vopak, Aegon, etc. Similarly, there are over
300 Indian companies present in the Netherlands,
including all the major IT companies such as TCS,
HCL, Wipro, Infosys, Tech Mahindra, as well as Tata
Steel and others.
Collaboration in Other Sectors
The India-Netherlands have a Strategic Partnership
on Water. The Netherlands is engaged with various
States and Municipalities in India to implement water
related projects including the States of UP (Namami
Ganga Programme), Tamil Nadu (water as leverage,
water management and conservation) and Kerala
(flood management).
India and Netherlands are also collaborating in the
domain of maritime cooperation as well as in the
establishment of a Green and Digital Sea Corridor
between India and Netherlands. Both sides are
cooperating in the field of healthcare and public health
as well as food safety, pharmaceuticals, medical
devices.
In the domain of agriculture, both sides have set an
ambitious agenda to establish 25 CoEs by 2025 in the
Agri sector, nine out of which are already functional.
The two countries are also cooperating in the domain
of capacity building in horticulture. The eighth meeting
of the Joint Agricultural Working Group (JAWG)
between India and the Netherlands was held on 31
October in New Delhi.
The Second meeting of the India–Netherlands Joint
Working Group (JWG) was held in Mumbai on 30
October. An LoI was signed between the Inland
Waterways Authority of India and the Netherlands on
training for dredging and river engineering. Another
LoI on Green and Digital Shipping Corridors was
signed.
India and Netherlands are cooperating in several
new
domains
like
maritime
cultural
heritage,
semiconductors and emerging technologies, digital

ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
216
and cyber space, establishment of a joint trade and
investment committee and cooperation in higher
education.
The Second India-Netherlands Consular Dialogue
was hosted by India in New Delhi on 9 October.
People-to-people ties
The Netherlands has the largest population of people
of Indian origin in the EU. It is home to approx. 90,000
people of Indian origin. Besides this there is a sizable
Surinamese Hindustani community now completely
integrated in Dutch society, which is estimated to be
approx. 200,000 strong. The Netherlands is a popular
education destination for Indian students, particularly
in the field of science and technology. Many Dutch
Universities like TU Delft, Leiden University and
Maastricht University have long standing collaboration
with Indian universities. The number of Indian students
has been growing over the years and more than 3500
Indian students are studying in the Netherlands
presently.
Portugal
India and Portugal share warm and cordial relations
based on historical maritime linkages, diaspora and
cultural connections. In 2025, the two countries
commemorated
the
50th
anniversary
of
re-
establishment of diplomatic relations. There is steady
momentum in our bilateral ties, with continuing high-
level interactions and cooperation across several
sectors. Several events in diverse areas ranging from
Literature, Academic, Arts and Sports, Ayurveda, Yoga
Film Festivals and Film Screenings were organised to
commemorate this milestone in diplomatic relations.
Portugal supports India's candidature for permanent
membership at the reformed UN security council and
is staunch proponent of India- EU relations.
High-level visits and meetings
The highlight of this year was the State Visit by
Hon’ble Rasthrapatiji from 6-8 April. During the
visit, she met with President Marcelo Rebelo de
Sousa. Both the Presidents also launched postage
stamps commemorating 50 years of diplomatic
relations between the two countries. She also met
with the President of Portuguese Parliament José
Pedro Aguiar-Branco. Prime Minister of Portugal Luis
Montenegro called on the President.
Speaker of Lok Sabha paid a visit to Lisbon in June and
met with President (Speaker) of the Assembly of the
Republic of Portugal Jose Pedro Aguiar-Branco.
Minister of Finance and Corporate Affairs paid a visit
to Portugal on 2-3 July and met Minister of Finance of
Portugal Joaquim José Miranda Sarmento. Secretary
of State of Agriculture Joao Moura led a 10 member
Portuguese delegation to World Food India 2025 in
September.
Trade and Economic cooperation
Bilateral trade for 2024-25 was worth USD 1.12
billion with Indian exports worth USD 920.24 million
and imports from Portugal worth USD 206.11 million.
Bilateral trade balance also continued to be in India’s
favour at USD 714.33 million. Portugal ranks 52nd in
Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) into India, with total
FDI inflows amounting to USD 126.31 million as of
June. Indian investments in Portugal are estimated to
be in the range of up to USD 500 million.
There has been exchange of commercial delegations
between India and Portugal. During the annual tourism
fair - Bolsa de Turismo Lisboa, India and Goa booth
was set up in Lisbon on 12-13 March in collaboration
with four tourism and tour operator companies from
India. Minister of Sports, Arts and Culture of Goa
inaugurated India and Goa booths. The event formed
part of the commemoration of the 50th anniversary
of re-establishment of diplomatic relations between
India and Portugal and also aimed at promotion of
Indian films.
Many commercial delegations from Portugal also
visited India. The Secretary of State of Agriculture, Joao
Moura led a 10-member Portuguese delegation to
World Food India 2025, which was held in New Delhi
in September. There was Portuguese participation
(5 entities), including representatives from PIBHub
in WAVES 2025 that was held in Mumbai in May.

Representatives of the prominent textile producers
in Portugal also participated in Bharat Tex 2025 held
from 14-17 February in New Delhi.
Celebration of 50th anniversary of re-establishment of
diplomatic relations
The year-long commemoration of the 50th anniversary
of re-establishment of diplomatic relations officially
began in Portugal on 3 January with an Indian
film festival organised by Embassy of India in the
historic Cinema São Jorge in Lisbon. The festival
was inaugurated by the Minister of Foreign Affairs of
Portugal Paulo Rangel.
On 21 March, Mission organised the launch of the Hindi
translation of the book of poems titled ‘Mensagem’ by
the Portuguese poet Fernando Pessoa, in collaboration
with ICCR, Instituto Camões and Grupo O Valor do
Tempo. On 28 March, a conference on ‘Indians in
Portugal - Advancement of Science and Technology’
was organised in collaboration with Bhoomi Portugal.
A two-day Indian film festival was organised in Sao
Miguel islands of the Azores archipelago on 24-25
October. This was the first ever Indian film festival
organised in the Azores Archipelago. A Bollywood
and saree workshop was also held as part of the film
festival. On 21 October, an interaction was organised
with the acclaimed filmmaker Tanvi Gandhi on the
evolution of Indian cinema, women empowerment
and new technologies in the entertainment industry.
Institutional Dialogue Mechanisms
Both countries engaged through regular dialogue
and exchanges under institutional mechanisms which
significantly contributed to steady progress in the
bilateral relationship across several sectors. The sixth
Joint Economic Committee meeting was held on 23
January. Both sides held discussions on economic
cooperation across sectors including trade and
investment, tourism, defence, science and technology,
infrastructure,
renewable
energy,
water
and
sanitation, maritime cooperation and blue economy,
health, pharmaceuticals and ayurveda, agriculture
and food processing and labour mobility. The second
Joint Working Group Meeting on Renewable Energy
between Portugal and India took place in June.
The Fifth India-Portugal FOC was held in Lisbon
on 3 November. Secretary (West) also called on by
Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and International
Cooperation of Portugal Ana Isabel Xavier to
strengthen political dialogue and expand cooperation
in trade, education and mobility.
Portuguese Secretary of State of Agriculture Joao
Moura led a 10-member delegation to World Food
India 2025, held in New Delhi in September.
Education, Cultural Cooperation and
People to People Exchanges
Speaker of the Lok Sabha launched the 10th anniversary
celebration of the International Day of Yoga in Portugal
on 7 June, in four cities of Lisbon, Porto, Montemor-o-
Novo, and Horta in Faial Island, Azores. On 21 June,
the commemoration of International Day of Yoga
was organised in front of the iconic Belem tower in
Lisbon, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In March, the
second International Ayurveda Congress was held in
collaboration with Portuguese Ayurveda Association
Amayur.
On 12 October, the state of Uttar Pradesh was
conferred with the Best Spiritual Tourism Destination
Award at the Seven Stars Luxury Hospitality and
Lifestyle Awards. From 10-13 November, a delegation
led by NASSCOM composed of around 10 companies
participated in the Websummit 2025, the annual
technology conference held in Lisbon, and called on
Minister of Infrastructure and Housing of Portugal
Miguel Pinto Luz.
The 50th anniversary of re-establishment of bilateral
relations was celebrated through a conference titled
‘Culture and Globalisation’ organised by University of
Lisbon and Jain University, Bengaluru On 13 October.
The first ever Indian film festival was organised in Sao
Miguel islands in the Azores Archipelago on 24-25
October. Vice President of the Portuguese Parliament
Marcos Perestrello inaugurated a film festival- Ritwik
Ghatak retrospective in December.
Portugal has a large Indian-origin diaspora estimated
to number around 1,20,000 spread across regions

and representing different communities and religions.
There are approximately around 1100 Indian
students in Portugal, mostly in Masters and PhD
programmes, in STEM and other areas such as social
sciences. Predominantly students undertake Masters
in Business Administration, Data Science, Industrial
Engineering, Sociology-Anthropology and disciplines
such as biotechnology. The year saw a steady increase
in the number of Portuguese tourists travelling to
India. About 90,000 Portuguese visited India in 2025
while about 38,000 Indians visited Portugal.
San Marino
Relations with San Marino remained cordial and
friendly. Both the countries have established a fruitful
cooperation, particularly within international fora, but
also at a bilateral level on issues of common interest.
The year 2025 also marked the 60th anniversary of
establishment of consular relations between India
and San Marino.
San Marino has been supportive of India’s candidatures
at multilateral bodies. They have supported India’s
candidature to the non-permanent seat of the UNSC
for 2028-29 and for election to membership of United
Nations Economic and Social Council for the term
2026-28.
International day of Yoga was organized at Cava dei
Balestrieri, a historical landmark in the city of San
Marino on 13 June with the support of the Government
of San Marino and in collaboration with several Yoga
Schools. To commemorate the 60th anniversary of
establishment of diplomatic relations with San Marino,
an Indian Film Festival was organized in San Marino
on 12 May.
Spain
Relations with Spain remained strong covering diverse
areas of defence, trade, urban mobility, tourism and
cultural cooperation. The ties between Spain and
India began on a high-note with the landmark visit
of EAM to Spain in January, which came within three
months of the highly successful visit of President
Pedro Sanchez to India in October 2024.
High-level visits
EAM visited Spain on 13 and 14 January. During his
visit, EAM held talks with Foreign Minister Jose Manuel
Albares and Defence Minister Margarita Robles and
also called on King Felipe VI and President Pedro
Sanchez. He became the first foreign guest to address
the Conference of Spanish Ambassadors. Two MoUs
on cooperation in sports, and in Sustainable Urban
Development, were signed during the visit.
Institutional Dialogue Mechanisms
The India-Spain Foreign Office Consultations were
held in New Delhi on 13 November between Secretary
(West) and Secretary of State for Foreign and Global
Affairs, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, European Union,
and Cooperation of Spain, Diego Martínez Belío.
Minister of State Law & Justice visited Spain from
12-14 November to participate in the Justice Leaders
Dialogue held as part of the Global Round-table on
Equal Access to Justice, organized by the Organisation
for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD),
and co-hosted by the Spanish Ministry of the
Presidency, Justice, and Parliamentary Relations.
EAM and Foreign Minister Jose Manuel Albares signed two
MoUs during the former's visit to Madrid, January 2025.
Minister of Finance and Corporate Affairs visited
Spain for the fourth United Nations Conference on
Financing for Development which took place in Seville
from 30 June-3 July. Minister of Road Transport
and Highways visited Spain in February. Minister
title: mea_annual_report

text:

219
of Culture and Minister of Tourism participated
in the World Conference on Cultural Policies and
Sustainable Development (MONDIACULT 2025),
held in Barcelona, Spain, on 29 September.
The All-Party Parliamentary Delegation for Operation
Sindoor visited Spain from 30 May- 2 June, to express
India’s firm stance on zero tolerance for terrorism.
Chief Ministers of Jharkhand and Madhya Pradesh
visited Spain in April and July respectively with
business delegations to promote Spanish investment
in their respective states.
Defence Cooperation
The cornerstone of India-Spain defence cooperation
remains
the
C-295
military
transport
aircraft
programme, a USD 2.5 billion project involving Airbus
Spain and Tata Advanced Systems Limited. The 16th
and final aircraft manufactured in Spain under the
programme was delivered ahead of schedule on 31
July. Defence Diplomacy has been further advanced
through academic and institutional exchanges. In
October, a 22-member delegation of future strategic
leaders from India’s College of Defence Management
(CDM), Secunderabad, visited Spain. Also, IAF as
the first non-NATO country Air Force took part in Ex
OCEAN SKY 2025 at Gran Canaria, Spain, from 20-
31 October. The Spanish frigate CSDS Méndez Núñez
made a Port Call in Mumbai on 18 September. It also
held Passage Exercise with INS Teg.
The Indian Air Force (IAF) became the first non-NATO
air force to participate in Spain’s major multinational
air combat exercise, Exercise Ocean Sky, held at
Gando Air Base, Canary Islands, from 15-31 October.
The Indian contingent operated alongside units from
Spain, Germany, Greece, Portugal, and the United
States, with over 50 aircrafts participating in total.
Commercial and Economic Cooperation
Commercial ties between India and Spain continue to
strengthen, with bilateral trade in goods reaching a
record USD 8.77 billion in 2024, reflecting a 5.7 percent
growth over the previous year. Similarly in 2024,
exports from India experienced a year-on-year increase
of 2.5 percent reaching USD 6.52 billion, whereas
imports from Spain showed a year-on-year increase
of 16.5 percent reaching USD 2.25 billion. Spain is the
16th largest investor in India with cumulative FDI stock
of USD 4.3 billion (April 2000 – June 2025). There
are more than 280 Spanish companies in India mainly
in the sectors of metallurgical industries, renewable
energy, automotive, ceramics, defence, infrastructure
and retail and consumer products. Similarly, around
80 Indian companies with a cumulative investment of
around USD 900 million are active in Spain, mainly in
software and IT services, pharmaceuticals, chemicals,
logistics and import-export sectors.
Cultural Cooperation
A wide range of activities in the ambit of culture
were undertaken through the year. The exhibition
Mystic Paths: The Living Tradition of Indian Art,
organized collaboratively by MOSA (Belgium), the
Museo de Antropología (Madrid), and the Indian
Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR), was held from
31 January-20 April. The second edition of Óle India
was held in Madrid on 15th March, featuring over 160
performers and attracting more than 1,200 attendees.
India was the Guest Country at the Feria del Pimiento
Morrón in Fresno de la Vega.
The twinning agreement between Ahmedabad and
Valladolid, originally signed in 2017, was renewed and
expanded on 15 September. This agreement fosters
cooperation in cultural, educational, technological,
and social fields, reflecting shared values of heritage
preservation,
tourism,
gastronomy,
innovation,
artificial intelligence and sustainable development.
United Kingdom
This was a landmark year in the India-UK
Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, with back to
back bilateral visits at the Prime Ministerial level, to
London in July and to Mumbai in October. The year saw
the signing of India-UK FTA; adoption of Vision 2035;
announcement of a Defence Industrial Roadmap;
inauguration of Gurugram campus of Southampton
University, first foreign university to open campus in

ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
220
India under New Education Policy, while eight other
UK universities were granted approvals to open
campuses in India; and the inauguration of two new
Consulates General of India in the UK in Manchester
and Belfast.
India-UK relations advanced with the UK Prime
Minister Keir Starmer's first visit to India in October,
focusing on the Comprehensive Economic and Trade
Agreement (CETA) signed in July. He visited with one
of the largest business and arts delegations in recent
UK history. During his visit, Prime Minister Starmer
delivered the keynote address at the Global Fintech
Fest in Mumbai on 9 October in the presence of Prime
Minister. The UK Prime Minister's visit coincided with
the port call of UK’s Carrier Strike Group and the Royal
Navy’s exercise KONKAN with the Indian Navy, which
was the first instance of complex, multivector naval
exercises between Indian Navy and Royal Navy.
Ahmedabad, Gujarat, was confirmed as host for
the 2030 Centenary Commonwealth Games on 26
November at the General Assembly in Glasgow,
Scotland. Separately, India was re-elected to the
IMO Council for 2026-27 in Category B with a record
154/169 votes at the 34th Assembly in London
on 28 November topping this category of Council
membership for the second straight term.
High-Level Exchanges
Prime Minister visited the United Kingdom on 23-24
July. Prime Minister also called on King Charles III.
Within three months of Prime Minister’s historic visit
to the UK, the UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer visited
Mumbai on 8–9 October with a 125-member strong,
largest ever, business delegation from UK to India.
Key announcements during Prime Minister’s visit
to the UK included the Comprehensive Economic
and Trade Agreement (CETA), the India-UK Vision
2035, the Defence Industrial Roadmap, the MoU
between India's CBI and the UK's National Crime
Agency. Major outcomes of the UK Prime Minister
visit entailed meeting of reconstituted India–UK
CEO Forum, resetting of India–UK Joint Economic
and Trade Committee (JETCO), and establishment
of India–UK Connectivity and Innovation Centre,
India–UK Joint Centre for AI, Establishment of Critical
Minerals Industry Guild, Launch of phase II of UK–
India Critical Minerals Supply Chain Observatory and
Establishment of Offshore Wind Taskforce.
Both the Prime Ministers held telephone call on
April 26 where Prime Minister Starmer expressed
horror and strong condemnation of the Pahalgam
terror attack. They also spoke on 6 May to announce
the conclusion of the landmark India–UK Free Trade
Agreement (FTA). They interacted on the sidelines of
the G7 Summit on June 17 in Kananaskis, Canada.
Lok Sabha Speaker visited the UK from 7-11 January.
He met with Commons Speaker Hoyle and Lords
Speaker Lord McFall of Alcluith. He visited Scotland
and met Alison Johnstone MSP, Presiding Officer of
the Scottish Parliament, and John Swinney MSP, First
Minister of Scotland and interacted with cross-party
Members of the Scottish Parliament. On 10 January,
He chaired the meeting of the Standing Committee of
Conference of Speakers and Presiding Officers of the
Commonwealth (CSPOC) in Guernsey.
EAM paid a bilateral visit from 3-9 March. During the
visit, EAM called on Prime Minister Keir Starmer and
met the Foreign Secretary, Deputy Prime Minister,
Business and Trade Secretary and Home Secretary.
He inaugurated two new Consulates General of India
in Manchester and Belfast at that time, bringing our
diplomatic presence up to five posts in the United
Kingdom. He also met Deputy First Minister of
Northern Ireland. EAM met Secretary of State for
Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs
of the UK Yvette Cooper at the sidelines of UNGA
in September. The then UK Foreign Secretary David
Lammy visited India on 7-8 June.
Minister of Finance and Corporate Affairs visited
the UK in April for the 13th Economic and Financial
Dialogue. Secretary of State for Business and Trade
Jonathan Reynolds visited in February on his first visit
as Secretary of State to resume FTA negotiations.
Minister of Commerce and Industry visited London in
April, May and June, to finalise negotiations for India–
UK FTA.

An all-party Indian Parliamentary delegation visited
the UK from 31 May to 3 June, to express India’s firm
stance on zero tolerance for terrorism and highlight
Pakistan’s role in cross-border attacks.
Minister of Law and Justice and Chief Justice also
visited the UK during the year. UK Secretary of State
for Culture Lisa Nandy visited India in May, to attend

Vernon Coaker visited India on 10 February.

Medium Industries of Karnataka, visited London from

major UK-based companies. Minister met UK Minister
for Commonwealth Affairs and Development Seema
Malhotra and engaged with leaders of major global
companies such as Martin-Baker, ARM, Linde, Fido
AI, Oxford Space Systems, and others. The delegation
also participated in the UK-India Business Council
meeting.

from

participated in the World Travel Market (WTM) London

States included Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Delhi,

Rajasthan, and Madhya Pradesh. The event was held
from 4-6 November at ExCeL London which brought
together over 5,000 exhibitors and 45,000 industry
professionals worldwide to network, showcase
destinations, explore travel trends, and promote
sustainable tourism.
Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh visited London
on 3 November. He held meetings with companies
including Octopus Energy, Rolls Royce, SRAM and
SAMKO Group, in addition to participating in a round
table organised by CII. Chief Minister of Assam
visited London on 17 November for the signing of a
Letter of Intent with the British Museum for the loan
of Vrindavani Vastra to the Government of Assam
for public display. He also toured the Regent Canal
Waterfront Development project.
Foreign Secretary met UK NSA Jonathan Powell
and Deputy NSA Matthew Collins during his visit in
November.
UK Minister for the Indo-Pacific, Seema Malhotra, made
her first official visit to India from 20 to 22 November,
to strengthen the UK-India partnership, focusing on
trade, investment, and strategic cooperation and
emphasized the importance of fostering cultural ties,
including the UK’s“living bridge” with India.
There were several visits from Indian State
governments to the UK. Chief Minister of West Bengal
visited UK in March. Minister of State for Sports and
Youth Service, Government of Gujarat, travelled to
the UK three times, in June, August and September to
present India’s bid for hosting the 2030 Commonwealth
Games. India's bid was formally accepted by the
Commonwealth
Sport
Executive
Committee
in
October. Minister of Cultural Affairs, Government of
Maharashtra visited the UK in August. During this visit,
he formally received the historic 18th-century sword
of Maratha general Raghuji Bhosale I, repatriated
from London to Maharashtra. Chief Minister of Tamil
Nadu accompanied by Industries Minister and senior
officials, visited the UK in September. A delegation
led by Minister of Higher Education and Minister
for Medical Education, Government of Karnataka
visited the UK in September. Minister for Information
Technology, Electronics and Communications, Real
Time Governance (RTG), and Human Resources
Development (HRD) for the Government of Andhra
Pradesh, visited the UK in September.
Economic Relations
The historic India-UK Comprehensive Economic
and Trade Agreement (CETA) was signed during
the visit of Prime Minister to the UK in July. CETA
provides an unprecedented duty-free access to 99
per cent of India’s exports to the UK, and 91 per
cent of UK’s exports covering nearly 100 per cent

222
of the trade value. This includes labour-intensive
sectors such as textiles, leather, marine products,
gems and jewellery, and toys as well as high-growth
sectors like engineering goods, chemicals, and auto
components. India will remove tariffs on 90 percent
tariff lines, signaling a substantial tariff for food and
drink, as well as advanced manufacturing exports. In
the services sector, the agreement includes a wide-
ranging package covering Information Technology /IT
enabled services, financial and professional services,
business consulting, education, telecom, architecture,
and engineering.
India and UK held the inaugural meeting of the
reconstituted India–UK CEO Forum on 9 October.
Both countries also reset the India–UK Joint Economic
Trade Committee (JETCO) which will support the
implementation of the CETA and drive economic
growth and job creation in both countries. India–UK
bilateral trade (both goods and services) stood at over
USD 56 billion in 2024. Out of the above, India’s total
imports from the UK amounted to USD 23 billion and
India’s total exports amounted to USD 34 billion.
Defence Cooperation
Both India and the UK have robust defence relations
exemplified through regular interaction at highest
levels as well as through institutional dialogues such
as Defence Consultative Group (DCG) meeting at the
level of Defence Secretary.
During the visit to the UK of Prime Minister in July, a
new Roadmap for Defence Industrial Cooperation was
signed. This Roadmap will align with the renewed
'Vision 2035' and promote collaboration in co-design,
co-development and co-production in the Defence
sector. UK Carrier Strike Group (CSG) visited India
in early October. Led by aircraft carrier HMS Prince
of Wales, it successfully completed the sea phase
of the bilateral maritime exercise KONKAN-25 with
the Indian Navy and IN aircraft carrier off the western
coast of India, including cross deck landings. The
UK and India held the eighth edition of their biennial
army exercise, Ajeya Warrior-2025, in November at
'Mahajan Field Firing Ranges' in Rajasthan.
Technology and Innovation
Under the Technology Security Initiative (TSI), the two
sides agreed to establish India-UK Connectivity and
Innovation Centre, the India-UK joint Centre for AI and
announced the Phase-two of the UK-India Critical
Minerals Supply Chain Observatory to expand Mineral
coverage, further integrate advanced technologies,
unlock new bilateral investment opportunities and
establish a new satellite campus at IIT-ISM Dhanbad.
Both sides also released an anniversary statement on
TSI during Prime Minister’s visit to the UK in July.
Education
Southampton University became the first foreign
university to open a campus in India. Its Gurugram
campus was inaugurated in July and it has welcomed
its first cohort of students. Apart from Southampton
University, eight other UK universities were granted
permission to open campuses in India. These include
Queen's University, Belfast, University of Surrey,
Coventry University at GIFT City, Gujarat; University
of Liverpool and University of Lancaster at Bengaluru
and University of Bristol, University of York, University
of Aberdeen at Mumbai.
Indian students are one of the largest cohorts of
international students in the UK. As per latest data
from Higher Education Statistics Agency, UK, there
were 166,310 Indian students in Academic Year
2023-24.
Diaspora
The UK has about 1.864 million Indian diaspora as per
the 2021 Census and forms 3.1 percent of the total
population of UK, which is 59.597 million.
