Indo-Pacific
C H A P T E R
10
India’s vision for the Indo-Pacific focuses on a free,
open and rules-based Indo-Pacific. India emphasises
respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity
of all nations in the region, equality among all
nations, peaceful resolution of disputes, avoidance
of the use or threat of use of force, and adherence
to international laws, rules, and regulations. India’s
objective is to have a multi-faceted engagement with
all countries in the region and those with interests
in it, encompassing political, security, economic, and
socio-cultural spheres, aimed at Mutual and Holistic
Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions
(MAHASAGAR).
During the year, India’s engagement with various
mechanisms in the Indo-Pacific frameworks, including
inter alia, Association of South East Asian Nations
(ASEAN), East Asia Summit (EAS), Indian Ocean Rim
Association (IORA), Asia-Europe Meeting (ASEM),
Mekong-Ganga Cooperation (MGC), Indian Ocean
Commission (IOC), Ayeyawady-Chao Phraya-Mekong
Economic Cooperation Strategy (ACMECS) and
Indonesia–Malaysia–Thailand Growth Triangle (IMT-
GT), witnessed a steady rise.
Association of Southeast Asian
Nations
India’s relationship with the Association of Southeast
Asian Nations (ASEAN) is a key pillar of its foreign
policy and the cornerstone of its Act East Policy and
the Indo-Pacific vision, that was thereafter built on
it. India supports ASEAN unity and centrality in the
evolving architecture in the Indo-Pacific. Formal
engagement of India with ASEAN began in 1992 as
a Sectoral Dialogue Partner and, subsequently, as a
Dialogue Partner in 1996, which was upgraded to the
Summit level in 2002, Strategic Partnership in 2012,
and Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in 2022.
India and ASEAN have a comprehensive engagement
covering a wide array of areas at all levels, including
six Ministerial engagements in Foreign Affairs,
Commerce, Tourism, Agriculture, Digital, and Defence,

as well as official-level dialogues across various areas
of cooperation.

strengthen tourism cooperation.

267
Improving connectivity with ASEAN has been a
key focus of India’s Act East policy. Currently, there
are direct flights to nine Member States, which is
crucial for businesses and tourism. Emerging fintech
collaboration and digital connectivity shall further
strengthen partnerships with ASEAN. Some ASEAN
Member States have also emerged as key technology
partners.
ASEAN has emerged as a key trade partner, a
significant source and destination for foreign direct
investment. To further expand cooperation, a review of
the ASEAN-India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA)
is underway, while efforts are underway to enhance
practical cooperation in maritime, cybersecurity, the
digital economy, and new and emerging areas.
A new ASEAN-India Plan of Action (2026-2030) was
adopted this year for strengthening the India-ASEAN
Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
East Asia Summit
Established in 2005, the Leaders-led East Asia
Summit (EAS) format is the most vital part of the
ASEAN-led frameworks, primarily because of its
contribution to building a strategic trust environment
in the region. India sees the EAS as the logical platform
for promoting a free, open, transparent, rules-based,
peaceful, and prosperous Indo-Pacific region.
India’s engagement with EAS is a multilevel interaction
process, at the apex of which are the EAS supported
by the EAS Foreign Ministers’ Meeting (EAS FMM)
and the EAS Senior Officials’ Meeting (EAS SOM).
EAM represented India and delivered India’s National
Statement at the 20th East Asia Summit held in Kuala
Lumpur, Malaysia, on 27 October. In the statement,
EAM highlighted India’s strong commitment to
enhance maritime cooperation, in line with the ASEAN
Outlook on the Indo-Pacific (AOIP) and shared
dedication to the 1982 United Nations Convention on
the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).
EAM attended the 20th East Asia Summit 2025, Kuala Lumpur,
Malaysia, October 2025
India hosted participating countries of the EAS for the
Knowledge Exchange Workshop on Energy Efficiency
Policies and Programmes – Lifestyle for Environment
and the Conclave of Heads of Higher Educational
Institutions at Nalanda University in India on 17-19
September.
Indian Ocean Commission
In 2020, India became an observer member of the
Indian Ocean Commission (IOC). India continues to
engage with the Western Indian Ocean countries in
the IOC as an observer.
Indian Ocean Rim Association
India has been a founding member of the Indian
Ocean Rim Association (IORA) since its establishment
in 1997. India is currently the Vice-Chair of IORA for
the period 2023-25. India is also leading the Working
Group on Maritime Safety and Security and Blue
Economy during this period. These decisions were
announced during the Council of Ministers Meeting

In 2025, India participated in the 27th Committee of
Senior Officials (CSO) and the 24th Council of Ministers
(COM), both organised virtually on 19-21 May under
the Chairship of Sri Lanka. The fifth Working Group
on Maritime Safety and Security (WGMSS) meeting,
the second under Indian leadership, was held virtually

on 2 May, during which the WGMSS work plan was
updated. India also attended the third Working Group
on Disaster Risk Management (WGDRM) meeting,
held virtually on 14 May, during which the WGDRM
work plan was updated. India also joined the Ad-hoc
Committee established under IORA Sub-Committee
on Finance (SCF) to strengthen the Secretariat’s
business processes.
India assumed the Chairship of IORA for the 2025-
2027 term on 12 November. The Sushma Swaraj
Institute of Foreign Service (SSIFS) organised a
diplomatic training program in New Delhi on 8-13
December to enhance the capacity of IORA Secretariat
officials. Designed in line with India’s MAHASAGAR
vision, the six-day course titled Special Course on
Functional Competencies for Smarter Diplomacy was
attended by 31 diplomats and officials from Mauritius,
Seychelles, and the IORA Secretariat.
Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative
In June 2018, the Prime Minister outlined India’s vision
for the Indo-Pacific region in his speech delivered at
the Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore. India calls for
a free and open Indo-Pacific, based upon respect for
the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all nations,
peaceful resolution of disputes through dialogue,
and adherence to international rules and laws. India’s
concept of the Indo-Pacific supports an approach that
respects the right of all to freedom of navigation and
overflight in international waters. India’s approach is
based on cooperation and collaboration, given the
need for shared responses to regional challenges, and
is premised on the principle of ‘ASEAN-Centrality’.
In November 2019, the Prime Minister launched the
Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI) at the 14th East
Asia Summit held in Bangkok, Thailand. As an open
global initiative, the IPOI draws on existing regional
cooperation architecture and mechanisms to focus
on seven central pillars: Maritime Security; Maritime
Ecology; Maritime Resources; Capacity Building
and Resource Sharing; Disaster Risk Reduction and
Management; Science, Technology and Academic
Cooperation; and Trade Connectivity and Maritime
Transport.
In response to India’s invitation to international
collaboration within the IPOI framework, several
countries have assumed leadership roles across
various pillars. The UK has agreed to co-lead the
Maritime Security pillar along with India; Australia
and Thailand are leading the Maritime Ecology pillar;
France and Indonesia have jointly agreed to lead the
Marine Resources pillar; India and Bangladesh are co-
leads on the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management
pillar; Germany, the EU and Netherlands have decided
to lead the Capacity Building and Resource Sharing
pillar; Singapore and Italy are co-leading the Science,
Technology, and Academic Cooperation pillar; and
Japan and the US are co-leading Trade Connectivity
and Maritime Transport pillar. During the year, New
Zealand and Fiji joined the IPOI in March and August,
respectively. In October, EAM highlighted the joining
of new members and the expanding strength of IPOI
at the 20th East Asia Summit held in Kuala Lumpur,
Malaysia on 27 October.
31 Diplomats and officers from Mauritius, Seychelles and the IORA Secretariat participated in a Special Course on Functional
Competencies for Smarter Diplomacy at SSIFS, New Delhi, December 2025.

Mekong Ganga Cooperation
Established in 2000, Mekong-Ganga Cooperation
(MGC) is the oldest sub-regional mechanism in the
Mekong sub-region. To give a further boost to the
cooperation under MGC, the member states agreed
to further streamline the functioning of MGC under
the ten identified areas of tourism, culture, education,
public health and traditional medicine, agriculture and
allied sectors, transport and communication, Micro,
Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (MSMEs), water
resources management, science and technology, skill
development and capacity building of cooperation,
through the system of lead country for each area. They
also agreed to establish the MGC Business Council to
further enhance trade cooperation.
Under the MGC Plan of Action 2019-24, Indian
Missions in Myanmar and Cambodia organised the
Mekong-Ganga Food Festival on 23-24 February
and on 22 March, respectively. This vibrant event
celebrated the deep-rooted cultural and culinary
ties between India and the Mekong region, bringing
together diverse flavours, traditions, and shared
heritage. The opening ceremony of the food festival in
Yangon was attended by officials, including the then
Union Minister of the Ministry of Hotels and Tourism
of Myanmar U Kyaw Soe Win and other regional
leaders. A tour of MGC countries’ tour operators to
prominent Buddhist sites in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh
was successfully organised on 2-10 June.
Under MGC, India implements Quick Impact Projects
(QIPs) in the CLMV countries: Cambodia, Lao PDR,
Myanmar, and Vietnam. Each QIP project has a budget
cap of USD 50,000. The primary focus of these
projects is to deliver quick, visible results that directly
benefit local communities, with a typical completion
time of up to one year. QIPs involve the creation or
enhancement of physical infrastructure, such as roads
and community centers, as well as social infrastructure,
including capacity building in sectors like education,
health, sanitation, and community development.
Since the MGC’s inception in the FY 2015-16, a
total of 197 QIP schemes have been initiated with
sanctions issued for 170 of these projects. Of these,
137 projects have been successfully completed while
33 are in various stages of implementation. Among
the 170 sanctioned QIP schemes, 65 have been
allocated to Cambodia, 56 to Vietnam, 34 to Lao PDR,
and 15 to Myanmar. During the year, Cambodia has
completed 45 of its 65 sanctioned projects; Vietnam
has completed all 56 sanctioned projects; Lao PDR
has completed 25 of 34; and Myanmar has completed
11 of the 15 QIPs sanctioned to it.
For capacity building, India has been offering 50 MGC
scholarships per year since 2005 to students from

Ayeyawady-Chao Phraya-Mekong
Economic Cooperation Strategy

undertaking joint projects in the following focus
areas of cooperation under the ACMECS master plan:
digital and physical connectivity; capacity building
for energy infrastructure; cooperation in MSMEs and
HRD; FinTech; sustainable water management; and
tourism and health. The ACMECS Master Plan (2019-
2023) envisages cooperation based on three pillars:
Seamless
Connectivity,
Synchronised
ACMECS
Economies, and Smart and Sustainable ACMECS.
Indonesia–Malaysia–Thailand
Growth Triangle

(IMT-GT) sub-regional cooperation was established
in 2005 to accelerate and facilitate economic
development in the participating countries by

BIMSTEC
The Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral
Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) is a
grouping of seven Member States located in the littoral
and adjacent areas of the Bay of Bengal. It is a unique
link connecting South Asia with South East Asia- five
members from South Asia (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India,
Nepal and Sri Lanka) and two from South East Asia
(Myanmar and Thailand). The BIMSTEC region brings
together 1.7 billion people- 22 percent of the world
population, with a combined GDP of USD 5 trillion.
The organisation came into existence on 6 June 1997
through the 'Bangkok Declaration'.
It was originally formed by four Member States under
the acronym 'BIST-EC' (Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka,
and Thailand Economic Cooperation). Following
Myanmar's inclusion in December 1997, it was
renamed 'BIMST-EC' (Bangladesh, India, Myanmar, Sri
Lanka, and Thailand Economic Cooperation). With the
inclusion of Nepal and Bhutan in 2004, the grouping's
name was changed to BIMSTEC.
BIMSTEC organises inter-governmental interactions
through
Summits,
Ministerial
Meetings,
Senior
Officials Meetings, Permanent Working Committee,
Joint Working Groups and Experts-level Meetings.
Five BIMSTEC Summits have been held so far- 2004
(Bangkok), 2008 (New Delhi), 2014 (Nay Pyi Taw),
2018 (Kathmandu) and 2022 (Colombo).
The Prime Minister participated in the sixth BIMSTEC
Summit held in Bangkok on 4 April. Prior to the Summit,
the 25th Session of the BIMSTEC Senior Officials’
Meeting (SOM) and the 20th Ministerial Meeting (MM)
were held on 2 and 3 April, respectively. During the
Summit, Prime Minister announced several India-led
initiatives towards institution and capacity building in
BIMSTEC, including setting up of BIMSTEC Centres
of Excellence in India on Disaster Management,
Sustainable Maritime Transport, Traditional Medicine
and Agriculture, Skill Development Programme–
BODHI [BIMSTEC for Organised Development of
Human Resource Infrastructure], a pilot study to
assess regional needs in Digital Public Infrastructure

and a capacity building programme for cancer care in

SAARC
India is a founding member of SAARC. India’s SAARC

The 60th meeting of the SAARC Programming

The annual activities of the Regional Centres and

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
274
80th Session of the UN General
Assembly
The UN marked its 80th anniversary this year. UN
Secretary-General António Guterres announced the
UN80 initiative in March during this commemorative
year. The initiative seeks to identify financial
efficiencies, review implementation of mandates,
and introduce structural changes and programme
realignment across the UN system. India supported
an ambitious approach to UN80 that focused on
reforming the UN to make it fit for purpose by
equipping it to respond effectively to contemporary
challenges, particularly conflicts. India argued that
UN80 needs to go far beyond achieving financial
efficiencies alone. In this context, India stressed the
need for adequate resources for the developmental
agenda and for peacekeeping operations to deliver
mandates effectively.
Former Federal Foreign Minister of Germany Annalena
Baerbock was elected as President of the 80th session
of the UNGA (PGA) on 2 June. Since assuming charge,
she has underscored the UN’s relevance and centrality
in her remarks on all important occasions. Some of
the other themes of focus for PGA Baerbock have
been improving the UN’s efficiency and effectiveness,
advancing the gender agenda, and promoting
multilingualism. An officer from the Permanent
Mission of India to the UN in New York (PMI) has been
assigned to the PGA’s office.
EAM led the Indian delegation at the high-level
week of the 80th Session that was themed ‘Better
together: 80 years and more for peace, development
and human rights.’ He delivered India’s national
statement on 27 September. He outlined India’s
overall priorities for engagement with the UN, as
well as specific areas of focus. Emphasising the
need for greater international cooperation within the
multilateral framework, he highlighted current gaps
in the UN architecture in fulfilling its core functions
across diverse domains. EAM made a strong case
for UN reforms and underlined India’s readiness to
assume greater responsibilities in a reformed Security
Council. India’s leadership of the Global South, with
development partnership as an important pillar, was
another key theme of the statement. India’s growing
capabilities in Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster
Relief (HADR), combating piracy, protecting maritime
shipping, and other areas were among the highlights
EAM noted. He underlined that India’s approach to
the world is guided by self-reliance (Atmanirbharta),
securing oneself (Atmaraksha), and self-confidence
(Atmavishwas).
During the high-level week, EAM had wide-ranging
engagements in both multilateral and bilateral
formats. Multilateral engagements included both
regional interactions and thematic engagements.
These engagements reinforced India’s focus on the
Global South, while also attesting to its inclination
to further consolidate existing partnerships with the
Global North. Expansion and diversification of India’s
foreign policy were evident in EAM’s multilateral
engagements. India also convened a High-Level
meeting of the Global South. In addition, Foreign
Minister level meetings with Community of Latin
American and Caribbean States (CELAC) and Central
American Integration System (SICA) groupings
of Latin America and Pacific Island countries
demonstrated India’s outreach to different regions of
the globe. India also participated in the L-69 and C-10
Joint Ministerial meeting on UNSC reform. The annual
G4 meeting at the Foreign Minister level was also
held. As the incoming Chair, India organised a BRICS
Foreign Ministers’ meeting. In addition, there were
G20 and IBSA meetings at Foreign Minister level.
Notably, EAM also interacted with a gathering of all
EU Foreign Ministers for the first time in New York on
22 September.
EAM’s bilateral interactions with his counterparts
included those with the US, Russia, UAE, Algeria,
Australia, Austria, Brazil, Canada, Denmark, Italy,
Netherlands,
Egypt,
Philippines,
Saudi
Arabia,
Singapore, Sri Lanka, and the UK, among others.

275
Two
multi-party
Parliamentary
delegations
comprising a total of 27 Members of Parliament (MPs)
from India visited New York, the first batch of 12 MPs
from 8 to 14 October and the second batch of 15 MPs
from 27 to 31 October. The delegation met the senior
leadership of the UN, Permanent Representatives and
think tanks, among others.
India’s participation at the Secretary-level in various
high-level events during the week underscored the
depth and breadth of India’s diverse engagements in
the UN. Secretary (Women and Child Development)
led the Indian delegation at the commemorative
meeting to mark the 30th anniversary of the Beijing
Declaration and Platform for Action (on gender
equality) on 22 September. Secretary (Youth Affairs)
led the Indian delegation at the High-Level meeting
to commemorate the 30th anniversary of the World
Programme of Action for Youth on 25 September.
Secretary (Health and Family Welfare) was the
leader of the Indian delegation at the fourth High-
Level Meeting on Prevention and Control of Non-
Communicable Diseases on 25 September. Secretary
(Electronics and Information Technology) was also
part of the high-level week.
The Ministry in collaboration with the Department of
Posts, organised an event named ‘Release of UN@80
Commemorative Stamp’ on 24 October, which is
observed as the UN Day annually. The stamp was
selected from more than 7,40,000 designs submitted
by artists from schools and art colleges across India, as
part of a stamp design competition led by the Ministry
and India Post to celebrate 80 years of the UN. The
winning stamp was released by EAM, Secretary
(West), and Secretary (Posts) in New Delhi on UN Day
in the presence of the former UN Resident Coordinator
in India Shombi Sharp, government representatives,
and diplomats.
Debates and processes
India has been actively engaged in debates,
negotiations, and processes within the UN General
Assembly. One of the main themes of our efforts has
been the reform of the UN Security Council (UNSC).
Additionally, development issues have been a key
focus area.
Our specific priorities include positioning India as
a leading voice for the Global South, enhancing
coordination with important groups such as LLDCs
(Landlocked Developing Countries), LDCs (Least
Developed Countries), and SIDS (Small Island
Developing States). We are also leveraging the India-
UN Development Partnership Fund and the IBSA
Fund and highlighting India's accomplishments in
women-led development.
Furthermore, India reaffirmed its commitment to
furthering the UN's peace and security functions
and responsibilities. This includes emphasising the
EAM jointly hosted the India–SICA Foreign Ministers’ Meeting with Minister of Foreign Affairs of Panama Javier Martinez-Acha Vasquez
in New York, September 2025

creator: PDFium

276
global significance of peacekeeping operations and
engaging effectively as a Troop Contributing Country
in the finalisation of mandates for UN peacekeeping
missions.
India also worked towards raising awareness about
issues related to counter-terrorism and advancing
India's pragmatic and constructive approach to
disarmament. Our efforts include active campaigning
for elections to UN bodies and increasing the
visibility and footprint of the use of Hindi within the
UN framework, particularly through the Hindi@UN
project.
UN Security Council Reforms
Despite India’s Security Council term ending in
December 2022, the nature and extent of its
participation in the Security Council processes were
remarkable. In the backdrop of the conflict in Gaza,
which has been gaining considerable attention in the
Council, India advocated diplomacy and dialogue as
the best means to resolve it. India also reiterated its
consistent position and reaffirmed its unwavering
support for the Palestinian people, while calling for a
two-state solution. Thematic issues, particularly those
related to peace and security, were another important
area in which India made its positions known. India’s
engagement with the Council was primarily two-
pronged: through inclusive formats such as open
debates and direct outreach to the UNSC members to
further issues of interest to India.
EAM joined the G4 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting along with his
counterparts from Japan, Germany, and Brazil in New York,
September 2025
India
also
continued
to
push
for
reformed
multilateralism, particularly UNSC reforms through
proactive engagement, including in the Inter-
governmental Negotiations (IGN) process. India’s
outreach and coordination with reform-oriented
groupings such as the G4, L-69, and C-10 continued
in 2025. During EAM’s L-69 & C-10 and G4 Ministerial
meetings in New York in September, the Ministers
underscored the urgent need for reforming the Council.
Expansion of both permanent and non-permanent
categories, early commencement of text-based
negotiations, clearly defined timelines and milestones
were highlighted by EAM in these meetings.
International Day of Yoga
The 11th International Day of Yoga, themed ‘Yoga
for Earth, One Health’, was celebrated at the UN
Headquarters on 20 June. Noted physician Deepak
Chopra conducted a meditation session during the
celebration, attended by over 1200 yoga enthusiasts,
including Permanent Representatives and delegates
from UN Member States, senior UN officials, members
of various yoga organisations, and representatives of
the Indian diaspora.
Non-Aligned Movement
As a founding member of the Non-Aligned Movement
(NAM), India has remained actively engaged in the
NAM. MoS (KVS) represented India at the NAM
Summit in Kampala on 15-16 October.
Peacekeeping
In peacekeeping, India remains cumulatively the
largest Troop/Police Contributing Country (T/PCC)
with about 3,00,000 personnel deployed since 1950.
183 Indian Peacekeepers have made the supreme
sacrifice in the line of duty. Presently, India has 4267
peacekeepers, including 158 women, deployed in nine
of the 11 existing UN peacekeeping missions. India’s
three largest contingents are in UNMISS - South
Sudan 1811, MONUSCO-DRC 1039, and UNIFIL –
Lebanon 643.

text:
UN & International Organisations
277
In 2025, India lost two UN Peacekeepers: MONUSCO
Havildar Sanjay Singh and UNMISS Subedar Sujit
Kumar Pradhan.
India co-hosted the International Day of UN
Peacekeepers on 29 May with Austria. The Group
of Friends on Accountability for Crimes against UN
Peacekeepers held its third Ambassadorial-Level
Meeting on 15 July. Representatives from around 40
countries attended the meeting. It may be recalled
that the Group was launched by India along with five
other countries on 15 December 2022 to promote
accountability for crimes against peacekeepers.
India has always supported greater participation of
women in peacekeeping, aligning with the Action for
Peacekeeping. India was also the first country to deploy
an all-women Formed Police Unit to a peacekeeping
mission, the UN Mission in Liberia (UNMIL), from 2007
to 2016. An all-women Female Engagement Team
(FET) with women soldiers of the Indian Army has
been deployed in MONUSCO, UNISFA, and UNMISS.
India’s commitment was reinforced in the Conference
for Women Peacekeepers from the Global South on
‘Enhancing the Role of Women in Peacekeeping’ which
was conducted in New Delhi in February, wherein
women peacekeepers from 35 partner countries
from the Global South including 17 from the African
Continent came together to discuss peacekeeping
challenges, highlighting the crucial role of women,
and promote gender balance. India also conducted
a United Nations Women Military officers’ course in
August, in which 15 countries participated.
The Conclave of Army Chiefs of UN Troop Contributing
Countries (TCCs) was held in New Delhi, India, from
14 to 16 October. The Conclave brought together
senior military leaders from over 30 nations and
high-level UN representation. It established a shared
and nuanced understanding of evolving operational
challenges such as cyber risks and asymmetric warfare.
Key outcomes focused on leveraging technology, with
demonstrations and discussions driving consensus on
the greater use of technology as a force multiplier for
mission effectiveness.
India professes and offers niche capabilities which meet
the extant and future requirements of peacekeeping.
Its offers include Quick Deployment Units, Specialised
Units and renewable energy assets. Indian contingents
saw a significant enhancement in operational mobility
and mandate execution capabilities following the
deployment of indigenously manufactured All-
Terrain Vehicles (Heavy) in UNMISS. The mission’s
extensive utilisation of the inducted ATVs for mandate
enforcement tasks has been met with appreciation
and positive feedback from relevant stakeholders.
Furthermore, 7 Madras Infantry Battalion Group
(INDBATT-XXV) serving with the United Nations
Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) from May 2024 to
July 2025 received a letter of appreciation from the
UN Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations
Jean-Pierre Lacroix.
The Indian Battalion-II (22 Maratha Li Inf Group)
serving with the United Nations Mission in the
Republic of South Sudan (UNMISS) was honoured by
Jonglei State, South Sudan. The Governor of Jonglei
State Riek Gai Kok Diang presented the Certificate
of Appreciation to the Battalion for going above and
beyond to demonstrate profound commitment to
humanitarian work.
The objective of Training of Trainers (ToT) on United
Nations Pre-Deployment Training (UNPDT) is to
prepare officers for the effective execution of their
tasks as part of Military Contingents and to equip
them to train their units/troops in UN peacekeeping
techniques. Later in the year, UNPDT-04 was
organised by the Ministry in partnership with CUNPK
at Manekshaw Centre, New Delhi in December. The
course was attended by 15 Foreign Participants and
10 Indian Participants. The valedictory address was
delivered by Secretary (West), who also handed over
certificates to the course participants.
Peacebuilding
As one of the top five TCCs, India has been a member
of the Peacebuilding Commission since its inception.
This year, India actively participated in the meetings of
the Peacebuilding Commission (PBC) in the discharge
of its advisory and bridging roles, including in the
ongoing negotiations on the 2025 Peacebuilding
Architecture Review (PBAR). In this context, India

278
emphasised that national prevention strategies
should remain voluntary. India underlined the need
for a greater role for UN Resident Coordinators to
strengthen coherence across UN entities in the field.
It highlighted the significance of Women, Peace and
Security (WPS) and Youth, Peace and Security (YPS)
agendas in peacebuilding. As the voice of the Global
South, India upholds the cardinal principle of national
ownership and leadership in peacebuilding efforts,
including in the financing of the projects funded
through the Peacebuilding Fund. India welcomed USD
50 million in assessed contributions from different
stakeholders to the Peacebuilding Fund. Secretary
(West) participated in a ministerial-level meeting on
the PBC during the High-Level Week and articulated
India’s position.
Counter Terrorism
One of India's top priorities at the UN is counter-
terrorism (CT), where it advocates comprehensive
multilateral action to counter terrorism, capacity-
building
support
to
member
states,
effective
implementation of UN CT-related sanctions, and
strengthening collective action against terrorism.
To show the impact of terrorism on people, India
organised a digital exhibition titled ‘The Human
Cost of Terrorism’ at the UN from June to July. EAM
inaugurated the exhibition on 30 June. The exhibition
shed light on the profound impact of terrorism on
individuals, families, and communities worldwide
through
a
curated
selection
of
photographs,
multimedia presentations, and testimonial displays.
It also highlighted a diverse range of national and
international efforts to prevent and counter terrorism
in all its forms and manifestations, underscoring the
achievements and ongoing challenges in the global
counter-terrorism landscape.
India actively supported the capacity-building efforts
of the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism (UNOCT)
and has supported a call for greater autonomy for
the Office. India also emphasised greater synergies
between UNOCT agencies and international forums
such as the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), to
promote and implement terror financing standards,
counter the use of new and emerging technologies
for terrorist purposes and advocate for ‘right to justice’
for victims of cross-border terrorism, among others. In
May, an interaction with the Monitoring Team of the
UNSCR 1267/1988 Sanctions Committee was held,
along with meetings with key functionaries in the UN
CT architecture.
Fourth Committee on Special
Political and Decolonisation
In the Fourth Committee, India continued to be
a leading voice in the fight against colonisation.
India strongly advocated a pragmatic approach to
decolonisation that would fulfil the legitimate wishes
of the people of 17 Non-Self-Governing Territories.
India has consistently emphasised that national
ownership is critical to all political solutions in the
debate over Special Political Missions.
Committee on Information
The 47th session of the Committee on Information was
held from 28 April to 9 May. India underscored its
commitment to ensuring safe, transparent and reliable
digital interactions for its citizens and bridging digital
divides. India called for enhanced global outreach
in languages beyond the official UN languages,
advocating collaboration with the Department of
Global Communication (DGC) to develop a model
consolidating news and multimedia content on the
UN News portal and on social media in Hindi. India
appreciated the UN’s support in commemorating the
International Day of Yoga, which has fostered global
awareness of this ancient tradition.
Hindi in the United Nations
Vishwa Hindi Diwas 2025 was commemorated on 13
February in the presence of MoS (Women and Child
Development). There was active participation in the
Hindi competitions held in the run-up to the special
occasion. Later in the year, Hindi Diwas was organised
at the UN on 8 October. The delegation of MPs
from India attended the event, which also featured
Permanent Representatives and other diplomats from
over 25 countries, senior UN officials, academics, and

text:
UN & International Organisations
279
members of the diaspora. Members of Parliament
felicitated the winners of various competitions that
were held in the run-up to the event.
The MoU on Hindi@UN Project was renewed on
26 February and is now valid until March 2030. As
per the MoU, India makes a voluntary contribution
of approximately USD 1.4 million annually to keep
the Hindi@UN project operational, ensuring that UN
news in Hindi is telecast regularly.
To strengthen the contribution of non-official
languages in the UN, and in view of the forthcoming
Multilingualism Resolution (negotiations will begin
in 2026), India joined the Group of Friends on
Multilingualism on 24 September. This is part of
India’s continued endeavour to promote the usage of
Hindi as a non-official language in the UN.
Financial Contributions
India contributes in full and on time to the regular
budget as a member of the United Nations, reflecting
its strong commitment to multilateralism. As in the
previous years, India paid its assessed contribution in
full and featured in the 2025 ‘Honour Roll’ of the UN.
Human Rights, Humanitarian and
Social matters
The Third Committee of the UN commenced its work
during the 80th session on 3 October and continued
until 21 November. The committee considered over
60 thematic resolutions, held interactive dialogues
with over 80 special mandate holders and discussed
issues related to social and cultural spheres and the
promotion and protection of human rights.
The Minister of Women and Child Development
(MoWCD) led the Indian delegation to the Commission
on the Status of Women held from 10-21 March.
During the general discussion, the Minister (MoWCD)
outlined India’s institutional framework for gender
equality, including gender budgeting and the decision
to reserve one-third of seats in national and state
legislatures for women. The outline also underscored
the increasing presence of Indian women across
diverse sectors, including STEM, the military, and
aviation.
MoS (MoWCD) led the Indian delegation to the
Commission on Social Development, held on 10-14
February. During the Commission’s general discussion,
MoS described India’s efforts and remarkable strides
in tackling multidimensional poverty, malnutrition, and
universal healthcare, while pioneering digital public
infrastructure for sustainable development. MoS also
outlined India’s focus on financial inclusion through
the JAM (Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile) initiative, with a
targeted focus on women and persons with disabilities,
a vision of women-led development, and efforts in
early childhood care, nutrition, and education.
Two events were also organised on the sidelines of
the Commission, in partnership with UN Women
and the Alliance for Global Good. The former was
a roundtable to address two topical themes for
accelerating women’s empowerment: digital and
financial inclusion for women’s empowerment,
and financing for women’s empowerment, and the
criticality of core resources, while the latter was on
women’s participation and leadership as key drivers
for economic growth and equality.
At the 58th Session of the Commission on Population
and Development (CPD58), held from 7 to 11 April,
India outlined its multi-pronged approach to ensure
healthy lives and promote well-being. During the
Commission, India co-sponsored the side event
organised by the Netherlands, Benin and the UN Youth
Office on the theme ‘Inter-generational Dialogue:
Ensuring Healthy Lives – Bridging Generations of
Action.'
India is a State Party to the Committee of States
Parties to the Convention on the Rights of Persons
with Disabilities (CoSP to CRPD) and attended the
18th session of the Conference of State Parties to
the Convention held on 10-12 June. India’s national
statement outlined its comprehensive approach to
empowering people with disabilities. India held a
side event to showcase the work of the Bhagwan
Mahaveer Viklang Sahayta Samiti (BMVSS) and
highlight the contribution of the iconic ‘Jaipur Foot’,

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
280
which revolutionised affordable, durable prosthetic
feet and made them available to millions in the
developing world.
The political declaration adopted at the Second World
Summit on Social Development was negotiated
and finalised in New York. The Summit was held in
Doha from 4 to 6 November. India negotiated the
text through the G-77, as the priorities of the Global
South align with social development issues. India was
able to reflect many national priorities in the text. The
reference to women-led development is an Indian
concept reflected in the UN document for the first time.
India, as an Executive Board member of UNDP/
UNFPA/UNOPS, UNICEF, and UN Women, actively
participated in the annual and regular sessions.
Legal matters at UNGA
During the 80th and 81st sessions of the Sixth
Committee, India actively participated in debates
on agenda items such as measures to Eliminate
international terrorism, the rule of law at national and
international levels, Criminal accountability of UN
officials and experts on mission, Protection of persons
in the event of disasters, Special Committee on Charter,
Universal Jurisdiction and Report of UNCITRAL.
During the year, the Indian delegation to the third UN
Ocean Conference in Nice, France was headed by MoS
(Earth Sciences). India also participated in the annual
session of the Special Committee on the UN Charter
and the Strengthening of the Organisation, held from
18 to 26 February. India also participated in the State
Parties Meeting of the UNCLOS in June.
An Indian delegation, headed by the Surveyor General
of India and comprising representatives from the
Department of Science and Technology, participated
in the Group of Experts on Geographical Names
and the Group of Experts on Geospatial Information
Management (GGIM) during October.
Economic and Social issues
The Economic and Finance Committee (Second
Committee) began its general debate and discussions
at the 80th session on 6 October, building on the
outcomes of the Fourth International Conference on
Financing for Development (FFD4), held from 30 June
to 3 July in Seville, Spain, which the Minister of Finance
attended. FFD4 was crucial for bridging the USD 4
trillion annual SDG financing gap and reaffirming
solidarity with developing countries through equitable
and inclusive growth. Building on the conference, the
Committee considered over 35 resolutions on various
agenda items, including macroeconomic policy,
sustainable development, and poverty eradication.
In the general debate of the Committee, India
highlighted its suggestions on multilateral solutions
for sustainable development over the next five years
to 2030. These include empowering women and
youth, deploying digital technology, fostering South-
South cooperation, and focusing on climate action in
a wider context of urgency, ambition, solidarity and
resource provision.
HLPF on Sustainable Development
The Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog represented India
at the High-level Political Forum on Sustainable
Development (HLPF) in July. This HLPF was special
for India since it presented its third Voluntary National
Review (VNR) alongside 34 other countries. The VNR
highlighted the country's progress and resilience
since 2020, a period marked by multiple global crises,
including the COVID-19 pandemic. It outlined India’s
achievements in Covid-19 and Pradhan Mantri Garib
Kalyan Anna Yojana, which promise food security for
800 million people. This VNR was prepared through
participatory discussions with all stakeholders,
including vulnerable sections of society. A side event
titled ‘SDGs: Keeping the Moment for Agenda 2030’
was organised on the sidelines of HLPF to highlight
India’s experience with SDG localisation. India also
participated in the decennial Third UN Conference on
Landlocked Developing Countries (LLDC3) from 5 to
8 August.

India-UNDP and IBSA Fund
The India-UN Development Partnership Fund was
established in 2017 with a USD 150 million budget.
The Fund operates under General and Commonwealth
Windows and caters to SIDS, LDC and LLDC. The
Fund provides end-to-end support, helping the host
government identify a sectoral need after which
the UN provides assistance in project formulation
and implementation, guided by the priorities and
approaches of the requesting Government. Projects
undertaken under the Fund cover diverse areas,
including health, education, livelihood development,
agriculture, etc. So far, the Fund has supported 89
projects in 67 countries with a budgeted outlay
of USD 89 million. The eighth anniversary of the
establishment of the Fund was commemorated at the
UN on 30 October. The annual event was attended by
a 13-member MP delegation from India, apart from
senior UN officials.
The India, Brazil, South Africa (IBSA) Fund, which
caters to the Global South, was established in 2004
and became fully operational in 2006. It has supported
48 projects in 38 countries at a total allocation of
USD 52 million to date. India assumed the Fund's
Chairmanship in 2025. Foreign Ministers of the three
countries met on the sidelines of High-Level Week
on 26 September in New York and took stock of the
activities of the Fund.
United Nations Convention on the
Laws of the Sea
In the wake of the adoption of the BBNJ Agreement
in 2023, India participated constructively in the
second session of the PrepCom (18-29 August) at
the UN Headquarters in New York, focusing on the
operationalisation of key governance mechanisms.
These financial and technical mechanisms will
underpin the treaty’s implementation. The Indian
delegation emphasised the importance of ensuring
equitable
participation,
capacity-building
and
technology transfer for developing States, and
safeguarding the principle of the common heritage of
humankind while facilitating sustainable use of marine
biological diversity beyond national jurisdiction.
In line with India’s consistent position, it stressed that
financial rules and the design of subsidiary bodies
must reflect the special needs and circumstances
of developing coastal States, and that the Clearing-
House Mechanism and benefit-sharing arrangements
are structured to support meaningful inclusion
and transparency. India reaffirmed its commitment
to ratification and to actively contributing to the
preparatory work of the first Conference of the Parties,
thereby reinforcing its role as a responsible maritime
State in the Indo-Pacific region and its support for
multilateral ocean governance.
International Day of Non-Violence
International Day of Non-Violence was commemorated
in the UN on 2 October. The event witnessed
participation of Permanent Representatives, senior
UN officials, and members of the Indian community.
International Labour Organisation
The Director General of the ILO visited India from 23 to
24 February to participate in the regional conference
under Global Coalition for Social Justice in New Delhi.
The 113th Session of the International Labour
Conference (113 ILC) was held in Geneva on 3-14
June. The Indian tripartite delegation comprising
representatives from Workers, Employers and the
Government, was led by the Minister of Labour and
Employment. The Minister addressed the 113 ILC
Plenary and participated in discussions of the Global
Coalition for Social Justice, a flagship initiative of
the ILO Director-General. The Minister met the ILO
Director-General and senior ILO officials, and held
bilateral meetings with Iran, Brazil, South Africa,
Germany, the US, and Switzerland on the sidelines of
the 113 ILC.
A side event focusing on India’s digital labour mobility
initiatives was organised during 113th ILC at the
Permanent Mission of India. During the event, the

ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
282
Minister of Labour and Employment underlined India’s
readiness to share digital initiatives such as e-shram
and E2E (Education to Employment) with the Global
South. This event saw participation of Labour Ministers
from Sri Lanka, Armenia, Rwanda and Kenya.
In March, Secretary (Labour and Employment) led the
Indian delegation to the 353rd session of ILO Governing
Body at ILO Headquarters, Geneva from 10 to 20
March. Later, the Secretary participated in the 355th
Session of ILO Governing Body at ILO Headquarters,
Geneva on 17-27 November.
On 16 September, India signed an MoU with ILO
to conduct a feasibility study on the International
Reference Framework for the classification of
occupations, a major outcome of the Employment
Working Group under India’s G20 Presidency. The
two-year study will focus on the development of a
standardised taxonomy and on informing policies on
recruitment, migration, education, and career guidance
in the green, digital, and care economies.
International Maritime Organisation
The Secretary General of the IMO Arsenio Domínguez
visited India from 19-21 February, where he visited the
Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA), participated
in the Green Shipping Conclave in Mumbai, and met
the Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. The
Secretary-General also met Secretary (West) in Delhi.
A significant development during the year was
discussion of reducing Green House Gases (GHG)
emissions from international shipping under the
IMO GHG Strategy. India remained actively involved
in the discussions on the establishment of market-
based mechanisms in this regard, during the Marine
Environment Protection Committee (MEPC) meeting
from 7-11 April.
A delegation led by Secretary (MoPSW) accompanied
by DG Shipping, participated in the 132nd session
of the IMO Council held at the IMO Headquarters
in London from 7-11 July. Being an election year
at IMO, the High Commission of India in London, in
coordination with the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and
Waterways, organised a networking reception at the
IMO headquarters to promote India’s candidature for
the IMO Council. The elections were held during the
34th IMO Assembly from 24 November to 3 December.
International Seabed Authority
As a State party to UNCLOS 1984, India is a member
state of the International Seabed Authority (ISA).
It is represented in the Council of the Authority as a
member of Group B and as a country that has made the
largest investments in preparation for and the conduct
of activities in the Seabed (Area), either directly or
through its nationals. India is also represented on
the Finance Committee and the Legal and Technical
Committee (LTC) of the Authority.
The Secretary General of ISA Letica Reis de Carvalho
visited India from 14-20 September, during which
she signed, on behalf of ISA, the second Polymetallic
sulphides exploration contract with India at the
Carlsberg Ridge in the Indian Ocean. This contract
made India the first ISA Member State to hold two
Polymetallic Sulphides (PMS) exploration contracts
and to have the largest area allocated by the Authority.
In commemoration of ISA's 30th Anniversary, the
eighth Annual Contractors Meeting of ISA was hosted
by India, and the Secretary General attended and
addressed the gathering.
India actively participated in the ISA Council session
(17–28 March) and the Assembly session (21–25
July) in Kingston, Jamaica, represented by delegations
from Permanent Mission of India to ISA in Kingston,
Ministry of Earth Sciences and Ministry of Mines. At
the Assembly Session in July, India was re-elected
to the ISA Finance Committee, reflecting trust in its
commitment to institutional governance. India also
participated in the Special 30th Anniversary High-
Level Commemoration of the ISA where it reaffirmed
its commitment to UNCLOS, the principle of the
Common Heritage of Humankind, multilateralism, and
responsible deep-sea governance.

International Organisation of
Migration
Additional Secretary (EP&W) participated in the 15th
Global Forum for Migration and Development on 2-4
September in Riohacha, Colombia.
India participated actively in the 116th Session of the
International Organisation for Migration (IOM) Council
in Geneva (8-10 December), highlighting migration's
role in development and emphasising safe, orderly,
and regular migration pathways, with the Ministry
delivering a statement stressing alignment between
development and migration policies for smart
outcomes. The session, titled ‘Aligning Development
Policy for Smarter Migration Outcomes”, featured
discussions on IOM's strategic direction and the
importance of global frameworks such as the Global
Compact for Migration.
UN Office for Disaster Risk
Reduction
The Principal Secretary to Prime Minister led a
delegation of senior officials from Ministry of Home
Affairs (MHA) and National Disaster Management
Authority (NDMA) to participate in the eighth Session
of the Global Platform for Disaster Risk Reduction from
2-6 June. On the sidelines of the Global Platform, the
Permanent Mission of India organised a High-Level
UNDRR-BIMSTEC event titled ‘Accelerating Sendai
Framework Implementation in BIMSTEC Countries’ on
5 June.
World Meteorological Organisation
Secretary-General of the World Meteorological
Organisation (WMO) Celeste Saulo visited India in
January, where she joined the Prime Minister and
other dignitaries at the 150th anniversary celebrations
of the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD).
The Director-General (DG) of IMD received the
prestigious UN Sasakawa Award 2025 for Disaster
Risk Reduction on the sidelines of the Global Platform
2025 in June.
The DG of IMD led a delegation that attended
the WMO Extraordinary Session of Congress and
Executive Council held from 20-24 October.
UNEP
An Indian delegation led by MoS (KVS) attended the
seventh session of the United Nations Environment
Assembly (UNEA-7), held from 8-12 December at the
United Nations Office at Nairobi (UNON). MoS (KVS)
met Cabinet Secretary for Environment of Kenya
Deborah Mlongo Barasa, Norwegian delegation led
by Minister of Climate and Environment of Norway
Andreas Bjelland Eriksen, and Deputy Minister of
Natural Resources and Environment of the Russia
Dmitri Tetenkin. UNEA-7 adopted India’s resolution
titled ‘Strengthening the Global Response to the
Management of Wildfires’ along with 10 other
resolutions. Furthermore, the Indian delegation
participated in the 37th Meeting of the Parties (MOP)
to the Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete
the Ozone Layer, including the high-level segment,
held in the UN Office at Nairobi from 3-7 November.
Ramsar Convention
The 16th Conference of Parties to Ramsar Convention
(COP16) was held in Victoria Falls, Zimbabwe. The
Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
led the Indian delegation and India’s resolution of
‘Promoting Sustainable Lifestyles for the Wise Use of
Wetlands’ was adopted at COP16.
At the 64th meeting of the Standing Committee of the
Ramsar Convention in Gland from 20-24 January, for
the first time, two Indian cities, Udaipur and Indore,
were recognised as Ramsar wetland-accredited cities.
The number of Ramsar Sites designated in India has
increased to 93.
Convention on International Trade in
Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and
Flora
A delegation led by Director General (Forests)
participated in the 68th session of the Standing
Committee in Geneva in February. Later in the year,

India will participate in the 20th Conference of the
Parties (CoP20) to the Convention on International
Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora
(CITES), scheduled to be held from 24 November to 5
December in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.
Basel, Stockholm and Rotterdam
Convention
The Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate
Change (MoEFCC) participated in the high-level
segment of the 17th meeting of the Conference of
the Parties to the Basel Convention, the 12th meeting
of the Conference of the Parties to the Rotterdam
Convention and the 12th meeting of the Conference of
the Parties to the Stockholm Convention in Geneva on
30 April and 1 May.
An inter-ministerial delegation led by Additional
Secretary (MoEFCC), along with representatives from
the Ministry of Agriculture, Department of Chemicals,
and Central Pollution Control Board, participated in
the negotiations of the Conference of Parties to Basel,
Stockholm and Rotterdam Conventions.
Second part of fifth session of
Intergovernmental Negotiating
Committee on Plastic Treaty (INC 5.2)
The resumed fifth session of the Intergovernmental
Committee on Plastic Treaty was held in Geneva
on 2-14 August. An inter-ministerial delegation
comprising MoEFCC (lead), Department of Economic
Affairs, Department of Chemicals and Department of
Commerce participated in the negotiations.
Minamata Convention
The sixth Conference of the Parties to Minamata
Convention was held from 3 to 7 November. An inter-
ministerial delegation comprising of the Ministry of
Environment, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare,
and Department of Chemicals participated in the
negotiations.
Bonn Climate Conference
The 62nd Session of the Subsidiary Bodies (SB62)
was held in Bonn, Germany, from 3 to 13 June. The
meeting discussed key issues, including climate
finance, adaptation, and the global stocktake. India
took part in all major discussions and highlighted the
importance of equity, climate justice, and support for
developing countries. The outcomes of SB62 will help
prepare for the decisions to be taken at COP30.
COP30
The 30th Conference of the Parties (COP30) was held in
Belém, Brazil on 10-21 November. India’s delegation
was led by the MoS (KVS). The COP30 focused
on several issues, including adaptation, modalities
of the global stocktake on the just transition work
programme, Baku to Belem Roadmap, gender action
plan, technology implementation programme and
response measures. India continued to call for fair and
balanced outcomes, with a focus on increasing means
of implementation for developing countries.
UN-Habitat
India attended the second session of the Open-
ended Intergovernmental Expert Working Group on
Adequate Housing for All, held from 22-23 October
at the United Nations Office at Nairobi (UNON).
Elections
India’s performance in elections at the UN and related
international organisations is listed below:
(i)
India got elected to the Governing Council of
Asian and Pacific Centre for the Development of
Disaster Information Management (APDIM) for
the term 2025-27.
(ii)
India got elected to the Asian and Pacific Training
Centre for Information and Communication
Technology for Development (APCICT) for the
term 2025-27.
(iii) India got elected to the Governing Council of
Statistical Institute for Asia and the Pacific (SIAP)
for the term 2025-27.
(iv) India got elected to the Governing Council
of
Centre

Agricultural
Mechanisation (CSAM) for the term 2025-27.

UN Human Rights Council
India continued its engagement and participation
in Human Rights Council (HRC) Sessions held in
2025, and in related human rights mechanisms and
processes. This includes the 58th (24 February – 4
April), 59th (16 June – 9 July), and 60th (8 September –
8 October) sessions of the Human Rights Council, and
37th Special session of the Council on deteriorating
human rights situation in the Democratic Republic of
Congo (DRC). India also participated in the 48th and
49th sessions of the Working Group on the Universal
Periodic Review (WG UPR) (20-31 January and 28 April
- 9 May) and other inter-sessional meetings organised
under the Council’s mandate. During the UPR working
groups, India engaged constructively with countries
under review and made recommendations on human
rights issues.
After two consecutive terms as a member of the
Human Rights Council, India took a break from council
membership and participated as an observer. As an
observer at the Council, India continued to underscore
its commitment to the Right to Development, technical
assistance, and capacity-building cooperation among
UN Member States. It actively engaged in interactive
debates, negotiations on human rights-related
resolutions, and other formal and informal activities
during the session.
During the 59th session, India was a member of the
core group of the resolution on ‘Access to Medicines’,
which was passed by consensus. India also co-
sponsored annual HRC Resolutions on the Right to
Development and human rights, and on unilateral
coercive measures, as part of the group of Non-Aligned
Movement countries. India also joined joint statements
by groups of countries at the HRC Sessions, including
on various thematic issues of importance, such as
health, women and children, education, etc.
The Permanent Mission of India organised side events
on India’s perspectives on Human rights during
the 58th HRC session on 13 March, which saw the
participation of Chairman of the National Human
Rights Commission, and on Gender Equality and
the Right to Development during the 60th session of
the HRC on 12 September, along with the Special
Rapporteur on the Right to Development. The events
were well received and attracted participation from
delegations of several member States.
India also co-sponsored the Portugal led resolution
titled ‘Question of the realization in all countries

of economic, social and cultural rights’ during the
58th session in March; Resolution on ‘Civil Society

titled ‘Promoting and protecting economic, social

India was elected to the Human Rights Council
for the 2026-28 term. It has always been on the
Council except for mandatory breaks, reflecting

UNAIDS
The Programme Coordinating Board (PCB) of UNAIDS
is the governing body responsible for setting policies
and priorities, and overseeing the budget, for the
global response to HIV/AIDS. India has been an active
partner in UNAIDS, contributing to global efforts
through its successful national HIV/AIDS programmes.
In December, India was elected as a member of the
UNAIDS PCB for the term 2026–2028.
World Health Organisation
In a landmark decision, the World Health Organisation
(WHO) member States adopted the Pandemic Treaty
during the 78th World Health Assembly (WHA
78). India played a constructive role in the drafting
of the Treaty, especially regarding provisions for
operationalisation of an equitable response to
pandemic emergencies.
Secretary (MoHFW) led a delegation in the 78th World
Health Assembly (WHA 78) in Geneva on 20-28 May.
At WHA78, India was conferred the Certificate of
Elimination of Trachoma as a Public Health Problem
by the Director-General (DG) of the WHO Tedros
Adhanom Ghebreyesus.
India organised two side-events on the sidelines of
the WHA78, one on Universal Health Coverage on 20
May with Secretary (MoHFW) and Health Ministers of
Malaysia, Bahamas, Zanzibar (Tanzania) participating
as speakers, and another on Traditional Medicine on
23 May which had speakers from WHO, WHO Global
Traditional Medicine Centre (GTMC), Ministry of
Ayush, Ministry of Health of Sri Lanka, Malaysia, and
Bolivia.
This year, WHO member states also adopted the
WHO Traditional Medicine Strategy for the period
2025-2034. India collaborated with WHO to advance
the Global Traditional Medicine Agenda. India and
WHO signed an MoU to develop a Traditional
Medicine module under the International Classification
of Health Interventions (ICHI) on 24 May.
This year, India also hosted the WHO–IRCH
(International Regulatory Cooperation for Herbal
Medicines) Workshop on Herbal Medicine Safety and
Regulations from 6-8 August.
India hosted the second WHO Global Summit on
Traditional Medicine in New Delhi from 17–19
December, reinforcing our leadership in evidence-
based traditional, complementary and integrative
medicine (TCIM). Anchored by the Ministry of AYUSH,
the summit’s theme, ‘Restoring Balance for People and
Planet’, aligned with the World Health Organisation’s
Traditional Medicine Strategy 2025–2034. A major
outcome was the launch of the WHO Traditional
Medicine Global Library, a 1.5-million-record digital
repository. India’s extensive AYUSH ecosystem was
showcased alongside policies that integrate AYUSH
into public health, strengthen regulation, research,
digitisation, and quality assurance, and advance global
confidence, access, and sustainability in traditional
medicine.
India actively participated in the meetings of the
Intergovernmental Working Group (IGWG), which
is negotiating the Annexure to the WHO Pandemic
Agreement on Pathogen Access and Benefit Sharing.
India has been voicing the concerns and priorities of the
Global South, especially regarding equity provisions
in the meeting. The two IGWG meetings were held on
9-10 July (IGWG1) and 6-10 October (IGWG2).

International Telecommunication
Union
Building on the successful hosting of the World
Telecommunication
Standardisation
Assembly
2024 (WTSA-24) at New Delhi on 15-24 October
2024, India continued its steady engagement with
International Telecommunication Union (ITU).
This year, the Department of Telecommunications
(DoT) signed two Letters of Intent (LoIs) with the
ITU, focusing on advancing AI-driven digital twin
technologies and a PhD-level research partnership
in February. India also hosted the third ITU-T Focus
Group meeting on Artificial Intelligence Native for
Telecommunication Networks (FG-AINN) in New Delhi
from 11-13 June, with participation from Indian and
international experts. This Focus Group addressed the
changes needed in network architecture to harness
the potential of AI fully.
As a Member of ITU Council, India actively
participated in ITU Council 2025 held on 17-27
July in Geneva. India also presented its proposal to
host the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference in 2030. In
October, DoT and ITU jointly organised ‘AI for Good
– Impact India Conference 2025’ and ‘Robotics for
Good Youth Challenge India 2025’, during the India
Mobile Congress 2025 held in New Delhi. Lastly,
India presented its candidate for the post of Director
of the ITU Radio-communication Bureau (2027–
2030), for which elections will be held during the ITU
Plenipotentiary Conference in 2026 in Doha.
UN Tourism
India was nominated as a member of the UN Tourism
Executive Board for the period 2025-2029 during the
60th meeting of the UN Tourism Commission for South
Asia held in Jakarta in April. India is currently a member
of the UN Tourism Executive Council for the period
2021-2025 and has proposed its candidature to the
Council at the UN Tourism General Assembly meeting
scheduled for November 2025 in Saudi Arabia. India
has been actively contributing to UN Tourism not
only as a member of the Executive Council but also
as a member of the Program and Budget Committee
and Committee on Affiliate Membership. In the 60th
meeting of the UN Tourism Commission for South
Asia, India was also renominated as Vice Chair of the
Commission.
India participated in the 123rd Executive Council
Session of UN Tourism held in Spain from 29-30
May. The Council reviewed the work for the preceding
year and established its programme of work for
the next year. The Council has nominated the new
Secretary General and examined UN Tourism’s
financial requirements for 2026-27. India renewed its
commitment to UN Tourism in fulfilling its mandate
and reiterated its commitment to safe and sustainable
tourism and building resilience in the tourism sector.
International Committee of the Red
Cross
PMI attended the first State consultation of Workstream
on the theme ‘Upholding International Humanitarian
Law in the Use of Information and Communication
Technologies (ICTs) during Armed Conflict’ under the
Global Initiative to Galvanise Political Commitment
to International Humanitarian Law (Global Initiative),
held on 15 May. The ICT Workstream aims to foster
shared understanding of the limits that IHL imposes
on the use of ICTs during armed conflict, with the
overarching goal of protecting civilian populations
from harm.
UN High Commissioner for Refugees
India participated in the 76th annual session of the
Executive Committee (ExCom) of UNHCR in Geneva
on 6-10 October. India renewed its commitment
to UNHCR in fulfilling its mandate. It reiterated the
view that the safe, speedy, and sustainable return of
displaced persons and refugees to their homes is the
best long-term solution to address refugee influxes.

UN Institute for Training and

The arrangement between the Ministry of Defence
and UNITAR concerning the assignment of experts
was signed by both parties in September. Under this
arrangement, at UNITAR’s request, India has seconded
a senior officer from the Indian Air Force as the Team
Leader, Military Pillar, at UNITAR.
Universal Postal Union
Secretary (Posts) visited Switzerland in February to
attend the meetings of UPU’s Council of Administration
and Postal Operations Council. Later in the year, India
won candidacies to the Postal Operations Council
and the Council of Administration for the term 2026-
29 during elections held on the sidelines of the UPU
Congress in Dubai on 18 August.
UNECE
Though India is not a member of United Nations
Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE), it is a
party to the Customs Convention on the International
Transport of Goods under Cover of TIR Carnets (TIR
Convention, 1975) under UNECE. A delegation led
by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
participated in 91st Session of WP-1 Global Forum for
Road Traffic Safety meeting from 15-19 September
and in 130th Session of Working Party on General
Safety (GRSG) on 6-9 October both in Geneva.
An Indian delegation led by the Joint Secretary
(CBIC) participated in the Working Party meeting as
part of the Customs Convention on the International
Transport of Goods under Cover of TIR Carnets

The 81st Commission Session of UNESCAP (81CS)
was held from 21-25 April at UN Conference Centre,
Bangkok, on the theme ‘Regional cooperation for
resilient and sustainable urban development in Asia
and the Pacific.’ A side-event was also organised on

National Centre for Ocean Information Services

500,000 contribution to the Trust Fund for Tsunami,
Disaster, and Climate Preparedness as a one-time
grant.
During the 81CS, elections were held for Governing
Councils of four Regional Institutions of UNESCAP
(APCICT, APDIM, CSAM, SIAP), in which India received
highest number of votes amongst all contestants in
each of the four institutions and was declared elected
to membership of the Governing Councils.

actively pursued India’s interests at UNESCO. India’s
commitment to education and cultural preservation,

The Permanent Representation of India to the UN
Rome-based Agencies (RBAs) of the Food and

for Agricultural Development (IFAD), and the World

and collaboration with both member countries and

Notable achievements and milestones of India at
the FAO included India’s unanimous re-election to
the FAO Council for the 2026–2029 term, as well as
the Minister of Agriculture and Alternate Permanent

being
unanimously

India was also elected to the International Steering
Committee of the Global Framework on Water
Scarcity in Agriculture (WASAG). India successfully
chaired and finalised the CFS policy on Strengthening

served as the Convenor for List B countries for the

and support of member states in India’s leadership
and its commitment to inclusive multilateralism.

reform agenda was launched to make the organisation
fit for purpose and future-ready. The Mission actively
participated and made substantive contributions,

developed in partnership with WFP, such as supply
chain optimisation, Annapurti Grain ATM, SMART

PMI and FAO signed an MoU for the refurbishment
and modernisation of the iconic ‘India Room’ at FAO

India in August and discussed issues related to food
security, humanitarian relief, capacity building, as well

On 21 July, a team comprising nine scientists led by a

Swedish research vessel R/V Skagerak from Reykjavik,
Iceland to the East Greenland Sea. The Ministry also

with officials from the Conservation of Arctic Flora

An Indian delegation-led by Indian Navy’s Rear
Admiral participated in the Arctic Frontiers Conference
and related engagements in Norway from 29 January
to 7 February. The visit included meetings with key
Arctic stakeholders, including the Arctic Council, the
Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Arctic
Economic Council, UiT – The Arctic University of Norway,
Kongsberg Satellite Services, and the Norwegian
Polar Institute. Discussions focused on enhancing
India’s participation in Arctic Council Working Groups,
strengthening cooperation in polar research, maritime
security, space applications, education, and industry
collaboration, and exploring new opportunities
in renewable energy, bioprospecting, and climate
security. The visit reaffirmed India’s commitment
to active and constructive engagement in the Arctic
region.
Later in the year, an Indian delegation-led by Indian
Navy’s Rear Admiral participated in the Arctic Circle
Assembly on 16-18 October. A session titled ‘Role
and Importance of Global South in the Arctic’ was
organised and moderated by the Indian delegation.
Two scientists from NCPOR and two officials from the
Ministry of AYUSH also participated. The delegation
also held bilateral meetings on the sidelines of the
Assembly.
At the Arctic Security Conference 2025, experts
discussed evolving power dynamics and governance
in the Arctic amid growing geopolitical rivalry and
climate challenges. The Indian delegation highlighted
India’s scientific engagement with the Arctic since
2007, emphasising the interlinkages between the
Arctic, the Himalayas, and the Indian monsoon, and
noting that ‘science is the currency’ of India’s Arctic
engagement. The delegation also underscored
that Arctic security extends beyond geopolitics to
encompass human security, traditional livelihoods,
and sustainable development, in line with India’s
Arctic Policy 2022. The delegation emphasised
India’s role as a bridge between the Global North
and South, advocating dialogue, multilateralism,
and collaborative climate research. A representative
from the Indian Naval War College reaffirmed India’s
commitment to peaceful engagement, maritime
cooperation, and science-driven participation in Arctic
governance and security.
The team of Indian scientists at Ny-Ålesund visited
Oslo and held meetings with the Indian Embassy.
The six-member delegation was led by an NCPOR
Scientist, who briefed officials on India’s research
activities in Ny-Ålesund. Appreciating the support
received from Kingsbay and the Norwegian authorities,
they elaborated on ‘Himadri’ (India’s research station
at Ny-Ålesund, Svalbard), especially after India
decided to deploy scientists year-round, including in
winter from December 2023.
Kimberley Process
The Kimberley Process is an international certification
scheme established in 2003 to ensure that rough
diamond exports are conflict-free and to prevent trade
in conflict diamonds. India is a founding member of the
Kimberley Process and plays a significant role as one
of the world’s largest diamond-cutting and polishing
centres. India was elected as the Vice-Chair (2025) /
Chair (2026) on 9 December.

South Africa assumed the G20 Presidency on 1
December 2024. At the first Sherpa meeting, held from
9–11 December 2024, the Presidency highlighted its
overarching focus on Africa’s development agenda,
strengthening support for the developing economies
of Africa and the Global South, and building on the
achievements of the Indonesian, Indian, and Brazilian
G20 Presidencies. Under the overarching theme of
‘Solidarity, Equality, Sustainability’, South Africa has
identified four key priorities:
(i)
Strengthening disaster resilience and enhancing
response mechanisms.
(ii)
Ensuring debt sustainability in low-income
countries.
(iii) Mobilising finance for a just energy transition.
(iv) Harnessing critical minerals to promote inclusive
growth and sustainable development.
India participated actively across G20 engagements
in 2025 under the South African Presidency,
contributing to consensus-building on geopolitical
and development issues, strengthening focus on
countering terrorism and its financing, and reinforcing
the centrality of the development agenda, including
Africa-focused priorities and the continuity of
outcomes from India’s G20 Presidency.

India ensured a high level of participation during
the South African G20 Presidency to meaningfully
contribute to the outcomes. Ministerial representation
was provided at several G20 Ministerial meetings

the Minister of Culture, MoS (PM), MoS (Commerce
and Industry), and the Principal Secretary to the Prime
Minister.

G20 Presidency, held on 20–21 February. During

BRICS has emerged as a useful platform for
consultations on a range of issues of common interest

Global South Cooperation for a More Inclusive and

Leaders’ Framework Declaration on Climate Finance;

Prime Minister participated in the Outreach Session of the 51st

Asia Cooperation Dialogue (ACD)
JS (Sports-Development) led the Indian delegation for

Disarmament & International Security

C H A P T E R
15
India actively participated in multilateral forums on
disarmament, non-proliferation, and international
security, while considering its national security
interests and priorities in this arena. During 2025,
India held bilateral engagements and presented its
perspectives in regional forums on these issues. India’s
contributions underlined its longstanding commitment
to the goal of universal and non-discriminatory
nuclear disarmament and to supporting global peace
and security in areas such as space, maritime security,
and non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction,
while responding to the evolving international security
environment and initiatives by various countries.
First Committee of the United
Nations General Assembly (UNGA)
India participated constructively and presented its
principled positions and views on disarmament and
international security matters at the 80th session of
the First Committee of the United Nations General
Assembly (UNGA) in New York from 8 October to 7
November.
The 80th UNGA First Committee adopted four
resolutions annually tabled by India. Resolutions
on ‘Measures to prevent terrorists from acquiring
weapons of mass destruction’ and ‘Role of science
and technology in the context of international security
and disarmament’ were again adopted by consensus
by the Committee. India’s two other resolutions in the
First Committee, ‘Convention on the Prohibition of the
Use of Nuclear Weapons’, which calls for negotiations
on an international Convention for prohibiting the use
or threat of use of nuclear weapons, and ‘Reducing
Nuclear Danger’, which calls for immediate steps to
reduce the risk of intentional or accidental use of nuclear
weapons, were also adopted by a broad support of
the UN member States. A total of 63 resolutions were
adopted during the 80th First Committee.

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
300
Conference on Disarmament (CD)
The Conference on Disarmament (CD) adopted a
Program of Work for 2025, based entirely on the one
adopted for the 2024 session, which was based on
the Indian proposal presented at the beginning of
2024 during its Presidency of the CD. The subsidiary
bodies discussed all core agenda items of the CD,
including nuclear disarmament, prevention of nuclear
war and all related matters, prevention of an arms race
in outer space, international arrangements to assure
non-nuclear weapon states against the use or threat
of use of nuclear weapons, and new types of weapons
of mass destruction and transparency in armaments.
United Nations Disarmament
Commission (UNDC)
The UNDC held its annual substantive session in
New York from 7 to 25 April. The session was the
second year of the ongoing three-year cycle that
began last year. The two working groups discussed
nuclear disarmament and the security implications of
emerging technologies. India actively participated in
the UNDC meetings.
Chemical Weapons Convention
(CWC)
India continued to play an active and constructive role
in advancing the objectives of the Organisation for the
Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW), including
the implementation of the Chemical Weapons
Convention
(CWC)
across
chemical
weapons
destruction, industry verification, national measures,
and international cooperation.
India participated constructively in the 30th Conference
of State Parties and the 109th and 110th sessions
of the Executive Council at The Hague, which
evaluated the Convention’s implementation and the
OPCW’s activities over the previous year and set out
future priorities for the OPCW. India presented its
perspectives on matters relating to the Convention
and its implementation, especially on the industry
verification and inspection regime. India fulfilled its
obligations under the Convention during the year
and extended support to the OPCW for the smooth
conduct of scheduled inspections of chemical facilities
in India.
India contributed to the OPCW’s capacity-building
activities through courses on developing analytical
and laboratory skills, conducted by the Indian Institute
of Chemical Technology (IICT) in Hyderabad in
collaboration with the OPCW Technical Secretariat.
Through this programme, 144 participants from 54
different State Parties were trained.
India hosted the 23rd Regional Meeting of National
Authorities on 1-3 July, bringing together 38
participants from 24 State Parties. At this forum,
India actively engaged with regional counterparts
to exchange best practices on national legislation,
inspection regimes, oversight of dual-use chemicals,
and capacity-building initiatives.
Biological & Toxin Weapons
Convention (BTWC)
India actively participated in the sessions of the
Working Group on Strengthening of the BTWC from
11 to 22 August and 8 to 12 December, and the
annual Meeting of States Parties to the BTWC from 15
to 17 December. During the meetings, India outlined
its priorities, including strengthening the Convention,
enhancing national implementation, promoting efforts
in response and preparedness, reviewing international
developments in the field of science and technology,
international cooperation and assistance in general,
and establishing a scientific review mechanism under
the BTWC. The international conference on ‘50 Years of
BWC: Strengthening Biosecurity for the Global South’
was organised by the Ministry to commemorate the
50th anniversary of the entry into force of the BTWC in
New Delhi on 1-2 December. It saw participation from
over 80 countries’ representatives from the Global
South, as well as panellists from different regional
and international organisations. It was highlighted as
a mark of India’s commitment to and contribution to
the strengthening of the Convention.

India also continued its annual submissions to the

During the year, India’s efforts to showcase the

A seminar was co-organised with the Ministry of
