Non-Proliferation Matters and
Strategic Export Control Regimes
India engaged with relevant mechanisms of the UN
on specific matters relating to the non-proliferation
of weapons of mass destruction and associated
developments of the DPRK and other UNSC
Committees and Panels.
Under India’s WMD Act 2005 and its Rules, the
various Advisory Committees held review meetings
on policy, implementation, and other relevant issues
during the year.
India
engaged
as
a
member
of
multilateral
export control regimes towards the goals of non-
proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and
their delivery systems, related materials, equipment
and technologies. This included sharing of best
practices or implementation experiences in the area
of export controls; participation in the development/
amendment of guidelines for export controls and lists
of materials, equipment and technologies regulated
under the Missile Technology Control Regime (MTCR),
Wassenaar Arrangement (WA) and Australia Group
(AG), and harmonising India’s national export control
list (SCOMET) with that of these regimes and the
Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG).
India participated in the Australia Group (AG) Inter-
sessional meeting (January - February) at Bucharest
and the AG Plenary (40th Anniversary) meeting (July)
at Sydney, the Experts Group and the General Working
Group meetings of Wassenaar Agreement (April, May,
September and October) at Vienna, and the Missile
Technology Control Regime (MTCR) Technical Experts
meeting (April) at Berlin, related to consultations on
evolving the control lists and best practice guidelines
of the respective export control regimes, as well as
information exchange on implementation experiences,
technological developments, proliferation trends, and
addressing these issues as they emerge.
The Ministry continued to contribute to the export
licensing processes of the Inter-Ministerial Working
Group (IMWG), led by the Directorate General of
Foreign Trade (DGFT) for export-controlled dual-use
items under India’s Special Chemicals, Organisms,
Materials, Equipment and Technologies (SCOMET)
list, as well as by the Department of Defence
Production (DDP) for export of Category 6 (Munitions
List) military items of SCOMET and by the Department
of Atomic Energy for export of nuclear-related items.
Further, the Ministry continued working with DGFT
to streamline the licensing process for certain
categories of dual-use items, taking into account the
item of export, end use, end user, and destination,
among other things, and moving towards enhanced
digitalisation of the licensing process and integration
with relevant agencies. The Ministry also engaged
with the enforcement mechanisms and agencies,
including the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and
Customs (CBIC) and its organisations, in the context
of our national non-proliferation objectives.
The Ministry, together with its partners, including the
DGFT, DDP, CBIC, various industry chambers, and
other stakeholders, conducted outreach activities
throughout the year to raise awareness of India’s
strategic export controls. Along with the focus on
region- and sector-specific outreach programmes that
have continued over the last few years, there was also
a thrust on reaching out to start-ups, micro, small,
and medium enterprises, academic and research
institutions, etc., through the relevant organisations.
In this regard, the Government of India (DGFT, the
Ministry, and relevant agencies), in partnership with
various industry bodies and other stakeholders, has
been organising the National Conference on Strategic
Trade Controls (NCSTC), which, since 2024, has
been restructured from earlier editions into a unique
format. This annual NCSTC (2025 edition was held
at Bengaluru in January) focuses on India’s strategic
trade control system and international best practices,
comprising wider participation of- the Government
agencies concerned, industry and other stakeholders
across

sectors,
international
speakers

This year the NCSTC was attended by over 600

International Atomic Energy
Agency (IAEA)
The Director General of the IAEA Rafael Grossi visited
India from 18 to 20 March. During his visit, he met
EAM and attended the Raisina Dialogue, where he
spoke on ‘Energy Access, Affordability and Security’.
He inaugurated the SN Bose Building of the Global
Centre for Nuclear Energy Partnership (GCNEP) and
introduced a certificate course on nuclear engineering.
The Director-General also visited the Kakrapar
Atomic Power Station. He concluded the visit to the
Tata Memorial Centre (TMC) in Mumbai by signing
an MoU recognising TMC as an IAEA Rays of Hope
Anchor Centre. The MoU strengthens India’s global
role in cancer care, research & training through nuclear
medicine.
EAM met Director General of the IAEA Rafael Mariano Grossi
on the sidelines of the Raisina Dialogue 2025 in New Delhi,
March 2025
India participated in the 69th session of the IAEA
General Conference, held in Vienna on 15-19
September, as well as in the Board of Governors
meetings held in March, June, September, October
and November. At these meetings, India contributed
to deliberations on nuclear safeguards, the peaceful
uses of nuclear energy, technical cooperation, nuclear
security, and safety-related issues. India and the
IAEA deepened cooperation in the peaceful uses of
nuclear energy, including through the IAEA’s flagship
programs.
India’s Global Centre for Nuclear Energy Partnership
(GCNEP) collaborates with the IAEA and various
partner countries to build capacity in areas such as
advanced nuclear energy systems, nuclear security,
the application of radioisotopes and radiation
technologies, radiological safety, and nuclear material
characterisation.
Civil Nuclear Cooperation
India engaged with various countries in the field of
nuclear power generation and other peaceful uses of
nuclear energy, including radioisotope applications in
medicine. GCNEP entered into an MoU with Tanzania
(August) for cooperation in the field of peaceful uses
of nuclear energy, along with a Declaration of Intent
to establish a partnership on SMRs/AMRs with France
(February).
India also continued to contribute to mega science
projects
involving
various
partners
towards
scientific research, including through its Associate
Membership of the European Organisation for Nuclear
Research (CERN), its partnership of the International
Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER), the
Square Kilometre Array Observatory, and with the
US on the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave
Observatory (LIGO) and Proton Improvement Plan-II
projects.
Outer Space Matters
India continued to participate actively and present
its perspectives on matters related to outer space at
the Conference on Disarmament, as well as meetings

of the United Nations Committee on the Peaceful

bodies. As Chair of the Working Group on the Long-

continued to closely engage with UN Member States

goal of a safe and responsible use of outer space.
The adoption, by consensus, of the group’s report by
COPUOS in June is an important achievement.
India participated in the sessions of the Open-Ended
Working Group on the Prevention of an Arms Race
in Outer Space, constituted following UN General
Assembly Decision 79/512, from 7 to 11 April and
from 21 to 25 July in Geneva.
India continued to implement the provisions of the
Hague Code of Conduct (HCoC), including pre-launch
notifications for India’s ballistic missile and space
launches and the submission of annual declarations to
the arrangement. India participated in the 24th Annual
Regular Meeting of the HCoC held at Vienna on 4-5
June.
Maritime Security Affairs
As an important stakeholder in maritime security in
the Indo-Pacific region and globally, India maintained
active engagement with countries and multilateral
organisations. India expanded engagement at the
Information Fusion Centre Indian Ocean region (IFC-
IOR), where various countries posted liaison officers,
including the first representative of the Djibouti Code
of Conduct, to enhance mutual understanding and
cooperation in the maritime domain.
India participated in the inaugural workshop to
establish the DCoC working group on operational
cooperation and coordination at sea. The eighth
DCoC–Jeddah Amendment (DCoC-JA) High-Level
Meeting was held in Mauritius from 12-14 November.
India participated virtually in the G7++ Friends of the
Gulf of Guinea Working Group on Education, Training
and Exercises on 31 July.
India continues to be an active member of ReCAAP
and contributes to the construct as an important
maritime security stakeholder in the region. The former
Additional Director General of the Indian Coast Guard
was elected as the Executive Director of the ReCAAP
Information Sharing Centre (ISC) for the years 2025-
2028. India also participated in the ReCAAP ISC
Capacity Building Senior Official Meeting held in
Thailand from 25-29 August.
India participated virtually in the Contact Group on
Illicit Maritime Activities (CGIMA) Strategic Session,
held in the margins of the 53rd SHADE Meeting in
Bahrain on 23 October. India was actively involved in
the deliberations on the strategic vision for the new
group.
India continued to actively engage with the Co-
operative Mechanism on the Straits of Malacca and
Singapore (SOMS), the Aids to Navigation Fund (ANF)
Committee in the Straits of Malacca, and other fora.
Since its establishment, India has continued to make
financial contributions, totalling USD 481,484 to date.
India participated in the 32nd ANF committee meeting
at Singapore on 6-7 May. The 33rd ANF Committee
meeting, being hosted by Singapore, was held on 5-6
November.
In addition to the above, India has also continued
to engage with the Indo-Pacific region to build and
enhance maritime resilience through the QUAD
Maritime Security Working Group (QMSWG). India
attended the QMSWG meeting in Tokyo, Japan, on 3-4
April, during which the Indian delegation proposed
several initiatives to strengthen collaborative efforts
among QUAD partners to enhance maritime security
in the Indo-Pacific region.
Dialogue with other countries
India held separate maritime security dialogues during
the year with the EU (in New Delhi on 21 March), Japan
(in Tokyo on 2 April), Norway (inaugural dialogue was
held in Oslo on 11 September), and Greece (inaugural
dialogue was held in Athens on 11 December)
to exchange assessments of maritime situations,
perspectives about the developments in areas of

interest, cooperation opportunities and strengthening

ASEAN REGIONAL FORUM (ARF)
MoS (PM) participated in the 32nd ARF in Kuala
Lumpur, Malaysia, on 11 July, and the Secretary (East)
represented India at the ASEAN Regional Forum Senior
Officials’ Meeting (ARF SOM) on 11 June at Kuala
Lumpur, Malaysia. India attaches great importance
to the ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF), as it provides
a vital platform for promoting dialogue, building
confidence, and advancing cooperative security in the
Indo-Pacific region. Through sustained engagement
in ARF Events, India contributed to capacity-building,
humanitarian assistance, disaster relief, and maritime
security initiatives.
During the year, India actively participated in the 16th
ARF ISM on Maritime Security, co-chaired by China and
Cambodia, held in Beijing, China on 24-25 April. India
shared perspectives on maritime security, including
successes achieved by its maritime security agencies,
and noted that they work independently and with
like-minded partners in the region. Additionally, India
advanced the agenda of the 26th ASEAN Regional
Forum (ARF) Ministerial Meeting and, through a multi-
ministerial delegation, delivered training to support
the formulation of a Best Practices Manual on the
International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS)
Code, which was completed in July.
Later in the year, India participated in the 13th
Expanded ASEAN Maritime Forum (13th EAMF)
at Port Dickson, Malaysia on 11 September. India
briefed the participants on its approach to the
region as encapsulated by its vision articulated in
MAHASAGAR-Mutual and Holistic Advancement for
Security and Growth Across Region, reflecting our
commitment to building a safe, secure and sustainable
maritime domain and tangible efforts taken towards
fulfilling our commitment towards ASEAN’s Master
Plan on Connectivity 2025. Meaningful initiatives and
concrete steps aimed at conserving and preserving
the marine environment continue to be supported,
including active support to UNEA Resolution 5/14,
signing agreement on BBNJ and recognising IUU as a
significant threat to marine biodiversity, regional food
security and the livelihood of millions who depend on
coastal and oceanic resources were also highlighted
in the forum.
ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF) and
ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting
Plus (ADMM-Plus)
Raksha Mantri led India’s participation at the 12th
ADMM-Plus meeting in Malaysia from 30 October
to 1 November, during which he delivered a speech
reflecting on the 15th year. In his speech, Raksha
Mantri reaffirmed India’s emphasis on the rule of law
and freedom of navigation. He added that overflight
in the Indo-Pacific is not directed against any country
but aimed at safeguarding the shared interests of
all regional stakeholders. He underlined that India’s
strategic engagement with ASEAN is long-term and
principle-driven, grounded in an open, inclusive and
non-coercive Indo-Pacific. He highlighted inclusivity
and sustainability as core to regional security, linking
defence cooperation with economic development,
technology sharing and capacity building. Stressing
India’s readiness to deepen cooperation through
dialogue and practical initiatives, Raksha Mantri said
India would continue to contribute constructively
under the vision of MAHASAGAR to promote regional
peace, stability, and collective security.
Conference on Interaction and Confidence
Building Measures in Asia (CICA)
Secretary General of CICA Kairat Sarybay paid a visit to
India on 18 March and met with the Secretary (West),
Joint Secretary (Disarmament and International
Security Affairs), and Joint Secretary (Counter
Terrorism). India is a Member State of CICA, and
during the meetings, there was a thorough exchange
of views on the growing role of CICA as an effective
tool of multilateral diplomacy, the significance of its
proposed gradual transformation into a full-fledged
international organisation, and India’s engagement
with various CICA initiatives. India participated in the

Informal CICA Ministerial Meeting held in New York
on 25 September.
India also attended and shared its perspectives at
various CICA events, such as ‘Conference on the
Development of the Transport and Logistics Potential
of the CICA Member States’ (May), ‘Intermodal
transportation as a factor in ensuring the economic
growth of the CICA Member States’ (May), CICA

Fellowship Programme on
Disarmament and International
Security Affairs
As part of India’s commitment to promote disarmament,
non-proliferation and arms control education and to
equip young diplomats with knowledge and skills in
these fields, the Sushma Swaraj Institute of Foreign
Service, in collaboration with the Disarmament and
International Security Affairs Division, organised the
fifth edition of the Disarmament and International
Security Affairs Fellowship for foreign diplomats from
13–31 January. It saw the participation of diplomats
from 33 countries. The initiative fulfils the mandate
of the UNGA Resolution ‘UN study on disarmament
and non-proliferation education’. It is in line with the
focus on ‘Disarmament Education’ in the UN Secretary
General’s Agenda for Disarmament ‘Securing our
Common Future’.
India-UN Capacity Building
Programme on UNSC Resolution
1540 and strategic trade controls
India supported the UNSC 1540 Committee’s mandate
and its work (on weapons of mass destruction-related
non-proliferation), wherever possible, by offering to
share knowledge and technical expertise in various
areas as part of the Committee’s assistance framework.
In this context, India (CBIC, the Ministry and relevant
Government agencies), in partnership with the United
Nations Office for Disarmament Affairs (UNODA),
organised the first-ever Capacity Building Programme
of its kind on the UNSC Resolution 1540 and Strategic
Trade Controls (STC) for relevant Government officials
from 8 Asia-Pacific Countries at the National Academy
of Customs, Indirect Taxes and Narcotics (NACIN)
Palasamudram in February.
Speakers and experts from the UNSC 1540
Committee and UNODA, relevant Government of
India agencies, and members of Indian industry shared
their implementation experiences and best practices
on pertinent aspects of UNSC Resolution 1540
and the STC. In view of the excellent feedback and
appreciation received from the UN and international
participants, this programme would be conducted
annually, sponsored by India under the ITEC
framework, and its second edition would be organised
for more countries from the Asia-Pacific and Africa.
This unique and flagship programme is a reaffirmation
of India’s robust credentials on non-proliferation and
a further demonstration of India’s contribution to the
international non-proliferation architecture.

Economic Diplomacy

Economic Diplomacy
C H A P T E R
16
Overview
The Economic Diplomacy (ED) Division is the economic
wing of the Ministry of External Affairs and works in
close coordination with Indian Missions and Posts
abroad, territorial divisions of the MEA, ministries
and departments of the Government of India, State
Governments and foreign missions and posts in India.
During the year, the ED Division played an important
role in advancing India’s economic diplomacy through
high-level business engagements, flagship investment
summits and outreach activities in collaboration with
line ministries, industry chambers, export promotion
councils, territorial divisions of the Ministry and Indian
Missions abroad. It further handled issues related to
energy security, healthcare, registration of companies,
processing of foreign direct investment proposals,
air services agreements, social security agreements
and engaged with multilateral organisations and
institutions such as UNCITRAL, the Permanent
Court of Arbitration, the International Solar Alliance,
the Coalition of Disaster Resilient Infrastructure, the
Global Biofuels Alliance and the partnership between
India, Israel, the United Arab Emirates and the United
States (I2U2).
Trade and Investment
To bolster the promotion of trade, tourism and
technology as key pillars of India's economic
diplomacy, the ED Division, in coordination with Indian
Missions and Posts abroad, strived to enhance India’s
trade and investment activities. These activities were
aimed at expanding bilateral trade and foreign direct
investment values, presence of Indian entities abroad,
sectoral trade shares, export expansion priorities,
challenge mitigations, innovative initiatives and
budgetary support across various funds.
Export Promotion Mission
The Export Promotion Mission (EPM) launched by the
Government of India was strengthened through five

creator: PDFium

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
308
region-wise high-level Export Promotion Workshops
conducted during November and December, with
participation from Indian Missions abroad, Export
Promotion Councils and Industry Bodies. The ED
functioned as a key coordination division between
Indian Missions and the Department of Commerce for
the EPM Workshops.
Promotion of Indian Coffee Abroad
ED Division, in collaboration with the Coffee Board
of India, undertook efforts to promote the export of
Indian coffee abroad. It coordinated with Missions and
Posts abroad to organise market intelligence studies,
coffee cupping sessions and seller delegations for the
export of Indian coffee.
Foreign Direct Investment
The ED Division was the nodal division in the Ministry
for processing foreign direct investment cases. It
played a facilitative role in processing such cases,
working with DPIIT, Invest India, state investment
agencies and Indian Missions abroad. India witnessed
a significant increase in foreign direct investment
during the first quarter of FY 2025-26 compared to FY
2024-25, amounting to USD 18.62 billion.
Acquisition of Critical Minerals Abroad
ED Division coordinated India’s international efforts
on critical minerals and facilitated collaboration with
the Ministry of Mines. The Division collated and
circulated information on investment opportunities
aligned with the National Critical Minerals Mission
and strengthened partnerships with Africa, Australia
and Latin America.
Internationalisation of Indian
Rupee (INR), SRVA & LCSS
Promoting the international use of the Indian Rupee
helps reduce foreign exchange risk, boost trade in
INR, and strengthen India’s economic sovereignty.
The introduction of Special Rupee Vostro Accounts
(SRVAs) and Local Currency Settlement Systems
(LCSS) has advanced this vision.
Local Currency Settlement System (LCSS)
The LCSS framework has a wider coverage and
includes all current account and permissible capital
account transactions between the partner countries.
Entering into LCSS arrangements would help further
internationalise the INR. India has signed LCSS
agreements with four countries: the UAE, Indonesia,
Mauritius, and the Maldives. Further to this, currently
the LCSS arrangement process has been initiated
with Qatar, Kuwait, South Africa and Kenya. Similar
arrangements are under consideration with Tanzania
and Nigeria.
Special Rupee Vostro Accounts (SRVAs)
ED Division coordinated with DEA and RBI to facilitate
SRVA operationalisation. The ED Division also
engages with Indian missions abroad to explore the
interest and readiness of partner banks and promote
INR trade settlements with strategic regions. Many
countries have shown positive interest in trade
settlement using mutual currencies.
The RBI has removed prior approvals (the earlier
requirement) for Authorised Dealer banks to open
SRVAs of correspondent banks, to enable invoicing,
payment, and settlement of imports/exports in INR.
Several foreign banks have since opened SRVAs with
banks in India, and the RBI has also signed MoUs
with some Central Banks to encourage cross-border
transactions in local currencies. These measures are
aimed at promoting ‘Ease of Doing Business’ and
boosting exports. As of now, Special Rupee Vostro
Accounts (SRVAs) are operational in 34 countries.
UPI apps
Acceptance of Indian UPI apps through QR codes has
been enabled in
Bhutan, France, Mauritius, Nepal, Singapore, Sri Lanka
and UAE. Indian tourists travelling to these countries

can use their UPI apps to make payments at merchant
locations.
NIPL has signed an agreement with Qatar National
Bank (QNB), the largest financial institution in the
Middle East and Africa, headquartered in Qatar, to
launch QR code-based Unified Payments Interface
(UPI) payments across the country. Implementation of
this project is in progress. An MOU has been signed
with the Maldives.
Tourism Expansion Activities
ED Division, in collaboration with state tourism
departments,
undertook
initiatives
to
boost
international tourism. An event was organised by
FICCI in July on medical value tourism. In February,
the ED Division participated in the International
Health Dialogue, chaired by Minister of Health and
Family Welfare and the EAM. In August, the ED
Division participated in the meeting of the Budget
Estimate Committee 2025-26 on medical tourism,
where discussions revolved around policy incentives,
infrastructure development and measures to position
India as a global hub for affordable and high-quality
healthcare, including initiatives such as Heal in India
and Heal by India.
Health and Medical Value Travel
To increase medical value tourism in India, specific
suggestions and inputs were shared with the Ministry
of Health on region-specific demand from tourists. ED
Division coordinated meetings on India–Saudi Arabia
investment and exports in the pharmaceutical sector
in January. Efforts were also made to get the Indian
Pharmacopoeia recognised in various countries. Indian
Pharmacopoeia was being accepted and recognised
as a drug standard in seventeen countries of Latin
America, the Caribbean, Africa and the Pacific regions.
Higher Educational Institutes (HEIs)
Abroad
ED Division supported the setting up of IITs abroad
under the New Education Policy through coordination
with the Ministry of Education and the IIT Council.
MoUs were entered into with the UAE for IIT Delhi,
which opened its campus in Dubai, and with Tanzania
for IIT Madras, which opened its campus in Zanzibar.
Both IIT campuses started their operations. Efforts
were underway to open IIT campuses in other
countries.
Energy Security
ED
Division
facilitated
engagements
between
line ministries and energy agencies, including the
International Energy Agency and the International
Renewable Energy Agency. The division is also a part
of the group of line ministries, involved in pursuing the
bilateral energy dialogues and improving institutional
ties with various countries. ED Division, in coordination
with the Ministry of Power and the Ministry of
Petroleum & Natural Gas, is working closely with the
International Energy Agency’s Secretariat towards
attaining India’s membership in the International
Energy Agency.
Major Events Supported or
Facilitated by ED Division (2025)
India Maritime Week 2025
India Maritime Week 2025, held from 27-30 October,
witnessed participation from ministers of twelve
countries: Singapore, the Netherlands, Norway,
Sweden, Italy, Sri Lanka, Mauritius, Myanmar, the
Maldives, Saudi Arabia, Liberia, and Antigua and
Barbuda. Ministers participated in the IMW inaugural
session, ministerial plenary, the Prime Minister’s
session on 29 October and various discussions.
Bilateral meetings were held with the ministers of
the Netherlands, Saudi Arabia, Sri Lanka, Myanmar,
Norway, Italy and Singapore, focusing on cooperation
in
maritime
connectivity,
port
development,
shipbuilding, logistics and blue economy.

ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
310
Prime Minister attended the Global Maritime Leaders Conclave
and chaired the Global Maritime CEO Round Table, October
2025.
MoS (KVS) attended the event on 29 October and
participated in the Global Maritime Leaders Conclave
and the Global Maritime CEO Round Table, chaired by

ministerial plenary and other engagements involving
partner countries. ED Division, MEA provided active
support and coordinated the foreign engagement
component of the IMW, both in the run-up to and
during the event.
Start-up Mahakumbh
In Start-up Mahakumbh 2025, ED Division supported
and facilitated the participation of foreign ambassadors
at the precursor event on 6 March, and supported
international linkages, stakeholder engagement, and
collaboration during the main event on 3-5 April.
World Food India 2025
World Food India 2025, the flagship international
event organised by the Ministry of Food Processing
Industries to position India as a ‘Global Food Hub,’
was held on 25-28 September. The ED Division
worked closely with MoFPI to facilitate international
participation in the event.
Advantage Assam 2.0 and North-East
Investors Summit
ED Division also supported state-level investment
summits, including Advantage Assam 2.0, held on
25–26 February, and the North-East Investors Summit
on 15 April. The Division facilitated the participation of
Foreign Missions at these events, enabling diplomatic
outreach and enhancing international investment
opportunities in the states.
Vibrant Gujarat Ambassador Roundtable
On 4 September, the ED Division supported the
Ambassador roundtable for the forthcoming Vibrant
Gujarat
Summit,
facilitating
participation
and
engagement of foreign resident Missions in New Delhi
to promote investment and partnership opportunities.
Market Expansion Activities
Under the ‘Market Expansion Activities’ budget, the
Ministry allocated financial resources to its Missions
and Posts abroad to advance India’s objectives in trade,
tourism and technology and to enhance the global
visibility of Indian business and industry. These funds
enabled Missions to respond to trade and investment
inquiries, assess economic and business environments
in their host countries and undertake market
intelligence and sectoral studies. They supported the
organisation of business seminars, trade promotion
events, investment roundtables and networking
sessions with local chambers of commerce, industry
associations and key stakeholders. For the current
year, the ED Division allocated INR 9 crore towards
these activities across various Missions and Posts
worldwide.
Industrial Outreach, Investment
Promotion and Publicity
During outgoing and incoming high-level visits,
the ED Division mounted and organised business
engagements to deepen trade and investment
linkages. A business delegation accompanied the
Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji to Slovakia on 9-11 April.
During the State Visit of Prime Minister of Mauritius
Navinchandra
Ramgoolam
to
India
on
9-16
September, the Division organised the India-Mauritius
Business Conclave in Mumbai on 10 September and a
business event in Varanasi on 11 September.

Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji addressed the Slovakia-India Business

A business interaction with Prime Minister of Sri
Lanka Harini Amarasuriya, was held in New Delhi on
16 October, with the participation of leading Indian
chambers. Within India, the Division supported
major investment and sectoral events, including

with the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
for the Ambassadors’ Roundtable on 27 August
and India Maritime Week 2025 on 27-31 October
(Mumbai) to promote international engagement in
the maritime and logistics sectors. The Division also
worked closely with the Ministry of Mines on the
National Critical Mineral Mission for securing supplies
and technologies in coordination with Indian Missions
and global stakeholders. Through these initiatives, the
Division significantly deepened international economic
engagement and promoted India’s profile as a trusted
global trade and investment partner.
Investment Treaties
India was actively engaged with various countries
in negotiating investment treaties based on the new
model BIT of 2015. India was negotiating investment
treaties with over 15 countries. The MEA was a
member of the Inter-Ministerial Group and an integral
part of BIT negotiations, and provided requisite inputs.
The ED Division is the nodal division in the Ministry
of External Affairs for investment treaty and related
matters, and it actively participated in investment
treaty negotiations. It coordinated negotiations and
provided requisite inputs from a policy, political and
international law perspective. Correspondence about
BIT with other countries was routed through the
Ministry by means of Notes Verbale, etc.
India faced close to 40 investment treaty-related
claims. The cases were at various stages, including
some cases where awards had been rendered. There
were close to 51 dispute notices by investors against
India, of which India won four arbitrations, lost three
arbitrations, resolved fourteen disputes amicably and
had over six active disputes. ED Division, as part of
the Inter-Ministerial Group of the Government of India,
was actively involved at every stage of the disputes
by providing necessary inputs, facilitating hearings
and coordinating other related actions in these cases
in foreign jurisdictions. These cases were before
international tribunals seated abroad and involved
questions of international law where the advice of
the Ministry was sought. In 2025, one new notice of
dispute was served on the Republic of India.
Social Security Agreements (SSAs)
Social
Security
Agreements
were
bilateral
arrangements between India and partner countries
that safeguarded the social security rights of workers
moving across borders. These agreements addressed
issues of ‘no coverage’ and ‘double coverage’ under
social security systems, ensuring equal treatment for
the workforce of both nations. SSAs offered tangible
benefits to Indian professionals and skilled workers
abroad by exempting them from dual social security
contributions, allowing the totalisation of contribution
periods across both countries and enabling the
exportability of benefits upon relocation or return to
India.
The Ministry of External Affairs served as the
competent authority for negotiating and concluding
these agreements, in coordination with the Ministry
of Labour and Employment and the Employees’
Provident Fund Organisation, which functioned as the
liaison agency for implementing SSA provisions.

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
312
India concluded 22 Social Security Agreements
and negotiations were underway with more than
20 additional countries to further expand this
network. Together, these efforts underscored India’s
commitment to promoting safe, orderly and mutually
beneficial labour mobility, while ensuring the long-
term social protection and welfare of Indian workers
overseas.
Civil Aviation
The ED Division is the nodal division in the Ministry
for all matters relating to Air Services Agreements
with foreign countries and airlines, and worked closely
with the Ministry of Civil Aviation on these matters.
The Division also provided inputs on these issues and
on the requirements of flight operations or code share
to promote tourism and to strengthen bilateral and
multilateral relations.
ICAO engagements
The elections for the ICAO Council were held during
the 42nd Assembly Session in September. ED Division
extended support for the ICAO elections, including
an engagement with resident ambassadors on 2
September, with the objective of maximising support
for India’s candidature in the ICAO Council elections.
India was re-elected to Part II of the ICAO Council
by securing more votes than in the 2022 elections,
reflecting growing confidence among member states
in its leadership and commitment to international civil
aviation. The ICAO audit was a significant milestone
for India’s civil aviation sector. Representing the MEA,
the ED Division ensured comprehensive responses
to all queries raised during the audit. Key issues
related to international standards and practices were
addressed, including efforts to demonstrate India’s
commitment to meeting global aviation norms.
Wings India
An international event dedicated to the civil aviation
sector, the event brought together global leaders,
policymakers, regulators, airline executives and
industry stakeholders. ED Division closely coordinated
with the Ministry of Civil Aviation in facilitating high-
level ministerial conferences, CEO forums, exhibitions,
and B2B/G2B/G2G meetings.
Bilateral talks on air service matters were held
with China, Indonesia and Kuwait on capacity
enhancements, designation of new carriers, increase
of points of call and addition of new routes with a
view to improving connectivity and economic activity.
Arbitration Cell
The Arbitration Cell in the ED Division handled
various legal issues, including numerous arbitrations
and litigations such as investment treaty disputes
and related court proceedings, investment treaty
negotiations, and work related to UNCITRAL and
the Permanent Court of Arbitration. Apart from this,
the Division handled various other commercial legal
issues and legal aspects pertaining to the International
Solar Alliance and the Coalition for Disaster Resilient
Infrastructure.
There were over 40 disputes as of date where India had
been made a respondent State, and these investment
treaty disputes involving India were at various stages,
including some cases pending before arbitral tribunals
and certain other cases at an advanced stage of
enforcement of arbitral awards in various jurisdictions
across the world.
Inputs to Various Boards and
Committees
ED Division continued to actively serve on various
boards and committees, providing strategic inputs
on trade promotion, economic diplomacy and
international collaboration. These included the India
Trade Promotion Organisation, Invest India, the Indian
Institute of Foreign Trade, the Engineering Export
Promotion Council, the Project Export Promotion
Council, the Export Promotion Council for EOUs and
SEZs and Water and Power Consultancy Services
(India) Limited. Through these arrangements, the

ED Division facilitated alignment between India’s
foreign policy objectives and export growth initiatives,
contributing to enhanced global market access and
investment inflows.
I2U2 (India, Israel, the UAE and the
USA)
The I2U2 Group, comprising India, Israel, the United
Arab Emirates and the United States, represented
a forward-looking minilateral framework aimed at
strengthening economic and technological cooperation
among the four countries. The initiative sought to
promote joint investments in six mutually identified
priority sectors: water, energy, transportation, space,
health and food security, to mobilise private sector
capital and expertise to modernise infrastructure,
decarbonise
industries,
enhance
public
health
and support innovation in emerging and green
technologies.
During the year, the I2U2 partners continued regular
consultations to expand cooperation under this
framework, identifying new areas of collaboration and
reinforcing coordination on projects of mutual interest.
The grouping underscored the shared commitment
of the four nations to sustainable economic growth,
innovation and regional stability, leveraging their
complementary strengths to deliver tangible and
high-impact outcomes.
World Economic Forum (WEF)
ED Division extended support to India’s participation
in the World Economic Forum's annual meeting, held
on 20-24 January in Davos-Klosters, Switzerland,
under the theme ‘Collaboration for the Intelligent
Age.’ The Division coordinated with key participating
ministries – Skill Development and Entrepreneurship,
Education, Electronics and IT, Civil Aviation, Jal Shakti,
and Food Processing Industries – to project India’s
initiatives. The Division facilitated inter-ministerial
coordination, international outreach and follow-
up on India’s engagement at WEF, aligning India’s
external economic diplomacy with global priorities on
workforce readiness, human capital investment and
future skills development.
International Solar Alliance
The International Solar Alliance aimed to contribute
to the implementation of the Paris Agreement by
bringing together countries to address the main
obstacles in the massive deployment of solar energy
in terms of technology, finance and capacity. In 2025,
Angola, Vietnam and Mongolia signed the ISA
Framework Agreements. Instruments of Ratification/
Accession for ISA Framework Agreements were
received from Romania, Kuwait, Moldova, Dominican
Republic, Lebanon, Qatar, Luxembourg and Vietnam
during the year. In total, 126 countries have signed the
Framework Agreement of the ISA, out of which 112
have also ratified the Framework Agreement.
Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji delivered the keynote address at the eighth General Assembly of ISA in New Delhi, October 2025

ED Division, being the depository of ISA, coordinated
with the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (the
nodal ministry) and the ISA Secretariat and facilitated
the organisation of the eighth General Assembly of
ISA in New Delhi on 28 October. It was chaired by
the Minister of New and Renewable Energy and co-
chaired by Special Envoy for Climate Negotiations,
French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs Benoit
Faraco. Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji delivered the keynote
address. Secretary (ER) presented the Depository

was participation of over 30 ministers and vice-
ministers, and representatives of about 137 countries
and 36 organisations. During the Assembly, ISA
amended the Rules of Procedure of the Assembly,
thereby enabling prospective countries to become
members of ISA through accession.
Coalition for Disaster Resilient
Infrastructure (CDRI)
CDRI functioned as an inclusive multi-stakeholder
partnership where knowledge was generated and
exchanged on different aspects of disaster resilience
of infrastructure. The coordination efforts between
the ED Division and CDRI were intended to engage
additional members, countries and international
organisations, representing varied geographic and
socio-economic contexts, disaster risk profiles, as well
as capacities to mitigate and adapt to climate change
and disasters.
As of 29 October, the Coalition’s membership
had grown to 51 national governments and 10
international organisations. Costa Rica was the latest
country to join CDRI. India and France, as co-chairs
of the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure,
extended joint demarches to 14 countries in Africa and
South-East Asia, inviting them to join the Coalition.
CDRI organised its annual International Conference
on Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (ICDRI) 2025 on
6-7 June in Nice, France, under the theme ‘Shaping a
Resilient Future for Coastal Regions,’ which brought
together over 300 participants from 53 countries,
including 49 representatives from 20 Small Island
Developing States. The Conference played a pivotal
role in advancing global dialogue on building resilience
in coastal regions, with a special focus on small island
developing states, supporting their efforts to address
climate-induced hazards while promoting economic
stability and ecological sustainability.
Global Biofuels Alliance (GBA)
The Global Biofuels Alliance, a multi-stakeholder
alliance, was launched during India’s G20 Presidency
by Prime Minister, along with leaders of eight other
countries
(Argentina,
Bangladesh,
Brazil,
Italy,
Mauritius, Singapore, the UAE and the USA) on 9
September 2023 as the chair’s initiative. GBA intended
to address challenges related to feedstock availability,
developing policy frameworks, streamlining biomass
supply chains and encouraging financing and
investment in biofuel production, including promoting
clean cooking. GBA worked towards defining common
technical standards, quality standardisation and
uniform certification to encourage global uptake of
biofuels.
Since its launch, GBA has made considerable progress,
expanding membership to 32 member countries
and 14 international organisations. This expansion
represented endorsement of GBA’s role in the biofuels
sector by the international community.
On 11 October 2024, the Government of the
Republic of India and GBA signed the Host Country
Agreement, facilitating GBA to set up its physical
Secretariat in India and provide necessary legal status
to GBA, including immunities and privileges under the
United Nations (Privileges and Immunities) Act, 1947.
The HCA entered into force on 23 November 2024
after completion of internal legal procedures by both
parties.
United Nations Commission
on International Trade Law
(UNCITRAL)
The ED Division participated in the UNCITRAL
General Assembly session and in the six UNCITRAL
Working Groups. In July, UNCITRAL held its 58th

Annual Commission Session, which was attended by
representatives of the ED Division and the L&T Division,
of this Ministry. In this session, the Commission
finalised work on (i) the draft convention on negotiable
cargo documents, (ii) a draft toolkit for expedited asset
tracing and recovery in insolvency proceedings and (iii)
draft background notes on asset tracing and recovery
in insolvency proceedings. Between September and
December, all six working groups resumed discussions
on outstanding legislative documents.
Under Working Group I on Warehouse Receipts,
UNCITRAL finalised and adopted the UNCITRAL-
UNIDROIT Model Law on Warehouse Receipts, and
approved in principle the draft guide to enactment
in 2024. The Commission is expected to formalise
further discussions on the topic as the agenda of the
working group was achieved in 2024.
Under Working Group II on Dispute Settlement,
which deliberated on UNCITRAL model clauses on
SPEDR, the Working Group finalised the clauses
along with draft explanatory notes and held a two-
day colloquium, after which it preliminarily considered
recognition and enforcement of electronic awards.
Under Working Group III on Investor-State Dispute
Settlement Reform, deliberations continued on
the draft statute of a standing mechanism for the
resolution of international investment disputes and
on procedural and cross-cutting issues; a multilateral
instrument on ISDS reform was also considered.
Under Working Group IV on Electronic Commerce,
the Working Group continued work on default rules
on data provision contracts under the mandate
given at UNCITRAL’s 55th session and reviewed the
guide to enactment of the UNCITRAL Model Law on
Automated Contracting.
Under Working Group V on Insolvency Law, the
Working Group adopted the text on asset tracing and
recovery in insolvency proceedings and a draft toolkit
for expedited asset tracing and recovery in insolvency
proceedings. The Working Group considered new
topics, including climate change and insolvency
proceedings.
Under Working Group VI on Negotiable Cargo
Documents, the Working Group adopted the
negotiable cargo documents instrument.
Permanent Court of Arbitration
The
Permanent
Court
of
Arbitration,
an
intergovernmental organisation headquartered at The
Hague, has had India as a member since 1950. India
had signed a Host Country Agreement with PCA in
2008 to set up a permanent facility in India. Steps
were taken towards opening a Permanent Regional
Facility of the PCA in India. Discussions on the
Memorandum of Understanding (which implements
the Host Country Agreement) between MEA and PCA
on the PCA regional facility were held during the year.
The handing over process of the PCA regional facility
is at an advanced stage.

Counter Terrorism
C H A P T E R
17
India has been at the forefront of global efforts to
counter terrorism. The topic of counter terrorism
found prominent mention in bilateral and multilateral
meetings at all levels during the year. India has Joint
Working Groups on Counter Terrorism (JWG-CT)
with 26 countries. India has also been engaging with
regional and multilateral bodies such as BIMSTEC,
G20, ASEAN Regional Forum, SCO, BRICS, EU, FATF
and the Quad on Counter Terrorism.
It was imperative for India to send a clear, strong and
resolute message after the Pahalgam terrorist attack
in Jammu and Kashmir on 22 April. Accordingly, India
responded through Operation Sindoor, hitting terrorist
infrastructure at nine sites in Pakistan and Pakistan-
occupied Jammu and Kashmir. India’s action through
Operation Sindoor was measured, non-escalatory,
proportionate and responsible. India’s approach
earned strong backing from the international
community and they supported India’s actions to
punish the perpetrators of cross-border terrorism as a
right to self-defence.
Bilateral Engagements (JWG on CT)
During the year, India held Joint Working Group
meetings on Counter Terrorism (JWG- CT) with Italy
(16-17 January), Tanzania (12-13 February), Egypt
(30 April), European Union (9 September), France (11
September), Uzbekistan (30 September-1 October)
Australia (Canberra, 29-30 October), Germany (New
Delhi, 27 November), USA (New Delhi, 3 December)
and Malaysia (New Delhi, 10 December).
Regional Engagements
During the year, India held two Working Group
meetings on Counter Terrorism (CTWG) with
multilateral groups including the BRICS and Quad
and one Senior Officials Meeting on Transnational
Crime (SOMTC) with the ASEAN.
ASEAN
India participated in the 12th ASEAN Senior Officials
Meeting on Transnational Crime (SOMTC)+India

Consultation held on 25 June in Putrajaya, Malaysia.
BRICS
India participated in the 10th Annual BRICS Counter
Terrorism Working Group (CTWG) Plenary and its
Sub-Groups’ Meetings held from 4-6 June in Brasília,
Brazil.
India and the USA held the 21st Meeting of the Joint
Working Group (JWG) on Counter Terrorism (CT) and the 7th
Designations Dialogue in New Delhi, December 2025.
European Union (EU)
From 13-15 October, India hosted the European Union
(EU), at the National Security Guard (NSG) campus in
Manesar, for a first-of-its-kind Joint Counter Terrorism
training program focused on emerging threats posed
by Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS).
Multilateral Engagements
NMFT
India participated in the fourth ‘No Money for Terror’
ministerial conference held in Munich, Germany on
13 February. India hosted the 3rd NMFT ministerial
conference in New Delhi on 18-19 November 2022.
FATF
The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Plenary and
Working Group meetings were held in Paris, France
from 17-21 February and FATF/MONEYVAL Joint
Plenary Week and Technical Assistance Peer-Learning
Meeting for Donors, Providers and the Global Network
were held on 10-14 June in Strasbourg, France.
India participated in the FATF Plenary and Working

EAG
India participated in the 42nd EAG Plenary Meeting
held on 29-30 May in Moscow, Russia.
India participated in the 43rd Plenary and Working
Group meetings of the Eurasian Group on Combating
Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism (EAG)
held in Minsk, Belarus from 24-28 November.
Quad
India hosted two Quad workshops/seminars on
‘countering use of unmanned aerial vehicles and

‘preventing terrorist exploitation of new and emerging

hosted the third Quad Counterterrorism Working Group
(CTWG) meeting and Table Top Exercise with QUAD
partners - Japan, Australia, and the United States of
America, in New Delhi from 4-5 December, as part of
India’s rotation to host the next QUAD Summit.
GCTF
India participated in the 25th Global Counter Terrorism
Forum (GCTF) Coordinating Committee Meeting and
its Working Group meetings, held from 20-22 October
in Doha, Qatar.

Development Cooperation
C H A P T E R
18
DPA I
Development partnership is an important pillar
of India’s foreign policy. India has been sharing
its resources, expertise, and skills with its partner
countries over the years. India’s model of development
cooperation is demand-driven and is strongly rooted
in the principles of non-interference and mutual
benefit. Government of India-supported Lines of
Credit have resulted in impactful projects of scale in
several countries across the neighbourhood, Africa,
and Latin America and the Caribbean. Lines of Credit
have played an important role in strengthening India's
partnership with countries in the Global South.
Lines of Credit
Lines of Credit (LoC), which are concessional loans
offered to partner countries, are governed by the
Indian
Development
and
Economic
Assistance
Scheme (IDEAS) of the Department of Economic
Affairs, Ministry of Finance, last amended in 2022.
This year saw the signing of new LoCs with Maldives,
Mongolia, and Mauritius.
In July, during the Prime Minister's State Visit to
Maldives,
an
Indian
Rupee-denominated
LoC
agreement was signed with Maldives. The credit
line of INR 4850 crore was extended to finance
various development projects in Maldives. This
marked the second Rupee LoC extended by India for
project financing under the Indian Development and
Economic Assistance Scheme (IDEAS), following the
first ever INR LoC signed with Mauritius in March
2025. The LoC funded a water pipeline replacement
project worth INR 487.60 crore. Additionally, during
the Prime Minister of Mauritius' State Visit to India in
September, a Special Economic Package, including an
INR LoC, was announced.
An additional LoC of USD 700 million to Mongolia
was signed in January to finance Package IV of
the Oil Refinery Project. This is the single-largest
project supported by India under IDEAS, with an
overall allocation of USD 1.692 billion. A composite

During Prime Minister’s State Visit to Bhutan in

Debt Relief
Demonstrating India’s continued commitment to assist
Sri Lanka in its economic recovery, India concluded the
debt restructuring process with Sri Lanka in April, with
the exchange of bilateral amendatory agreements.
During the State Visit of the Prime Minister to Maldives
in July, an amendatory agreement was signed to
enable a reduction in the annual debt repayment
obligations of Maldives to Exim Bank of India by
around 40 percent.
Projects completed/commissioned in 2025
India has completed several infrastructure projects in
partner countries across the globe. Some of the key
LoC projects completed this year include:
Guyana: Phase-I of the East Coast-East Bank
road linkage project (partially financed through a
Government of India-supported credit line of USD
50 million) was commissioned by the President of
Guyana on 30 June. EAM addressed the inaugural
ceremony through a video message. The East Coast-
East Bank linkage project is a vital arterial road that
will improve connectivity and provide a strong boost
to the infrastructural development in Guyana.
Nicaragua: A transmission line and substation project
under the Government of India-supported Line of
Credit of USD 31.29 million was commissioned on 24
September. MoS (PM) addressed the event through a
video message. The project provides reliable power
supply to the rural communities in Nicaragua.
Maldives: The Addu City development project, valued
at USD 160 million, was inaugurated during the State
Visit of the Prime Minister to Maldives in July. The
project includes the construction and upgradation of
more than 120 km of road network, installation of
CCTVs, street lighting, and a drainage system in the
city of Addu in Maldives.
Under a Fisheries Expansion Project valued at USD
21.98 million, a 50-tonne ice plant in Gemanafushi
was inaugurated in February. The facility includes a
100 MT storage capacity, further supporting the local
fishing industry.
The Hanimadhoo International Airport Project was
jointly inaugurated by the President of Maldives and
the Minister of Civil Aviation on 09 November. The
project valued at USD 132 million is expected to
further boost domestic as well as international air
connectivity of Maldives.
The Hanimadhoo International Airport, funded under India-
supported LoC worth USD 132 million was inaugurated in
Maldives, November 2025
Mauritius: The 8 MW solar plant at Henrietta Falls,
financed under an LoC of USD 7.52 million, was
handed over to Mauritius in March. The solar plant
is running at 120 percent capacity, contributing
significantly to Mauritius' renewable energy needs.
Cameroon: A Cassava Plantation Project, financed
under the Government of India-supported LoC of USD
42 million, was completed in April. The project further
strengthens food security in Cameroon.

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
320
Projects Under Implementation
This year, regular project review meetings, country-
level bilateral LoC review meetings, and bi-annual
portfolio reviews were conducted to actively monitor
LoC projects. These included: Bilateral LoC Review
Meetings and site visits to Maldives, Rwanda,
Bangladesh, Mauritius, Nepal, Tanzania, Mongolia,
Côte d’Ivoire, Lao PDR, Cuba, Guyana, Nicaragua and
ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development.
At the directive of Government of India, Exim Bank
appointed Lender’s Engineer for better monitoring
of projects in Bangladesh, Maldives, Mongolia,
Mozambique and Nepal.
Some of the major projects expected to be completed
over 2026 include the upgradation of airports in
Maldives; power transmission projects in Togo and the
Democratic Republic of Congo; irrigation and water
supply projects in Benin and Côte d’Ivoire; construction
of the forensic science lab project in Mauritius, etc.
Events
As part of India’s initiative to explore new and
innovative models of project financing abroad
including ‘Aid to Investment’ models, the Ministry
engaged a wide variety of stakeholders, including
public sector banks, NBFCs, companies, private equity
firms, CDRI, ISA, World Bank / MIGA, IFSCA, GIFT
City, NIIF, resident Missions in Delhi, Indian Missions
abroad etc. The most recent meeting, held in July in
Delhi, was chaired by Secretary (Economic Relations)
and was attended by more than 110 participants.
The inaugural conference of the Quad Ports of the
Future Partnership (PFP) was held on 29-30 October
in Mumbai on the margins of the India Maritime
Week (27-31 October). The Conference saw robust
participation from around 120 delegates from 24 Indo-
Pacific partner countries. Thematic panel discussions
centred on advancing a shared Quad vision for
resilient, secure and future-ready ports; strengthening
collaboration on infrastructure, financing, regulatory
frameworks, workforce development, technology,
digital ecosystems, cybersecurity and sustainability
were held. The conference officially launched the Quad
PFP – announced in the Quad Leaders’ Statement
in September 2024. The initiative aims to leverage
the Quad’s collective expertise to coordinate efforts,
exchange best practices, and mobilise public and
private investments towards quality port development
across the Indo-Pacific.
DPA II
Within the DPA, the DPA-II Division is designated
to carry out development partnerships through
capacity-building initiatives. Apart from the flagship
ITEC scheme (which provides fully funded training
opportunities at eminent Indian training institutions
for government professionals), DPA-II Division also
carries out capacity building initiatives in the form
of foreign deployment of Indian experts, IT-related
trainings through the establishment of Centres of
Excellence in IT (CEIT) projects, and the organisation
of artificial limb fitment camps.
During the year, DPA II Division implemented
capacity-building solutions for India’s developing
partner countries by delivering nearly 14,000
training opportunities to government and security
professionals from nearly 114 countries. As of
November, close to 4000 professionals have availed
themselves of these training opportunities. In addition
to training, the Division also conducted four artificial
limb fitment camps and administered the deployment
of experts abroad as part of its mandate.
Capacity Building through Indian
Technical and Economic Cooperation
(ITEC)
The ITEC scheme provides fully funded training
opportunities in eminent Indian training institutions
for government professionals-civilian, defence and
paramilitary, of the Global South countries. Courses
are offered both on a multi-country basis and on a
country-specific, customised basis.
With a robust domestic training landscape, ITEC offers
courses ranging from conventional development
subjects like agriculture and entrepreneurship to
advanced technology-oriented subjects like AI,
title: mea_annual_report
creator: PDFium

text:
Development Cooperation
321
biotechnology and cyber. Over the years, the ITEC
scheme has not only become a visible tool of India’s
bilateral diplomacy but also a recognised name in
the global capacity-building landscape. ITEC training
courses are designed as short, residential, immersive
programmes with both classroom and experiential
content, supplemented by cultural exposure to India’s
vibrant cultural landscape. Government professionals
interested in availing of ITEC training apply through
Indian embassies and must be nominated by their
governments to participate in these courses.
During the year, on the civilian side, a total of 250
menu-based/multi-country and more than 100 single-
country/customised courses have been approved for
implementation. These include courses for packages
like Sagar Amrut (for Pacific Island countries) and
the Quad Infrastructure Fellowship (for Indo-Pacific
countries).
Defence-related training for friendly foreign countries
(FFC) is provided under the Defence-ITEC modality.
On the defence side, 3900+ slots were offered under
Defence-ITEC modality in various defence courses
at the 100+ defence training institutes of the Army,
Navy, Air Force, and Coast Guard. These courses
are implemented in partnership with the Ministry
of Defence (MoD). In particular, 41 slots have been
offered to 33 countries for the prestigious, year-long
course on ‘National Security and Strategic Studies’
at National Defence College (NDC), New Delhi.
Similar high-value/defence management courses are
also provided at prestigious institutions such as the
College of Defence Management, Secunderabad; the
Defence Services Staff College (DSSC), Wellington;
the Military Institute of Technology (MILIT); and the
National Defence Academy (NDA), Pune.
An emerging aspect of the ITEC capacity building
involves training police and armed paramilitary
forces, particularly in neighbouring countries, through
a dedicated ITEC-Security programme. Under this
modality, administration of the course has been
both simplified for ease of participation and adapted
for meeting security protocols. High-value courses
at prestigious institutions like the National Police
Academy and National Security Guard (NSG) are
provided along with tactical courses at training
institutions catering to disaster relief, intelligence,
detective training, forensic analysis and border
management. In the current financial year, close to 38
courses are being conducted for training approximately
1000 force personnel.
In order to provide policy-oriented and experiential
training for senior-level officials, the DPA II Division
regularly organises high-value training courses
under the ITEC-Executive modality. During this year,
two courses in this format have been conducted to
date, with another three to four courses likely to be
conducted till March 2026. These include a joint
civilian and military course called the International
Strategic Engagement Programme (INSTEP) by NDC;
courses for wildlife and conservation practitioners at
Nagarhole and Bandipur Tiger Reserve through the
International Big Cat Alliance, and courses on human
rights by the NHRC.
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), in
partnership with the Ministry organised ITEC Executive
Capacity Building programme on human rights for senior-level
functionaries of NHRIs of the Global South, September 2025
To broaden the reach of the ITEC scheme, the ITEC-
Professional modality has been introduced to engage
regulated professionals in banking/medical/legal
and corporate/accountancy sectors. During this year,
Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI) was
onboarded to provide courses for company secretaries/
legal compliance officials.

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
322
Under the ‘India-UN Capacity Building Initiative for
Global South’, triangular format capacity building
courses are being implemented for countries of the
Global South in partnership with UN agencies active
in India and eminent ITEC partner institutes. This
initiative was formally launched in August with four
courses to be implemented by CDAC-New Delhi
(on health informatics), NIESBUD(on technical and
vocational education), NIFTEM (on food fortification)
and NSSTA (on census statistics).
In December, the ITEC program was expanded
by sanctioning 46 additional short-term civilian
courses. This update added 1,380 slots to the current
financial year. These included menu-based courses
as well as customised courses, based on the specific
requirements of the partner countries. With these
additions, the total approved ITEC courses for the
current year have reached 350 courses and 10,630
slots.
India’s sustained capacity building partnership over
the years has built a sizeable global alumni. Since its
inception in 1964, it is estimated that over four lakh
professionals have been trained under ITEC. A large
portion of this figure-close to 75,000-who have been
trained since 2014, remain active as alumni, and are
an important source of engagement for Missions. To
further our engagement with these alumni, missions
in ITEC partner countries commemorate ITEC Day
on or around 15 September each year. The Division
provides a dedicated amount for supporting ITEC
Day events/outreach. For this year, INR 4.39 crore
was sanctioned for 111 Missions towards ITEC Day,
while this year, INR 4.4 crore was sanctioned for 112
Missions (latest addition being Bolivia).
ITEC-Experts and ITEC-Onsite
Capacity building support abroad through foreign
deputation of Indian experts is also carried out by the
DPA II Division under the ITEC Scheme. In the current
financial year, experts deployed include: one professor
from Pondicherry University as Advisor to DG, Civil
Service College, Mauritius; and one professor from
Central Sanskrit University as a Sanskrit cum Hindi
faculty member at the University of Fiji. In addition,
requests are underway for the selection of a Vice
Chancellor to Atal Bihari Vajpayi Institute of Public
Service and Innovation, Mauritius; for a sugar industry
expert to Fiji and for AYUSH sector professionals to
Malaysia. Defence/military experts deployed abroad
include Indian Military Training Team (IMTT) teams
deployed in Seychelles and Uganda; Indian Army
Training Team (IATT) to Kazakhstan and Tanzania;
experts to Mauritius Gallery Range and Afloat Support
Team (AST)to Seychelles.
DPA II Division also provides capacity-building
support abroad through institutions via the ITEC-
Onsite modality. Conservation experts from Indira
Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA) are
being deployed in Laos PDR and Cambodia for the
assessment of damaged murals at important heritage
sites in these countries.
Other activities of the Division
In addition to the above, DPA II Division is the
administrative division for implementing Centre of
Excellence in IT (CEIT) projects, under which the
implementing agency C-DAC operates IT training
centres abroad; and the ‘India for Humanity’ scheme,
under which funds are provided to the implementing
agency Bhagwan Mahavir Viklang Sahayta Samiti
(BMVSS) for conduct of artificial limb fitment camps.
A total of 58 CEIT projects in 47 countries have been
implemented to date, with nearly two lakh trainees
being trained in subjects like high-performance
computing, AI/ML and big data. Currently, CEIT projects
are operational in Vanuatu, the Solomon Islands,
and Argentina. Training support is being provided
for centres in Jordan and Tanzania. C-DAC is also
supporting the upgradation of the CEIT established
in Kazakhstan. New projects are being considered for
implementation in Egypt, Benin, Paraguay, Suriname,
and Timor-Leste.
A total of 35 artificial limbs fitment camps, fitted
approximate 20,000 limbs, have been organised by
BMVSS under ‘India for Humanity’ programme in
the countries viz Vietnam, Myanmar, Malawi, Iraq,
Kathmandu, Egypt, Senegal, Tanzania, Namibia,

Development Cooperation
323
Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Syria, Uganda, Djibouti, Sri
Lanka, Equatorial Guinea, South Sudan, Fiji, Lebanon,
Cambodia, Palestine, Mongolia, Madagascar, and
Papua New Guinea. This year, camps were organised
in Afghanistan, Myanmar, Nicaragua, Mozambique
and Trinidad and Tobago.
DPA-III
Inspired
by
the
philosophy
of
‘Vasudhaiva
Kutumbakam’,
India's
international
development
cooperation has expanded significantly in recent
years in its geographical reach as well as in the
areas of cooperation. Given the focus of India’s
external engagement on its immediate and extended
neighbourhood, supported by the 'Neighbourhood
First' and 'Act East' policies, a majority of development
projects are being implemented in these regions.
As the Development Partnership Administration
(DPA) arm of the Ministry has gained experience over
the years, the sustainability of projects, besides project
delivery and implementation, has received increased
attention. India’s development partnership model has
received a high degree of acceptance from its partners
due to its demand-driven nature and the focus on
keeping the requirements and priorities of the partner
country at the heart of projects executed abroad.
India’s development partnerships have extended to
new areas of focus, such as Digital Public Infrastructure
(DPI), healthcare, public transport, renewable energy,
and small and medium enterprises, based on the
priorities of the partner countries involved. Further,
India’s developmental partnership portfolio continues
to intensify with new projects in the neighbourhood,
which also extends to Africa, Latin America and the
Caribbean region, West Asia and Oceania.
India’s development assistance has been a major
catalyst for the creation of much-needed infrastructure
in partner countries, such as railway links, roads and
bridges, waterways, border-related infrastructure,
transmission lines, power generation, hydropower
and also extends to socio-economic areas such as
healthcare, education, and housing.
IIFCL Projects Limited (IPL), a wholly owned subsidiary
of the Ministry of Finance (MoF), has been engaged
for setting up the Project Monitoring Unit (PMU) in
the Ministry. The Memorandum of Understanding
(MoU) between IPL and the Ministry was signed on
21 February for setting up the PMU, which will be
responsible for providing technical and administrative
support in the implementation of development
projects handled by the DPA Divisions of the Ministry.
Afghanistan
India has been a steadfast partner in reconstruction
and development efforts in Afghanistan despite
serious security challenges. The principal focus of
India’s development assistance to Afghanistan has
been to build the capacities of Afghan nationals and
their institutions for governance and delivery of public
service, develop socio-economic infrastructure, secure
lives and promote livelihoods.
Some of the key Indian projects in Afghanistan are the
Parliament Building in Kabul (2015), and the Afghan
India Friendship Dam, earlier known as Salma Dam
(2016), which underline India's commitment to the
rebuilding of a united, democratic and prosperous
Afghanistan. Both countries together launched the
'New Development Partnership' in September 2017
to further enhance India’s development assistance to
Afghanistan.
India supported High Impact Community Development
Projects (HICDPs) spread across all 34 provinces of
Afghanistan by extending grant assistance. Since
2005, three phases of community-based projects
funded by Indian grants and covering areas like
agriculture, education, labour, rural development and
public health have been implemented by the Afghan
government agencies, thus building local capacity
towards project management. Under Phases one
and two implemented during 2005-2009, USD 20
million was provided for undertaking 116 projects.
Under the third phase, launched in 2012, funding
of USD 100 million was provided for 420 projects,
of which 350 have been completed. At the 2020
Afghanistan Conference held in Geneva in November

2020, EAM announced the launch of the fourth
phase of HICDPs with grant assistance of USD 80
million for implementing around 100 new projects in
Afghanistan. India also supplied 75,000 MT of wheat
to Afghanistan as humanitarian assistance despite
challenges caused by COVID-19.
Support
for
education
and
capacity-building
programmes is an important aspect of India's
development partnership with Afghanistan. Under
the Special Scholarship Scheme for Afghan Nationals
(SSSAN) administered by the Indian Council for
Cultural Relations (ICCR), 1000 annual scholarship
slots are provided to Afghan students for studying
at universities and institutes across India. Since
2006, more than 10,000 Afghan students have been
trained under this scheme. In addition, another 500
scholarship slots are provided for children/dependents
of martyrs of the Afghan National Defence and
Security Forces and 614 fellowships for Agricultural
studies, administered through the Department of
Agricultural Research and Education and the Indian
Council of Agricultural Research.
India also supported the establishment of the
Afghanistan National Agriculture Sciences and
Technology University (ANASTU) in Kandahar, which
is the first university of its kind in Afghanistan, through
post-graduate courses for Afghan students. Online
teaching of the new batches of M.Sc. started from
30 April in Agronomy, Horticulture, Plant Protection,
Agricultural Economics, and Livestock Production
& Management. Till date, seven batches in four
courses of Agronomy, Horticulture, Plant Protection,
and Animal Husbandry have been completed under
the ANASTU programme. India extends support
for scholarship programmes to students presently
enrolled in Indian Universities. As part of the ongoing
healthcare cooperation with Afghanistan, India gifted
15 Basic Life Support (BLS) and five Advanced Life
Support (ALS) ambulances to Afghanistan as a special
gesture. A symbolic handover of five ALS ambulances
was done by EAM following his meeting with the
Foreign Minister of Afghanistan Amir Khan Muttaqi on
10 October in New Delhi.
Myanmar
India is executing two major road connectivity
projects in Myanmar, which aim to strengthen
regional connectivity by building the road network
between Myanmar and the North-Eastern States
of India. Under the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit
Transport Project (KMMTTP), an international port has
been built at Sittwe in Myanmar. The stretch of the
Kaladan River connecting Sittwe Port with Paletwa
has been developed for navigation, and an Inland
Water terminal has been established at Paletwa.
Sittwe Port was inaugurated in May 2023 and is now
operational. However, due to the ongoing security
situation, inland waterways from Sittwe to Paletwa
are not in operation. Operation and Maintenance
(O&M) operations at Sittwe Port are currently being
undertaken by India Ports Global Limited (IPGL),
a wholly owned subsidiary of the Ministry of Ports,
Shipping and Waterways, since April 2024. Work is
also ongoing to build a road between Paletwa and
Zorinpui on the India-Myanmar border.
India has supported the implementation of the
India-Myanmar-Thailand (IMT) Trilateral Highway,
including the upgrade of the Kalewa-Yagyi road
section and the 69 bridges (Tamu-Kyigone-Kalewa
section). Once completed, the Trilateral Highway
will provide seamless connectivity for the North
Eastern states of India with Myanmar, Thailand and
other ASEAN countries and facilitate the movement
of goods and traffic. Besides, the connectivity project
will also facilitate India’s economic and cultural ties
and strengthen bilateral and multilateral relations
with Southeast Asian neighbours. The completed
segment of 52 km between 60 km to 112 km of the
Kalewa-Yagyi Road section of the India-Myanmar-
Thailand Trilateral Highway was handed over to the
Government of Myanmar in October.
India also provided support for capacity building
projects in Myanmar, namely the establishment of the
Myanmar Institute of Information Technology (MIIT) in
Mandalay, the India Myanmar Centre for Enhancement
of IT Skills (IMCEITS) in Yangon and the Advanced

Centre for Agricultural Research and Education
(ACARE) near Naypyidaw. India also provided
10,000 MT of rice and 200 MT of wheat in 2022 as
humanitarian assistance. Government of India has
been assisting the Government of the Republic of the
Union of Myanmar (GoM) in establishing and running
the IMCEITS in Yangon since 2008. Since its inception,
2839 students have graduated from IMCEITS,
benefiting the region by creating skilled manpower
and capacity building for employment generation.
Furthermore, IMCEITS has made a significant impact
by producing industry-ready IT specialists employed
by both local and international companies. Five Master
Trainers from IMCEITS, Yangon, are undergoing six
months advanced Post Graduate Diploma Courses,
which commenced on 21 August at C-DAC in Pune.
Graduates hold positions such as Software Engineer,
Network Engineer, Mobile Developer, System
Administrator, Multimedia Specialist, and Operation/
Project Manager. The project has been appreciated
by GoM and the population alike for its positive
impact and benefits, as outlined above.
India also provided 10,000 MTs of rice and 200 MTs
of wheat in 2022 as humanitarian assistance. Several
books on advanced Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics
and Economics for use by graduate and research
students of Naypyitaw State Academy were handed
over, as a grant-in-aid support, in the presence of
Deputy Education Minister U Nay Myo Hlaing, on
19 September. Keeping in view the needs of the
Indian diaspora in Myanmar, the supply of cremation
machines to the Hindu community in Myanmar is in
process.
Nepal
India-Nepal
developmental
partnership
is
all
encompassing including both infrastructure and
supply projects in areas of railways, road, electricity
transmission lines, police training and vocational
training. India is undertaking the development of rail
links with Nepal to enhance the ease of movement of
people and goods. Under the first phase, Jayanagar-
Bardibas Rail Link (68.72 kms) and Jogbani-Biratnagar
Rail Link (18.60 kms) are being developed at an
estimated cost of around Rs. 950 crores. The Jaynagar
to Kurtha rail section (34km), which is the first broad
gauge passenger rail line in Nepal has been completed
and flagged off by the Prime Minister and the then
Prime Minister of Nepal virtually on 2 April 2022.
The Kurtha-Bijalpura section is physically complete
and was handed over to Nepal on 29 May 2023.
Consequently, train operations were inaugurated
on 15 July 2023. Under the Jogbani-Biratnagar Rail
Link project, Bathnaha (India) to Nepal Custom Yard
was inaugurated by both Prime Ministers on 1 June
2023. Also, the Final Location Survey for construction
of a new electrified rail line connecting Raxaul to
Kathmandu has been completed by Konkan Railway
Corporation Limited (KRCL) and the survey report was
handed over at the Prime Minister level in June 2023.
India has completed the construction of three
Integrated Check Posts (ICPs) at Birgunj, Biratnagar
and Nepalgunj in Nepal along the India-Nepal Border
to facilitate trade and movement of goods and
traffic. These were handed over to the Government
of Nepal in 2018, 2020 and 2024, respectively. The
development of ICP Bhairahawa is currently underway
and is expected to be completed and handed over to
the Government of Nepal in 2026.
To facilitate integrated customs and immigration
services, a decision has been taken to construct another
ICP - the fifth along the India-Nepal international
border at Dodhara Chandani as the western link for
Nepal. It will provide direct access to India’s northern
and western states as well as to Jawaharlal Nehru
Port Trust in Mumbai. Government of India is funding
the establishment of a National Police Academy
(NPA) at Panauti, Nepal, which commenced in 2022.
NPA is one of the largest projects to be fully funded by
the Government of India under the Grant-in-aid. The
academy is planned to replace the existing, smaller
police academy to become a state-of-the-art training
hub for Nepal Police personnel with multiple buildings,
including training, residential and administrative
structures. It is expected to be completed by March
2026.
