text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
326
India is also in the process of supplying 20 Electric
Buses to Nepal. Government of India will supply over
500 vehicles to assist the Government of Nepal in
conducting general elections.
Bangladesh
India has completed the construction of the Akhaura-
Agartala Rail Link, which connects the existing
station of Agartala in India to the Gangasagar station
in Bangladesh. Bangladesh's portion of the project
was jointly inaugurated by the Prime Minister and his
counterpart, the then Prime Minister of Bangladesh, on
1 November 2023. During the COVID-19 pandemic,
India also supplied 109 ambulances to Bangladesh in
various hospitals as a humanitarian gesture.
Sri Lanka
India’s development assistance in Sri Lanka extends
to a wide spectrum of projects including infrastructure
projects. A modern state-of-the-art Cultural Centre
has been constructed at Jaffna under the India-Sri
Lanka development partnership. The Cultural Centre
includes a two storied museum, a 12-storied learning
tower, an auditorium block, a public square and a
floating stage for cultural performances. The project
was inaugurated by EAM on 28 March 2022. Earlier,
India had helped establish an island-wide Emergency
Ambulance Service with a total of 209 ambulances in
Sri Lanka during 2018 -2019.
A prime example of this development assistance is the
flagship grant-in aid initiative by the Government of
India to construct or renovate houses for Sri Lankans.
The overall aim of the Indian Housing Project is to
provide sustainable houses to Internally Displaced
Persons and Indian-Origin Tamils. Phases three
and four of the Indian Housing Project are currently
underway. Under Phase three, 4,000 houses have
been constructed under a community-driven approach
in the Central, Uva and Southern Provinces by India.
Under Phase four, a total of 10,000 houses are
proposed to be built across Northwest, Central, Uva,
Southern, Western and other provinces. Of the 10,000
houses, construction of 1300 houses is in progress.
Stage two of Phase four was launched on 12 October,
in which the Sri Lankan government plans to cover
4,700 beneficiaries. Out of these 4700 beneficiaries,
2000 have received their house ownership certificates
by December.
India launched the construction of 10,000 houses under Phase IV of the Indian Housing Project to be built across Northwest, Central,
Uva, Southern, Western and other provinces of Sri Lanka, October 2025

text:
Development Cooperation
327
Maldives
India and Maldives have a growing development
partnership involving both grant and LoC assistance.
The new Ministry of Defence building for Maldives
was jointly inaugurated by the Prime Minister and
the President of Maldives Mohamed Muizzu on 25
July. The Construction of the National College for
Policing and Law Enforcement (NCPLE) in Maldives
has been completed and the project was inaugurated
by EAM on 27 March 2022. India provided grant for
construction of additional facilities at the Composite
Training Centre at Maafilaafushi Island built up with
India’s assistance.
The construction work on the India-supported Greater
Malé Connectivity Project, through a grant of USD 100
million and a LoC of USD 400 million, is progressing at
a rapid pace. The foundation of the project was jointly
laid by the Prime Minister and the then President of
Maldives Ibrahim Mohamed Solih in August 2022.
The Greater Malé Connectivity Project (GMCP)
involves the construction of bridge and causeway
links between the Islands of Villingili, Gulhifalhu and
Thilafushi with Malé. As the largest infrastructure
project to be undertaken in the country, it will become
an economic lifeline and a force multiplier for Maldives
once completed.
Mauritius
India has been providing development assistance to
Mauritius in various sectors, including infrastructure,
health, education and capacity building. Under its
assistance programme, India has extended a grant of
USD 353 million as a Special Economic Package to
Mauritius in 2016, for implementation of six projects in
Mauritius, namely, Metro Express (USD 267 million),
New Supreme Court Building (USD 30 million),
Education-Tablets (USD 14 million), Social Housing
for Poor (USD 20 million), New ENT Hospital (USD
14 million) and four Medi-clinics & two Area Health
Centres (AHCs). The new Supreme Court building
in Port Louis, built with the grant assistance of USD
28.12 million from India, was jointly inaugurated
by Prime Minister and the then Prime Minister of
Mauritius Pravind Kumar Jugnauth on 30 July 2020.
The Social Housing Units Project in Port Louis has
also been completed and jointly inaugurated by Prime
Minister and the then Prime Minister of Mauritius
Pravind Kumar Jugnauth in January 2022. The first
phase of the Metro Express Project in Port Louis, built
under the India-Mauritius Development Partnership,
was operationalised in 2020, and it proved to be a
major success, with a record number of riders reached
in the first year. Phase two of the Metro Express has
also been completed and jointly inaugurated by Prime
Minister and the then Prime Minister of Mauritius
Pravind Kumar Jugnauth in October 2022. The line
from Rose Hill to Reduit, spanning 3.4 kms, under a
combined LoC of USD 90 million, and a grant of USD
10 million, was inaugurated on 22 January 2023 by
the then Prime Minister of Mauritius Pravind Kumar
Jugnauth.
Other significant infrastructure and capacity building
projects completed by India in Mauritius are building
an ENT Hospital, and the E-Tablet project to provide
teaching aids for primary schools in Mauritius. India is
also providing grant assistance for the construction of
a Civil Services College in Mauritius, which was jointly
inaugurated by Prime Minister and the Prime Minister
of Mauritius Navinchandra Ramgoolam on 12 March.
Construction of Forensic Science Laboratory through
Indian grant-in-aid is underway. The Mediclinic at
Grand Bois has been inaugurated and handed over
to the Government of Mauritius on 17 July, 2024 and
is now running successfully for patient service. Two
Area Health Centres (AHCs) in New Grove and Cap
Malheureux have been inaugurated on 4 October and
15 March respectively. Work on the Renal Transplant
Unit at the Jawahar Lal Nehru Hospital in Mauritius
under Government of India grant assistance of USD
10 million is complete and is likely to be handed
over to the Government of Mauritius soon. To combat
rising drug menace in Mauritius, supply of anti drug
and smuggling unit equipment was handed over by
Foreign Secretary to the Government of Mauritius on
1 July.

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
328
India is also in the process of procuring and supplying
100 electric buses and 20 chargers on grant basis
to the Government of Mauritius. Out of these, 40
e-Buses and 11 chargers were delivered to Mauritius
by December. The delivery of remaining 60 e-buses
and nine chargers are expected to be completed in
2026.
Senegal
India has extended assistance in setting up the
Entrepreneurial Training & Development Centre
(ETDC) at Dakar. The institute was initially set up by
HMT International Ltd. in 2001 and was inaugurated
in March 2002. As the technology and training had
since become obsolete, it was decided to upgrade
and modernise the Centre. India facilitated the
modernisation and upgradation of the Centre in two
phases. In the first phase, M/s HMT (I) undertook
reconditioning, retrofitting and refurbishing of the
general-purpose machines set up earlier, which were
useful for basic training. This phase was completed
and inaugurated in June 2019. In the second phase,
HMT (I) supplied the latest technology machines and
equipment for identified trades, trained Senegalese
personnel in India and deputed Indian experts for ‘On-
the-Job Training’ of the Centre facilitators in Dakar.
This phase was also completed and handed over to
the Government of Senegal in September 2023.
Zambia
The Government of India has supplied Medical
equipment to the Government of Zambia worth USD
9.6 million through a grant-in-aid. The equipment was
handed over to the Minister of Health of Zambia on
18 April. India has also gifted 600 sewing machines
to Zambia to support skill training and women's
economic empowerment activities of the Ministry of
Community Development and Social Services. The
sewing machines were delivered in September.
South Africa
With a view to promote quality vocational education
and training to meet the training requirements of
young people and the artisan skills requirements of
South Africa, an MoU for setting-up of the Gandhi
Mandela Centre of Specialisation for Artisan Skills
(GMCOS) was signed between India and South
Africa during Prime Minister’s visit to South Africa
in July 2018. The MoU entails setting-up of Centres
of Excellence in South Africa. The Government of
South Africa identified Tshwane South Technical and
Vocational Education and Training (TVET) College,
Pretoria, as the first location of the Gandhi-Mandela
Centre. Under Indian assistance, machinery and
equipment, computer hardware, software, peripherals
and video conferencing facilities in skills in demand in
South Africa have been supplied. The GMCOS at TVET
College was launched in October 2021. Given the
utility of the project, the Government of South Africa
has requested an extension of the project, which India
has agreed to, and the annual maintenance of the
facility is also underway.
São Tomé and Príncipe
The Government of India has gifted a fleet of six school
buses to the Government of the Democratic Republic
of São Tomé and Príncipe. In a ceremony held in São
Tomé on 10 April, these buses were handed over
to the Minister of Education, Culture, Science and
Higher Education of the Democratic Republic of São
Tomé and Príncipe by the Ambassador of India to the
Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe.
Ethiopia
The Government of Ethiopia has sought India's
support for the installation of a new Data Centre at
the Ethiopian Foreign Ministry, on a grant basis. The
project is under initial stage of implementation.

Development Cooperation
329
Mongolia
India is providing support for the construction of
the India-Mongolia Friendship Secondary School
in Ulaanbaatar. The project work is in progress and
expected to be completed by 2026.
Comoros
India is supporting Comoros in the supply of public
transport vehicles, including buses, ambulances and
pick-up vans, intended to improve access to mobility
for the common people of Comoros. The ambulances
and pick-up vans were delivered to Comoros in
August.
Latin American and Caribbean (LAC)
Countries
India delivered Small and Medium Enterprises (SME)
machinery to CARICOM (Caribbean Community) and
SICA (Central American Integration System) countries,
fort the creation of sustainable businesses. In August,
Saint Vincent and the Grenadines received equipment
for a leafy vegetables and root crop processing
and packaging plant. In July, Trinidad and Tobago
was provided with machinery for an integrated
automatic processing and packaging plant for fruits,
vegetables, and flour. Machinery for Barbados, Belize,
and Honduras is expected to be dispatched shortly.
Proposals from the Dominican Republic, Guyana,
St. Kitts and Nevis, and Guatemala are in the early
implementation phase.
To strengthen cricketing relations between India and
Jamaica, electronic scoring systems and video boards
were installed at Sabina Park Stadium in Kingston.
The official handover occurred during the T20 match
between West Indies and Australia at Kingston on 20
July.
Prime Minister announced ‘Solar Electrification of one
Government Building in each CARICOM country’ during
the second India-CARICOM Summit in Georgetown
in 2024. Since then, project proposals have been
received from Jamaica, Trinidad and Tobago, Belize
and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines. The projects
are under initial stages of implementation. During his
official visit to the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago in
July, Prime Minister announced a gift of 2000 laptops
to support Trinidad and Tobago’s flagship educational
programme. The project is under implementation and
is expected to be completed in 2026.
Suriname
With the aim of supporting small and medium sized
enterprises in the countries of the Global South, a
grant of USD 1 million was announced by Prime
Minister under the Supply of Equipment for Efficient
Development of SMEs (SEEDS) Initiative during the
second India-CARICOM Summit held in Guyana in
2024. Under the ‘SEEDS’ Initiative, establishment of
a plant for processing and packaging unit for passion
fruit in Suriname is underway. The Government of
India supported the implementation of the Integrated
Social Welfare Program of Government of Suriname
under the Extended Fund Facility of the International
Monetary Fund with procurement and supply of 28
different items of food grains for a period of six months.
The food items were handed over to Government of
Suriname in three phases from January to May.
Pacific Island Countries
India will supply 16 sea ambulances to nine Pacific
Island Countries (PICs), one of the deliverables
announced by the Prime Minister during the FIPIC
(Forum for India-Pacific Islands Cooperation) III summit
held in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea, on 22 May
2023. The sea ambulances are intended to improve
emergency medical services across the Pacific Island
Countries (PICs), which often face challenges due to
their remote locations and lack of access to timely
medical care. This commitment underscores India’s
role as a key development partner for the PICs,
focusing on humanitarian assistance and sustainable
development.
Fiji
The Government of India is working closely with
the Government of the Republic of Fiji (GoRF) in
developing a new 100 bedded Super Specialty
Cardiology Hospital in Suva as a Government of
India Grant-in-aid project, which was announced by

Prime Minister at the Third FIPIC Summit in 2023.
An MoU between Government of India and GoRF for
the design, construction, commissioning, operation
and maintenance of a Super-Specialty Hospital in Fiji
was signed on 24-26 August during the official visit
of the Prime Minister of Fiji Sitiveni Rabuka to India.
Construction of this super specialty hospital will
improve overall health outcomes across Pacific Island
Countries.
India and Fiji signed an MoU on Design, Construction,
Commissioning, Operation And Maintenance Of A Super-
Specialty Hospital In Fiji, during the visit of Prime Minister of
Fiji Sitiveni Ligamamada Rabuka to India, August 2025
India has started the process for the supply of 12
agriculture drones to Fiji to help with the optimisation
of fertiliser application for increased crop yields and
enhanced agricultural productivity in the sugarcane
industry of Fiji.
Palau
In January, MoS (PM) visited Peleliu Island in Palau,
where he formally handed over 12 water tanks, gifted
by the Government of India for rainwater harvesting,
to the Governor of the Peleliu Island.
QUAD
Delivering on its QUAD commitments, the Government
of India has committed around USD 2 million to provide
solar cold storage, solarisation of health care facilities,
and solar water pumping systems to Comoros, Fiji,
Madagascar, and Seychelles in the Indo-Pacific region.
Solar equipment for Comoros, Fiji, Madagascar and
Seychelles were delivered in October and December.
Digital Public Infrastructure
India is promoting digital public infrastructure
incubated in India, viz., the digital offerings of the
Unified Payments Interface (UPI), Digital Identity
platform, DigiLocker, eSanjeevani, among others,
worldwide, especially among countries of the Global
South. This emanated from deliberations under the
Voice of the Global South Summits held in 2023 and
2024. India’s push for DPI is in furtherance of digital
transformation in both India and foreign countries and
to enhance cooperation in ecosystem-centric digital
initiatives (such as India Stack). Governmental efforts
to promote IndiaStack DPI with Foreign Governments
have fructified into 23 MoUs. India signed six MoUs on
‘Cooperation in the Field of Sharing Successful Digital
Solutions Implemented at Population Scale for Digital
Transformation’ with partner countries including
Venezuela, Sri Lanka, Lesotho, Maldives, Brazil, and
Mongolia. The MoU would enable the adaptation
of IndiaStack platforms such as Aadhaar, UPI, and
DigiLocker, to promote efficient public service delivery
globally.
For the export/promotion of UPI abroad, till date, six
Letter of Intent have been signed between RBI and
the Central Bank of host countries, which are Guyana,
Peru, Uruguay, Namibia, Fiji and Nigeria.
So far, UPI Interface has been implemented in Nepal,
Bhutan, the UAE, Singapore, Mauritius, Sri Lanka,
France and Maldives. Commercial Agreements have
also been signed between NIPL (NPCI International
Payments Limited) and its counterpart in Namibia, Peru
and Trinidad and Tobago. The solution is expected to
go live by 2026 in these countries.
India is assisting the implementation of the Sri Lanka
Unique Digital Identity programme with Indian
grant assistance. The implementation of this project
would lead to more effective and efficient delivery of
government services and enhanced socio-economic
inclusion in Sri Lanka.
India has undertaken outreach activities on PM
Gati Shakti - National Master Plan for Multi-modal
connectivity (PMGS-NMP) with several partner
countries in the Global South, including countries in
the neighbourhood.

Development Cooperation
331
DPA IV
DPA IV Division is entrusted with the responsibility to
deal with the projects for restoration and conservation
of heritage sites, which define the cultural landscape of
partner countries as a part of India’s cultural diplomacy
outreach. While these projects are implemented by
Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), the designated
technical agency under the Ministry of Culture, they
are coordinated and funded by the Ministry. Projects
currently under implementation are in Cambodia (Ta
Prohm and Preah Vihear), Lao PDR (Vat Phou) and
Vietnam (E & F) groups of Temples. This Division also
collaborates with other organisations to implement
projects related to restoration and conservation of
intangible heritage assets like murals, manuscripts,
etc.
Ta Prohm Temple, Cambodia
This project is the Ministry’s oldest project of its kind,
having commenced in February, 2004. The current
ten-year-long phase III of the project is likely to be
completed in November 2026. During the year,
conservation work has been completed for major
segments like the Hall of Dancers, bringing the overall
physical progress to more than 81 percent. The
Cambodian Government has requested the restoration
and conservation of five additional structures of the
Temple as the fourth phase, which is under active
consideration by this Division.
Preah Vihear Temple, Cambodia
This is the latest project taken up by the Ministry and
the second project in Cambodia. This project has been
sanctioned in 2020. It is likely to be completed in 10
years. During the year, the implementation of project
activities has picked up pace with the completion of
baseline assessments, scientific studies and creation
of tourist accessibility facilities. Despite conflict-
induced disruptions to work, the overall physical
progress is almost 25 percent.
Vat Phou Temple, Lao PDR
The project is currently in its second phase, after
successful completion of the first phase (May 2007-
May 2017). The 10-year-long second phase had
commenced in November 2018. Overall physical
progress achieved as of date is close to 35 percent.
The major scope of work includes the Western Brick
Gallery, the Southern Quadrangle, restoration of the
first terrace on the east side of the retaining wall,
conservation of the ceremonial pathway, the Naga
Linga, and the phallic-shaped pillar.
The second phase of restoration of Vat Phou Temple in Lao PDR achieved 35 percent progress in 2025

My Son group of Temples, Vietnam
Work at the “E” and “F” groups of the Temple complex
was initiated as a new project in the current year,
following the successful restoration of the previous
three groups of temples - H, K & A. To date, physical
progress of 12 percent has been achieved, with
preliminary studies and ground preparation works/
surface rain water management studies being
completed.
Conservation of murals at Wat Raja Bo
Pagoda, Cambodia
This project is being implemented as a grant-in-aid,
with ASI providing supervisory and technical expertise
to Cambodian officials. Restoration work is underway,
and two instalments of the grant amount have been
released.
Conservation of Kutishvara Temple,
Cambodia
The Ministry will support the local monument
authorities in Cambodia through a grant-in-aid for the
conservation of the Kutishvara Temple at Angkor Park
in Siem Reap Province. The temple is considered to be
one of the oldest in the region.
Conservation of Indic manuscripts in
repositories abroad
After successful completion of the first phase
involving 1100 manuscripts, Project ‘South Asian
Manuscript Histories and Textual Archive’ (SAMHITA)
has been extended to this year to cover an additional
3000 manuscripts in eight countries/ repositories.
As of date, metadata analysis has been carried out
for 1,420 manuscripts, and data for an additional
900 manuscripts have been linked to the PANDiT
database. The entire library of digitised manuscripts
has been put in the public domain as the ‘South Asian
Manuscript Histories and Textual Archive’ at www.
samhita.iicdelhi.in.

Policy Planning & Research
C H A P T E R
19
Policy Planning and Research (PP&R) is the nodal
division of the Ministry for initiatives relating to
medium-term policy planning and research. In addition,
the division also undertakes outreach activities with
the strategic, think-tank, and academic community
specialising in foreign policy. PP&R division conducts
in-house policy analysis for the Ministry on a regular
basis on key international issues. The research output
is utilised by the Ministry and Indian Missions and
Posts abroad in dealing with their various mandates.
The division holds Policy Planning Dialogues (PPDs)
with policy planning bureaus of foreign counterparts
to exchange views and understanding on regional
and global issues. It is also the nodal Division for the
Voice of Global South Summits (VoGSS) initiative
of the Government and for coordinating India’s
Neighbourhood First Policy in the Ministry.
The Division also supervises the functioning of the
MEA’s Library and Boundary Cell. It is also the nodal
administrative agency for matters pertaining to the
Indian Council for World Affairs (ICWA) and Research
and Information System for Developing Countries
(RIS), the two autonomous policy research bodies
supported by the Ministry.
In this year, the Division held Policy Planning
Dialogues with counterpart Policy Planning Divisions/
bureaus of the Foreign Ministries of Poland, Indonesia,
and Vietnam. A policy planning dialogue was jointly
held with BRICS member states.
PP&R Division, in collaboration with leading think tanks
and academic institutions, spearheads India’s foreign
policy outreach through its four flagship initiatives:
the Raisina Dialogue, Indian Ocean Conference, Asia
Economic Dialogue, and Global Technology Summit.
It also organises a range of high-impact strategic
dialogues, including forums like India-US, India-
Japan, India-Europe among others, reinforcing India’s
engagement on global and regional issues.
In this year, the 10th edition of the Raisina Dialogue
was organised on 17-19 March in New Delhi, with
the theme ‘Kalachakra: People, Peace, and Planet’, in

collaboration with the Observer Research Foundation
(ORF). The dialogue witnessed participation of over
3500 representatives from about 125 countries

The ninth edition of the Global Technology Summit
(GTS) was co-hosted by the Ministry and Carnegie
India in New Delhi on 10-12 April. The theme for this
year’s Summit was ‘Sambhavna’, meaning possibilities,
and explored how emerging technologies can drive
inclusive growth, strengthen digital governance,
and deepen cross-border partnerships. The second
edition of GTS Innovation Dialogue was organised in

EAM addressed the ninth edition of GTS in New Delhi, April

The eighth India-US Forum was held on 21-23 April
in New Delhi, organised in collaboration with Ananta

The Raisina Quad Young Fellows Programme was
held on 9-15 August in collaboration with ORF. The
programme enables fellows to engage in high-level
thematic discussions and brings together scholars
and practitioners from across Quad countries.
The second India-Nordic Track 1.5 Dialogue was
organised in Reykjavik, Iceland on 4-5 September
in collaboration with Ananta Centre. The dialogue
focused on strengthening India's ties with Nordic
nations through trade, tech, and tourism.
MoS (KVS) addressed the second India Nordic Track 1.5
Dialogue in Reykjavik (Iceland), September 2025
The second edition of the India-Indonesia Track 1.5

The fourth Raisina Forum for Future of Diplomacy
was organised in New Delhi on 3-12 October, in
collaboration with ORF. The forum saw participation
of 46 diplomats and representatives from 37 nations
& four international organisations.
The India-EU Track 1.5 Dialogue was held in Brussels
on 8-10 October. The dialogue brought together
senior policymakers, experts, and business leaders
from both sides to discuss and strengthen India-EU
cooperation.

India’s evolving role and interests over this strategic

horizon. The Division produced a range of publications,
including the Foreign Policy Daily Report, NITI series
newsletters covering Economy, International Legal
Developments, Defence, Technology, Under the Lens
Briefs, and Think Tank Compendium. The division is
also mandated to prepare and publish the Annual
Report of the Ministry which is tabled in the Parliament.
The Annual Report is the most comprehensive public
document on India’s foreign policy and a key reference
for the academic and thinktank community in India and
abroad.
During the year, the Division spearheaded the Niti
Shakti Initiative under which Divisions in the Ministry
can commission short term study/research projects on
any topic of interest through think tanks and academic
institutions across the country.
Indian Council of World Affairs
(ICWA)
The PP&R Division is the administrative and nodal
division in the Ministry for all matters relating
to the Indian Council of World Affairs (ICWA).
ICWA’s mandate to formulate the Indian discourse
on foreign policy was carried out throughout the
year. ICWA organised 100+ intellectual activities
including lectures, talks, seminars, conferences,
panel discussions, book discussions, dialogues and
interactions with foreign dignitaries, focused on
themes of contemporary relevance and importance
in international affairs. Outreach to young scholars
and students was enhanced through increased
internships, outreach programmes supported by
grants in universities across India, and through their
enhanced participation in ICWA’s discussions.
During the year, ICWA published 63 Issue Briefs,
68 View Points and 22 Special reports. In addition,
ICWA’s long-term research projects were published in
the form of eight books on issues ranging from global
and regional developments to diplomacy, trade,
culture, civilisation, maritime security and international
law. ICWA’s Journal ‘India Quarterly’ is brought
out regularly. Further, nine Special Publications
comprising papers by eminent experts on subjects
including Maritime Domain Awareness, India’s Space
and Satellite Diplomacy, Critical Minerals in Africa,
Migration and Mobility, multilateralism, among others,
were published. A vertical on International Law was
established in ICWA in July.
ICWA hosted Sapru House Lectures by visiting
foreign dignitaries. The objective of the lectures is to
facilitate interaction of the visiting dignitaries with an
informed audience on issues of bilateral relations and
international affairs. This year, ICWA hosted lectures
by Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of
Republic of Fiji Sitiveni Ligamamada Rabuka, President
of the Republic of Chile Gabriel Boric Font, Secretary
General of Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)
Nurlan Yermekbayev, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the
Republic of Armenia Ararat Mirzoyan, and the 55th
Sapru House Lecture by Minister of Foreign Affairs of
the Republic of Cyprus Constantinos Kombos.
Some important bilateral Track 2 dialogues were held
with ICWA’s MoU partners in Saudi Arabia, Qatar,
Russia, Iran, and Uzbekistan and Track I.5 dialogues
were held with ICWA’s MoU partners in New Zealand,
Japan, and Vietnam on areas of mutual interest and
concerns. ICWA signed several MoUs with institutions
from Ukraine, Nepal and Uzbekistan for collaborative
activities.
As a part of ICWA’s Foreign Policy Awareness
programme, outreach activities in several Universities
and Colleges including its MoU partners across
the country were organised. ICWA supported 33
outreach conferences out of which eight outreach

Kowdiar (Kerala), Koni (Chattisgarh), Ahmedabad,

Policy Planning & Research
337
The Sapru House Library, housed in ICWA, is a premier
resource center for Indian and foreign scholars over
the past seven decades. The library has grown into
a premier research resource centre for Indian and
international scholars. A new Library Brochure was
developed, highlighting resources and services for
outreach and promotion. Prasar Bharati produced a
special Hindi documentary on the Sapru House Library
under the series ‘पुस्तकालयों के प्रसार एवं संरक्षण’ Filmed
within the library, the documentary was telecast on
Doordarshan on 16 January. Recognising the quality
services rendered by the Sapru House Library, it
was awarded the ISO 9001:2015 certification in
September, a rare distinction held by only a few
libraries in the entire country.
Research and Information System
for Developing Countries (RIS)
The PP&R Division is the nodal division for all matters
relating to Research and Information System (RIS)
for developing countries. RIS is an autonomous
policy research institute that specialises in issues
related to international economic development, trade,
investment, and technology. It fosters policy dialogue
and capacity building among developing countries
on global and regional economic issues. The primary
focus is on promoting South-South Cooperation and
collaborating with developing countries in multilateral
negotiations in various forums.
Housed at RIS, the Global South Centre of Excellence
(DAKSHIN) fosters knowledge sharing and mutual

sustainable solutions for countries of the Global South.
DAKSHIN has organised a number of workshops on
agriculture, health, and digital public infrastructure. It
has also collaborated with partner think tanks from
across the Global South and held numerous interactive
sessions with them. Through these engagements,
DAKSHIN continues to strengthen knowledge sharing,
promote South-South cooperation, and support
inclusive development across key thematic areas.

thematic

interactive

Agricultural Resilience, and the major International

on
Global
South
and

session of its Dialogue with Ambassadors of the
Global South with the Ambassador of Egypt, and
organised targeted capacity-building efforts such as
the workshops on Gender-Responsive Budgeting
and Women-Led Development for Inclusive Growth.
The Centre launched its Special Lecture Series on the
Global South, and the India–Vietnam conference on
working together for the Global South, highlighting
opportunities in digital public infrastructure, climate
action, traditional medicine systems, and South-
South cooperation. Across these diverse activities,
DAKSHIN deepened partnerships, expanded expert
engagement, and advanced its mission of sharing
development experiences and fostering collaborative
solutions across the Global South.
RIS has initiated capacity building programs that
have become an important modality of South-South
cooperation. RIS organised a special course for
diplomats from Kuwait, Oman, and Saudi Arabia in

This year, RIS convened a wide-ranging set of

conferences,
workshops,

and high-level interactions covering an expansive

also organised thematic discussions on blue economy

and

global partnerships. Collectively, these and other
engagements reflected RIS’s continued commitment

Legal and Treaties Division
C H A P T E R
20
The Legal and Treaties (L&T) Division oversees
all legal matters of the Ministry of External Affairs
advising from the international law perspective. In
2025, the Division continued to provide advice on
issues of critical importance handled by the Ministry as
well as Government of India as a whole. The Division
also deals with examination, vetting and facilitating

Engagement with the United
Nations and other International
Organizations
United Nations
Sixth Committee of the United Nations
General Assembly
The Sixth Committee of the United Nations General
Assembly (UNGA) also known as the Legal Committee,
is dedicated to addressing matters of global importance,
fostering the development of international law and
resolving various legal questions. It reviews reports
from the International Law Commission (ILC) and
formulates recommendations on critical legal issues,
which are then presented to the General Assembly for
consideration and necessary action.
During the 80th Session of the UNGA, held from 9-29
September, India played an important role in the Sixth
Committee. India delivered statements on various
agenda items which include -Measures to Eliminate
International Terrorism, Rule of Law at National and
International levels, Criminal Accountability of UN
officials and Experts on Mission, Protection of Persons
in the event of Disasters, Special Committee on Charter,
Universal Jurisdiction and Report of UNCITRAL. The
L&T Division of the Ministry has been actively engaged
in the working of the Sixth Committee throughout the
year and contributes to strengthening the principles of
international law by raising its voice to secure common
good of the Global South.

ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
340
International Law Week
India participated in the 35th Informal Meeting of
Legal Advisers, held from 27-28 October during
the international law week at the UN Headquarters,
New York, USA. The topics of this year for discussion
included ‘Commemoration of the 78th Anniversary of
the United Nations’ and the ‘Right to Self-Defence’.
Special Committee on UN Charter
The annual session of the Special Committee on UN
Charter and strengthening the role of the Organization
was held on 18-26 February. A national statement in
line with India’s position was delivered.
The Asian-African Legal
Consultative Organisation
(AALCO)
The Asian- African Legal Consultative Organisation
(AALCO) is an inter-governmental organization
headquartered in New Delhi. AALCO is mandated to
serve as an advisory body in the field of international
law for its Asian and African member States. It
functions as a forum for Asian-African cooperation
in legal matters of common concern. India hosts the
Secretariat of AALCO and is one of the founding
members of AALCO. The Legal and Treaties Division
participated in the 63rd Annual Session of AALCO
held in Kampala, Republic of Uganda from 7-12
September.
During the AALCO’s Annual Session, Member States
recognized the need to collectively combat pressing
global challenges of climate change, cybercrimes,
sea-level rise, degradation of marine biodiversity,
protectionist tendencies in trade and investment,
corruption and asset recovery and armed conflicts.
BIMSTEC
The L&T Division is actively engaged in the activities of
the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical
and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC). During the
year, the Division undertook preparations to host the
10th Meeting of the BIMSTEC Sub-group on Legal and
Law Enforcement Issues and remained involved in the
negotiations on the BIMSTEC Convention on Transfer
of Sentenced Persons.
Hague Conference on Private
International Law (HCCH)
During the year, the Legal & Treaties (L&T) Division
continued its active engagement with the Hague
Conference on Private International Law (HCCH),,
an intergovernmental organization based at the
Hague, Netherlands mandated with the progressive
unification of the rules of private international law.
India, a Member State of the HCCH since 2008,
is a Contracting Party to four HCCH Conventions,
namely the Convention Abolishing the Requirement
of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents, 1961
(Apostille Convention); the Convention on Protection of
Children and Co-operation in Respect of Intercountry
Adoption, 1993; the Convention on the Service
Abroad of Judicial and Extrajudicial Documents in Civil
or Commercial Matters, 1965; and the Convention on
the Taking of Evidence Abroad in Civil or Commercial
Matters, 1970.
The L&T Division, functioning as India’s National
Organ for the HCCH, facilitated coordination and
communication between the HCCH Permanent
Bureau, Member States, and the national Central
and Competent Authorities in India under the various
HCCH Conventions. The Division also coordinated
with nodal Ministries and concerned authorities for
effective implementation and engagement under
these Conventions.
During the period, the India has contributed to
several projects and initiatives of the HCCH and
actively participated in meetings of various Working
Groups and Expert Groups, including those on Legal
Parentage and International Surrogacy Arrangements,
Carbon Credits, Digital Assets, and Jurisdiction, as
well as in the Council on General Affairs and Policy
(CGAP-2025).

text:
Legal & Treaties Division
341
UNCITRAL
The United Nations Commission on International
Trade Law (UNCITRAL), established in 1966, is the
primary legal entity within the United Nations system
devoted to international trade law. The Legal &
Treaties Division as a nodal legal division continuously
participates in the deliberation of all UNCITRAL
Working Groups and making significant contributions
to negotiation and adoption of conventions, guidelines,
on international trade law evolution. This year also,
the Division maintained its continuous involvement,
closely following selected Working Group activities
and providing valuable inputs. participated in
various Working Group meetings including the
Working Group on ‘Reforming Investor-State Dispute
Settlement’ in 2025, Negotiable Cargo Instruments,
Investor State Dispute Settlement Reform, Dispute
settlement regarding recognition and enforcement of
electronic arbitral awards, Draft guide to enactment
of the UNCITRAL Model Law on Applicable Law in
Insolvency Proceedings, Electronic Commerce and
Negotiable Cargo Documents.
At the 50th Session in Vienna, Austria in January,
the Working Group deliberated on draft provisions
addressing procedural and cross-cutting issues,
including transparency, third-party funding and
early dismissal of frivolous claims. It also examined
a draft statute for a standing mechanism to resolve
international investment disputes. The 51st session,
held in two parts (February and April) at New York dealt
with the operationalization of an Advisory Centre for
developing countries and the design of a multilateral
instrument to implement reform outcomes. The second
part revisited the standing mechanism and procedural
reforms. By the 52nd session in Vienna, Austria in
September, the Working Group had progressed to
reviewing draft statutes for both a permanent tribunal
and an appellate mechanism, while also addressing
complex issues such as exhaustion of local remedies,
denial of benefits, shareholder claims, and the right to
regulate.
The Division actively participated in the above said
discussions which are beneficial for India as India had
long advocated for a more balanced and transparent
ISDS framework. The emphasis on procedural
safeguards, such as early dismissal and cost
allocation, aligns with India’s concerns about frivolous
claims and litigation costs. The focus on preserving
regulatory space, especially the right to regulate in
public interest, resonates with India’s stance in its
model Bilateral Investment Treaty, reinforcing its
ability to pursue domestic policy objectives without
undue external interference.
Law of the Sea
India proactively engaged in various international
maritime forums. India participated in the informal
Consultations of State Parties to the UN Fish Stocks
Agreement (ICSP17), held at New York from 14-
16 May, showcasing commitment to collaborative
efforts for sustainable fisheries management. India
also participated in the 35th Meeting of the States
Parties to the United Nations Convention on the Law
of the Sea (UNCLOS), held from June 23-27 and
delivered its national statement. India participated
at the 30th Session of the Council and Assembly
meeting of the International Seabed Authority (ISA),
where discussions centered on negotiations on the
draft regulations for exploitation of seabed mineral
resources and development of a Common Heritage
Fund. Actively participating in the United Nations
Open-ended Informal Consultative Process on
Oceans and the Law of the Sea, India engaged in
discussions on ‘Capacity building and the transfer of
marine technology: New Developments, Approaches
and Challenges’ during its twenty-fourth meeting
from 16-20 June.
Indian delegation headed by the Minister of State for
Earth Sciences participated in the third UN Ocean
Conference held at Nice, France from 9-13 June. In
April, India submitted its amended Continental Shelf
Claims to the Division of Ocean Affairs and Law of the
Sea (DOALOS). On 16 July, the Indian scientific experts
from Ministry of Earth Sciences made a presentation
before the Commission on the Limits of Continental
Shelf (CLCS).

ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
342
Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction
(BBNJ)
It aims to address the growing concerns over long-
term protection of marine biodiversity in the high seas.
India remains committed and pro-active to the global
cause of environmental conservation and sustainable
development. India signed the BBNJ agreement on 25
September 2024 and is in the process of ratification
of the same.
Outer Space
India participated in the 68th Session of the UN
Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space from
25 June - 2 July and also attended the 64th Session
of the Legal Subcommittee of UN Committee on the
Peaceful Uses of Outer Space (United Nations Office
for Outer Space Affairs) from 5-16 May, in Vienna,
Austria. Various legal questions related to peaceful
exploration and use of outer space were discussed
at the Session. Topics on the Legal Sub-Committee
agenda included - definition and delimitation of outer
space, character and utilization of the geostationary
orbit, including consideration of ways and means
to ensure the rational and equitable use of the
geostationary orbit without prejudice to the role of the
International Telecommunication Union.
Environment and Climate Change
CoP30 Negotiations
India participated in the 30th Conference of the
Parties (CoP30) to the United Nations Framework
Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), held on
10-21 November, in Belém, Brazil. Among other
things, a major decision on the establishment of the
Just Transition Mechanism was adopted. This decision
aims to help operationalize equity and climate justice at
both global and national levels. Additionally, Division
contributed to discussions on various other crucial
topics such as adaptation, mitigation, compliance
mechanisms under the Paris Agreement, response
measures, and the implementation of the UNFCCC,
Kyoto Protocol and Paris Agreement commitments.
Subsidiary Body for Scientific and
Technological Advice
The Legal & Treaties Division participated in the 62nd
session of the Subsidiary Body for Scientific and
Technological Advice (SBSTA), held in Bonn, Germany
from June 16-26 June. The session focused on a range
of critical issues related to climate change, namely
adaptation and mitigation strategies, response
measures, climate finance, policy and institutional
coherence in climate governance and strengthening
the means of implementation for effective climate
action through cooperation.
Subsidiary Body on Article 8(j) and Other
Provisions of the Convention on Biological
Diversity (COP 16)
The Division participated in the first meeting of
Subsidiary Body on Article 8(j) and Other Provisions
of the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP 16)
related to Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities
from 27–30 October in Panama City, Panama.
The meeting focused on Strategies for mobilizing
resources to ensure the availability of and access
to financial resources and funding, as well as other
means of implementation, including capacity-building,
development and technical support for indigenous
peoples and local communities, including women
and youth, to support the full implementation of the
Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.
International Legally Binding Instrument
on Plastics Pollution, including in the
Marine Environment Negotiations
The Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee on
Plastic Pollution (INC) was established in March 2022
following a resolution adopted at the UN Environment
Assembly (UNEA-5.2) to develop a legally binding
international Instrument on plastic pollution, including
in the marine environment. Since its establishment,
the INC has convened multiple negotiating sessions,
with the most recent being the resumed fifth session
(INC-5.2) held in Geneva from 5-14 August. The
Division actively participated in the negotiations
during the INC-5.2 session in Geneva. During the

Antarctic Treaty System
The 47th Antarctic Treaty Consultative Meeting (ATCM)
and the 27th Committee for Environmental Protection
(CEP) was held from 23 June - 3 July in Milan, Italy. It
brought together representatives from 29 Consultative

pressing Antarctic issues. The meeting also endorsed
a revision on the strategic priority, expanding its scope
from surveying to broader data collection and sharing
initiatives. The Legal & Treaties Division attended the
ATCM meeting and contributed to the discussions.

India is a party to the Convention on Supplementary

from the Legal & Treaties Division are engaged in

peaceful uses of atomic energy.

Seminar on Hague Judgements
Convention and UNIDROIT Principles on
Digital Assets and Private Law
On 30 January, at New Delhi the Legal & Treaties
Division successfully organized a seminar on the
‘2019 Hague Judgments Convention and UNIDROIT
Principles on Digital Assets and Private Law,’ drawing
a remarkable turnout of legal scholars, practitioners,
and policy experts from across jurisdictions. The event
fostered discussions on cross-border enforcement
of judgments and the evolving legal frameworks
surrounding digital assets, reflecting the growing
relevance of these topics in international private law.
International Humanitarian Law
The Legal & Treaties Division participated in the
2025 Asia and the Pacific Regional Conference on
International Humanitarian Law (IHL) held in Manila,
Philippines from 11-14 August. The Conference at the
backdrop of the ongoing international armed conflicts,
discussed legal implications from International
Humanitarian Law (IHL) perspective, principle of
distinction, protection of Hospitals, School and also
focused on national IHL Committees.
Mutual Legal Assistance in
Criminal Matters and Extradition
The Legal & Treaties Division examines Mutual Legal
Assistance in Criminal Matters Treaties (MLAT) and
Extradition Treaties and requests. As the central
authority overseeing MLAT matters, the Ministry of
Home Affairs provided comprehensive texts of draft
treaties for legal scrutiny.
Many Mutual Legal Assistance in Civil and Criminal
Matters and Extradition requests, both originating
from
India
and
foreign
countries,
underwent
meticulous scrutiny in the Legal & Treaties Division
and comprehensive legal opinions were provided.
Trade and Investment

negotiation of the India-UK Free Trade Agreement
(called
Comprehensive
Economic
and
Trade
Agreement between the Republic of India and
the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern
Ireland). The Agreement signed on 24 July deals with
not only goods and services but also cooperation in
technology, innovation, and sustainable development.
It includes significant concessions such as slashing
import duties on automobiles, introducing progressive
chapters like Trade and Gender Equality, and granting

The Division also participated in the ongoing

New Zealand Free Trade Agreement and India-

is also involved in the negotiation of the Amending

Investment Arbitration Cases
The Legal & Treaties Division provides legal advice to
various Ministries on arbitration cases filed against the
Government of India, involving violations of Bilateral
Investment Treaties. In the Arbitration proceedings
initiated against India.
Climate Change case before ITLOS
The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea
(ITLOS) invited the State Parties to UNCLOS and
others to present written statements on the questions
submitted to the Tribunal for an advisory opinion in
the case ‘Request for an Advisory Opinion submitted
by the Commission of Small Island States on Climate
Change and International Law’. The Division assisted
in the preparation of the written statement, and the
delegation was led by Joint Secretary (L&T), who
presented India’s Stand.
ICJ Case on Climate Change
The International Court of Justice (ICJ), in the Advisory
Opinion on ‘Obligations of States in respect of Climate
Change’, referred to by the General Assembly of the
United Nations through resolution A/RES/77/276
started its hearings. It seeks an advisory opinion on
the obligation of States under international law to
protect the climate system and the consequences for
those failing to do so. The Division participated in the
proceedings and argued that the developed countries
which have historically been the largest contributor
to anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions must
be held accountable for the harm caused by climate
change and take the lead in greenhouse gas reduction.
Domestic Court cases
The Legal & Treaties Division plays a major role in
litigations filed by or against the Ministry before the
domestic courts. As the nodal point for all court cases
involving the Ministry, it offers comprehensive legal
support, including the thorough vetting of affidavits
and preparation of responses to petitions filed against
the Ministry. The Division also liaises with the panel
advocates representing the Ministry in court, ensuring
legal representation and assistance on issues related
to the Ministry.
Treaty Practice, Online Treaty
Database and legal vetting
The Legal & Treaties Division facilitates the signing
and ratification of treaties on behalf of India. To sign
the treaties on behalf of India, this Division issued
Instruments of Full Power, as detailed in Annexure-
II. Similarly, the implementation of signed bilateral
and multilateral treaties was achieved through the
issuance of 24 Instruments of Ratification, a process
handled by the Legal & Treaties Division, with a list
available in Annexure -III.
In its capacity as the depository of all treaties signed on
behalf of India, the Division ensures accessibility and
transparency. Annexure-IV provides a detailed list of
260 Agreements/Treaties signed by India during the
year. The Legal & Treaties Division further provides its
service by indexing and uploading the text of these
treaties into the Indian Treaties Database, which is
consistently updated. This comprehensive database,
accessible through the web link https://www.mea.
gov.in/treaty.htm encompasses treaties from 1950 to
2025, exceeding 4000 Agreements and is open to the
public, emphasizing the commitment to transparency
and providing valuable historical and contemporary
insights into India's international engagements.

ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
348
Consular, Passport & Visa Services
C H A P T E R
22
Consular, Passport and Visa (CPV) Division is the
nodal Division responsible for providing consular
and visa services to Indian nationals and foreigners,
including the Indian Diaspora in India and abroad.
Consular Services
As an integral part of welfare of Indian nationals living
abroad, Indian Missions and Posts abroad render all
possible consular assistance to the Indian nationals
and provide various consular services like attestation
of documents, registration and solemnisation of
marriages of Indian nationals, relief and repatriation of
distressed Indian nationals, registration of births and
deaths of Indian nationals, transportation of mortal
remains of deceased Indian nationals and serving
of summons received from Indian Courts to Indian
nationals residing abroad. For Indian nationals arrested
or imprisoned abroad, Consular officers of Missions
and Posts abroad, during consular access visit them
in prisons to ascertain their welfare and safety. Open
Houses and Consular Camps are regularly organised
by most Missions/Posts to provide consular services
at different locations. Our Missions and Posts in Gulf
countries and Malaysia have specialised Community
Welfare and Labour Wings to attend to employment-
related issues.
In line with the Government of India's vision and the
flagship Digital India initiative, SEWA project was
launched. It aims to create an online platform for a
range of consular services, enabling Indian nationals
to apply online for various miscellaneous consular
services at Indian Missions and Posts abroad.
The CPV Division, in consultation with the line
Ministries and Departments in the Government of
India, state Governments, and foreign Diplomatic
Missions in India, also deals with the consular matters
of foreign nationals in India, mainly concerning issues
related to their safety and security.
Consular Dialogue Mechanism
The Consular Dialogue mechanism is aimed at
title: mea_annual_report
creator: PDFium

text:

349
discussing outstanding Consular, Visa and diaspora
related matters with a view to engage in discussing
and resolving issues faced by the Indian Diaspora/
NRIs abroad. India has so far established a bilateral
Consular Dialogue mechanism with over 36 countries.
In 2025, Consular Dialogues/Consultations were
held with Iran, Turkmenistan, Russia, Germany, South
Africa, Uzbekistan, Australia, Netherlands, United
Arab Emirates, Costa Rica and the Maldives.
Visa- Exemption Agreements
India has so far signed ‘Visa Exemption/Waiver
Agreements’ for the holders of Diplomatic and
Official/Service passports with 139 countries. In 2025
alone, India signed/operationalised such agreements
with the Governments of Mauritania, Nauru, Timor
Leste, Togo and Saudi Arabia. Further visa exemption
agreement on Official Passports was also signed and
implemented with Ukraine in 2025, which was, till
then, only for Diplomatic Passport holders.
Overseas Citizens of India (OCI)
Card Scheme
The Ministry is committed to strengthening the
connection between the Persons of Indian Origin(PIO)
and their roots in India, encouraging them to visit and
invest in India and foster greater and deeper ties. In
line with the above objective, the CPV Division, in close
coordination with the Ministry of Home Affairs, has
been facilitating the easier issuance of OCI Cards. The
OCI facility has been extended up to the 6th generation
of Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs) in Trinidad & Tobago
on 28 June, in Malaysia on 5 August, and up to the 7th
generation of PIOs in South Africa on 22 October.
Since the introduction of the OCI Card Scheme, more
than 5.3 million OCI Cards have been issued, with
265,150 cards being issued in 2025.
e-Visa Scheme
The e-Visa facility is now available to nationals from
176 countries, making it more convenient for a wider
range of travelers to visit India, In April, Mauritania,
Kuwait, and Bahrain were included in the list of
eligible countries for e-Visa in April 2025. The e-Visa
system was expanded with the inclusion of four more
Visa categories in 2025 under the system, which were
earlier granted only as a paper visa. Out of 41,96,231
visas, 32,72,740 e-Visa and 9,23,491 regular visas
were issued this year.
Extradition
MEA is the Central Authority for extradition matters
in India. The Ministry, in coordination with relevant
law enforcement authorities in India, has been
actively pursuing the extradition of persons accused
of terrorism, money laundering, economic offences,
drug-trafficking and other criminal offences. In April,
Tahawur Hussain Rana, one of the main co-accused
in the 26/11 Mumbai Terror attacks, was successfully
extradited from the USA. Several other fugitive
criminals were extradited or deported from foreign
countries. To facilitate the extradition of fugitive
criminals,
60
Extradition

are currently in force, and the Ministry is further
negotiating extradition treaties/arrangements with
several other countries, signed prior to 1947. The
Ministry also facilitates negotiations for Agreements
on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters and
in Civil and Commercial Matters and Agreements on
Transfer of Sentenced Persons.

the supervision of Joint Secretary (CPV) has
been appointed as the Nodal Authority for Public
Grievances pertaining to the MEA on Centralised
Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System
(CPGRAMS). It deals with grievances pertaining
to various Missions and Posts abroad as well as
Divisions and Regional Passport Offices (RPOs) in

MADAD
The MADAD portal, launched in February 2015 as
part of the Government's good governance initiative, is
a comprehensive online grievances redressal platform
for Indian nationals facing distress abroad, including
those stranded overseas. The Portal is accessible via
www.madad.gov.in or a mobile app on iOS, Android
and Windows platforms and enables registration
and resolution of complaints. All Indian Missions and
Posts abroad, along with MEA Branch Secretariats in
Chennai, Guwahati, Hyderabad, Kolkata and Mumbai,
are integrated for real-time consular grievance
tracking and follow-up. Missions and Posts abroad
actively address complaints and regularly update
their status. MADAD covers a wide range of consular
issues, including repatriation, transportation of
mortal remains, death compensation, work-related
problems, imprisonment, missing persons, passport
services, and student concerns. Enhanced features
include Multilingual Call Center services through the
Pravasi Bharatiya Sahayata Kendras (PBSKs), Student
Registration, integration with the e-Migrate Portal
and State Governments, and assistance through the
Indian Community Welfare Fund (ICWF). Additionally,
'X' (formerly Twitter) Sewa (@meaMADAD), launched
in March 2017, facilitates grievance management and
responses on social media.
A total number of 6158 grievances were received on
MADAD portal during this year, and a total of 6454
(104.8%) grievances were resolved, including the
pending grievances carried forward from the previous
year.
Passport Seva Programme
The Passport Seva Programme (PSP) Division
provides passport-related services across India and
abroad. Passport issuance has emerged as one of
the most prominent statutory and citizen-centric
services provided by the Ministry. To ensure timely,
transparent, accessible, and reliable passport delivery
in a comfortable setting, the Ministry implemented
significant quantitative and qualitative improvements
through streamlined processes and a dedicated,
trained, and motivated workforce.
Indian passports along with other travel documents
such as Certificates of Identity for Stateless persons,
Emergency Certificates for returnees to India, Police
Clearance Certificates, Surrender Certificates, and
Line of Control Travel Permits in the Union Territory of
Jammu and Kashmir were issued by the MEA through
the PSP Division, the Central Passport Organization
(CPO), and its all-India network of 37 Passport
Offices, the CPV Division for issuance of diplomatic
and official passports and the Andaman and Nicobar
Islands Administration.
There are 93 Passport Seva Kendras (PSK) in Public-
Private Partnership (PPP) mode and 452 Post Office
Passport Seva Kendras (POPSK) in association with
the Department of Posts as extended arms of the
37 Passport Offices. The total number of PSK’s
functioning in the country stood at 545 as on 31
December, including PSKs and POPSKs. For Indians
living abroad, Passports and Emergency Certificates
are being rendered through 203 Indian Missions/
Posts abroad connected to the PSP system.

v2.0. e-Passport is a combined paper and electronic
passport with a Radio Frequency Identification chip
and an antenna embedded as an inlay. The main

and Nagpur on a pilot basis. Subsequently, from
January onwards, PSP v2.0 was rolled out in a phased
manner, and all RPOs were in PSP v2.0 by 26 May.
PSP v2.0 offers an interactive portal for online filing of

experiences.
PSP, an IT-driven mission-mode project, successfully

and accountable passport services to citizens across

and quickly. During this year, more than 1.27 Crore

Appointments
The Ministry released 90,912 appointments per
day. Securing online appointments for submission of
passport applications at PSKs has been simplified.
The current provision allows applicants to choose
any appointment date from the earliest five available
dates (working days) for scheduling/rescheduling an
appointment for passport-related services. It made
the process of issuing passports easier and quicker.
Outreach of Passport Services
The objective of the Government has been to cater to
the growing demand for passports and to reach out to
the people located far away from the Passport Offices.
a. Passport Office:
The list of the 37 passport offices in India is at
(Annexure – V)
b. Passport Seva Kendras (PSKs):
As of December, 93 PSKs are functioning across the
country. The list of the same is placed at (Annexure
–VI).
c. Post Office Passport Seva Kendras
(POPSKs):
The Ministry, in association with the Department of
Posts (DOP), announced an innovative initiative on
24 January 2017 to open Passport Seva Kendras
(PSK) at the Head Post Offices (HPO)/Post Offices
(PO) in the country, called ‘Post Office Passport Seva
Kendras’ (POPSKs). The Ministry has functionalized
452 POPSKs (Annexure - VII).
Applicants, applying for their passports online through
the passport portal can schedule an appointment and
then visit the designated POPSK to complete the
formalities similar to those at the PSK, necessary prior
to the issue of the passport.
d. Mobile Passport Seva Vans:
One Mobile Passport Seva Van has been allotted to
each of the 37 Passport Offices. Mobile Vans have
the provision for 1 Citizen Service at Counter A and
one Verification Officer at Counter B. To cater to the
needs and demand of passport services at remote/
hilly locations, institutions, etc. Mobile Passport Seva
Vans are being deployed under respective RPOs for
providing the doorstop service to the passport seekers.
The Total number of passport applications processed
till the end of this year is 39,811.
Simplification of procedures
The Ministry has taken steps to simplify the procedure
for getting passports by the general public. These
involve simplification of the passport rules and
outreach to the people in the delivery of passport-
related services.
1. Simplification of provision for issue of
passports to children born through IVF:
In order to simplify the process of issuance of passports
to children born through IVF, the Ministry pursued the
matter, detailed discussions were held with concerned
stakeholders i.e. Ministry of Health & Family Welfare
and the Department of Legal Affairs of, Government
of India, to examine the issue. The Ministry formulated
the policy related to the issuance of passports to
children born through IVF. Accordingly, instructions
were issued to all Passport Issuing Authorities in India
and abroad prescribing the documents required for the
issuance of passports to children born through IVF.
2. Amendment in the Passport Rules on
proof of Date of Birth for passports GSR
156(E):
As per guidelines issued under the Unique Identification
Authority of India (UIDAI) and ‘The Registration of
Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2023’. GSR156
(E) was issued to incorporate the amendments and
streamline the process of issuance of passport.

3. Reissue of Passport in ‘Gender change’

As per directions received from the Delhi High Court to

The Ministry has received references with regard to

with Passport applications for minors. To address
the difficulties to applicants and further strengthen
the passport issuance process to minors revised
Annexures were shared with Passport Issuing
Authorities in India and abroad.
e-Passport
e-Passport is a combined paper and electronic passport
with a Radio Frequency Identification Chip and an
antenna embedded as an inlay. The main benefit of
the ePassport will be its enhanced ability to maintain
the integrity of its data, thereby increasing the level of
confidence in the Indian Passport. e-Passports would
also facilitate the ease of travel for Indian citizens,
making their interface with immigration authorities
much smoother.
The project involves setting up of complex technical
ecosystem,
including
Public
Key
Infrastructure
(PKI), Key Management System (KMS), Inter-
operability test bed, Project Management Unit (PMU),
ePersonalization, as well as creation of e-Passport
verification set-up at Immigration Check Points by the
Bureau of Immigration.
During the year, 87 Lakh ePassports were issued
by RPOs in India, and 1.87 Lakhs ePassports were
issued by Missions/Posts abroad. In total, 88.87 Lakh
e-Passports were issued.
Production and Personalisation of
Travel Documents
Indian travel documents are produced by India
Security Press, Nashik, which is a unit under the
Security Printing and Minting Corporation of India
Limited (SPMCIL). All Regional Passport Offices in
India and select Missions/Posts abroad have been
provided with machine-readable passport printers. All
Passport Issuing Authorities issue machine-readable
passports (MRPs) as per the guidelines laid down by
the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO).
At 28 Indian Missions/Posts abroad, the Passport/
OCI printing is done locally. For the majority of Indian
Missions/Posts abroad (wherever passport printing
facility is not available), Machine Readable Passports
and OCI are printed at the Central Indian Passport
Printing System (CIPPS) in PSP Division, MEA, New
Delhi.
Certificate of Identity (CoI)
The Passports Act 1967 provides for issuance of
CoI ‘for the purpose of establishing the identity of a
Stateless person residing in India’. During this year, a
total number 21,95 CoIs were issued.
Appeals under Section 11 of the
Passports Act 1967
Under Section 11 of the Passports Act, an appeal
against the decisions of Passport Issuing Authorities
(PIAs) is a statutory right conferred upon the affected
persons. Joint Secretary (PSP) & Chief Passport Officer
is the Appellate Authority for such cases. During this
year, a total of 117 appeals have been disposed of.

Secretary CPV & OIA conducted the Regional
Passport Officers’ Conference, which was held by
MEA at New Delhi on 23-25 June. All the 37 Regional
Passport Officers and stakeholders of Passport
Seva Programme (PSP) deliberated upon, in detail,
the functioning of Passport Issuance system, its
achievements as well as challenges faced, and future
initiatives to make the process smoother and more

International Civil Aviation
Organisation (ICAO)
Since February 2009, India has been a participating
member of the ‘Public Key Directory (PKD) on
ePassport’ of ICAO, which has been implementing the
guidelines on Machine Readable Travel Documents.
India participated in the 32nd ICAO PKD Board
Workshop & Meeting held from 9-11 November in
Montreal, Canada.
Public Grievance Redressal
Mechanism
Public Grievance Redressal Mechanism Under the
Passport Seva Programme, the Ministry has put in
place a robust Grievance Redressal System, whereby
a multilingual National Call Centre with a toll-free
number (1800-258-1800), operating in 17 languages
and on a 24 x 7 basis, has been set up to disseminate
information about various passport-related services,
including handling grievances and citizens’ feedback.
The passport portal also has an email-based helpdesk,
where suggestions and grievances can be posted.
Citizens can also monitor the status of their passport
applications/grievances online through this portal.
A Public Grievance Redressal Cell (PGRC) has been
set up in the PSP Division under the supervision of
the Joint Secretary (CPV), who is also designated
as the officer in-charge of Public Grievances of the
Ministry for the Centralized Public Grievance Redress
and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS). It deals with
grievances received through telephone, e-mail,
and post, directly from the general public and also
references from various Government offices, such
as the President’s Secretariat, Prime Minister’s
Office, Cabinet Secretariat, and Central Vigilance
Commission, etc. The names and contact details of
the Public Grievance Officer are also displayed in the
RPOs/PSKs and on the website of the RPOs.
During this year, 21,603 grievances were received
at CPGRAMS, of which 20,482 grievances, i.e., 95%,
were disposed of.
Central Passport Organisation
The Central Passport Organisation (CPO) was created
in 1959 as a subordinate office of the Ministry of
External Affairs and is headed by Joint Secretary and
Chief Passport Officer, who also acts as Appellate
Authority under the Passports Act, 1967.
The personnel of the CPO Cadre are deployed in 37
Passport Offices, 93 PSKs, and 452 POPSKs across
the country. The sanctioned strength of CPO is 2640,
and the working strength is 1721.

Emigration Policy and Welfare
Division
In recent times, international migration has assumed
a pivotal role, shaped by demographic shifts and
technological
progress,
significantly
impacting
labour markets worldwide. India is a leading country
in the international migration dynamics and is
advantageously poised with its demographic potential.
By 2030, India's working-age population is set to
peak at 68.9 per cent, reaching 1.04 billion persons.
India’s diaspora is over 35 million strong, making India
one of the top remittances receiving country in the
world with inward flow of remittance to the tune of
USD 135 billion in the year 2024. Recognising their
potential, the Government of India promotes safe,
orderly and regular migration to provide employment
opportunities for workers, professionals and other
categories of citizens traveling abroad.
Mobility Arrangements
The Emigration policy and Welfare Division of
the MEA has been working towards establishing
institutional mechanisms to foster the global
mobility of Indian workers, students, academicians,
researchers, business persons and so on. The Ministry
has been proactively furthering the mobility for Indian
workforce through diverse MoUs and agreements
such as, Migration and Mobility Partnerships (MMPA),
Labour Mobility and Labour Welfare with destination
countries. These agreements and MoUs establish
a robust framework for legal migration. They aim
to foster people-to-people ties, streamline visa
procedures, prevent irregular migration, strengthen
bilateral relations, and support skill development.
Major developments related to the Migration and
Mobility and Labour Mobility Agreements signed with
various countries during the current year are as below:

Russia
On 4 December, two Agreements were concluded
between India and Russia viz. ‘Agreement on
Temporary Labour Activity of Citizens of one State in
the Territory of the other State’ and the ‘Agreement
on Cooperation in Combating Irregular Migration.’ The
former agreement provides for reciprocal engagement
of workers of one state in the territory of the other
state, while expanding its purview to include workers
studying full time in the host country's educational
organisations and institutions. It also outlines
the processes and the necessary documentation
determining the labour activity to be carried out by
the worker. The latter outlines the legal framework for
bilateral cooperation in combating irregular migration
while promoting favourable conditions for legal
travel of nationals of both parties. It further provides
for cooperation between both parties in information
sharing, processing of requests for transfer and
admission of persons in irregular situations.
United Kingdom
During the visit to India in April, the then Minister of
Border Security & Asylum of the UK Angela Eagle
signed an Addendum and Standard Operating
Procedure (SOP) to the MoU on the India-UK MMPA.
The Addendum enables the verification of nationality
through biometrics. Both sides are in discussion to
finalise the mechanism to operationalise the biometric
matching capabilities. India and the UK also finalised
a reciprocal agreement in August allowing nationals
of their countries to give oral evidence via video-
link in immigration-tribunal proceedings that are
jurisdictionally taking place in either country.
In 2023, pursuant to the MoU, the United Kingdom
launched the India-UK Young Professionals Scheme
(YPS). The scheme permits up to 3,000 Indian and UK
citizens aged 18-30 to live and work in each other’s
country for a period of up to two years. In 2025, two
ballots were held one in February and another in
July. The February ballot advertised the majority of
the slots (up to 2,500), and the remaining slots were
opened in the July ballot.
Fiji
A delegation led by Minister of Employment,
Productivity and Industrial Relations of Fiji Agni
Deo Singh met Secretary (CPV&OIA) in February.
They discussed, inter alia, mobility of skilled and
professional persons from India and assistance in
skill development through knowledge sharing and
Training of Trainers (ToT). During the visit of Prime
Minister of Fiji to India in August, a Declaration of
Intent (DoI) on Migration and Mobility between India
and Fiji was signed.

Migration

ballot under MATES opened in December 2024 and

Both sides are currently discussing mechanisms to
expand the outreach for wider participation of Indian

Labour market Demand mapping

Welfare Schemes for Indians Overseas
The Government of India accords high priority to safety
and welfare of Indian citizens living abroad. Welfare
schemes like Indian Community Welfare Fund (ICWF),
Pravasi Bharatiya Bima Yojana (PBBY), Pre-Departure
Orientation Training (PDOT) etc. proved to be critical
tools towards this objective.
Indian Community Welfare Fund (ICWF)
The Indian Community Welfare Fund (ICWF), set up in
2009, is aimed at assisting Overseas Indian nationals
in times of distress in the most deserving cases on a
means-tested basis by providing emergency medical
assistance, air passage to stranded Indians, legal
assistance, emergency medical assistance, boarding
& lodging, assistance to Indian women facing marital
issues and transfer of mortal remains to India. The
scheme has been revised in 2017 and has been set up
in all Indian Missions and Posts abroad. The number of
Indian nationals assisted in distress situations abroad
has reached to 3,61,215 with a total expenditure of
INR 732 Crores till date.
Pre-Departure Orientation Training
Program (PDOT)
The Pre-Departure Orientation Training (PDOT)
Programme was launched by the Ministry of External
Affairs in January 2018 under the Pravasi Kaushal
Vikas Yojana (PKVY) with an aim at enhancing soft
skills of Indian migrant workers, largely going to the
Gulf and other ECR Countries. Under this programme,
the emigrant workers are given free-of-cost one-day
orientation training to enable them to understand
the culture, language, tradition and local rules and
regulations of the destination country. The orientation
training also helps to sensitise the migrant workers
about pathways to safe and legal migration and
various government programmes for their welfare,
safety and protection such as ICWF, MADAD, PBBY
etc. Since inception of the PDOT programme, a total
of 2,25,110 emigrant workers have been imparted
training through 46 PDOT Centres as of November.
Pravasi Bharatiya Bima Yojana (PBBY)
The Pravasi Bharatiya Bima Yojana (PBBY) is a
mandatory insurance scheme for all Emigration
Check Required (ECR) category workers going to
ECR countries. The scheme provides an insurance
cover of INR 10 Lakhs in case of accidental death or
permanent disability and other benefits at a nominal
insurance premium of INR 275 for two years or INR
375 for three years validity. The scheme was revised
from 1 August 2017, to include Emigration Check Not
Required (ECNR) category workers on a voluntary
basis and to make settlement of claims simpler for
the benefit of our workers and to ensure expeditious
settlement of claims. The PBBY scheme has so far
provided insurance cover to 83,88,143 Indian migrant
workers till date.
Diaspora Engagement Division
In 2025, the Ministry continued its concerted efforts
to strengthen India’s engagement with its global
diaspora comprising both Persons of Indian Origin
(PIOs) and Non-Resident Indians (NRIs). The global
Indian diaspora numbered over 34 million, making
it the largest in the world (Annexure - VI). Of this,
about 17.1 million were Non-Resident Indians (NRIs),
and 17.2 million were PIOs. The countries with the
largest Indian diaspora populations included the
United States, the United Arab Emirates, Malaysia,
Canada, Sri Lanka, South Africa, the United Kingdom,
