text:
Emigration Policy, Welfare & Diaspora Engagement (Overseas Indian Affairs)
359
Kuwait, Australia, and Singapore. These communities
contributed significantly to their host countries
while maintaining enduring cultural, economic, and
emotional connections with India. Through flagship
initiatives,
outreach
programmes,
and
welfare
schemes, this Ministry endeavoured to strengthen its
engagement with the diaspora.
During the course of 2025, Ministry continued with
its several key diaspora engagement programmes
like, the Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (PBD) Convention,
Pravasi Bharatiya Samman Award (PBSA), Know
India Programme (KIP), Scholarship Programme for
Diaspora Children (SPDC), Bharat Ko Janiye Quiz,
and Promotion of Cultural Ties with Diaspora (PCTD)
to expand and deepen engagement with the large
and diverse Indian diaspora across the globe. It also
addressed matters relating to marital disputes and
child custody cases involving overseas Indians, issues
faced by Indian students abroad, and other grievances
of the diaspora community.
Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (PBD) Convention
Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (PBD) is the flagship event
of the government and is celebrated on 9 January
biennially to mark the contribution of the Overseas
Indian community in the development of India, and to
reconnect and deepen India’s engagement with the
diaspora at the apex level. It provides a platform to
the overseas Indian community to engage with the
Government of India to share issues of concern and
ideas to promote India overseas.
The 18th PBD Convention was held at Bhubaneswar,
Odisha on 8-10 January, in partnership with the
Government
of
Odisha.
The
Convention
was
inaugurated by the Prime Minister on 9 January.
President of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago
Christine Carla Kangaloo was the Chief Guest of the
Convention, and participated virtually. Prime Minister
flagged off the maiden run of the Pravasi Bharatiya
Express under the Ministry’s Pravasi Bharatiya Teerth
Darshan Yojana, and inaugurated four exhibitions
during the event.
Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji chaired the Valedictory
Session on 10 January, during which she conferred
the Pravasi Bharatiya Samman Awards (PBSA) on
27 distinguished members of the Indian diaspora
(Annexure-VII). PBSA is the highest honour conferred
on NRIs, PIOs, or institutions established and run by
them, to recognise their achievements and honour
their contributions in various fields, both in India and
abroad.
The Youth PBD was held on 8 January, co-chaired by
EAM and the Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports and
Labour. CEO of Newsweek Dev Pragad, from the USA
participated as the Guest of Honour at the event. The
three-day PBD Convention comprised of five Plenary
Sessions featuring diaspora panelists from across
the world and witnessed participation of over 7,500
delegates from over 57 countries.
Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji chaired the Valedictory Session and conferred the Pravasi Bharatiya Samman Awards in Bhubaneswar,
January 2025.

ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
360
Scholarship Programme for Diaspora
Children (SPDC)
The Scholarship Programme for Diaspora Children
(SPDC) was introduced in the Academic Year 2006-
07 for the children of PIOs and NRIs to enable them to
pursue undergraduate courses in Indian Universities/
Institutions and promote India as a centre of higher
learning. Under the SPDC scheme, the Ministry offers
150 scholarships of up to USD 4,000 per annum for
professional and non-professional courses, including
medical studies and related courses, with 50 seats
reserved for children of Indian workers in Emigration
Check Required (ECR) countries. Since its inception,
1,687 scholarships have been awarded till the
academic year 2023-24. In 2025, 433 scholarships
were awarded under the scheme.
Know India Programme (KIP)
The Know India Programme (KIP) is a flagship
initiative of this Ministry to engage young members
of the Indian diaspora, who are Persons of Indian
Origin (PIOs). It aims to strengthen the connection
of PIO youth aged 21–35 years with their ancestral
homeland, while enhancing their understanding of
contemporary India’s socio-economic development,
as well as its arts, heritage, and culture. In 2025, five
editions of the KIP (80th -84th editions) were conducted,
with participation of 193 diaspora youth representing
various countries.
Promotion of Cultural ties with Diaspora
(PCTD)
Under the Promotion of Cultural Ties with Diaspora
(PCTD) scheme, the Ministry extends grants to Indian
Missions/Posts abroad to support their initiatives
aimed at strengthening ties with the Overseas Indian
Community, and to preserve, maintain and showcase
their Indian heritage and culture. The scheme aims to
nourish and strengthen the cultural bonds between
India and its diaspora. The scheme also supports think
tanks and organisations in India that conduct events
pertaining to the Overseas Indian community. In 2025,
financial assistance was extended to 114 Missions/
Posts under this scheme.
Videsh Sampark Programme (VSP)
The Videsh Sampark Programme (VSP), launched
in 2017, is an outreach initiative of the MEA, which
aims to strengthen engagement with the State
Governments of India. These outreach events,
organised in partnership with the State Governments,
facilitate dialogue on issues related to welfare and
protection of Indian diaspora abroad, dissemination of
information on Ministry’s schemes, and collaboration
with the State Governments for furthering welfare of
the Overseas Indian community and curbing illegal
migration.
A total of 12 outreach events have been organised
till date in collaboration with the State Governments
of Telangana, Maharashtra, Kerala, Gujarat, Madhya
Pradesh, Karnataka, Punjab, Haryana, Bihar, Tripura,
and Uttarakhand. In 2025, a Videsh Sampark
Programme was conducted in Andhra Pradesh.
Assistance to NRI Women Affected by
Marital Issues
The Ministry continued to address grievances from
distressed women married to overseas Indians,
including
cases
of
abandonment,
desertion,
harassment,
and
child
custody
disputes.
The
aggrieved women were provided counselling, legal
guidance,
and
information
regarding
available
grievance redressal mechanisms. This year, 112 such
complaints were addressed by the Ministry.
Student Issues
There are approximately 1.33 million Indian students
pursuing higher education abroad. The Ministry, in
coordination with Indian Missions and Posts, continued
to address issues concerning the welfare and safety of
Indian students enrolled in foreign universities. These
included visa-related challenges, exploitation by
fraudulent agents, and lack of awareness regarding
unaccredited or fake universities, among other
concerns. During the year, Ministry had addressed
several such issues aimed towards protecting and
promoting the interests of the Indian students abroad,
including their repatriation from Israel and Iran under
Operation Sindhu during the Gaza conflict.

Emigration Policy, Welfare & Diaspora Engagement (Overseas Indian Affairs)
361
Viksit Bharat Run
The Ministry organised the Viksit Bharat Run in
coordination with the Ministry of Youth Affairs and
Sports across 136 prominent cities of the globe,
primarily involving the Indian diaspora as part of the
Seva Pakhwada from 17 September-2 October. The
3-5 km run marked the Seva Parv, and celebrated
service, unity, and collective national responsibility
rooted in the Indian value of Seva Bhav. With the theme
‘Run to Serve the Nation’ the initiative promoted youth
engagement, diaspora participation, and global unity.
Participants took two pledges - ‘Viksit Bharat’ and
‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’, reinforcing their commitment
to nation-building. A unique tree plantation drive, ‘Ek
Ped Maa Ke Naam,’ was also organised to symbolise
environmental responsibility and remembrance. The
initiative brought together communities worldwide
in a shared mission of service and pride in India’s
heritage, strengthening the collective resolve to build
a stronger, inclusive, and developed nation.
One Stop Centres
The Ministry is in the process of establishing One Stop
Centres at nine Indian Embassies and Consulates
abroad including in Dubai, Riyadh, Singapore,
Toronto, Doha, Muscat, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jeddah,
to support Indian women in distress in foreign
lands. These Centres will provide round-the-clock
assistance, including legal counselling, psychological
support, and help in reaching out to local authorities
for redressal of their grievances and inconveniences.
OE&PGE Division
The process of emigration of Indians holding
Emigration Check Required (ECR) category passports
is regulated under the Emigration Act, 1983, which is
administered by the Ministry of External Affairs. The
Protector General of Emigrants (PGE) enforces the Act
with the help of 16 offices of the Protector of Emigrants
(POEs) located at Mumbai, Chennai, Delhi, Kolkata,
Chandigarh, Hyderabad, Cochin, Thiruvananthapuram,
Jaipur, Raebareli, Patna, Bengaluru, Guwahati, Ranchi,
Bhubaneswar and Agartala. Recruiting Agents (RAs)
are required to obtain Registration Certificate (RC)
from the PGE before they could engage in recruitment
for overseas employment. Emigration of ECR passport
holders is regulated by way of grant of Emigration
Clearance (EC) by any of the above 16 POE offices for
employment in any of the 19 notified ECR countries,
namely, Afghanistan, Bahrain, Indonesia, Iran, Iraq,
Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Malaysia, Oman,
Qatar, Saudi Arabia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria,
Thailand, United Arab Emirates and Yemen.
Recruiting Agents Conclave
A
one-day
Recruiting
Agents
(RA)
Conclave
was organised in March. MoS (KVS) presided
over the inaugural session of the Conclave with
the representatives of the MEA-registered RA
Associations in New Delhi. The Conclave was attended
by representatives from 14 RA associations, 13 State-
run RAs, 16 Protector of Emigrants, senior officers
from the Ministry of Labour and Employment (MoLE),
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
(MSDE), MEA, Resident Commissioners of State
Governments/UTs and media personnel. As part of
Ministry’s efforts to generate awareness about safe
and legal migration, MoS (KVS) also launched a Pravasi
Bharatiya Sahayata Kendra social media channel
which will be utilised to disseminate information
about legal and safe mobility in form and content
easily understood by the masses. The Conclave was
organised with an objective to forge greater synergies
with the RA fraternity for effective implementation of
the Emigration Act 1983 and minimise the space for
illegal recruitment. The Conclave also provided an
opportunity to discuss and deliberate upon various
facets of emigration process, upcoming opportunities
and work process related challenges on the e-Migrate
portal. Three thematic panel discussions focusing on
Skill Development, streamlining Foreign Employer
Registration, and Grievance Redressal were held
during the Conclave.
Inclusion of Iran in ECR List
With a view to protect and safeguard the interests
of citizens of India going to Iran for employment
purpose, the Government withdrew the exemption

creator: PDFium

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
362
granted to them from the operation of Section 22
of the Emigration Act, 1983. Accordingly, the Indian
emigrants holding ECR passport and travelling to
Iran for employment purpose shall require Emigration
Clearance from Protector of Emigrants (PoE).
Discontinuation of requirement of
Country Specific Order for recruitment of
nurses
To simplify the recruitment procedure, enhance
administrative efficiency, and promote ease of doing
business, the requirement of Country Specific Order
(CSO) for recruitment of nurses from India to the
ECR countries has been discontinued. However, the
nurses emigrating to any of the ECR countries would
continue to require the emigration clearance (EC) from
the Protector of Emigrants (PoE).
The Global Mobility Conclave 2025
The Global Mobility Conclave 2025 was organised
by the Ministry in collaboration with the NORKA
Department, Government of Kerala in October at
Thiruvananthapuram. The Conclave was inaugurated
by the Chief Minister of Kerala and issues like ethical
recruitment, skill mobility, and Kerala’s evolving
migration landscape were discussed during the
Conclave which was well covered in the local media.
System-based allocation of Emigration
Clearance applications among PoEs
In an attempt to rationalise the workload among
PoE offices and improve efficiency, transparency,
and service delivery, a system-based randomised
distribution
mechanism
for
allocation
of
EC
applications has been introduced in December.
This reform has made the process of allocation and
processing of EC applications fully digital, logic-
driven and faceless thereby ushering transparency in
the whole emigration process.
Trends in migration during the year 2025
Every year, a large group of people from India go
abroad for employment purposes. Major outflow
of emigrant workers from India continues to the
Gulf countries. During the year, a total of 4,49,110
Emigration Clearances (ECs) were issued through the
eMigrate Portal for ECR passport holders emigrating
to ECR countries. This includes 8,602 ECs issued to
nurses emigrating to ECR countries. During the same
period, eMigrate Portal also added 9,700 new Foreign
Employers (FEs) and 237 new registered Recruiting
Agents (RAs). 1,896 new employment-related
Grievance Requests (GRs) were registered, and 667
GRs were successfully resolved. Uttar Pradesh, Bihar,
Rajasthan, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh,
Punjab, Kerala, Telangana, and Maharashtra were the
top 10 states in terms of the number of ECs issued
during the year. The top five destination countries for
ECs were the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia,
Kuwait, Oman, and Qatar.

States Division
C H A P T E R
24
The States Division’s main objective is to facilitate
trade, investment, tourism, academic, and other
external linkages of the States and Union Territories
of India through coordination with (i) the Governments
of States and Union Territories, (ii) Indian Missions and
Posts abroad, and (iii) Foreign Diplomatic and Trade
Missions in India. The States Division also facilitates
the organisation of activities of the States and Union
Territories in foreign countries through Indian Missions
and Posts abroad. In addition, Branch Secretariats,
Regional Passport Offices, and Passport Offices in
India are involved in the external outreach activities
of States and Union Territories with foreign investors
and foreign trade missions.
Liaising with States and Union Territories through
Chief Secretaries and Resident Commissioners
is undertaken continuously to facilitate matters
involving visits of foreign dignitaries, resident foreign
Ambassadors/High Commissioners, etc. The signing
of several MoUs and Letters of Intent between
State Governments and their entities with foreign
counterparts was facilitated in areas such as trade and
investment promotion, skill development, education,
health, and agricultural research. The Division also
processed and facilitated Sister-City and Sister-State
agreements to establish friendly and cooperative
relations between Indian States and cities and foreign
provinces and cities.
Funds Disbursed Under States
Facilitation Abroad (SFA) Budget
Head
Each year, the States Division provides funds to Indian
Missions and Posts abroad from the ‘State Facilitation
Abroad’ (SFA) budget. Although the demand for funds
from Missions and Posts has been increasing annually,
the States Division has been able to provide adequate
funding to all Missions and Posts abroad from the
allotted budget. Several State-promotion activities
are organised by Missions and Posts abroad in foreign
countries, and the allotted budget is optimally utilised.

New Emerging and Strategic Technologies (NEST) & Cyber Diplomacy
367
New Emerging and Strategic
Technologies (NEST) & Cyber
Diplomacy
C H A P T E R
25
NEST
The New, Emerging and Strategic Technology (NEST)
Division was established to engage in technology
diplomacy and manage the foreign policy and
international legal aspects associated with new
and emerging technologies. During the year the
Division functions as a nodal point within the Ministry
of External Affairs (MEA), keeping the Ministry
updated, coordinating with domestic stakeholders,
and collaborating with foreign partners amidst the
rising geopolitical influence of technology. In this
context, the Division actively worked to evolve and
coordinate Indian positions on technology governance,
strengthening India’s role as a determinant player
in shaping national and global perspectives on new,
emerging, and strategic technologies. The Division
continued to strengthen India’s bilateral, plurilateral,
and multilateral engagements in these areas,
working closely with partner countries, international
organisations, industry, academia, and start-ups.
The year 2025 was marked by significant diplomatic
progress across India's key strategic technology
partnerships, majorly encompassing the India-UK
Technology & Security Initiative (TSI), the India-EU
Trade & Technology Council (TTC), and the India-US
TRUST initiative, all focused on securing technology,
talent, and supply chain resilience.
The India-EU Trade & Technology Council (TTC) held
its second meeting in New Delhi in February, which
advanced cooperation across multiple technical and
trade domains, such as enhancing the resilience of
semiconductor supply chains and facilitated talent
exchanges and skill development in the semiconductor
field. The US-India TRUST (Transforming the
Relationship Utilizing Strategic Technology) initiative
was announced in February, during the Prime
Minister’s visit to Washington, DC. This initiative

Division participated in inter-ministerial consultations
and stakeholder meetings convened to develop India’s
position on key global technology issues and ensured
that India’s diplomatic outreach supports its national
innovation agenda.
NEST Division supported institutional capacity-
building and knowledge development within the
Ministry, particularly for its personnel and officer
trainees. The Division facilitated collaborations with
leading Indian think tanks, and industry associations
to design training modules, expert lectures, and policy
dialogues with the aim of strengthening the Ministry’s
internal expertise, enhancing foresight on emerging
technologies, and equipping officers with the
necessary skills to engage effectively in technology
diplomacy and international negotiations.
To ensure broad awareness of global and domestic
developments, the Division consistently published
its monthly newsletter, Tech Pulse throughout
the year, circulated to all Indian Missions abroad,
and foreign missions in India, line ministries, State
Governments, educational institutes and industry
bodies. Additionally, technology inputs and updates
received from Indian Missions overseas are regularly
consolidated and shared by the Division with relevant
domestic stakeholders to facilitate informed policy
coordination and strengthen India’s global technology
engagement.
Cyber Diplomacy
The Cyber Diplomacy Division of the Ministry is
a specialised division dealing with international
developments in cyberspace and Artificial Intelligence
(AI). The Division has engagements with various
countries bilaterally for exploring and strengthening
cooperation in cyber matters and advocates India’s
cyber priorities and interests at the regional and
multilateral fora, including the United Nations.
Bilateral cyber dialogues, regional engagements in
the BRICS, Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO),
ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF) in the information
security discourses, participation in the UN processes
on global cyber norms and policy developments
were highlights during the reporting period. On AI,
our important engagements included co-chairing AI
Action Summit with France, exploration of bilateral
AI initiatives, and participation in regional and global
discourses in AI Governance.
Bilateral Cyber Engagements
India had bilateral cyber engagements with the
European Union (EU), Israel, Brazil, and Australia
during this period that explored capacity building
and training cooperation, exchange of best practices
and information sharing, finding synergy and
complementarities in cyber policy and strategies,
protection
of
critical
information
infrastructure,
exchange of perspectives in global cyber norms
and policy developments. The eighth India–EU
Cyber Dialogue held on 20 March in New Delhi
reviewed the cyber threat landscape and exchanged
views on contemporary developments in cyber
policies, security standards and protection of critical
information infrastructure, as well as cooperation in
multilateral fora on ICT security. The dialogue also
explored bilateral cooperation on standardisation of
6G, security standards for telecom equipment and
joint capacity building activities.
The first India–Israel Cyber Dialogue, which was held
on 26 and 27 March in Jerusalem, exchanged views
on the cyber threat landscape and contemporary
developments in cyber policies. The dialogue explored
areas of complementarities in security standards,
protection of critical information infrastructure and
security standards, exchange of best practices on
security standards for telecom equipment, joint
capacity building activities and cooperation at the
multilateral forums on ICT security issues.
The bilateral cyber engagement with Australia on
9 April in New Delhi reviewed ongoing bilateral
cyber mechanisms and identified focus areas for
strengthening further cooperation such as cyber
capacity building and training, complementarities
in national cyber strategies and policies, exchange
of best practices in protection of critical information
infrastructure and cooperation in critical and emerging
technologies, security of telecommunications network

and equipment as well as technical standards.
The first India–Brazil Cyber Dialogue and Digital
Dialogue were held on 25 and 26 November in
Brasilia. The cyber dialogue had exchange of views on
cyber threat landscape, national cyber strategies and
policies, data protection, security standards, protection
of critical information infrastructure, exploration of
bilateral cooperation in cyber capacity building as
well as exchange of perspectives on global cyber
developments in multilateral fora including the United
Nations. The Digital Dialogue had exchange of views
‘inter-alia’ on national policies and regulatory initiatives
on Data Governance, global AI developments and
explored cooperation opportunities in DPIs.
Regional and Multilateral Cyber
Engagements
India participated in the 10th and 11th sessions of the
UN Open-Ended Working Group (OEWG) on the
security of and in the use of ICTs in February and
July respectively, where countries explored finding
common grounds on evolution of rules, norms and
principles of responsible state behaviour in cyberspace,
the applicability of international law, cooperation
mechanisms for capacity building and confidence
building among countries. These meetings concluded
by adopting a consensus report that recommended
the setting up of a permanent institutional Global
Mechanism under the auspices of the United Nations
on developments in the field of ICTs in the context of
international security and advancing responsible State
behaviour in the use of ICTs. The report is particularly
notable as it recommends establishing a dedicated
Global ICT Security Cooperation and Capacity Building
Portal, which is an Indian proposal, within the United
Nations.
India participated in the ASEAN Regional Forum
meetings on ICT security in March and the 11th BRICS
Working Group on countering misuse of ICTs for
criminal purposes in April. These meetings provided
useful exchanges on the cyber threat landscape, global
cyber developments, regional cyber capacity-building
efforts, exploration of academic cooperation, exchange
of best practices and promotion of institutional
cooperation against cybercrime. India continued to
support cyber capacity building cooperation under
the ARF, Conference on Interaction and Confidence
Building Measures in Asia (CICA) and India-Brazil-
South Africa (IBSA) frameworks to promote training,
exchange of best practices, and sharing of experiences
through workshops and exercises.
Developments in Artificial Intelligence
On the invitation of the President of France Emmanuel
Macron, Prime Minister co-chaired the AI Action
Summit in Paris on 10 and 11 February. During the
Summit, Prime Minister’s advocacy for collective
global efforts in ensuring access to AI for all,
democratisation of technology and AI applications to
achieve SDGs, and development of pro-innovation
led AI governance and standards found synergy with
countries, especially the Global South.

Protocol Division
C H A P T E R
26
The Protocol Division was responsible for all
international protocol matters, including foreign visits
of the Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji, Hon’ble Vice-President,
and Prime Minister abroad and visits to India by
their foreign counterparts and foreign ministers. The
Division also provided support for the organisation of
international conferences and meetings held in India
and was responsible for the welfare of the resident
diplomatic corps, including all matters of their
privileges and immunity.
During the year, the Division successfully supported
the organisation of the 18th Pravasi Bharatiya Divas,
Raisina Dialogue, and the India–Central Asia Foreign
Ministers Dialogue. In addition, this year, the Division
facilitated 10 state visits, eight official visits at the
Head of Government/Head of State level, and 32
Vice-President/deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister
level visits to India. The Division organised the visit of
the Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji to six foreign countries, the
Hon’ble Vice President to one country, and the visit of
the Prime Minister to 22 foreign destinations.
The
Division
also
organised
the
credential
presentation ceremony for 36 new heads of mission.
During the period, two new resident foreign missions
were opened in New Delhi, taking the total of such
foreign missions to 164. In the same period, four new
honorary consulates were opened. The period saw an
addition of 204 new diplomatic posts in the foreign
diplomatic corps in India.
The Protocol Division also coordinated property-
related issues of foreign diplomatic missions and
international organisations, and was responsible
for the upkeep and maintenance of the historic
Hyderabad House. The Division assisted in organising
the excursion trip to Prayagraj, Varanasi, Kaziranga,
and Guwahati for resident Heads of Mission during
the year. The Division facilitated more than 9,300
requests for facilitation at airports and organised 368
entertainment events at the level of head of state,
head of government, ministers, and secretaries.

27
The External Publicity and Public Diplomacy Division
(XPD) continued to spearhead India’s global outreach
by amplifying foreign policy priorities through strategic
communication and engagement. This was achieved
through effective utilisation of digital diplomacy tools,
proactive media management, and organisation
of impactful outreach initiatives. These initiatives,
articulated
through
structured
campaigns
and
collaborations with Missions/Posts abroad, have been
instrumental in reinforcing the Ministry’s objective
of positioning India as a responsible and influential
global actor, while ensuring that the Government’s
message is disseminated with clarity and consistency.
The Division regularly engaged with the media through
press briefings, press releases, advisories, and other
initiatives, providing comprehensive insights into the
Government's stance on various foreign policy issues.
New Initiatives
XPD Division undertook the following new initiatives
in 2025 to advance its objectives:
‘Human Cost of Terrorism’ exhibition
The Division supported Missions in organising the
exhibition titled ‘The Human Cost of Terrorism’
to highlight the profound impact of terrorism on
individuals, families, and societies. The exhibition
was first launched by the EAM at United Nations
Headquarters at New York on 30 June for a period of
12 days. The exhibition featured photographs, videos,
multimedia presentations, testimonials, and creative
works by survivors from around the world, aiming
to humanise the statistics and narratives associated
with terrorism and foster international solidarity in the
fight against the menace. It chronicled major terrorist
incidents in India and abroad with a timeline, while
also featuring an interactive section on global counter-
terrorism efforts and recent attacks including the one
in Pahalgam, India. The exhibition created a space
for collective mourning, remembrance, dialogue,
and policy advocacy. The exhibition reiterated that
terrorism is a global scourge and can only be defeated
with collective actions by the global community. It also
created a space for collective mourning, remembrance,
dialogue, and policy advocacy.

The popularity of Indian music continues to grow
globally reflecting its universal appeal and cultural
resonance across diverse audiences. Catering to this
surging interest, the Division extended support to 114
Missions/Posts by providing a curated collection of
Indian music. These music resources are being used
by Missions/Posts for gifting to foreign dignitaries,
diplomats and local communities thereby amplifying
India’s cultural soft power and fostering deeper
people-to-people ties through the universal language
of music.
Public Diplomacy
Articles Commissioned
The Division commissioned articles on various themes
on the occasion of 79th Independence Day and 76th
Republic Day. The articles were authored by retired
Indian diplomats and eminent experts and were
published in local newspapers by Indian Missions/
Posts abroad in their respective countries.
India Perspectives Magazine
The Ministry’s flagship magazine ‘India Perspectives’ is
under the process of being given a makeover and will
be relaunched as a digital magazine. Since its launch,
the magazine has been published in 16 languages -
Arabic, Bahasa Indonesia, Chinese, English, French,
German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Pashto, Persian,
Portuguese, Russian, Sinhala, Spanish, and Tamil.
‘एक पेड़ मां के नाम’ (#Plant4Mother)
As the nodal point for the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’
campaign in the MEA, the Division, ensured world-
wide implementation of this campaign through the
Missions/Posts. Till December, more than 28,000
trees have been planted by Indian Missions/Posts and
the Regional Passport Offices in India.
Book Committee
The 45th Book Committee selected 482 book titles
under categories such as Indian classics, foreign
policy and strategic affairs, technology and popular
science, Hindi & Sanskrit, art & culture, religion &
spirituality, children books and politics & economy, for
dissemination of these titles by the Missions/Posts.
Demand for approximately 42,000 copies of these
titles were received from 121 Missions/Posts. Apart
from this, books were also provided to Missions/Posts
abroad for establishing India Corners in universities,
colleges, schools, libraries and literary & cultural
centres in the area under their jurisdiction.
Children Books
In order to engage young minds and familiarise them
with Indian history, art, culture and heritage, the
Division supported initiatives of Indian Missions/Posts
of translating children’s books containing Jataka Tales
and other stories into foreign languages including
Bangla, Chinese, Icelandic, Japanese, Khmer, Korean,
Norwegian, Sinhala, Thai and Vietnamese.

India Corners
The Division continued to establish India Corners in
universities, colleges, schools, libraries and literary
& cultural centres abroad. This has been one of the
important public diplomacy tools extensively used by
Missions/Posts. Till date, more than 600 India Corners
have been set by Missions/Posts and more than
300 have been proposed to be set up. The Division
has expanded the suggested list of books for India
Corners from 51 titles to 124 titles, ranging from
classical titles to more contemporary books on India.
The Missions/Posts have been provided flexibility to
edit the suggested list to make it relevant to local
preference. In 2025, books were provided to 20 Indian
Missions/Posts in 18 countries for establishment of
India Corners.
Supporting Public Diplomacy Initiatives
Abroad

Diplomacy initiatives of the Missions/Posts abroad,
such as:

f
Financial assistance to 21 Missions/Posts for
various Public Diplomacy activities such as special
publications, publication/translation of books in
foreign languages, celebration of establishment
of diplomatic relations, media fest/symposium,
‘Ek Ped Maa ke Naam’, organising Indian festivals
and fairs, establishment of India Corners and other
Publicity and promotional events.

f
Organising a digital exhibition titled ‘Human Cost
of Terrorism’ by 19 Missions.

f
Organising Indian Film Festival in Prague (Czech

Outreach in India
Distinguished Lecture Series
The Division revamped the Distinguished Lecture
Series program, which engages universities and
other academic institutions in India to inform the
discourse on India’s foreign affairs, its achievements
and challenges, among students and youth across
the length and breadth of the country. The program
also serves as a strategic communication tool aimed
at building a positive narrative about Indian foreign
policy and the Ministry’s people-centric initiatives.
Between January and December, a total of 21 lectures
were organized by the Division.
Mann Ki Baat
The Division coordinated with Missions/Posts to
compile stories for the monthly broadcast of Prime
Minister’s Mann Ki Baat programme. Between
January and December, inputs shared by the Ministry
were covered in seven episodes of the Mann Ki Baat
programme.

C H A P T E R

Administration
The Administration Division of the Ministry is
entrusted with the primary responsibility of managing
human resources and advancing capacity building
across the Ministry’s headquarters and its 224 Indian
Missions and Posts abroad. The Division oversees
all aspects of cadre management, encompassing
recruitment, training, postings, transfers, deputations,
and career progression, thereby ensuring a structured,
transparent, and merit-based personnel framework.
It also formulates and updates administrative
regulations governing both Indian officials serving
abroad and locally engaged staff in Indian Missions
and Posts.
The sanctioned strength of the Ministry stands
at 4,879 personnel, of which 54.9 percent are
deployed in Missions and Posts overseas. The staffing
pattern spans multiple cadres, including the Indian
Foreign Service (IFS), IFS General Cadre, Branch
B, Stenographers, Interpreters, and the Legal &
Treaties cadre, collectively reflecting the multifaceted
operational
requirements
of
India’s
diplomatic
machinery.
To maintain institutional responsiveness to evolving
foreign policy imperatives, the Ministry periodically
undertakes organisational restructuring exercises.
These reviews enable the refinement of divisional
mandates
and
operational
responsibilities
in
accordance with emerging global priorities. Four new
Territorial Divisions- Central America (CA), South
America (SA), Northern Europe (NE), and Southern
Europe (SE)- were created through the bifurcation of
two existing Divisions, namely the Latin America and
Caribbean (LAC) Division and the Central Europe (CE)
Division.
This year, India expanded its diplomatic footprint
through the establishment of one new Mission in
Quito (Ecuador) and seven new Posts in Manchester
(United Kingdom), Belfast (United Kingdom), Fukuoka
(Japan), Boston (United States of America), Los
Angeles (United States of America), Kazan (Russia)

and Yekaterinburg (Russia) after receiving Cabinet
approval. These additions are in consonance with
India’s broader objective of deepening political,
economic, and strategic engagement across regions,
strengthening its presence in multilateral fora, and
facilitating greater trade and consular outreach.
The Administration Division accords high priority to
the effective use of technology as a means to enhance
administrative
efficiency
and
inter-institutional
coordination. Key platforms in this endeavour include
the MEA e-Samiksha portal, which facilitates real-time
interaction between headquarters and field offices;
the MEADOWS system, which streamlines transfer-
related procedures; and the e-Office platform, which
supports paperless workflow management. The
Division also utilises the Government e-Marketplace
(GeM) for the procurement of manpower and vehicle
services, ensuring transparency, accountability, and
standardisation in administrative processes.
The Ministry’s Capacity Building Plan, operationalised
in 2024, continues to guide professional development
initiatives. All personnel are encouraged to actively
engage with the iGOT Karmayogi platform for
continuous learning and compliance-related training.
Structured
pre-departure
programmes,
multi-
dimensional training modules, and mentorship
schemes for new entrants have been institutionalised
to facilitate professional adaptation and enhance
skill sets. The Ministry focused special attention to
development of foreign linguistic skills of officers,
including at interpretation level. Over time, this has
resulted in the creation of a large pool of officers with
quality foreign language skills. The training curricula are
periodically reviewed and updated to ensure optimal
utilization of human resources. The Administration
Division has also instituted mechanisms for the
furtherance of a dedicated commitment to the holistic
well-being of all Ministry personnel.
The
Ministry's
Internship
Programme
remains
an important initiative to foster greater public
engagement, especially among students. This year, 60
students were selected across two terms, reflecting
the Ministry’s continued commitment to nurturing
young talent and fostering a deeper understanding of
diplomacy among the youth. The selected students
showcased a strong trend of fostering gender diversity
with over half the selected applicants being female
applicants in the past six terms (three years).
The Administration Division’s approach is shown by
its efficient human resource management, strategic
expansion of India’s diplomatic presence, sustained
investment in capacity building, and adoption of
modern digital tools. These efforts collectively
highlight the Ministry’s proactive, professional, and
forward-looking orientation in advancing India’s
diplomatic objectives.
Establishment
The Establishment Division takes care of the Ministry’s
offices in various buildings (repair & maintenance,
allotment, housekeeping, gardening etc.), residential
accommodations (R&M of residential complexes,
Integrated Facility Management Services (IFMS),
allotment of regular as well as transit accommodations,
coordination with MOHUA for GRPA accommodation
etc.), provision of day-to-day use items viz. office
equipment, furniture items, stationery, newspaper,
telephone and intercom, and canteen facility. It is also
the nodal point for processing tender proposals of all
Missions/Posts abroad for housekeeping, supply and
R&M of cars, special items viz. flags, Od’A items, brass
plates and emblems, special stationery items etc.
The Ministry was one of the six Ministries/
Departments, which were allotted space in the
first phase of ‘Central Vista Project’ of the of the
Government of India. The Ministry has been allotted
space in the newly developed Kartavya Bhawan-3
(KB3 3rd floor). In addition, the Division also undertakes
a large number of R&M, construction, renovation,
upgradation and refurbishing projects for conducting
smooth movement of divisions out of South Block and
into new addresses.
Under annual ‘Swachhata Abhiyan’, the Division
coordinated a large-scale weeding-out of the old
and obsolete records, wherein a target was given

to all Divisions to reduce their document storage
requirement by at least 25 percent in preparation

Under 'Swachhata Hi Seva-2025', the Division
coordinated cleanliness activities across all the
Ministry's offices in India (Headquarters in Delhi,
all RPOs, POEs, and Branch Secretariats) and all
Missions/Posts abroad under the 'Swachhotsav'

key focus areas, viz.: (i) Transformation of Cleanliness
Target Units (CTUs); (ii) Clean Public Spaces; (iii)
SafaiMitra Suraksha Shivirs; (iv) Clean Green Utsav;
(v) Swachhata Advocacy events. The Division
coordinated the Ministry’s global activities covering
transformation of 301 CTUs, conducting of 25 health
camps for SafaiMitras, 52 Clean and Green Utsav, and
34 Swachhata advocacy events viz. Cyclathons and
Marathons, Painting competition, Essay competitions,
Waste-to-Art competition, ‘Say No to Single Use
Plastic (SUP) drive etc. As part of welfare measures for
SafaiMitras, The Ministry upgraded and refurbished
the gender friendly space cum rest area for SafaiMitras
in JNB.
The Ministry embarked upon a project to implement
Prime Minister’s ‘Surya Ghar Yojana’ at the Jawaharlal
Nehru Bhawan. An MoU with Solar Energy
Corporation of India (SECI) for installation of a rooftop
solar power project under the ‘Renewable Energy
Service Company (RESCO)’ model was signed on 22
November. It envisages implementation of the project
in a time-bound manner. Once implemented, the
scheme will be extended to all the Ministry offices all
over India for implementation under RESCO (Pay As
You Use) or CAPEX (Self Ownership) model.
The Division has finalised a dedicated portal for the
e-Auction of Toshakhana items i.e. gift items received
by Prime Minister, Ministers and senior government
officers from foreign dignitaries. The portal is being
prepared for launch.
The Ministry conducted a review of the transit
accommodation facilities available to its officers
at the time of incoming and outgoing movement
between headquarters and Missions/Posts abroad,
and upgraded them by providing a number of
essential items of daily use to make the stay
comfortable. The Division facilitated establishment
and operationalisation of the Crèche facility at the
Commonwealth Games (CWG) Residential Complex,
and the Dwarka Housing Complex for use by the
Ministry personnel.
Global Estate Management (GEM)
The Global Estate Management (GEM) Division actively
pursued acquisition, construction, redevelopment and
renovation of properties for Indian Missions/Posts
abroad and RPOs/ ICCR/ POEs/ Branch Secretariats
within India during the year.
In India, several projects were taken up such as the
construction of a Regional Passport Office (RPO) in
Kolkata. A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)
for the renovation of the Sushma Swaraj Institute of
Foreign Service (SSIFS) was signed on 28 April 2024
and the work in Phase I is underway. Land has been
acquired on a 60 years lease from the Andhra Pradesh
Capital Region Development Authority (APCRDA) for
the construction of a proposed new RPO Complex
in Amaravati. The project for establishment of a
Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA) on the fourth
floor of the Indian Society of International Law (ISIL)
building was completed in June and the Central
Public Works Department (CPWD) handed over the
premises to the Economic Diplomacy (ED) Division in
July. Land is also being acquired for the construction of
RPO Trivandrum.
With regard to the ongoing redevelopment of the
Ministry's Complex at KG Marg Project, 40.3 percent
physical progress has been achieved and 46.5 percent
physical progress in MEA Residential Complex – Gole
Market Project has been achieved so far.
In terms of acquisitions, the acquisition of the Consul
General’s residence in Marseille was completed. Other

Right to Information

A total of 3904 RTI applications and 219 First appeals

Implementation of Official Language
Policy
C H A P T E R
29
During the year, the Rajbhasha and Bharatiya
Bhashayein, I&T (RBB, I&T) Division of the Ministry has
undertaken significant initiatives to advance India’s
Official Language Policy through a comprehensive
scheme focused on the promotion and propagation of
Hindi language. This comprehensive approach involves
organising International Regional Conferences on
Hindi and engaging various stakeholders, including
Indian Missions and Posts abroad, Persons of Indian
Origin (PIOs), Non-Resident Indians (NRIs), Non-
governmental Organisation (NGOs), and cultural
institutions, to promote Hindi globally.
Key events such as World Hindi Day on 10 January,
Hindi Divas on 14 September, and Hindi Pakhwada
have been integral to these efforts. The Division
expanded its activities, markedly increasing the
number of locally appointed temporary Hindi teachers
in Indian Missions and Posts abroad from 25 in 2024
to 36 in 2025, further demonstrating a commitment to
enhancing Hindi education globally.
Noteworthy amongst the new initiatives was the
International Gita Mahotsav (IGM) 2025 held on
24-25 November. In response to a request from the
Government of Haryana, the Ministry collaborated
with the Kurukshetra Development Board (KDB)
to celebrate the Annual Gita Mahotsav on an
international scale. A total of 54 Missions and Posts
abroad organised parallel events for the IGM-2025.
The Ministry facilitated the participation of 22
distinguished foreign Sanskrit scholars, international
invitees, craftsmen, and artists at IGM Kurukshetra,
Haryana.
Additionally, translations of the Bhagavad Gita in more
than 32 languages received from Missions abroad
were prominently displayed at IGM Kurukshetra,
highlighting the efforts to share the text with a diverse
audience. The Ministry also provided INR 1.47 crores
in financial support to Missions and Posts abroad for
activities related to IGM-2025.
Further contributing to the dialogue on cultural and
ethical considerations, a conference titled ‘Dharma

and Global Ethics’ in association with Nalanda
University, Bihar was held on 28 November. It
was followed by the ‘International Sanskrit Ganga
Sangam Sammelan’ organised in partnership with
Uttarakhand Sanskrit University, Haridwar, from 30
November to 1 December. These gatherings aim to
foster collaboration and enhance appreciation for
India’s linguistic and spiritual heritage while actively
engaging international scholars and pandits.
The RBB, I&T Division has supplied books and teaching
materials to Missions and Posts abroad to promote the
Hindi language. Additionally, the Division provided
approximately INR 1.19 crores in financial support to
these Missions and Posts to facilitate the engagement
of local teachers to conduct Hindi language classes.
The Division also played a crucial role in coordinating,
through Missions, the granting of scholarships to
international students to study Hindi at Kendriya Hindi
Sansthan in Agra, along with the necessary follow-
up on their enrollment at the institute upon receiving
these scholarships.
Moreover, the responsibility for monitoring the
progressive use of Hindi in the Regional Passport
Offices (RPOs) has been entrusted to the RBB, I&T
Division, in collaboration with the Passport Seva
Programme (PSP) Division. This responsibility is
fulfilled through periodic inspections conducted by
the Division. During this period, inspections were
carried out at four RPOs: RPO Ranchi on 20 May, RPO
Pune on 2 June, RPO Ghaziabad on 3 June, and RPO
Delhi on 4 June.
The first Sub-Committee of the Committee of
Parliament
on
Official
Language
successfully
conducted official language inspections of the
Ministry’s subordinate offices, including RPO Guwahati
(11 April), RPO Shimla (12 June), RPO Chandigarh (12
June), and RPO Patna (29 August). These inspections
aimed to review the progressive use of Hindi in official
work, resulting in valuable suggestions to enhance its
utilisation. The Sub-Committee’s recommendations
are currently being implemented.
World Hindi Day was celebrated with great
enthusiasm by Missions and Posts abroad, as well
as at Headquarters and MEA’s subordinate offices
on 10 January. In addition, Hindi Pakhwada was
organised from 14-28 September, in commemoration
of Hindi Diwas. These events witnessed remarkable
participation, including a significant turnout of foreign
nationals during the World Hindi Day celebrations.
An allocation of approximately INR 2.99 crores was
granted to Missions and Posts for World Hindi Day
celebrations, and INR 2.62 crores for Hindi Diwas
and Hindi Pakhwada events. Various competitions
and activities, such as Hindi essay writing, noting
and drafting in Hindi, Hindi poetry recital, Official
Language-related quiz competitions, and Hindi
vakyansh translation competitions, were organised
during these occasions.
The Division successfully hosted the fifth Executive
Meeting of the World Hindi Secretariat in Port Louis,
Mauritius, on 14-16 July. This meeting convened key
stakeholders, language experts, and representatives
from member countries to discuss strategic initiatives
to advance Hindi internationally. The event served
as an essential platform for fostering international
collaboration, reviewing progress, and charting the
Secretariat’s future directions.
Throughout the year, the Division efficiently conducted
a significant volume of translation work in Hindi
and English, responding promptly to requests from
various Divisions at the Ministry Headquarters and
our Missions and Posts abroad.

Parliament & Coordination Division
C H A P T E R
31
The responsibilities of the Parliament & Coordination
Division
broadly
include
parliamentary
work,
coordination
within
and
outside
the
Ministry,
participation in nationwide campaigns carried out by
other Ministries, monitoring and reviewing of MoUs
signed by India with other countries, admission
of certain categories of foreign students to Indian
educational institutions, and uploading the Ministry’s
inputs on various digital portals to facilitate digital
monitoring of work.
Parliament Section
The Parliament Section serves as the Ministry’s
interface with Parliament and acts as the nodal point
for all Parliament-related work of the Ministry. The
Section ensured a timely response to the issues raised
by Parliament, in compliance with the guidelines laid
down for Parliamentary work.
During the calendar year 2025, the Parliamentary
Standing Committee on External Affairs held sittings
on the following subjects:

EAM chaired the first Consultative Committee Meeting of 2025

Bangladesh, the Maldives, Myanmar, and Sri Lanka.
Since 1 January, a total of 40 matters of significance
have been raised in Parliament under Special
Mention, Rule 377, and Zero Hour. Responses have
been provided to all but two of these matters. In
addition, replies have been furnished to 459 admitted
Parliamentary Questions.
During the year, the Annual Reports and audited
Accounts of the Indian Council for Cultural Relations,
South Asian University, and Nalanda University were
laid before Parliament.
Coordination Section
The Ministry, through its Missions and Posts abroad,
played a key role in the celebration of flagship events
of the Government of India overseas, such as Har Ghar
Tiranga, Rashtriya Ekta Diwas/Week, Constitution
Day, Ayurveda Day, International Women’s Day, and
Janjatiya Gaurav Divas, among others.
The International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA), an initiative
of the Government of India, was launched by Prime
Minister on 9 April 2023, commemorating 50 years
of Project Tiger, with the objective of establishing a
platform to promote the conservation and protection
of the seven Big Cats of the world. To operationalise
the Framework Agreement for IBCA, the matter
was followed up by the Parliament & Coordination
Division, and the agreement came into force on 23
January 2025, following its ratification, acceptance, or
approval by five countries. The Government of India
has provided one-time financial support of USD 18
million for the project and signed the Headquarters
Agreement in April, which designates India as the
host for the IBCA Headquarters and Secretariat. 14
countries, namely India, Cambodia, Eswatini, Liberia,
Nicaragua, Somalia, Guinea, Bhutan, Suriname,
Armenia, Nepal, Rwanda, Ethiopia, and Mongolia,
have already signed the Framework Agreement.

for

abroad,

year to facilitate applications for the grant of political
clearances to foreign nationals to attend or participate
in conferences, seminars, workshops, and sports
events organised in India by the government or private
bodies in a streamlined manner.
The Parliament & Coordination Division served as
the nodal division for facilitating the visits of seven
all-party delegations to key nations from late May
to early June, in connection with Operation Sindoor,
underscoring
India’s
collective
resolve
against
terrorism. The delegations comprised Members of
Parliament, non-government representatives, political
figures, former Ambassadors, and officials of the
Ministry.
Approximately 225 Action Points were monitored and
updated monthly on the eSamikSha Portal concerning
Cabinet decisions, observations of the Cabinet,
recommendations of the Committee of Secretaries, the
Vision Document of the Ministry (SGOS-10), progress

on the implementation of Pragati Projects funded

A special campaign was undertaken for the timely
and effective disposal of pending public grievances,
references from Members of Parliament, State
Governments, inter-ministerial consultations, and
Parliamentary assurances; the conduct of cleanliness
drives; and the management of records (files). The
Ministry participated in the Special Campaign 5.0
on Swachhata across its Missions worldwide. The
Campaign ran from 2 October to 31 October.
As part of Special Campaign 5.0, the Ministry undertook a
range of activities to promote environmental consciousness,
health, hygiene, and civic responsibility, including cleanliness
drives and plantation activities, community-driven initiatives
such as park and sea-beach clean-ups, consular camps across
Missions as part of citizen-centric activities, and the Viksit
Bharat Run.
The main focus areas of the Campaign included
e-waste management, cleanliness drives, Swachhata
awareness
activities,
citizen-centric
initiatives,
effective disposal of public grievances, references from
Members of Parliament, parliamentary assurances,
disposal of scrap, and weeding out of obsolete
files. During this period, the Ministry conducted 949
cleanliness drives, including Swachhata awareness
activities. A total of 1,71,241 physical files were
weeded out, freeing approximately 19,964 sq. ft. of
space. Additionally, revenue of INR 3,09,361 was
generated through scrap removal. Furthermore,
644 public grievances were resolved, and 11 PMO
references and 57 MP references were addressed.
Monitoring Cell
The Monitoring Cell coordinates the review of MoUs
and Agreements signed with foreign countries by
various Ministries and Departments of the Government
of India, assessing their continued relevance and
status. The Ministry liaised with and followed up
regularly with the line Ministries, Divisions within the
Ministry, and India’s Missions and Posts abroad.
This year, of the total 3,382 MoUs and Agreements,
265 were reviewed. Of these, 247 MoUs were
continued, while 18 were identified for discontinuation.
Education Section
The Education Section of the Ministry managed
the
selection,
nomination,
and
admission
of
foreign students from 57 friendly neighbouring
and developing countries for MBBS, BDS, B.Arch.,
B.E., B.Tech., B. Pharmacy, and Diploma courses in
Engineering and Pharmacy at various government
institutions in India under the Self-Financing Scheme,
against seats allocated to the Ministry by the Ministry
of Health and Family Welfare and the Ministry of
Education. Persecuted religious minority migrants
from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, and Pakistan residing
in India were also offered seats under this scheme.
During the academic year 2025–26, 26 eligible
applicants were allotted seats in the B.E., B.Tech.,
B.Arch., and B. Pharmacy courses. A total of 252
applications were received for MBBS and BDS courses
from foreign nationals and persecuted migrants from
minority communities residing in India.
The Education Section also processed political
clearances for foreign students attending elective
training, observerships, and short or long-term
training programmes, as well as those appearing in
various postgraduate medical and allied entrance
examinations. Clearances were also issued for foreign
students studying Hindi at the Central Institute of
Hindi (KHS), Agra, and for Research Visas.

Rapid Response Cell
397
Rapid Response Cell
C H A P T E R
33
Rapid Response Cell (RRC) is the nodal division
of the Ministry to undertake the Government’s
Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR)
efforts worldwide. Established in 2021 with a focus
on COVID-19-related responsibilities, the RRC has
been actively engaged in HADR operations following
disasters and providing need-based humanitarian
assistance to partner countries globally.
The RRC’s mandate also includes evacuating Indian
nationals from crisis-affected areas. Additionally,
the RRC plays a key role in expanding the Ministry’s
health diplomacy initiatives, including the Quad
Health Security Partnership (QHSP), Digital Health
Initiatives for Indo-Pacific countries, recognition of the
Indian Pharmacopoeia (IP) by partner nations, and
the establishment of Janaushadhi Kendras in partner
countries.
Major Developments
Between January and December, India conducted
complex, rapid operations to meet the diverse needs
of disaster-stricken partner countries. India’s HADR
efforts have expanded significantly beyond the
neighbourhood to include regions in Africa, Latin
America, the Caribbean, and Oceania. Additionally,
India responded swiftly and effectively to assist Indian
nationals stranded overseas.
In line with its established reputation as a ‘First
Responder and Credible HADR Provider,’ India carried
out four major operations in 2025: Operation Brahma,
Operation Sindhu, repatriation of Indian nationals
from the Myanmar-Thailand border, and Operation
Sagar Bandhu. Furthermore, HADR assistance was
extended to more than 20 countries throughout the
year.
Operation Brahma
On 28 March, a 7.7 magnitude earthquake struck
Myanmar, resulting in over 3,000 deaths and 5,017
injuries, alongside widespread destruction. The
earthquake damaged homes, hospitals, schools, and
title: mea_annual_report

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025

essential infrastructure, including airports, roads,
buildings, and bridges. In response to the devastation,
a state of emergency was declared in six of the most
affected regions, where entire communities were
displaced, forcing people to seek shelter in makeshift
conditions. This situation disrupted markets, worsened
psychosocial distress, and brought essential services,
such as food, clean water, sanitation, and healthcare,
to the brink of collapse.
In the aftermath of the devastating earthquake in Myanmar
and Thailand, INS Satpura and INS Savitri sailed for Yangon,
as part of the Indian Navy’s immediate HADR response under
Operation Brahma, March 2025
Within hours of the disaster, India launched Operation
Brahma to provide HADR to the people of Myanmar.
The first shipment of relief aid arrived in Myanmar
on 29 March. During the operation, India provided
approximately 1000 MT of HADR supplies, including
tents, blankets, sleeping bags, hygiene kits, generators,
essential medicines, medical consumables, and food
aid such as rice and cooking oil. Additionally, India sent
20 prefabricated structures and cement to support the
rehabilitation of government offices.
To assist in the search and rescue efforts in Mandalay,
India deployed NDRF’s 80-member Heavy Search
and Rescue (SAR) specialist team. A 127-member
Indian Army Field Hospital team (60-para) was
also dispatched to Mandalay, where they treated
2,519 patients. Furthermore, a six-member Engineer
Reconnaissance team from the Indian Army was sent
to Mandalay and Naypyidaw to assess structural
damage and recommend restoration of the affected
infrastructure.
Nine IAF aircraft and five IN ships were deployed to
deliver the aforementioned assistance. Operation
Brahma represented India’s whole-of-government
endeavour to respond to the extensive destruction
in Myanmar and to demonstrate solidarity with its
people.
Operation Sindhu
India launched Operation Sindhu on 18 June to
evacuate Indian nationals from conflict zones in Iran
and Israel. A total of 4415 Indian nationals (3597 from
Iran and 818 from Israel) were evacuated through 19
special evacuation flights, including three IAF C-17
aircraft. Additionally, 14 OCI card-holders, nine Nepali
nationals, four Sri Lankan nationals, and one Iranian
spouse of an Indian national were also evacuated
from Iran.
Indian Minister of State for Parliamentary Affairs welcomed
Indian nationals repatriated under Operation Sindhu from
Sharm El-Sheikh, Egypt, who were residing in Israel upon their
arrival in New Delhi, June 2025

Repatriation of Indian nationals
from Myanmar-Thailand border
(ongoing)
India, with the support of Myanmar and Thailand, has
been actively facilitating the repatriation of Indian
nationals trapped in online scam centres operating
in regions along the Myanmar-Thailand border.
Since March, a total of 1,500 Indian nationals were
repatriated, including a recent operation in November.
These efforts are being undertaken in coordination
with Thai authorities, with rescued individuals
transiting through Mae Sot and returning to India on
special or commercial flights via Bangkok.
India arranged for the safe repatriation of 266 Indian nationals
who were released from cyber-scam centres in Southeast Asia,
March 2025
Operation Sagar Bandhu
In response to Cyclone Ditwah in Sri Lanka, India
launched Operation Sagar Bandhu on 28 November
to provide HADR to the affected population. Within
the first three days following the cyclone, India
delivered a total of 53 tonnes of emergency relief
materials. This included 9.5 tonnes of emergency dry
rations delivered by INS Vikrant and INS Udayagiri,
31.5 tonnes of relief materials airlifted by three IAF
aircraft (two C-130Js and one IL-76), and 12 tonnes of
essential supplies delivered by INS Sukanya.
INS Vikrant handed over emergency relief provisions for
distribution to Cyclone Ditwah-affected communities in
Colombo, Sri Lanka, December 2025
Overall, under Operation Sagar Bandhu, India provided
over 1,100 tonnes of relief supplies to Sri Lanka. The
aid included emergency dry rations, tents, tarpaulins,
blankets, hygiene kits, ready-to-eat food, essential
medicines, and two BHISHM (Bharat Health Initiative
for Sahyog Hita & Maitri) modular trauma cubes. Also,
an Aarogya Maitri team operated a medical unit for
several days, using the BHISHM cubes to provide
urgent medical assistance and conducted on-site
training for Sri Lankan Air Force medical officers.
Additionally, India established a fully modular Indian
Army Field Hospital, equipped with ambulances,
trauma care units, operating theatres, and 73 medical
personnel, along with 500 mobile water purification
units to address urgent medical needs. The aid was
transported to Sri Lanka through IAF special flights
and Indian military ships.
India was the first country to deploy trained disaster
responders, including 80 NDRF personnel and a K9
Search and Rescue unit. Furthermore, two Chetak
helicopters from INS Vikrant and the IAF’s two Mi-17
V5 helicopters were deployed to rescue vulnerable
groups in coordination with the Sri Lankan Air Force.
The rescued individuals included nationals from Sri
Lanka, India, Germany, Slovenia, the United Kingdom,
South Africa, Poland, Belarus, Iran, Australia, Pakistan,
and Bangladesh. In addition, over 2,500 stranded
Indians were evacuated via special IAF flights and
commercial flights.

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
402
Bolivia
To tackle the environmental crisis and health issues
caused by forest fire in the Amazon region of Santa
Cruz, Beni and Pando regions in Bolivia, India sent
humanitarian aid of fire-fighting equipment, viz, fire-
fighting gears, first-aid kits, medicines and other
utilities to Bolivia in two tranches in January and April.
India also supplied 3,00,000 doses of Measles and
Rubella (MR) vaccines, along with the necessary
supplies for administration to Bolivia on a grant basis
following the Measles outbreak in Bolivia in July. In
addition, India also provided humanitarian assistance
in the form of medical supplies.
Afghanistan
In a significant humanitarian gesture, India donated
4.8 tonnes of vaccines to Afghanistan in April to help
combat Rabies, Tetanus, Hepatitis B, and Influenza,
potentially saving thousands of lives across the
country. This vital consignment underscores India’s
enduring friendship with the people of Afghanistan
and the deep-rooted people-to-people ties between
the two nations.
Further, India has extended continued humanitarian
assistance to Afghanistan by supplying medical
equipment and consumables to the 300-bed and
400-bed hospitals in Kabul. This support aims to
enhance the country’s healthcare infrastructure
through phased deliveries.
For the 400-bed hospital, three tranches were
supplied: first tranche of 626.56 kg was delivered
on 18 May, second tranche of 554.54 kg on 11 June,
and third tranche of 877.89 kg on 6 October. For the
300-bed hospital, two tranches were delivered in
September and October, respectively. These efforts
reaffirm India’s unwavering commitment to the well-
being of the Afghan people and its resolve to support
Afghanistan’s health sector through humanitarian
cooperation and goodwill.
India also provided multiple humanitarian relief
consignments to Afghanistan following the August-
November earthquake period. On 2 September, India
airlifted 21 tonnes of relief items, including family tents,
blankets, sleeping materials, hygiene kits, medicines,
generators, kitchen sets, water purifiers, and water
storage tanks to Kabul. On 15 September, additional
tents, blankets, and medical kits were provided.
After another strong earthquake in early November,
India sent 15 tonnes of food supplies, such as wheat
flour, pulses, rice, oil, and baby food, by air on 3
November. This was followed by another consignment
of approximately 75 tonnes of medicines, medical
devices, and equipment delivered in November and
December. Overall, the relief support focused on
assisting displaced families in need of temporary
shelter, food, and medical assistance.
Additionally, India supplied a consignment comprising
31,867 doses each of Meningitis and Influenza
vaccines in May, November, and December to support
Afghanistan’s ongoing public health initiatives. A
shipment of medicines for vector-borne diseases was
also delivered in October. These efforts reflect India’s
steadfast partnership with the people of Afghanistan
and its commitment to supporting the country’s
healthcare resilience and recovery.
Nepal
Reaffirming its Neighbourhood First policy, India
extended medical assistance to Nepal, comprising
medicines and vaccines for patients suffering from
Thalassemia and Sickle Cell Disease in April. The
consignment included Influenza Vaccine, Salmonella
Vaccine,
Meningococcus
Vaccine,
Haemophilus
Influenza Vaccine, and Streptococcus Pneumonia
Vaccine.
These vaccines will play a crucial role in improving
the quality of life of individuals affected by Sickle
Cell Disease and Thalassemia in Nepal. This gesture
stands as a testament to the close bonds of friendship
and cooperation between India and Nepal. It reflects
their shared vision for a healthier, more resilient future
for their citizens.
Following the devastating floods and landslides
caused by heavy rains in Nepal on 3-5 October,
which resulted in extensive infrastructure damage
title: mea_annual_report

text:
Rapid Response Cell
403
and disrupted connectivity in several areas, India has
promptly responded to Nepal’s urgent request for
assistance. In November, India dispatched the first
set of Bailey Bridges, with an additional nine sets
scheduled for delivery progressively over the next
five months. This response illustrates India’s strong
commitment to supporting Nepal’s disaster recovery
efforts and enhancing bilateral cooperation during
challenging times.
Cameroon
India reaffirmed its commitment as a reliable partner
to Cameroon during challenging times by providing
humanitarian assistance. In June, India delivered relief
materials, life-saving essential medicines, and 1,000
MT of rice to support the victims of the devastating
floods that affected the Far North Region of Cameroon
in 2024. This action reflects India’s solidarity with the
people of Cameroon in their time of need and aims
to strengthen cooperation among the nations of the
Global South.
Syria
In July, India delivered a 5 MT consignment of
humanitarian
assistance,
including
life-saving
medications such as anti-cancer drugs, antibiotics, and
anti-hypertensives to Syria. This act symbolises India’s
significant goodwill toward the Syrian population.
Somalia
India sent a 10-ton consignment of humanitarian
assistance, including essential medicines, surgical
items, hospital supplies, and biomedical equipment in
July.
Maldives
In July, India gifted two BHISHM cubes to the
Maldives. The cubes are mobile medical units that can
be rapidly deployed in emergencies and are designed
to enhance the Maldives’ disaster preparedness. Each
cube is equipped to handle up to 200 emergency
cases, including trauma, burns, and fractures. Prime
Minister handed over the cubes to the President of
Maldives Mohamed Muizzu during his visit on 25 July.
Mozambique
India initiated a humanitarian outreach program and
provided 20 MT of HADR material to Mozambique.
This aid includes medicines, surgical supplies,
and consumables, delivered as part of India’s
MAHASAGAR vision.
The first shipment was sent through ICGS Sachet on
11 October. A second shipment was dispatched by
sea in December. These efforts demonstrate India’s
commitment to enhancing Mozambique’s public
health and disaster management capabilities. Future
plans include organising medical camps and artificial
limb camps in collaboration with Indian donors.
The first tranche of India-gifted medicines and equipment to Mozambique was handed over to the Mozambique Minister of Health in
Maputo, October 2025.
title: mea_annual_report

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
404
Indonesia
In October, India responded to a request from Indonesia
by supplying Prussian Blue capsules to help address
contamination from Cesium-137. This action reaffirms
India’s role as a First Responder and its commitment
to MAHASAGAR vision and regional cooperation. The
provision of Prussian Blue capsules aided Indonesia in
its efforts to mitigate potential nuclear or radiological
emergencies, specifically those involving Cesium-137
contamination.
India swiftly mobilised and gifted required Prussian Blue
capsules to Indonesia to mitigate the effects of Caesium-137
contamination, October 2025.
Peru
In a show of solidarity with its partners in the
Global South and to reaffirm friendship and support
during natural disasters, India dispatched a 32-ton
humanitarian aid consignment to Peru. This aid aims to
address the urgent needs of communities devastated
by recent floods and landslides. Delivered in
November, the shipment includes essential medicines,
250,000 units of saline solution to treat dehydration,
tents, food packages, and water purification materials.
Timor-Leste
A severe rabies outbreak is currently underway,
leading to a significant shortage of rabies vaccines and
posing a serious threat to public health and safety in
Timor-Leste. In response, India provided humanitarian
assistance by supplying 10,000 doses of rabies vaccine
and 2,000 doses of Rabies immunoglobulin for human
use. Delivered in November, the assistance will help
contain the ongoing rabies outbreak in Timor-Leste,
strengthen collaboration in the healthcare sector, and
further affirm India’s role as a reliable partner.
Fiji
India reaffirmed its strong commitment to enhancing
public health cooperation and supporting Fiji in
its efforts to combat the rising incidence of HIV. In
November, India provided more than three tonnes of
Anti-Retro Viral (ARV) drugs to Fiji as grant assistance.
This delivery marked the largest single consignment
of medicines ever gifted by India to Fiji. The aim was to
augment the current supply and ensure uninterrupted
access to treatment for people living with HIV in Fiji,
especially in light of the recent surge in reported cases.
Venezuela
In November, as part of its commitment to
humanitarian assistance, India sent a consignment
of 2.7 tonnes of life-saving vaccines to address the
significant challenges faced by Venezuela’s national
vaccination program.
Seychelles
India reaffirmed its commitment to supporting
Seychelles’ development priorities by supplying a
consignment of 3.5 tonnes of medicines in November.
These medicines were intended for cardiovascular
diseases, diabetes, gastrointestinal ailments, and
vitamins and supplements.
Jamaica
Demonstrating its commitment to global solidarity and
disaster response, India delivered around 20 tonnes
of HADR supplies to Jamaica in November, following
widespread devastation from Hurricane Melissa. The
consignment included the BHISHM modular trauma
unit, along with generators, tents, bedding, mats,
kitchen and hygiene kits, solar lanterns, and other
essential materials to support post-hurricane recovery.
Sierra Leone
India extended humanitarian assistance to Sierra
Leone to help strengthen its medical infrastructure
title: mea_annual_report
creator: PDFium

text:
Rapid Response Cell
405
and enhance public health outcomes. In December,
a consignment of 15 Haemo-Dialysis Machines,
complete with portable reverse osmosis (RO) units
and consumable kits, was delivered. This effort reflects
India’s enduring ethos of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam,
the spirit of South-South cooperation, and a steadfast
commitment to Africa, as envisioned by Prime Minister.
Tanzania
In December, at the request of Shree Hindu Mandal
Hospital, a registered non-profit trust founded in 1919
and serving the Tanzanian community in health care,
education, social welfare, and youth development,
India provided medical equipment to the hospital.
HADR Assistance to Health Infrastructure
in Pacific Island Countries
In line with India’s commitment to the Pacific Island
Countries (PICs) made during the third FIPIC Summit,
the first consignment of 12 hemodialysis machines
equipped with portable reverse osmosis (RO) units
was delivered to Papua New Guinea in November
2024. Following this, one hemodialysis machine with a
portable RO unit was supplied to each of the Solomon
Islands, Marshall Islands, Nauru, and Palau in January
and April. Additionally, a six-bedded container-based
dialysis unit was delivered to Kiribati in May. These
supplies will significantly strengthen the healthcare
infrastructure of the Pacific Island Countries, reflecting
India’s commitment to development partnership
and capacity-building cooperation under the FIPIC
framework.
Food-Grain Assistance
Cameroon
In line with its humanitarian assistance and
commitment to the Global South, India sent 1000
MT of rice, along with essential medicines and relief
materials, to the people of Cameroon. This aid was in
response to the devastating floods, which resulted in
significant loss of livelihoods, land, and livestock. The
humanitarian consignment was delivered in June.
Sudan
Affirming its partnership with the Global South, India
provided a humanitarian aid consignment of 2000
MT of rice to Sudan. This effort aimed to address
food insecurity and nutritional needs of those facing
hardships due to prolonged civil conflicts. The aid was
delivered in July.
Fiji
As part of its Act East Policy, India sent five MT of
Black-eyed Cowpea seeds to support agricultural
production in Fiji. The delivery of this consignment
was completed in August.
Health Cooperation
Jan Aushadhi Kendra
This year, India signed agreements with four
partner countries for the Jan Aushadhi initiative: the
Maldives, Nauru, Guyana, and Fiji. This agreement
aims to provide cost-effective, ‘Made in India’ generic
medicines at affordable prices, enhancing public
healthcare and strengthening bilateral cooperation in
the health sector among countries in the Global South.
Prior to this, Mauritius became the first country to
adopt the Jan Aushadhi Scheme, allowing it to source
approximately 250 high-quality medicines from the
Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India
(PMBI) through HLL Lifecare Limited.
Second edition of Policymakers’ Forum
The Ministry, in collaboration with the Ministry of
Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) and the Indian
Pharmacopoeia Commission, organised the second
Policymakers’ Forum on 16-19 June. This event
brought together 45 policymakers and senior drug
regulatory officials from 21 countries, including Liberia,
Togo, Mali, Mauritania, Sierra Leone, Cameroon,
Rwanda,
Lesotho,
Eswatini,
Kenya,
Botswana,
Ethiopia, Comoros, Seychelles, Madagascar, Papua
New Guinea, Zimbabwe, St. Lucia, St. Vincent & the
Grenadines, Barbados, and Chile. Delegates from
the Caribbean Public Health Agency (CARPHA) also
