creator: PDFium

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
406
participated, reaffirming India’s role as a valued and
trusted partner in global health.
This forum was built on the momentum of the first
Policymakers’ Forum held in August 2024, during
which
several
participating
countries
formally
recognised the Indian Pharmacopoeia as a standard for
drug quality. The forum highlighted India’s proactive
efforts in advancing global public health objectives.
During the forum, delegates participated in technical
sessions focused on pharmacopeial standards, India’s
regulatory landscape, and successful public health
schemes. Additionally, site visits were arranged to
IPC’s state-of-the-art laboratories in Ghaziabad,
a Jan Aushadhi Kendra in Agra, and prominent
pharmaceutical and vaccine manufacturing and R&D
facilities in Ahmedabad, providing delegates with
firsthand exposure to India’s robust scientific and
regulatory systems.
MoUs on recognition of Indian
Pharmacopoeia
The Indian pharmacopoeia is gaining international
recognition through diplomatic efforts and alignment
with global standards. As of 2025, the Indian
pharmacopoeia has been accepted as a standard
reference in 19 countries in the Global South,
including nations in Africa, South Asia, and Latin
America. India signed an MoU on pharmacopoeia
cooperation with Sri Lanka, Cuba, Maldives, Trinidad &
Tobago, Fiji, Botswana, and Liberia. This collaboration
aims to foster mutually beneficial cooperation in
pharmaceutical trade and public health between India
and these partner countries.
Quad Initiatives
Quad Workshop on Pandemic
Preparedness for Indo-Pacific Region
Under the presidency of Quad, India organised a
‘Quad Workshop on Pandemic Preparedness for
Indo-Pacific Region’ on 17-19 March. MoS (Health)
inaugurated the workshop. Key speakers at the
inaugural session included Principal Scientific Advisor,
Secretary (Health), Additional Secretary (MoH & FW),
and Additional Secretary (Americas).
India hosted Quad Workshop on Pandemic Preparedness in New Delhi, March 2025
title: mea_annual_report
creator: PDFium

text:
Rapid Response Cell
407
An outcome of the sixth Quad Leaders’ Summit held
in September 2024, the workshop brought together
senior health officials and technical experts from
the Quad nations - India, US, Japan, and Australia.
In addition, over 25 delegates from 15 countries
across the Indo-Pacific region participated, including
representatives from Cambodia, Fiji, Indonesia, Kenya,
Kiribati, Madagascar, the Maldives, Mozambique,
Palau, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Tanzania, Thailand,
Tonga, and Tuvalu, as well as international health
organisations.
During the workshop, participating countries shared
their experiences and best practices in pandemic
preparedness, specifically focusing on governance,
surveillance,
and
innovation.
The
discussions
centred on strengthening global health frameworks,
enhancing preparedness and resilience, ensuring
coordinated pandemic responses, and promoting
the implementation of the One Health approach.
Topics also included risk communication, community
engagement, disease surveillance, and capacity
building. This workshop marked a significant
milestone in establishing a robust and coordinated
health security framework for the Indo-Pacific region.
Quad Cancer Moonshot Initiative
The Cancer Moonshot Initiative was launched by the
Quad countries in September 2024, with the goal of
reducing the burden of cancer across the Indo-Pacific
region. Under this initiative, India has committed to
providing HPV sampling kits, detection tools, and
cervical cancer vaccines valued at USD 7.5 million to
the region.
This significant contribution aims to strengthen local
efforts to prevent and detect cervical cancer early and
to empower communities with affordable, accessible
screening and prevention tools. It also supports HPV
vaccination programmes designed to reduce the
disease burden across the Indo-Pacific. As part of this
commitment, a total of 226,000 units of each type of
HPV Sampling Kit and HPV Diagnostic/Testing Kit
will be supplied in phases to the identified countries
in the region.
Quad Partnership on HADR in the Indo-
Pacific
India hosted the inaugural Quad HADR Tabletop
Exercise (TTX) and Strategic WG meeting in New
Delhi in December 2022, which provided a platform
for the Quad to come together and deliberate on an
effective HADR response mechanism for the Indo-
Pacific region. Following Australia (2023) and Japan
(2024), the US hosted the fourth Quad HADR TTX and
strategic meeting in Honolulu in December. The Quad
WG actively engages and exchanges information on
HADR efforts. The current Chairship is with the US for
2025-26.
As a foundational pillar of the Quad partnership,
HADR is central to the group’s efforts to promote
peace, security, prosperity, and resilience in the Indo-
Pacific. The coordinated delivery of humanitarian
assistance in response to the devastating earthquake
in Myanmar in March demonstrated the Quad’s ability
to mobilise resources quickly and provide essential
life-saving aid.
Indo-Pacific Logistics Network (IPLN)
Quad partners met at the Asia-Pacific Centre for
Security Studies in Honolulu, Hawaii, to conduct a
TTX from 28 April to 2 May. This simulation aimed
to launch the Quad Indo-Pacific Logistics Network
(IPLN). The IPLN is an initiative designed to enhance
coordination and interoperability among partner
nations in logistics and HADR operations across the
Indo-Pacific region.
Quad partners - India, Australia, Japan, and US - met at the
Asia-Pacific Centre for Security Studies in Honolulu, Hawaii, to
conduct a Tabletop Exercise, April-May 2025

Through activities such as tabletop exercises (TTXs)
and technical working groups, the IPLN seeks to
strengthen multinational airlift planning, streamline
resource-sharing mechanisms, and improve collective
response capabilities during regional crises. The
network emphasises practical cooperation, information
exchange, and the development of resilient, flexible
logistics frameworks to support a free, open, and
secure Indo-Pacific.
The Quad partners successfully conducted the first
Field Training Exercise (FTX) alongside Operation
Christmas Drop at Andersen Air Force Base in Guam
on 8-12 December. This exercise was part of the
Quad Indo-Pacific Logistics Network (IPLN).
Furthermore, IPLN, in collaboration with the Indo-
Pacific Partnership for Maritime Domain Awareness,
showcases the Quad’s dedication to sustaining a free
and open Indo-Pacific. It also underscores the need
to enhance practical cooperation to address regional
challenges.

text:
Sushma Swaraj Institute of Foreign Service
409
Sushma Swaraj Institute of Foreign
Service
C H A P T E R
34
The Sushma Swaraj Institute of the Foreign Service
(SSIFS) is one of the 25 Central Training Institutes of
the Government of India. It was established in 1986
to impart professional training to the newly inducted
officers of the Indian Foreign Service (IFS) each year.
Over the years, the Institute's training ambit has
expanded to include time-bound Mid-Career Training
Programs (MCTPs) for serving MEA officers, as well
as in-service and promotion-related training programs
for other MEA personnel and members of other GoI
Ministries and Central Training Institutes. It also
conducts pre-posting training programmes for officers
other than MEA posted to Indian Missions and Posts
abroad. SSIFS regularly conducts training programs
for foreign diplomats, as a tool to deepen friendly
bilateral relations based on trust, cooperation and
shared growth and development, particularly with the
Global South. All training programmes at SSIFS focus
on building/enhancing the behavioural, functional, and
domain competencies of the participants.
SSIFS has been acknowledged by the Capacity Building
Commission (CBC) for effectively incorporating
the Commission's stated mandate of capacity
enhancement and promoting decompartmentalisation,
both in terms of the quantum of programs and
their quality. For the first time, SSIFS conducted the
Induction Training Program for the 2024 Batch of IFS
Officer Trainees through the Learning Management
System (LMS), which it used extensively as a central
hub for learning content, tracking learners’ progress,
administering assessments, and creating a repository
for future use. Learning through LMS was extended
to MCTPs and to foreign diplomats’ programs, thus
moving towards becoming a Centre of Excellence by
imparting high-quality training more professionally.
Active engagement of SSIFS with other civil service
training academies, including LBSNAA, NACIN, etc.,
in terms of delivering curated sessions on Foreign
Policy and Diplomacy has been acknowledged and
lauded by CBC. SSIFS is currently undertaking re-
accreditation based on the revised accreditation
parameters, NSCSTI 2.0, issued by CBC. In addition,

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
410
SSIFS, in coordination with the Administration Division
and other relevant Divisions of MEA, have added self-
paced courses on the iGOT Karmayogi Portal.
SSIFS also engaged actively with other Diplomatic
Training Academies- Dean (SSIFS) attended the 51st
International Forum on Diplomatic Training (IFDT)
themed "Navigating Change in a Complex world:
Innovation in Diplomatic Training" in Cuzco, Peru, on 11-
14 November, in which 77 participants took part from
around the world. Dean took part in a high-level Panel
Discussion on ‘What Do the 21st Century Diplomats
Need to Know? Rethinking Diplomatic Education’,
in which he outlined how training institutions need
to adapt their curricula to diplomacy's expanding &
diversifying role in a rapidly changing world.
The Institute was represented by Dean (SSIFS) at the
Conference of Central Training Institutes, hosted by
LBSNAA on 26-27 November, which highlighted the
need for compassionate, mindset and skillset oriented
training with a whole-of-nation approach towards
‘Viksit Bharat’. The Conference was held to mark the
conclusion of the 100th Foundation Course for the
2025 Batch Officer Trainees.
Induction Training Programmes for
IFS Officer Trainees
33 IFS Officer Trainees of the 2024 batch and 2
Bhutanese diplomats joined SSIFS on 2 December
2024 for their Induction Training Program (ITP).
The nine-month-long ITP was divided into three
segments – Phase I, Desk Attachment, and Phase II -
each spanning nearly three months, culminating in the
valedictory ceremony on 26 August.
The training program comprised classroom sessions
that, inter alia, covered procedural aspects, including
administrative rules and finance, as well as domain-
specific subjects such as bilateral and multilateral
diplomacy, economic diplomacy, science and tech
diplomacy, defence diplomacy, and public & cultural
diplomacy. The sessions also included simulation
exercises, which enabled more active learning and
involvement of the Officer Trainees. During the
course of the training program, the Officer Trainees
also had various attachments, including the Mission
Attachment and Army/Navy/Air Force Attachments,
which provided essential insights and learning
opportunities. While the Officer Trainees had the
chance to call on EAM and Foreign Secretary in
the early days of the ITP, they also called on the
Hon'ble Rashtrapati ji and Prime Minister towards the
completion of the program.
On 1 December, SSIFS also commenced the Induction
Training Program of the 2025 Batch of IFS, comprising
52 Officer Trainees along with 2 Bhutanese Diplomats.
Particularly noteworthy was the 3-day module
organised by Clingendael Academy on Law of Seas
and maritime governance, which was a first of its kind
and marked institutional cooperation between SSIFS
and Clingendael.
Prime Minister interacted with Officer Trainees of the 2024 batch of the Indian Foreign Service, August 2025

text:
Sushma Swaraj Institute of Foreign Service
411
Mid-Career Training Programmes
for IFS Officers
SSIFS held Mid-Career Training Program (MCTP) I, II
and III. MCTP-I was held for 2013-14 Batches from
5-23 May, facilitating the timely promotion of the
batches to Director rank. MCTP-II was held between
7-27 April for the 2009 Batch officers, to enable
their promotion to Joint Secretary rank. MCTP-III was
organised from 18 August to 5 September for 2000-
01 batches for their promotion to the Additional
Secretary rank.
All the Mid-Career Training Programs consisted of
two weeks of training at SSIFS, comprising foreign
policy modules and sessions on leadership, emotional
intelligence, and related topics. Upon completion
of these modules at SSIFS, the Officers undertook
a week-long State Attachment, including visits to
aspirational districts, where feasible, as part of MCTPs.
Special Training Programmes for
other Services
During the year, SSIFS conducted the pre-deployment
training programs for Officers/Officials of the Cabinet
Secretariat from 3-4 November, and for Defence
Attache Designates from 24-28 November.
Special Courses for Foreign
Diplomats
SSIFS conducts Special Courses for diplomats from
partner countries and regional groupings. This year,
SSIFS conducted three Flagship Programmes viz the
fifth Edition of Annual Disarmament & International
Security Affairs Fellowship in collaboration with
the D&ISA Division during 13-31 January with the
participation of 34 diplomats from 33 countries,
the 72nd Professional Course for Foreign Diplomats
(PCFD) from 19-30 May with the participation of 30
diplomats from 28 countries and the third Edition
of Global South Young Diplomats Forum (GSYDF)
on 8-19 September with the participation of 42
diplomats (including one from India) from 42 countries
in the Global South. SSIFS launched the first Special
Course for diplomats from IORA Member Countries
from 28 April to 3 May, with 17 diplomats from 15
countries participating.
SSIFS conducted four country-specific programmes
this year. These included second Special Course for 31
diplomats from Myanmar from 17-27 March, second
Special Course for 32 diplomats from the Democratic
Republic of Congo from 19-28 March, fifth Special
Course for 34 diplomats from Iraq from 9-18 June and
second Special Course for 32 diplomats from Egypt
from 8-17 October.
Officer Trainees of the 2024 batch of the Indian Foreign Service called on the Hon’ble Rashtrapati ji, August 2025

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
412
SSIFS organised five programmes, each covering select
countries from distinct regions. These included first
Special Course for 12 diplomats from Kuwait, Oman
& Saudi Arabia from 17-25 February, first Special
Course for 41 diplomats from seven Central and West
African countries (Republic of Guinea, Chad, Niger,
Gabon, Ghana & Libya) from 16-25 July, first Special
Course for 40 diplomats from North and East African
Countries (Eritrea, Libya, Somalia, & South Sudan) from
4-13 August, first Special courses for 46 diplomats
from 21 countries from Central and South America
and Caribbean Island and CARICOM Secretariat on 29
October – 7 November, second Special Course for 15
diplomats from BIMSTEC Member Countries on 17-22
November and first Special Course on diplomatic soft
skills on behavioural and functional competencies for
31 diplomats and officers from Mauritius, Seychelles
and IORA Secretariat on 8-14 December.
Memorandum of Understanding
(MoU)
In 2025, seven MoUs were signed between the SSIFS
and the Departments and Training Institutes of Ireland,
Armenia, Mauritius, Slovakia, Trinidad and Tobago,
Japan and Israel. Starting with Peru in 1997, SSIFS
has so far signed 106 MoUs with partner countries,
including three MoUs with plurilateral organisations-
IBSA, BRICS and BIMSTEC.
Fourth Sushma Swaraj Lecture
2025
The fourth Sushma Swaraj Lecture 2025 on
‘Introduction to India’ was held at SSIFS in collaboration
with India Foundation on 19 November, in which 24
diplomats participated from 21 resident Missions in
New Delhi. The visiting diplomats gained insightful
perspectives on India’s foreign policy, history, polity,
economy, and the new world order from renowned
experts in their respective fields.
Fifth Atal Bihari Vajpayee
Memorial Lecture
The fifth Atal Bihari Vajpayee Memorial Lecture
was delivered by Chairman Temasek Holdings and
Senior Advisor to the Prime Minister of Singapore Teo
Chee Hean on 9 December on the topic – ‘Enduring
Partnerships in a Changing World’. The event
witnessed the august presence of the EAM and senior
officers of the Ministry.
The annual memorial lecture was organised by the
SSIFS at the Sushma Swaraj Bhawan as a tribute
to the late Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee, a towering
statesman and visionary, for his lifelong contribution
towards nation-building and India’s foreign policy as
both External Affairs Minister and Prime Minister.
Training Programme for Other
MEA Officials
Various training courses for Non-Representational
Grade
(NRG)
officials
(Section
Officers/Private
Secretaries and below) were conducted during the
year. These included an Induction Training Programme
for Personal Assistants & Stenographers and
Promotion-related Training Programmes for Section
Officers, Assistant Section Officers, Principal Private
Secretaries, Private Secretaries, Personal Assistants,
and Stenographers. All Promotion-related training
sessions were conducted in a hybrid format to facilitate
participation by officials from various Missions and
Posts abroad. SSIFS conducted the Stenography test
for Personal Assistants and Stenographers, and the
typing test for Junior Secretariat Assistants and Multi-
Tasking Staff. In addition, SSIFS conducted several
pre-posting domain-based, skill-updation training
programmes for MEA officials on Accounts, IMAS
(Integrated Mission Accounting System), and IVFRT
(Immigration, Visa and Foreigners' Registration &
Tracking). A total of 1200 officials benefited from the
NRG training programmes.

Sushma Swaraj Institute of Foreign Service
413
Know India Programme
Endeavouring to develop a closer connection with
the Younger Indian Diaspora to help them strengthen
their ancestral linkages with their current homeland,
SSIFS conducted half day long orientation programme
for the 37 young Indian Diaspora participants from 14
countries for the 83rd Know India Programme (KIP) in
collaboration with the Diaspora Engagement Division
of the MEA. The 84th edition of the programme
registered participation of 39 young visitors from 17
countries.
Transparency Audit under RTI Act,
2005
The SSIFS has been mandated to carry out a
Transparency Audit of proactive disclosures by public
authorities under the RTI Act, 2005, with respect to
public authorities under the MEA. This year, SSIFS
successfully conducted an audit of 191 public
authorities from the Ministry and Indian Missions
and Posts abroad, which had submitted their self-
appraisals on the Central Information Commission
(CIC) portal dedicated to the purpose.

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
414
Indian Council for Cultural Relations
C H A P T E R
35
Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR), in its
endeavour towards strengthening cultural relations
and exchanges across the world, kept buzzing with
activities and made many advances. The Council
worked with its 38 Indian Cultural Centres abroad, five
zonal offices, four sub-zonal offices, and two regional
offices in India. The activities of ICCR included regular
activities, as well as new initiatives and special events.
Major Events
The Council observed several significant occasions,
including the celebration of 150 years of Vande
Mataram on 7 November, the organisation of an
event to commemorate the 137th Birth Anniversary of
Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, Founder President of ICCR,
on 11 November, and the celebration of Constitution
Day on 26 November.
Administration
The 75th Foundation Day of ICCR was celebrated on 9
April, with EAM as the Chief Guest. The event featured
artistic performances by Indian and international
artists, the presentation of Annapurna Certificates, an
art exhibition, and a visual showcase of ICCR’s global
journey.
ICCR organised a three-day induction training
programme for 33 IFS probationers of the 2024 batch
and two Bhutanese diplomats from 6-8 August in
New Delhi.
Scholarships
Scholarships for foreign nationals are an important
tool to encourage them to study and appreciate
Indian arts, heritage, and culture. This helps to create
outreach, a feeling of goodwill, and promote India's
influence across the world.

Indian Council for Cultural Relations
415
In the academic year 2025-26, ICCR offered 4047
scholarship slots to foreign nationals under its 21
scholarship schemes, including 1000 scholarships
for Afghan nationals to pursue online undergraduate/
postgraduate courses.
ICCR coordinated the visit of two ten-member
delegations of Purohits from Trinidad & Tobago and Fiji
for a three-month Purohit Training Course at Banaras
Hindu University (BHU). This course was initiated
pursuant to announcements made by the Prime
Minister during his visits. The course was conducted
in online (two months) and offline (one month)
modes. During the programme, the delegations also
participated in the International Gita Mahotsav (29–
30 November) in Kurukshetra.
ICCR organised Exit Engagement Evening 2025 for
foreign students who had completed their studies
through ICCR scholarships in Shillong (23 June),
Visakhapatnam (28 June), Pune (5 July), Lucknow (9
July), New Delhi (10 July), and Kolkata (11 July). A
total of 1165 students participated.
Chairs
ICCR facilitated the setting up of Chairs of Indian
Studies (Political Science, History, Economics, and
Buddhist Studies), Indian languages such as Hindi, and
dance and music in foreign universities. Throughout the
year, five MoUs were signed with various universities,
five ICCR chairs were established, and 13 scholars
were deployed as ICCR Visiting Professors at various
foreign universities.
Conferences and Seminars
ICCR moderated Thematic Plenary Session V titled
‘Diaspora Dialogues: Stories of Culture, Connection,
and Belongingness’ during the 18th Pravasi Bharatiya
Divas held from 8-10 January in Bhubaneswar.
The seventh International Conference on Yoga, the
first for the Central Asia region, was organised in
collaboration with the Embassy of India in Tashkent,
the Ministry of Ayush, and the Yoga Federation of
Uzbekistan at Tashkent City. The conference was
conducted on 17-19 September, based on the theme
‘Yoga for One Earth One Health’.
ICCR, in association with the Embassy of India, Beijing,
organised a Conference on Indian Philosophy titled
‘Sangamam – Confluence of Indian Philosophical
Traditions’ on 25 October.
ICCR deputed Sadhana Naithani from Jawaharlal
Nehru University, New Delhi, as a visiting faculty to
deliver a keynote address and talks in the International
Conference on ‘From Coast to Coast: Folklore and the
Cultural Lives of the Western Indian Ocean’, organised
by the L'Orientale University of Naples, Italy, from 18-
28 November.
ICCR supported a three-and-a-half day international
workshop
on
‘Tithi
Shastrarth:
Scientific
Multidisciplinary discussion to structure chronology of
major historical events of Before Common Era (BCE) to
decode date of Kurukshetra War’ from 3-5 December.
ICCR facilitated the international air travel of Prof. Zsolt
Balassy, a distinguished researcher from Budapest,
to participate as a speaker at the 26th INCOFYRA
International Conference on Frontiers in Yoga Research
and its application, organised by S-VYASA University,
Bengaluru, from 18-21 December.
Outgoing Cultural Delegations
Between January and September, ICCR sponsored 60
cultural troupes across 57 countries. These included
classical dance forms such as Kathak, Bharatanatyam,
Manipuri, and Odissi, as well as folk dance and music
groups representing traditions such as Punjabi,
Bhojpuri, Gujarati, and Rajasthani, among others.
Between October and December, ICCR sponsored
an additional 12 cultural troupes to perform in 16
countries. These comprised classical genres such as
Kathak and Odissi, along with folk dance and music
groups including Punjabi, Bhojpuri, Gujarati, and
Rajasthani traditions.

text:
Nalanda University
419
Nalanda University
C H A P T E R
36
Nalanda University, established under the Nalanda
University Act, 2010, continued to build upon its
mandate to revive the ancient global centre of learning
that once shaped intellectual exchanges across Asia.
Supported by East Asia Summits' 18 Participating
Countries, including India, the University functions
as an international, non-state and self-governing
institution. The inauguration of its 455-acre net-zero
Green Campus at Rajgir by the Prime Minister on 19
June 2024 marked a major milestone in its evolution.
The campus integrates advanced sustainability
features including a 6.5 MW solar power plant,
decentralised wastewater systems, biogas-based
energy generation under installation, extensive water
bodies, and thermal storage systems.
Academic Programmes, Schools
and Centres
After two years of interim arrangements, new Vice
Chancellor was appointed this year. During the year,
the University continued to operate six Schools of
Studies: the School of Buddhist Studies, Philosophy
& Comparative Religions, School of Historical Studies,
School of Ecology and Environmental Studies, School
of Management Studies, School of Languages &
Literature/Humanities, and the School of International
Relations & Peace Studies. These Schools offer
Master’s programmes, Global Ph.D. programmes, Post-
Doctoral Fellowships, and a wide range of certificate
and diploma courses. The academic framework
was supported by specialised Centres, including
the Centre for Bay of Bengal Studies, the Common
Archival Resource Centre, the Centre for Indo-Persian
Studies, the Centre for Conflict Resolution & Peace
Studies, and the Centre for Studies in Development
and Sustainability.
India announced the establishment of the Centre for
Southeast Asian Studies at Nalanda University during
the 22nd East Asia Summit on 26 October, reinforcing
the University’s role in regional studies, Asian
civilizational research, and Indo-Pacific academic
cooperation.

text:
ANNUAL REPORT | 2025
420
Student Enrollment, Faculty
Strength and Scholarships
During the academic year, the University recorded
a total enrolment of 1,268 students, including 637
residential students in postgraduate and doctoral
programmes. Among them, 332 are international
students drawn from more than 22 countries across
Asia, Africa, Europe, and Latin America. Student
numbers have grown consistently over the last five
years, reflecting the University’s rising academic
profile and stronger global outreach. Faculty strength
stood at 76, including visiting faculty, against the long-
term Cabinet-approved capacity of 307. To support
international student mobility and academic diversity,
the University awarded 363 scholarships during the
year, comprising 180 ASEAN-India Fund scholarships,
100 BIMSTEC scholarships, 60 Bhutan Government
scholarships funded by the Ministry, and 23 endowed
scholarships including the Pyong Rae Lee Scholarship
and the Saraswati Narsingrao Fellowship.
In October, the University also operationalised a
Training and Placement Cell to strengthen career
guidance, industry engagement, and employment
readiness, particularly for students of the School of
Management Studies and allied disciplines.
Infrastructure and Campus
Development
The University’s campus infrastructure expanded
significantly during the year. The academic and
administrative complexes, two large auditoriums, a
1,000-seat multipurpose hall, hostels accommodating
548 students, residential quarters, international guest
facilities, a yoga centre, a modern sports complex, and
well-equipped dining and utility centres became fully
operational. The Central Library, designed to hold
300,000 books, reached structural completion, with
interior works scheduled for completion by January
2026. The campus’s sustainability architecture,
including solar energy generation, biogas-based
waste-to-energy
systems,
large-capacity
water
treatment plants, and extensive ecological water
bodies, reinforces Nalanda University’s position as
India’s premier net-zero higher-education campus.
Academic Engagements, Research
Output and Events
Academic activity across all Schools remained
vigorous, supported by faculty publications in
internationally
indexed
journals,
high-impact
research projects, and participation in national and
international conferences. Students and faculty
contributed to archaeological fieldwork, ecological
studies, manuscript research, Buddhist philosophy
seminars, South-South cooperation dialogues, and
international relations conferences. The University’s
digital learning environment continued to expand
through the mLibrary and associated databases.
Key academic and cultural events included SPIC-
MACAY performances, heritage learning programmes,
Raj Bhavan-Nalanda University Lecture Series,
sustainability workshops, Cross-Asian Dialogue on
Rural Development and community-based initiatives
under Sahabhāgita Samvāda, which engaged over
350 students and teachers from local communities.
International Collaborations and
Global Outreach
Nalanda University has expanded its international
engagement through academic collaborations and
institutional partnerships. Till date, the University
has signed more than 50 MoUs with universities
and institutions in Bangladesh, Cambodia, the Czech
Republic, Indonesia, Japan, Nepal, Republic of Korea,
Russia, Spain, Sri Lanka, US, and Vietnam, as well as
with leading institutions in India.
Under the ASEAN–India Network of Universities
(AINU), Nalanda University has established over 25
active collaborations involving IITs, NITs, IIM Bodh
Gaya, the Indian Maritime University, and universities
across Southeast Asia.
As part of its global academic outreach efforts, the
University participated in engagements in New York
and Washington DC with institutions like Columbia
University, UN, UNOSSC, and World Bank in July.
These interactions focused on areas including
sustainable development, knowledge diplomacy,
digital public goods, and international academic
cooperation.

Archives & Record Management
421
Archives & Records Management
Division
C H A P T E R
37
Archives & Records Management (A&RM) Division
is the custodian of important records of the Ministry
having archival value and a repository of 1.85 Lakh
physical files. The Division regularly undertakes the
job of appraisal and transfer of files to the National
Archives of India (NAI).
Completion of Digitisation work &
Inauguration of New Server
The Division has successfully transferred existing
digitised data (including TIF-to-PDF conversion, OCR,
and Metadata creation) from the old server to the
latest technology platform, the new server, for easier
record retrieval. The new server was inaugurated by
the then Secretary (East) on 28 March.
Revised Records Retention
Schedule 2024
A&RM Division circulated the revised Records
Retention Schedule (RRS) 2024 to all the concerned
stakeholders of the Ministry for compliance on 19 June
after getting approval from the NAI. Prior to this, the
last revised RRS had been issued in 2012.
Appraisal of Ordinary Records
As per the provisions of the Public Records Act, 1993,
and the Public Records Rules, 1997, the NAI must
regularly appraise declassified/ordinary records before
transferring selected records to the NAI. In line with
this, the first appraisal for this year was held in August,
in consultation with NAI. Out of 2,384 ordinary files,
1,016 selected physical files of important historical
and archival value have been transferred to NAI for
permanent preservation and uploading to the public
domain. The remaining 1,368 files/documents were
left in the Division.
In line with this, the second appraisal for this year
was organised in November in consultation with NAI.
Out of 1546 ordinary files, 129 selected physical files
of important historical and archival value have been
transferred to NAI for permanent preservation and

uploading to the public domain. The remaining 1417
files/documents were sent to the concerned Divisions
for Review/ Declassification. In total, during this year,
3,930 files have been appraised by NAI, out of which
1,145 files have been transferred to NAI.
Review/Declassification of records
Under the Public Records Act of 1993, records must
be reviewed by the NAI once they reach 25 years of
age. Since classified records cannot be appraised by
NAI, they need to be declassified beforehand. Since
January, a total of 4,113 physical files older than 25
years have been sent to the relevant Ministry divisions
for declassification or review. During November and
December alone, 1,268 files were forwarded to the
appropriate divisions. Overall, in this year, the A&RM
Division has dispatched 5,381 physical files to various
divisions for review and declassification.
Weeding out of physical files
Since January, the Division has weeded out 2,169
physical files of ordinary nature after obtaining
approval from the concerned Divisions of the Ministry.
Of these, 369 files were cleared by September, and
1,800 files were weeded out in October as part of
Swachhta Campaign 5.0. The Division also held three
cleanliness drives during this period. In November
and December 2025, an additional 96 physical files
were weeded out. Overall, a total of 2,265 ordinary
physical files have been destroyed in this year after
approval from the concerned Ministry Division.
